name: Aegean Hake Tomato Stew
hook: Tender fish in bright tomato broth

steps.t: Pat the hake dry and cut it into large pieces, then season lightly. Wet fish leaks into the stew and flakes before it has a chance to set.
Warm the olive oil in a shallow pan and soften the onion and green pepper until they slump but still look green at the edges. Browning them makes the broth heavy for a summer dish.
Add the garlic and pul biber and stir until the pepper flakes tint the oil. If the garlic catches, start again; burnt garlic is obvious in a light stew.
Pour in the grated tomatoes and fish stock, then simmer until the tomato foam settles and the broth tastes rounded rather than raw.
Stir in the olives and a squeeze of lemon, then slide in the hake pieces in one layer. Do not stir after this or the fish will break into flakes.
Cover and simmer gently until the fish turns opaque and separates in large moist petals when pressed with a spoon.
Take the pan off the heat, scatter with parsley and add more lemon to sharpen the broth. Boiling after the parsley goes in kills its grassy lift.

note: Any firm white fish such as cod, haddock or pollock works if cut into thick pieces.

name: Whole-Roasted Za’atar Mushrooms
hook: Meaty caps, tahini, pomegranate sparkle

steps.t: Heat the oven to 220°C fan and put a large tray inside to heat. A cold tray makes the mushrooms leak before they roast.
Wipe the mushrooms clean and trim only the dry stem ends, keeping them whole. Washing them under the tap loads them with water and dulls the roast flavour.
Toss the mushrooms with olive oil, za’atar, cumin, garlic and salt until the caps shine all over. Patchy oil leaves dry, wrinkled spots instead of juicy edges.
Tip them onto the hot tray stem-side down, spaced apart. If they touch, they stew in their own liquid rather than roasting.
Roast until the caps are deeply browned, the stems are tender and the juices on the tray have reduced to sticky dark spots.
Whisk tahini, lemon juice and cold water with a pinch of salt until pale and pourable. It may seize at first; keep whisking or it stays grainy.
Spoon the tahini onto a platter, pile the whole mushrooms on top and drizzle with pomegranate molasses. Finish with pine nuts and torn mint; add mint while the tray is hot and it blackens.

note: Serve with warm flatbread so the roasted mushroom juices do not get wasted.

name: Green Peppercorn Pumpkin Stew
hook: Peppery coconut, sweet squash, lime brightness

ingredients.name: peeled pumpkin or squash, cut into 3 cm chunks

steps.t: Heat the oil in a wide saucepan, add the curry paste and fry until it darkens slightly and smells roasted; if it stays raw and pasty, the stew will taste flat.
Add the pumpkin and aubergine and turn them through the paste until the edges are stained orange; dry patches mean those pieces will taste under-seasoned.
Pour in the coconut milk and stock, then add the peppercorns, soy sauce and sugar. Stir from the bottom so the paste does not catch and scorch.
Simmer uncovered until the pumpkin is tender at the centre but not collapsing into mush; a lively boil splits the coconut and makes the aubergine ragged.
Add the green beans and simmer until bright green with a little snap left; put them in too early and they go army-green and squeaky.
Turn off the heat, squeeze in the lime and tear over the herbs. Taste now, because lime boiled in the pot turns dull and bitter.

note: Serve with jasmine rice if you want it more filling; the stew itself stays vegetable-led.

name: Koji-Roasted Whole Sea Bream with Burnt Spring Onion Ponzu
hook: Deeply savoury fish, crackling roasted fins

ingredients.name: whole sea bream or sea bass, gutted and scaled

steps.t: Pat the fish very dry inside and out, then cut three shallow slashes on each side; wet skin steams instead of roasting and the marinade slides off.
Rub the shio koji and mirin over the fish and into the belly, lay the kombu inside with the lemon slices, then refrigerate uncovered; covering it traps moisture and softens the skin.
Take the fish out 45 minutes before roasting and scrape off any thick clumps of koji; left on in lumps, it burns before the flesh cooks.
Heat the oven to 220°C. Oil a tray, set the fish on it and tuck the fins close so they crisp rather than char to ash.
Roast until the skin blisters, the fins are brittle and the thickest part near the head reaches 63°C or flakes cleanly from the bone; undercooked flesh clings glassily to the spine.
While the fish roasts, put the spring onions under a hot grill or in a dry pan until blackened in patches and soft in the middle; pale onions taste raw and harsh.
Chop the burnt spring onions and mix with soy sauce, yuzu or lemon juice, rice vinegar and ginger. Spoon it over the rested whole fish at the table so the roasted skin keeps its crackle.

note: Ask the fishmonger to gut and scale the fish; leave the head and bones for the best roast flavour.

name: Smoked Gochujang Mushroom Tofu Bowls
hook: Wood-smoked mushrooms, sticky chilli glaze

ingredients.name: king oyster mushrooms, torn into thick strips

steps.t: Press the tofu between a board and kitchen paper until it feels firm and no longer weeps; watery tofu steams in the smoker and dilutes the glaze.
Tear the mushrooms with your hands, not a knife, so the rough edges catch smoke and sauce; neat slices stay slippery and bland.
Mix gochujang, soy, sesame oil, vinegar, honey and garlic. Toss half with the mushrooms and cubed tofu, keeping the rest clean for finishing.
Line a wok or deep pot with foil, add the wood chips, set a rack above them and put the mushrooms and tofu on the rack. Keep the food clear of the chips or it will taste sooty.
Cover tightly and heat until a thin stream of smoke appears, then smoke over medium heat; if smoke pours out aggressively, lower the heat before the glaze turns bitter.
Tip the smoked mushrooms and tofu onto a hot tray or pan and cook until the glaze goes tacky at the edges; stopping while it is wet leaves no chew.
Serve over brown rice with edamame, sesame seeds and the reserved glaze. Keep the reserved sauce away from the raw-tossed bowl so it stays safe and clean-tasting.

note: Each serving lands high in protein from tofu and edamame, with the mushrooms carrying the smoke.

name: Ginger Silk Steamed Egg Custard
hook: Quivering custard, warm ginger syrup

steps.t: Simmer the ginger, water and 30 g of the sugar until the syrup smells hot and gingery; boiling it hard makes it sharp and reduced before the custards are ready.
Warm the milk with the remaining sugar and salt until just steaming, not bubbling; milk that is too hot scrambles the eggs on contact.
Whisk the eggs only until no streaks remain, then slowly whisk in the warm milk and vanilla. Frothy eggs give a pocked, bubbly top instead of silk.
Strain the mixture into four small heatproof bowls and skim off surface bubbles; missed bubbles set as little craters.
Cover each bowl with foil and steam over the gentlest simmer until the custard wobbles like soft jelly at the centre; hard steam makes it split and honeycomb.
Rest off the heat with the lids on so the centres finish softly; lifting them straight away can wrinkle the surface.
Spoon the warm ginger syrup over the custards and finish with sesame seeds. Do not flood them while boiling hot or the tops loosen and turn watery.

note: Serve warm for comfort, or chill fully for a cleaner slice of ginger sweetness.

name: Coal-Grilled Sardine Tostadas with Lime-Cabbage Crunch
hook: Smoky oily fish, sharp crunchy slaw

steps.t: Light the coals and wait until they are grey with a steady glow; cooking over flames blackens sardine skin before the flesh is hot.
Pat the sardines dry, then rub with oil, cumin, paprika and salt. If the skin is damp, it welds itself to the grill.
Toss the cabbage with lime juice, jalapeño and a pinch of salt until it squeaks less between your fingers; dry cabbage falls off the tostadas in stiff shreds.
Grill the tortillas until crisp with toasted brown freckles, turning once; pale tortillas bend under the fish and go soggy.
Grill the sardines over the coals until the skin blisters and the flesh pulls from the backbone with a fork; keep moving them too soon and the skin tears.
Flake the sardines away from the bones while warm, checking with your fingers for fine bones; rushing this leaves sharp surprises in the tostadas.
Spread each crisp tortilla with a little mayonnaise, then add avocado, sardine, lime-cabbage slaw and coriander. Build just before eating so the bases stay snappy.

note: Fresh sardines are one of the cheapest oily fish; tinned sardines will not grill the same way.

name: Brazilian Griddle Chicken with Winter Feijão Farofa
hook: Smoke, citrus and beans for cold nights

steps.t: Mix the garlic, lime zest and juice, orange juice, cumin, smoked paprika, salt and 1 tablespoon oil. Coat the chicken thoroughly; if the thighs are folded, open them out or the thick seams will cook pale and late.
Leave the chicken to season while the griddle heats until a drop of marinade snaps on contact. A lukewarm griddle steams the meat and you lose the smoky stripes.
Griddle the chicken in one layer, presentation side down first, until the ridges mark it dark mahogany and the edges tighten; turn only when it releases easily or the crust will tear.
Cook the second side until the thickest piece reaches 74°C and the juices are clear, not glassy. Rest on a warm plate; cutting now spills the citrusy juices you worked for.

In a wide pan, melt the butter with the remaining oil, then add the cassava flour. Stir until it smells nutty and turns pale gold; if it goes bronze too fast, pull it off the heat because cassava catches quickly.
Fold in the black beans and cavolo nero, crushing a few beans so the farofa clumps rather than eating like dry sand. Cook until the greens are glossy and the beans are hot through.
Slice the rested chicken across the grain and spoon over any juices. Serve on the feijão farofa so the crumbs soak up the smoky citrus drips.

note: Built for winter: smoky griddled thighs over buttery bean farofa with just enough lime to lift the richness.

name: Lahori Crisp Halloumi Breakfast Parathas
hook: Crisp edges, hot chai energy

steps.t: Pat the halloumi very dry. Wet cheese makes the coating slide off into the oil, leaving leathery slabs instead of crisp ones.
Whisk the egg in a shallow bowl. Mix the flour, nigella, chilli, turmeric and garam masala on a plate, breaking up spice lumps so they do not fry bitter in one spot.
Dip each halloumi slice in egg, then press into the spiced flour. Tap off loose flour; dusty patches burn before the cheese warms through.
Heat the oil in a frying pan until a pinch of flour fizzes immediately. Shallow fry the halloumi in batches until the edges are frilled and deep golden, not beige.
Turn and fry the second side until crisp. Keep the heat at a steady sizzle; too fierce and the coating blackens while the centre stays cold.
Stir the yoghurt with mint and lime until sharp and spoonable. If it tastes flat beside the salty halloumi, add another squeeze of lime rather than salt.
Cook the parathas in a dry hot pan until the layers puff and spot brown. Pile with the crisp halloumi and mint yoghurt, then eat while the coating still crackles.

note: A salty, spicy breakfast built around properly shallow-fried halloumi and flaky paratha.

name: Vietnamese Pickled Halloumi Herb Table
hook: Bright pickle, salty cheese, herb drama

steps.t: Whisk the rice vinegar with the sugar until the grains disappear. If the sugar sits at the bottom, the first bites will be sour and the last syrupy.
Add the daikon, carrot and halloumi cubes, turning them gently so the cheese does not crumble. The brine should smell sharp but clean, not harsh enough to catch your throat.
Mix the fish sauce, lime juice and chilli in a small bowl. Taste it now: it should be salty, sour and lightly hot, because the vegetables will mute it once dressed.
Drain the pickled halloumi and vegetables well. Do not skip this or the platter will flood and wash the dressing off the leaves.
Arrange little gem leaves on a wide plate, then scatter over cucumber, pickled vegetables and halloumi. Build height loosely; compact piles look tidy but eat watery.
Spoon over the lime-fish sauce dressing just before serving, catching the halloumi cubes as well as the leaves so the salty cheese tastes intentional rather than separate.
Finish with whole herb leaves and crushed peanuts. Add the peanuts last, while dry, or they soften before guests get the first crisp bite.

note: A no-fuss centrepiece: quick-pickled crunch, squeaky halloumi and a bright Vietnamese-style dressing.

name: Amalfi One-Dish Pork with Courgettes and Tomatoes
hook: Juicy pork, tomatoes, lemony garden heat

ingredients.name: lemon, zested and cut into wedges

steps.t: Heat the oven to 220°C. Put the courgettes, tomatoes, fennel, onion, garlic, lemon wedges, olive oil, wine and salt into a large baking dish, tossing until glossy; crowded dry corners scorch before the pork cooks.
Bake the vegetables until the tomatoes begin to split and the fennel bends rather than snaps. This head start matters because pork tenderloin cooks faster than summer vegetables soften.
Rub the pork with lemon zest and a slick of the hot juices from the dish. Nestle it on top of the vegetables, not buried underneath, or it will steam grey instead of roasting.
Bake until the pork reaches 63°C in the thickest part and the tomatoes have collapsed into a light sauce. Start checking early; tenderloin goes from juicy to woolly quickly.
Lift the pork to a board and rest it loosely covered. If you slice straight away, the juices run into the board instead of staying in the meat.
Stir the basil through the hot vegetables off the heat so it wilts fragrant and green, not black. Crush a few tomatoes with a spoon to loosen the lemony pan juices.
Slice the pork into thick coins and lay it back over the vegetables. Spoon the bright tomato-fennel juices over the top for a light summer plate.

note: Everything bakes in one dish, with wine, lemon and tomatoes keeping the pork light rather than heavy.

name: Kolkata Slow-Braised Egg Kosha
hook: Silky masala clinging to jammy eggs

ingredients.name: ripe tomatoes, grated or finely chopped

steps.t: Lower the eggs into simmering water and cook for firm yolks that will survive braising. Cool under running water, then peel carefully; torn whites catch and toughen in the masala.
Warm the ghee in a heavy pan and add the onions. Cook slowly, stirring often, until they slump into a deep bronze tangle; pale onions give a thin gravy, burnt edges make it bitter.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and fry until the raw sting disappears and the fat smells savoury. If it sticks hard, splash in a spoon of water rather than scraping burnt paste through the dish.
Stir in the tomatoes, chilli, coriander and turmeric. Cook until the masala darkens, thickens and the ghee freckles the edges; watery tomato will not cling to the eggs.
Beat the yoghurt with a spoon of hot masala, then stir it into the pan on low heat. Add it cold and fast and it can split into grainy curds.
Make shallow slashes in the peeled eggs, nestle them into the masala and add 150 ml water. Cover and braise gently so the sauce bloops slowly, not boils hard, which makes egg whites rubbery.
Uncover, add garam masala and crushed kasuri methi, and simmer until the sauce is glossy and coats the eggs in a thick layer. Finish with coriander and serve as small shared spoonfuls.

note: A slow onion masala does the real work; the eggs are braised gently so they stay tender on a shared table.

name: Hanoi Ginger-Steamed Mushrooms with Peppery Glass Noodles
hook: Warm ginger steam, deep mushroom comfort

ingredients.name: mixed mushrooms, such as oyster, shiitake and chestnut
fresh ginger, cut into fine matchsticks

steps.t: Soak the glass noodles in just-boiled water until they bend without a chalky core; leave them too long and they turn slippery before the steamer even starts.
Tear large mushrooms into bite-sized pieces and slice firm stems thinly, keeping everything similar in thickness so the delicate caps do not collapse while the stems stay rubbery.
Mix soy sauce, vegetarian oyster sauce, sesame oil, sugar, white pepper and hot stock in a shallow heatproof bowl; taste it now, because steaming softens salt and pepper.
Drain the noodles hard, pile them into the bowl, then scatter over mushrooms, ginger and the pale spring onion slices; keep the mushrooms loose, not packed, or they steam grey and watery.
Steam over a lively simmer with the lid tight until the mushrooms look glossy and the noodle mound has drunk in the broth at the edges.
Rest the covered bowl off the heat so the noodles finish swelling in the ginger-soy steam; skip this and the broth sits thin underneath.
Finish with coriander and green spring onion, then lift from the bottom as you serve so every bowl gets peppery broth as well as mushrooms.

note: Use a wide bowl that fits your steamer basket; crowding the mushrooms makes them sweat instead of steam cleanly.

name: Uova alla Brace with Pancetta, Sage and Charred Ciabatta
hook: Smoky eggs with crisp sage edges

steps.t: Light the barbecue and wait for a bed of coals with a pale ash skin; flames lick the pans and scorch the egg bottoms before the whites set.
Set two small cast-iron pans on the grate to heat, and oil the ciabatta and tomatoes; cold pans make the pancetta stew instead of crisp.
Divide pancetta between the pans and cook until the cubes spit and the edges are amber, moving them to a cooler patch if the fat smokes hard.
Add sage and chilli for the last fragrant crackle, then crack in the eggs; keep the yolks away from the hottest edge or they tighten before the whites turn opaque.
Grill the ciabatta and tomatoes alongside until the bread has black bar marks and the tomato skins split but still hold their shape.
Shut the barbecue lid, or tent the pans with foil, until the egg whites are just set and the yolks still wobble when the pan is nudged.
Rub the toast with garlic, season the eggs, shower with Parmesan and serve straight from the pans; wait too long and the residual iron cooks the yolks solid.

note: A heavy pan is essential here; thin trays scorch over coals and give no control.

name: Kerala Lime-Cured Mackerel with Coconut Curry Leaf Oil
hook: Silky fish, hot coconut crackle

ingredients.name: sushi-grade mackerel fillets, previously frozen and thawed in the fridge
small red onion, very finely sliced

steps.t: Keep the mackerel fridge-cold and pull out any pin bones with tweezers; warm oily fish softens fast and loses the clean slices that make this dish elegant.
Slice the fillets on a slight angle into 5 mm pieces, wiping the knife between cuts so the silver skin stays neat rather than dragging.
Stir lime juice, salt and sugar until dissolved, then spoon over the fish in a single layer; a heap cures unevenly, leaving sour edges and raw centres.
Chill until the surface turns satin-opaque while the middle remains glossy and tender.
Briefly rinse the sliced onion in cold water and drain hard; unrinsed onion shouts over the fish and wet onion dilutes the cure.
Warm coconut oil, mustard seeds and curry leaves until the seeds pop and the leaves go glassy, then take it off the heat before the leaves blacken and taste bitter.

Arrange the fish on a cold platter with onion, chilli, coconut, coriander and crushed cumin, then spoon the warm curry leaf oil around, not directly over every slice, so the mackerel stays barely cured rather than cooked through.

note: Use only fish sold as suitable for raw eating, or fish frozen for parasite control; ordinary cooking mackerel is not appropriate for this dish.

name: Bangkok Basil Tofu with Cucumber and Lime Crunch
hook: Hot wok tofu, cool lime snap

ingredients.name: green beans, cut into short lengths
palm sugar or light brown sugar
cucumber, deseeded and cut into half-moons

steps.t: Wrap the tofu in a clean tea towel and press gently until the surface feels dry; wet tofu cools the wok and sheds water instead of catching at the edges.
Cut the tofu into chunky rectangles and mix soy sauce, lime juice and sugar in a small bowl; once the wok is hot there is no time to hunt for bottles.
Heat the wok until a drop of water skitters and vanishes, then add oil; if it only sits and bubbles, the tofu will stick and steam.
Lay in the tofu and leave it alone until the underside has golden freckles, then toss once; constant stirring breaks it into crumbs.
Add garlic, chilli and green beans and stir-fry hard until the beans turn vivid green with blistered spots but still snap when pressed.
Pour in the sauce around the side of the wok so it sizzles on contact, then toss until it clings in a shiny coat rather than pooling underneath.
Turn off the heat, fold through Thai basil and cucumber, and plate at once with peanuts; basil goes muddy and cucumber slumps if they cook in the wok.

note: This is best cooked in one small batch; doubling in the wok lowers the heat and makes it heavy.

name: Miso-Griddled Lamb with Negi Salt and Lemon
hook: Charred lamb, sharp scallion salt

steps.t: Slice the lamb across the grain into 5 mm pieces; thicker slices stay chewy on a hot griddle and thinner ones dry before they char.
Mix miso, mirin, soy and ginger, then smear it lightly over the lamb; a heavy coating burns black before the meat is cooked.
Stir spring onions with sesame oil and flaky salt, squeezing once with your fingers until glossy; leave it coarse so it tastes like a relish, not a paste.
Heat a flat griddle until faintly smoking and brush with neutral oil; if the pan is only warm, the miso leaks and boils around the meat.
Griddle the lamb in a single layer until the first side has dark lacquered patches and releases without tearing.
Flip and cook just until the second side is charred in spots and the centre still springs softly; overcooked lamb turns woolly fast at this thickness.
Move to a warm plate for a short rest so the juices settle instead of flooding the platter.
Scatter with sesame seeds, spoon over the negi salt and serve with lemon wedges for squeezing at the table.

note: Cook in batches if needed; a crowded griddle steams the lamb and turns the miso grainy.

name: Winter Orange Halloumi Dakos
hook: Warm honeyed walnuts over briny winter citrus

steps.t: Segment the oranges over a bowl so you catch every drop of juice; squeeze the membranes hard, because dry rusks stay chalky instead of turning plush.
Whisk the orange juice with the vinegar, 2 tbsp olive oil and a pinch of the salt, then spoon it over the broken dakos. Stop while the pieces still have corners; flooding them makes a paste.
Beat the yoghurt with the remaining salt and smear it on a winter-warm plate. If the yoghurt is fridge-cold, it tightens the halloumi rather than softening it.
Lay the softened dakos, orange segments, halloumi slices, onion and olives over the yoghurt in loose layers, not a pile, so the hot dressing can touch the cheese.
Warm the remaining 2 tbsp olive oil with the walnuts, honey and oregano until the honey foams and the walnut edges smell toasted; if the oil smokes, the oregano will taste bitter.
Pour the hot walnut dressing straight over the halloumi and leave it just long enough for the cheese edges to relax and shine, then serve before the rusks collapse.

note: Use pasteurised halloumi, as it is only warmed by the dressing rather than fried.

name: Pul Biber Pork Saç Breakfast Hash
hook: Charred pork, peppers and yolk-rich potatoes

ingredients.name: pork shoulder steak, sliced into thin strips
waxy potatoes, cut into 1 cm dice

steps.t: Put the potato dice in a covered microwaveable bowl with a splash of water and half the salt; cook until a knife meets only slight resistance. Raw potato will burn outside before the pork is safe.
Pat the pork dry and toss it with the cumin, pul biber and remaining salt. If it goes into the pan wet, it steams grey instead of catching like a saç stir-fry.

Heat a wide frying pan until a drop of water skitters, add 1 tbsp oil, then spread the pork in one layer. Leave it alone until the undersides are dark at the edges and the strips are cooked through with no pink centre.

Move the pork to a clean plate, not the raw-meat plate. Add the remaining oil, potatoes, onion and peppers to the pan and stir-fry hard until the potato corners turn crisp and the pepper skins blister.
Add the tomatoes and return the pork with any resting juices. Toss until the tomato skins wrinkle but the pieces have not turned saucy, or the hash will lose its breakfast crunch.
Make two hollows, crack in the eggs, and cover the pan just until the whites set and the yolks still wobble. Overcook them and you lose the sauce that pulls the hash together.
Scatter with parsley and serve from the pan while the pork edges are still sizzling.

note: This uses Turkish breakfast flavours and saç-style heat with pork, rather than claiming to be a traditional Turkish household dish.

name: Pomegranate Lentil Kofta Platter
hook: Griddled lentils, tahini silk, jewel-bright crunch

ingredients.name: tinned green lentils, drained and rinsed

steps.t: Spread the lentils on a clean tea towel and blot them until the towel stops picking up moisture; wet lentils make kofta that smear across the griddle.
Mash two thirds of the lentils roughly, leaving the rest whole for texture, then mix with chickpea flour, spring onions, parsley, garlic, cumin, baharat and 1 tbsp olive oil.
Rest the mixture until the chickpea flour hydrates and the mash feels like soft clay rather than damp rubble.
Shape 12 short kofta with oiled hands, pressing out cracks as you go. Cracks become split seams once they hit the griddle.
Heat a ridged griddle or heavy frying pan until properly hot, brush with 1 tbsp oil, and cook the kofta until the ridges are dark and the bottoms release without tearing.
Turn gently and griddle the second side until the centres feel springy, not squishy. If you keep flipping, the crust never forms.
Whisk tahini with lemon juice and enough cold water to make a glossy ribboning sauce; if it seizes, keep whisking and add water a spoon at a time.
Swipe labneh on a platter, add the kofta, drizzle with tahini, then finish with pomegranate seeds and the remaining olive oil for a guest-table finish.

note: The mix can be shaped a few hours ahead and griddled when guests arrive.

name: Crisp Chermoula Chicken with Courgette Ribbons
hook: Lacy chicken, lemon herbs, cool courgette

steps.t: Flatten any thick chicken pieces to an even 1.5 cm so they cook before the crust darkens; uneven pieces give you either raw centres or burnt semolina.

Mix coriander, parsley, lemon zest, half the lemon juice, garlic, ras el hanout and 1 tbsp olive oil. Spoon half over the chicken and keep the rest separate for the salad, never touching it with raw-chicken utensils.
Set up flour, beaten egg and semolina in three shallow dishes. Coat the chicken lightly in flour, then egg, then semolina; heavy flour patches turn gluey in the pan.
Shave the courgettes into ribbons and toss with tomatoes, the reserved herb mix and remaining lemon juice. Dress now, but do not salt heavily or the courgettes will flood the plate.
Heat 4 tbsp olive oil in a wide pan until a pinch of semolina fizzles on contact. If the oil is quiet, the coating drinks it and turns heavy.
Shallow fry the chicken in batches until the crust is sand-gold and crisp, and the thickest piece is piping hot through with clear juices. Crowding the pan drops the heat and softens the crust.
Drain on a rack, not kitchen paper, so steam can escape underneath. Serve over the courgette ribbons while the chicken still crackles.

note: For extra safety, check the thickest chicken piece reaches 74°C if using a probe.

name: Sherry-Pickled Mussels with Paprika Oil
hook: Smoky vinegar, sweet mussels, bread-ready juices

steps.t: Scrub and debeard the mussels, discarding cracked ones and any open mussels that do not close when tapped; bad shellfish cannot be rescued by vinegar.
Bring the wine to a hard boil in a lidded pan, add the mussels, cover and shake until the shells open. Stop as soon as they gape, or the meat shrinks tight.
Lift the mussels out, discard any that stayed closed, and strain 3 tbsp of the cooking liquor through a fine sieve so grit does not end up in the pickle.
Pull most mussels from their shells, leaving a few in half-shells for the platter. Keep them in a shallow dish so the escabeche can coat rather than drown them.
Warm the olive oil with garlic and bay until the garlic turns pale straw, then take it off the heat before adding paprika; paprika scorches in seconds and becomes dusty.
Stir in sherry vinegar, the strained mussel liquor, red onion and orange zest, then pour the warm dressing over the mussels. Let them pickle until the onion softens and the oil stains red.
Finish with parsley and serve at room temperature with bread for dragging through the smoky, sharp juices.

note: Cooked mussels should be eaten the same day and kept chilled if not serving straight away.

name: Za'atar Roast Eggs with Silk Onions
hook: Runny yolks under crackling za'atar oil

steps.t: Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Toss the sliced onions in a small roasting tin with the olive oil, butter, cumin and salt; if the onions sit dry rather than glossy, they will scorch before they soften.
Roast the onions until collapsed, jammy and amber at the edges, stirring once so the corner pieces do not burn black.
Stir the yoghurt, tahini, lemon juice and grated garlic until smooth; if it tastes flat now, it will taste dull under the hot eggs, so season it clearly.
Make four hollows in the hot onions and crack in the eggs whole. Keep the yolks centred in the onion nests, or the whites run thin and overcook before the yolks warm.
Sprinkle za'atar over the eggs and return the tin to the oven until the whites are just set and the yolks still wobble when you nudge the tray.
Spoon the cool tahini yoghurt onto warm plates and slide the onion eggs on top; do not leave them in the roasting tin, as the residual heat keeps cooking the yolks.

note: Serve with warm flatbread for scooping through the onions and yoghurt.

name: Smoked Chermoula Mushrooms on Semolina Toast
hook: Wood-smoke mushrooms with bright green heat

ingredients.name: thick slices semolina bread or sourdough

steps.t: Put the mushrooms in a wide pan with the olive oil and cook hard until they squeak, shrink and give off no puddle; if you crowd them, they stew grey instead of taking smoke.
Add the smoked paprika and cumin, stirring for a few seconds until the oil turns brick-red; let the spices sit still too long and they turn bitter.

Cover the pan with a tight lid and trap a small piece of smouldering food-safe smoking wood or a smoking gun hose under the lid; smoke the mushrooms until they smell like a charcoal breakfast stall, not an ashtray.
Mix the garlic, coriander, parsley, preserved lemon and lemon juice into a loose chermoula; do not blitz it to paste, because the herbs taste muddy once bruised too far.
Toast the bread until the cut face is crisp enough to scratch with a knife; soft toast collapses under the mushrooms.
Fold half the chermoula through the warm smoked mushrooms, spread labneh on the toast, then pile the mushrooms high and spoon over the remaining chermoula.

note: Use a smoking gun or food-safe smoking chips only; never burn treated wood or paper for smoke.

name: Saffron-Steam Hake with Sherry Clams
hook: Pearly fish in golden shellfish steam

ingredients.name: small fennel bulb, very thinly sliced

steps.t: Check the clams and discard any cracked ones or any open ones that do not close when tapped; one bad clam can taint the whole pan.
Warm the olive oil in a wide lidded pan and soften the fennel until it bends without browning; browned fennel makes the saffron broth taste heavy.
Add the garlic and saffron, stir until the garlic smells sweet, then pour in the sherry; if you do not boil off the raw alcohol, the steam tastes sharp.
Add the fish stock and clams, cover and steam until the clams open wide; remove them to a warm bowl as they open so the early ones do not turn rubbery.
Season the hake lightly and lay it in the saffron steam. Cover and cook until the flakes separate with gentle pressure but the centre is still glossy, not chalk white.
Lift the hake onto a platter, whisk cold butter and lemon juice into the pan liquor, then return the clams and parsley; boiling hard now splits the sauce and toughens the clams.
Spoon the clams and golden broth around the hake and serve at once, while the fish still holds its pearly sheen.

note: Serve in a shallow platter so guests see the opened clams and saffron broth.

name: Coal-Grilled Girolles with Tarragon Vinaigrette
hook: Smoke-kissed mushrooms, sharp herb gloss

ingredients.name: large girolles or mixed wild mushrooms, brushed clean

steps.t: Light the coals and wait until they are glowing with a thin grey ash; flames lick mushrooms black before their centres warm through.
Toss the mushrooms with olive oil and salt, keeping them barely coated rather than wet, because dripping oil causes flare-ups and soot.
Whisk the rapeseed oil, vinegar, mustard, shallot, capers and tarragon into a sharp vinaigrette; if it tastes mellow on its own, it will disappear against smoke.
Grill the mushrooms in a perforated grill pan or on a fine rack until the ridges darken and the stems relax, turning once so they do not dry into leather.
Tip the hot mushrooms straight into half the vinaigrette and toss until glossy; waiting until they cool means they will not drink in the dressing.
Scatter rocket over a platter, spoon on the warm mushrooms, then finish with the remaining vinaigrette; do not drown the leaves or the plate stops feeling summery.

note: Excellent with a chilled Loire white and a piece of grilled baguette.

name: Citrus-Cured Mackerel with Old Bay Crackers
hook: Silky mackerel, salt snap, citrus bite

ingredients.name: sashimi-grade mackerel fillets, pin-boned and chilled

steps.t: Keep the mackerel fridge-cold and slice it on a clean board into 5 mm pieces; warm fish smears under the knife and tastes oily rather than clean.
Stir grapefruit juice, lime juice, salt, sugar and Old Bay until dissolved; undissolved grains cure some pieces harshly and leave others bland.
Lay the mackerel in a shallow dish and spoon over the citrus cure so every slice shines; piling it deep leaves hidden raw-tasting patches.
Chill until the edges turn opaque but the centres remain glossy and tender, like ceviche rather than cooked fish.
Drain off most of the cure, then fold in grapefruit zest, lime zest, red onion, olive oil, dill and celery; leaving it swimming in acid makes the fish chalky.
Spoon the mackerel onto a cold plate with saltines on the side; top crackers only as people eat, or they lose their snap before the platter reaches the table.

note: Use fish sold for raw consumption and keep it refrigerated until serving.

name: Lace-Crisp Gochujang Chickpea Jeon
hook: Craggy edges, chilli warmth, quick crunch

ingredients.name: tin chickpeas, drained and patted dry

steps.t: Crush half the chickpeas roughly with a fork and leave the rest whole; if they are wet, the batter steams instead of frying crisp.

Whisk flour, potato starch, egg, gochujang, soy and 80 ml cold water to a thick cream, then fold in chickpeas, spring onions and kimchi; stop mixing as soon as no dry flour shows or the jeon turns bready.
Heat the oil in a wide frying pan over medium-high heat until a small drip of batter sizzles straight away; if the oil is only warm, the first pancake drinks it.
Spoon in two palm-sized pancakes and press them thin, leaving ragged edges; fry until the undersides are lace-brown and the centres look set at the rim.
Flip once and fry the second side until it sounds scratchy when nudged with a spatula; repeated flipping knocks off the crisp crust.
Drain on a rack, not kitchen paper, then splash with rice vinegar and scatter sesame seeds over while hot so the surface stays sharp rather than soggy.

note: Serve with extra kimchi or a quick cucumber salad if you want more freshness.

name: Red-Oil Pickled Chicken with Black Vinegar
hook: Cool meat, sharp brine, numbing chilli

steps.t: Put the chicken, half the ginger, half the spring onions and the Shaoxing wine in a pot, cover with cold water and bring to the gentlest simmer; a hard boil tightens the skin and clouds the meat.
Poach until the thickest thigh reaches 74°C at the bone, then lift the chicken into iced water; guessing here risks undercooked chicken, so use a probe if you have one.

Boil soy, vinegar, sugar, Sichuan peppercorns, star anise, remaining ginger, remaining spring onions and 250 ml water for a glossy pickling liquor; take it off once the sugar has gone and the pepper smells lemony, not scorched.
Cool the liquor completely before it touches the chicken; warm brine softens the skin and keeps the meat in the food-safety danger zone too long.
Pack chicken and liquor into a clean container, weight the pieces so they are submerged, and refrigerate until the flesh tastes seasoned to the bone.
Drain the chicken, remove the bones, and slice through the skin with a sharp knife; sawing with a dull blade tears the chilled skin away from the meat.

Smack the cucumber until split, cut it into chunks, then dress with sliced chicken, chilli oil, two spoonfuls of pickle liquor and sesame seeds; dress at the end or the cucumber collapses before serving.

note: This is a cooked, refrigerated pickle rather than a raw ferment; keep it chilled and eat within three days.

name: Chipotle Prawn Black Bean Protein Bake
hook: Smoky rice, juicy prawns, clean heat

steps.t: Heat the oven to 220°C fan and use a deep baking dish that holds the rice in a shallow layer; a cramped dish leaves hard grains in the middle.
Stir rice, black beans, passata, stock, chipotle, red pepper, sweetcorn, red onion and garlic directly in the dish until the chipotle has dissolved; pockets of paste make smoky hot spots.
Cover the dish tightly with foil, crimping the edges so steam cannot escape; loose foil is the difference between fluffy rice and dry pellets.
Bake until the rice has swollen and the liquid is mostly absorbed, with a little sauce still bubbling around the edges.
Season the prawns, fold them through the hot rice in one even layer, then re-cover; burying them in clumps makes the outside rubbery before the centre cooks.
Return to the oven until the prawns are pink, curled and opaque all the way through; pull them as soon as they lose their glassy stripe.
Rest covered, then squeeze over lime and scatter coriander; skipping the rest makes the rice seem wet even when it is cooked.

note: Prawns go in near the end so the dish stays high-protein without turning tough.

name: Mastiha Honey Steamed Egg Custards
hook: Silky steam-set sweetness with piney honey

steps.t: Crush the mastiha with the caster sugar until powdery; whole crystals cling to the bowl and give one bitter, resinous mouthful.
Warm milk, cream, honey, mastiha sugar and lemon zest until steaming at the edge, not boiling; boiled dairy tastes flat and scrambles the eggs on contact.
Beat the eggs just until smooth, then whisk in the hot milk a little at a time; rushing it in cooks yellow threads through the custard.
Strain into four small ramekins and skim off foam; bubbles left on top set as pockmarks instead of a glossy surface.
Cover each ramekin with foil and steam over barely trembling water until the edges are set and the centre wobbles like soft jelly; a rolling boil makes the custard grainy.
Lift out and stand for 5 minutes before uncovering, so condensation runs onto the foil rather than into the custard.
Finish with pistachios and a thin thread of honey while warm, or chill for a firmer spoonful.

note: Mastiha is powerful; use a tiny amount for a clean pine-honey finish.

name: Biber Salçası Pork and Bean Stew
hook: Peppery broth, soft beans, thrifty comfort

ingredients.name: pork shoulder, cut into 2 cm pieces
Turkish red pepper paste, biber salçası

steps.t: Heat the oil in a heavy pan and brown the pork in a single layer; crowding it makes grey liquid that dilutes the stew before it starts.
Add onion and carrot to the pork fat and cook until the onion is soft and sweet-smelling; if it still smells raw, the finished broth will taste thin.
Stir in garlic, cumin and biber salçası, scraping the pan until the paste darkens brick-red; stop before it catches black or it turns bitter.
Add tomatoes and stock, then scrape the browned bits from the base; leaving them stuck means leaving most of the flavour behind.
Simmer gently, half-covered, until the pork yields when pressed with a spoon; a fast boil toughens the shoulder and breaks the sauce greasy.
Fold in the white beans and dried mint, then simmer until the beans are hot and the broth coats them rather than washing over them.
Rest off the heat for 5 minutes before eating, so the pepper paste settles into the beans instead of tasting sharp on top.

note: Pork is not traditional in Turkish cooking; this uses Turkish stew flavours around the requested meat.

name: Tarragon Halloumi Ratatouille Gratin
hook: Golden squeak over jammy Provençal vegetables

steps.t: Heat the oven to 220°C fan. Cut the vegetables quite slim; chunky courgette stays watery while the halloumi over-browns.
In a shallow baking dish, whisk the oil, mustard, vinegar, garlic and tarragon until glossy, then toss in the vegetables. Keep the salt very light or the halloumi will make the whole dish briny.
Bake the vegetables until the tomatoes split and the onion tips start to singe; if they still look raw and wet, the gratin will steam instead of roast.
Stir once, scraping the sweet juices through the dish, then lay the halloumi on top and scatter over the breadcrumbs. Do not bury the cheese or it turns rubbery rather than golden.
Bake again until the halloumi has freckled brown spots and the crumbs are toast-coloured, not pale beige.
Rest for 3 minutes before serving; straight from the oven the tomato juices are too loose and will run all over the plate.

note: A fast tray-style gratin with French seasoning and Cypriot cheese, built entirely in one baking dish.

name: Smoky Cider Pork Pot with Cornmeal Dumplings
hook: Fork-soft pork under fluffy yellow caps

ingredients.name: boneless pork shoulder, cut into 8 cm chunks
cornmeal dumpling dry mix, equal parts self-raising flour and fine cornmeal

steps.t: Salt the pork chunks all over and leave them uncovered in the fridge or on a cool counter for 1 hour; skip this and the braise tastes seasoned only at the edges.
Heat the oil in a heavy casserole and sear the pork in batches until each side has a dark mahogany crust. Crowding the pan gives grey steamed meat and a thin sauce later.
Lower the heat, add the diced vegetables and cook until the onion turns translucent and the brown pork bits start loosening. If the base blackens, the cider will pull bitterness into the pot.
Stir in the garlic, tomato purée and smoked paprika for a minute, then pour in the cider and scrape hard. Leave stuck patches behind and you lose the deep roast flavour.
Add the stock and pork, cover, and braise at 150°C until a spoon can press the meat apart with almost no effort. If it still springs back, it is not weekend-soft yet.
Mix the dumpling dry mix with the milk and melted butter just until no dry flour shows, then spoon mounds onto the bubbling braise. Overmixing makes the dumplings heavy.
Cover and bake until the dumplings are puffed, set and yellow at the edges. Do not keep peeking, because the steam is what cooks their centres.
Rest uncovered for 10 minutes, skim any loud orange fat, and break the pork into large pieces; shredding it too fine makes the pot eat like paste.

note: A proper long braise with a cider backbone and Southern-style cornmeal dumplings.

name: Chimichurri Lentil Guiso with Eggs
hook: Herby heat, soft yolks, serious protein

steps.t: Warm the oil in a wide pan and cook the onion and pepper until the onion is soft and the pepper smells sweet. If they stay crunchy, the stew tastes like salsa with lentils dumped in.
Add the garlic, tomato purée, paprika and cumin, stirring until the purée darkens brick-red. Stop too early and it tastes tinny; scorch it and the paprika goes dusty-bitter.
Stir in the lentils and stock, then simmer until the liquid looks slightly thick and glossy around the spoon. A hard boil will split the lentils into sludge.
Fold in the spinach until just wilted and bright green. Cook it to khaki and you lose the fresh lift that balances the eggs.
Make six hollows, crack in the eggs, cover and simmer gently until the whites are opaque and the yolks still wobble when the pan is nudged. Furious bubbling gives rubbery whites before the tops set.
Spoon chimichurri over the eggs just before eating; boiling it in the stew dulls the parsley and turns the garlic harsh.

note: Two eggs per serving plus lentils make this a high-protein, meat-free gym bowl.

name: Steamed Coconut Quindim Cups
hook: Glossy gold custard with coconut chew

ingredients.name: caster sugar, plus extra for dusting

steps.t: Butter six small heatproof cups and dust them with sugar. Miss a corner and the custard grips there, tearing the glossy top when you unmould it.
Stir the coconut into the coconut milk and leave it to plump until it looks snowy and damp rather than dry. Unsoaked coconut steals moisture from the custard.
Whisk the yolks, whole eggs, sugar, vanilla, lime zest and salt gently, then strain into a jug. Beating in foam gives pitted custards instead of that smooth quindim shine.
Stir the soaked coconut into the egg mixture and divide it between the cups. Keep the coconut evenly suspended or one cup gets all chew and another all custard.

Set the cups on a trivet in a lidded pan with simmering water halfway up their sides, then steam gently until the edges are set and the centres tremble like jelly. A rolling boil punches holes through the custard.
Rest the cups for 10 minutes, then chill or serve barely warm; unmoulding while hot makes the custard slump and leak syrup.

note: A steamed, cup-sized take on Brazilian quindim, rich with yolks and coconut.

name: Karachi Smoked Pollock Masala Rice
hook: Smoky flakes through spiced tomato rice

ingredients.name: smoked white fish fillets, such as pollock or haddock

steps.t: Rinse the rice in a sieve until the water runs much less cloudy. Skip this and the grains glue together before the fish has warmed through.
Fry the onion in the oil over medium heat until the edges turn copper-brown. Pale onion leaves the rice flat; black onion makes the whole pan taste burnt.
Stir in the garlic-ginger paste, garam masala and turmeric until the raw garlic smell disappears. Spices left dry on the pan catch quickly and turn bitter.
Add the tomatoes and cook until they thicken and small orange oil dots appear at the edges. If the tomatoes stay watery, the rice finishes soupy in the middle.
Stir in the rinsed rice, peas and 250 ml boiling water, then lay the smoked fish on top. Cover tightly and cook on low until the rice has absorbed the liquid and the fish is steaming hot and flaky.
Turn off the heat and rest without lifting the lid, then flake the fish through the rice, checking for skin or stray bones. Stirring too soon snaps the rice and makes it starchy.
Finish with lemon juice and coriander. Add them earlier and the coriander wilts into the masala instead of tasting fresh.

note: Built around inexpensive smoked white fish, pantry rice and one covered pan.

name: Chimichurri Mackerel Sartenazo
hook: Hot pan, oily fish, sharp green fire

steps.t: Cut the mackerel into 4 cm pieces and pat it very dry; if it goes into the pan damp, the skin steams and tears instead of crisping.
Stir parsley, vinegar, oregano, garlic, chilli flakes, salt and 1 tbsp olive oil into a rough chimichurri; do not blend it smooth or it turns grassy and bitter.
Heat a wide frying pan or wok until a drop of water skitters away, then add 1 tbsp olive oil; if the pan is only warm, the vegetables slump before they char.
Stir-fry the onion, pepper and potatoes hard until the pepper blisters and the potato cut sides turn golden at the edges.
Push the vegetables aside, lay the mackerel skin-side down and leave it until the skin tightens and freckles brown; moving it early is what makes it break up.
Turn the fish once, toss everything together for the last minute, then take the pan off the heat as soon as the flakes just separate; overcooked mackerel tastes metallic and dry.
Spoon over the chimichurri at the table, not in the pan, so the parsley stays bright and the garlic keeps its snap.

note: Use leftover boiled potatoes to make this genuinely weeknight-fast.

name: Dendê-Griddled Tofu with Cassava Farofa
hook: Smoky tofu, coconut edges, sandy crunch

steps.t: Wrap the tofu in a clean tea towel, weight it with a heavy pan and press until it feels firm rather than bouncy; skip this and the marinade slides off into the griddle.
Whisk coconut milk, dendê, lime juice, garlic, paprika and salt, then slice the tofu into thick slabs and coat them; thin slabs dry out before they char.
Marinate the tofu in a shallow dish, turning once so every face stains orange; if it sits piled up, the centre pieces taste plain.
Cook onion and red pepper in butter until soft and sweet, then stir in cassava flour until it looks like damp golden sand; rush it and the farofa tastes dusty.
Heat a ridged griddle until it smokes lightly, oil it with a folded piece of kitchen paper, and lay on the tofu with space between pieces; crowding drops the heat and gives you boiled tofu.
Griddle the tofu until dark lines appear and the edges look coconut-glazed, then turn once with a thin spatula; repeated flipping scrapes away the crust.
Brush with a little remaining marinade and griddle briefly until sticky, not wet; raw-looking marinade on the plate tastes flat and greasy.
Serve the slabs over the warm farofa with coriander scattered over so the crunch stays separate from the glossy tofu.

note: Dendê is potent; two tablespoons give colour and aroma without making the dish heavy.

name: Crisp Lahori Lamb Chapli Patties
hook: Craggy lamb edges with gym-day heat

steps.t: Mix lamb, onion, gram flour, egg, pomegranate molasses, spices and salt with your fingers until the mince turns tacky; if it stays loose, the patties crack in the oil.
Shape into six thin, rough-edged patties and press a shallow dent in each centre; thick domed patties burn outside before the lamb is safely cooked through.
Rest the patties in the fridge so the gram flour hydrates and the edges set; frying them warm makes them shed juices and stew.
Heat the oil in a heavy frying pan until a crumb of mixture sizzles at once, then lay in three patties; a cool pan gives grey, greasy lamb.
Shallow fry until the undersides are deep brown and crisp enough to release without tugging; forcing them early leaves the crust behind.
Turn once and cook until the second side is crisp and the centre is piping hot with no pink lamb remaining; undercooked mince is not worth the risk.
Drain on kitchen paper for a minute, then serve with cold yoghurt and lemon; leaving them sitting in the pan softens the craggy edges you worked for.

note: Lean lamb keeps the protein high, while gram flour gives the chapli-style crispness.

name: Vietnamese Coffee Steamed Egg Flans
hook: Silky custard under bitter caramel

steps.t: Cook sugar and water in a small pan without stirring until the bubbles slow and the caramel turns the colour of dark tea; take it too far and it tastes burnt, not bitter.
Divide the caramel between four ramekins and swirl to coat the bases before it sets; if you dawdle, it hardens in the pan.
Whisk eggs, yolk, milk, condensed milk, coffee and salt gently until even, keeping the whisk low; frothy custard steams into a pitted surface.
Strain the custard into a jug, then fill the ramekins; skipping the sieve leaves white strands of egg in the finished flan.
Set the ramekins in a steamer, cover each with foil and steam over the gentlest simmer until the edges are set and the centres wobble like jelly; hard boiling makes tunnels and curdles the eggs.
Lift the flans out and cool until the ramekins are no longer warm to the touch; unmoulding hot custard makes it slump and split.
Chill until cold, then run a thin knife around each edge and invert onto plates so the coffee caramel floods the top.

note: A low simmer is the secret: steam should be quiet, not rattling the lids.

name: One-Tin Roman Chicken Pasta Bake
hook: Tomato-stained pasta with crisp chicken corners

ingredients.name: boneless chicken thighs, cut into chunks

steps.t: Heat the oven to 200°C fan and choose a deep roasting tin; a shallow tray lets the stock evaporate before the pasta cooks.
Toss chicken, onion, garlic, olive oil, oregano and chilli in the tin, spreading the chicken out so it roasts rather than sweats.
Bake until the onion edges soften and the chicken corners start to colour; if it is still pale, the finished bake tastes boiled.
Stir in the dry penne, tomatoes and hot stock, making sure every pasta tube is mostly submerged; exposed pasta turns leathery instead of tender.
Cover tightly with foil and bake until the pasta has swollen and the sauce bubbles hard at the edges; loose foil leaks steam and leaves crunchy centres.
Remove the foil, stir well from the corners where pasta sticks first, then scatter over the cheese.
Bake uncovered until the top is speckled golden and the chicken is piping hot through with no pink in the thickest piece.
Rest for five minutes before serving, because the sauce thickens as it stands; spoon it out immediately and it runs like soup.

note: Chicken thighs stay forgiving and cheap, which is exactly what a student bake needs.

name: Goan Tamarind Squid Winter Braise
hook: Dark, tangy warmth with velvet-soft squid

ingredients.name: cleaned squid, bodies sliced into rings, tentacles halved

steps.t: Pat the squid very dry and check for any hard quill or beak; wet squid steams the masala thin before the braise can grip it.
Heat the oil in a heavy casserole, add the onions with a pinch of salt, and cook until they collapse to sticky bronze strands; stop at pale gold and the finished sauce tastes raw and sweet.
Stir in the garlic and ginger for a minute, then add coriander, chilli and turmeric; keep it moving until the oil stains brick-red, because scorched spice turns bitter fast.
Add the tomatoes and cook hard until the spoon leaves a clear trail and the oil freckles the surface; if it still looks watery, the coconut milk will taste flat.
Pour in the coconut milk and tamarind, then fold in the squid so every piece is coated; a furious boil tightens the squid before it has time to soften.
Cover and braise on the lowest bubble until the squid cuts with a spoon edge and the sauce has darkened to rust; if the pan dries, splash in water rather than letting coconut catch on the base.
Uncover, stir in the garam masala and simmer until glossy and spoon-coating; serve while the squid is relaxed, as repeated reheating makes it springy again.

note: Best with basmati rice or buttered rotis for a proper cold-night bowl.

name: Bangkok Mackerel Morning Stew
hook: Bright rice broth, rich flakes, chilli heat

ingredients.name: palm sugar or light brown sugar

steps.t: Put the rice, stock, lemongrass, ginger and lime leaves in a saucepan and bring to a gentle simmer; a hard boil bursts the rice unevenly and muddies the broth.
Simmer until the grains swell and the liquid turns softly cloudy but still loose; if it looks like porridge already, add a little water before the fish goes in.
Season with fish sauce and sugar, tasting for salty depth rather than sweetness; under-season now and the oily mackerel will taste heavy.
Lay the mackerel fillets skin-side up on the simmering rice and cover; do not stir yet, or the fillets break into dry shreds before they set.
Lift out and discard the lemongrass and lime leaves, then slide in the pak choi; cook just until the stems lose their raw snap, as dull greens make the bowl feel tired.
Break the mackerel into large flakes with a spoon, keeping the skin in pieces if you like its richness; mashing it small makes the stew oily rather than silky.
Ladle into warm bowls with chilli, coriander and lime wedges; squeeze lime at the table so the broth stays bright, not cooked-sour.

note: A Thai-style breakfast bowl with enough body to carry you through a cold morning.

name: Yuzu Miso Whole-Roast Pork Collar
hook: Lacquered edges, juicy slices, citrus miso

ingredients.name: yuzu or unwaxed lemon, zest and 1 tbsp juice

steps.t: Take the pork from the fridge 30 minutes before cooking and dry the surface thoroughly; cold, damp meat roasts unevenly and the glaze slides off.
Heat the oven to 210°C fan and set the pork on a rack over a roasting tin; roasting flat in its juices gives you steamed sides instead of a proper crust.
Mix miso, mirin, sake, soy, honey, ginger, garlic and citrus zest to a smooth paste, then rub two thirds over the pork; thick clumps burn before the centre is hot.
Roast until the glaze starts to blister in dark mahogany patches, watching the honey at the edges because it can go from lacquered to bitter quickly.
Lower the oven to 150°C fan, spoon 150 ml water into the tin and roast until a probe in the centre reads 68–70°C; guessing by colour is unreliable with miso-stained pork.
Brush with the remaining glaze and roast until sticky and shining, not blackened; if the tin runs dry, the drips will smoke and taint the meat.
Rest the joint loosely covered until the juices settle, then stir citrus juice into the pan drippings for a sharp spoon sauce; slicing too soon floods the board and dries the pork.
Carve into thick slices and scatter with spring onions; cut too thin and the roast loses its generous, guest-table feel.

note: Serve with plain rice, pickles and a bitter green salad to balance the richness.

name: Tea-Smoked Mayak Eggs with Cucumber Ice
hook: Cool crunch, smoky yolks, sesame bite

steps.t: Lower the eggs into simmering water and cook for set whites with creamy centres; dropping them into a rolling boil cracks shells and leaks white.
Chill the eggs in iced water, then peel carefully under water; torn whites catch too much smoke and turn leathery at the scars.
Line a wok or deep pan with foil, add rice, tea and brown sugar, and set a rack above it; if the foil has gaps, burnt sugar welds itself to the pan.
Put the peeled eggs on the rack, cover tightly and heat until a steady wisp of smoke appears, then smoke gently; billowing smoke makes the eggs acrid rather than fragrant.
Move the eggs to a plate and cool uncovered until the surface feels dry; trapping them hot under film makes condensation wash away the smoke.
Toss cucumber with soy, rice vinegar, sesame oil and gochugaru just before serving; salt it too early and it slumps instead of staying icy-crisp.
Halve the eggs and arrange over the cucumber with spring onions and sesame seeds; cut with a clean wet knife so the smoky yolks stay neat, not smeared.

note: Keep the smoking light and brief; the plate should feel summery, not barbecue-heavy.

name: Steamed Aubergine with Black-Vinegar Ribbons
hook: Silky purple folds, sharp garlic gloss

steps.t: Cut the aubergines lengthways into quarters, then into long batons; pieces of mixed thickness steam unevenly, leaving some cottony while others collapse.
Set the aubergine skin-side up in a steamer in a single loose layer; piling it high traps water and makes the flesh taste boiled.
Steam over rapidly boiling water until the batons bend easily and the cut sides look translucent; stop too soon and the aubergine keeps a woolly bite.
Lift the aubergine out and let it drain in a colander for a few minutes; sauce poured onto wet aubergine slides straight off into the plate.
Stir garlic, ginger, soy, black vinegar, sugar, chilli oil and sesame oil until the sugar dissolves; undissolved grains give harsh sweet spots instead of a clean dressing.
Arrange the warm aubergine as loose ribbons on a shallow plate and spoon the dressing along the length; tossing hard breaks the pieces into mash.
Finish with spring onions and coriander, then serve warm or at room temperature; fridge-cold aubergine dulls the vinegar and stiffens the silky flesh.

note: A clean vegetable plate for a spread of dumplings, greens and pickles.

name: Coal-Lime Hake Tacos
hook: Smoke, lime and flaky white fish

steps.t: Light a small bed of coals and wait until they are glowing with a thin grey ash; cook over flames and the fish will taste sooty before it flakes.
Mix lime zest, half the juice, chipotle, cumin, oil and salt, then rub it over the hake; leave it while the grill settles, but do not drown it or the surface will steam instead of char.
Toss the cabbage with the remaining lime juice and a pinch of salt until it squeaks and softens at the edges; skip this and the tacos eat dry and raw.
Oil the grill bars, lay on the fish and cook until the underside has dark grill marks and the edges turn opaque; if you prod too early, the fillet tears.
Turn the fish once and cook until it flakes in broad, juicy pieces, not chalky crumbs; thinner tail pieces may need lifting off first.
Warm the tortillas on the grill until they blister in spots and bend without cracking; stack them in a cloth so they stay supple.
Break the fish into chunky flakes and pile into tortillas with cabbage, avocado and coriander; finish while the smoke is still on the fish.

note: Use any firm white fish fillet of similar thickness; pollock works if you handle it gently.

name: Santorini Scallops in Chilled Tomato Water
hook: Silky scallops, briny capers, cold sun

steps.t: Stir the tomatoes with the salt, then tip into a muslin-lined sieve over a bowl; press hard and the water turns cloudy rather than jewel-clear.
Chill the dripping tomato water overnight, covered; leave it warm on the bench and it loses its clean, bright flavour.
Keep the scallops refrigerated until the last moment, pat them very dry and slice each into three coins; any sour smell means they are not for this dish.
Whisk lemon juice, olive oil and ouzo until glossy, then spoon half over the scallops; too much acid too early tightens them like rubber.
Stir capers and cucumber into the cold tomato water, tasting for salt; it should taste like a clear Greek salad, not tomato juice.
Swipe yoghurt thinly across chilled plates so it anchors the scallops; dollops make the dish heavy and hide the shellfish.
Lay on the scallops, spoon over tomato water, scatter dill and finish with the remaining ouzo oil; serve immediately while the scallops are cold and satin-soft.

note: Buy scallops sold for raw eating from a reputable fishmonger, keep them below 5°C, and serve the day you prepare them.

name: Urfa Beef and Pepper Sac Sizzle
hook: Lean beef, hot pan, smoky peppers

ingredients.name: lean beef rump steak, thinly sliced

steps.t: Pat the beef dry and salt it lightly; wet slices boil in their own juice and never get the kebab-shop edges you want.
Heat a wok, sac or heavy frying pan until a drop of water skitters away at once; start cool and the beef will stew grey.
Add half the oil and stir-fry the beef in one loose layer until the edges char and the centres are still springy; crowd the pan and the protein leaks out.
Lift the beef to a plate, add the remaining oil, peppers and onion, then toss until blistered at the tips but still bright.
Stir in Urfa chilli and tomato paste until the paste darkens brick-red and smells roasted; leave it raw and the whole pan tastes metallic.
Return the beef with any juices and toss just until glossy and hot; another minute turns lean rump chewy.
Serve over warm bulgur with yoghurt and parsley, keeping the yoghurt to the side so it cools the chilli instead of splitting in the pan.

note: For extra protein without extra fuss, increase the yoghurt rather than overcooking more beef.

name: Orange Blossom Steamed Egg Custards
hook: Soft wobble, date syrup, pistachio

steps.t: Set a steamer over a gentle simmer, not a rolling boil; fierce steam makes pitted custard instead of a smooth wobble.
Whisk eggs, sugar, cardamom and salt just until the whites disappear; froth on top bakes into bubbles and spoils the texture.
Warm the milk until it feels hot but not scalding, then whisk it slowly into the eggs; pour fast and you scramble the base.
Stir in the orange blossom water, then strain into four heatproof cups; skipping the sieve leaves stringy egg in the finished dessert.
Cover each cup tightly with foil and steam until the edges are set and the centre trembles like set jelly; uncovered cups drip with condensation.
Rest the custards off the heat until the wobble steadies; move them immediately and the surface can split.
Spoon date syrup over the warm custards and scatter pistachios on top, keeping the nuts dry until serving so they stay crisp.

note: Serve warm for the softest texture, or chill and add the syrup just before eating.

name: Chermoula-Crisp Tofu with Carrot Couscous
hook: Crunchy tofu, lemony herbs, pennies

steps.t: Wrap the tofu in kitchen paper and press with a plate until the surface feels tacky, not wet; damp tofu spits and drops its crust.
Cover the couscous with 150 ml boiling water and a pinch of salt, then lid it; too much water makes paste instead of separate grains.
Cube the tofu and toss with cornflour, cumin, paprika and salt until every face looks dusty; bare patches fry pale and soft.
Heat the oil in a frying pan until a crumb of tofu coating fizzes at once, then add the tofu with space between pieces; crowding cools the oil and makes it leathery.
Shallow fry, turning with tongs, until all sides are crisp and rust-gold; if you keep stirring, the coating breaks off.
Fluff the couscous with carrot, lemon zest, half the juice, garlic and coriander; fork it up from the bottom or the carrot clumps in one corner.
Drain the tofu briefly on paper, splash with the remaining lemon juice and serve on the couscous while the crust still crackles.

note: A non-stick pan lets you use the full crunch with less oil, but still wait for the oil to properly fizz.

name: Rioja Escabeche Lamb with Butter Beans
hook: Sharp sherry cuts through velvet lamb

ingredients.name: lamb shoulder, cut into 5 cm chunks
Rioja or other dry red wine

steps.t: Season the lamb hard with salt, then brown it in the olive oil in a heavy casserole until the corners are walnut-dark; if the pan is crowded it will steam and the escabeche will taste flat.
Lift out the lamb, add the onion and cook until soft and honey-coloured at the edges; stop short of dark brown or the vinegar will make it bitter.
Add the garlic, smoked paprika, rosemary and bay, stirring for just long enough for the paprika to smell smoky; let it catch and it turns acrid.
Pour in the sherry vinegar and Rioja, scraping the base until it feels smooth under the spoon, then return the lamb with any juices and add enough water to almost cover.
Cover and simmer very gently until a spoon presses through the lamb with little resistance; a rolling boil tightens the meat before it has time to relax.
Stir in the butter beans and simmer uncovered until the liquor looks glossy and clings lightly to the beans; if it is watery, the dressing will slide off the lamb.
Rest off the heat, then dress with parsley, orange zest and a final spoon of raw olive oil; add them too early and the winter brightness disappears.

note: Escabeche is best warm rather than hot, when the vinegar, oil and lamb juices taste rounded.

name: Lyonnais Breakfast Tian of Potatoes, Leeks and Cream
hook: Golden edges, soft leeks, quiet luxury

ingredients.name: waxy potatoes, scrubbed and thinly sliced

steps.t: Heat the oven to 190°C and butter a shallow baking dish; a deep dish leaves the middle pale and sleepy instead of breakfast-crisp.
Cook the leeks in butter and olive oil until they collapse into soft green ribbons with no squeak left; undercooked leeks stay stringy in the bake.
Whisk the crème fraîche, milk, Dijon, thyme, nutmeg, salt and pepper until smooth; streaks of mustard mean the seasoning lands in sharp patches.
Layer half the potatoes, all the leeks, then the remaining potatoes, seasoning each potato layer lightly; dump them in loose and the top scorches before the centre cooks.
Pour over the cream mixture, press the slices down until the surface glistens, then scatter with Comté; dry potato tips turn leathery, not crisp.
Bake until a knife slips through the centre without crunch and the rim is bubbling bronze; if the top races ahead, cover loosely with foil.
Rest until the bubbling calms and the cream settles back around the potatoes; cut too soon and it spills like soup.

note: Serve with black coffee and a sharp dressed salad if breakfast is edging into brunch.

name: Bourbon Cider Braised Chicken with Pecan Crumb
hook: Glossy chicken, orchard smoke, crisp pecans

steps.t: Salt the chicken and dust the skin side lightly with flour, tapping off excess; thick flour turns the sauce pasty instead of glossy.
Sear skin-side down in hot oil until the skin is deep amber and releases without tearing; move it early and the best crust stays glued to the pan.
Turn for one minute on the flesh side, then lift the chicken out; browning the flesh hard dries the side that should braise tender.
Soften the shallots in the chicken fat until translucent and sweet, then add garlic for the final minute; scorched garlic will shout through the bourbon.
Add bourbon off the hottest flame, then cider, stock, maple and vinegar, scraping until the browned bits dissolve; leave them stuck and the sauce lacks depth.
Return the chicken skin-side up, keep the liquid below the skin, cover and braise at a lazy bubble until the meat is tender at the bone; submerged skin goes flabby.
Uncover and simmer until the sauce coats the back of a spoon in a shiny layer; if it tastes sweet before reducing, wait before adding salt.
Spoon sauce around the chicken and finish with toasted pecans just before serving; add them earlier and they lose their crackle.

note: A wide casserole makes this look generous at the table and keeps the skin proud of the braise.

name: Patagonian Shellfish Cazuela with Tomato and Torrontés
hook: Briny broth, sweet tomato, summer lift

ingredients.name: Torrontés or other dry white wine

steps.t: Warm the oil and cook onion and red pepper until they soften without browning; browned vegetables make this light cazuela taste heavy.
Add garlic and paprika, stirring until the garlic smells sweet and the oil turns brick-red; if the paprika burns, start again because the broth will be dusty.
Add tomatoes and wine, then simmer until the tomato looks pulpy rather than raw and the wine’s sharp edge has blown off.
Check the mussels and discard any cracked ones or any open ones that do not close when tapped; bad shellfish can ruin more than dinner.
Add the mussels, cover and simmer until most shells spring open; keep the lid on or the top layer will sulk shut in cool steam.
Add prawns, re-cover and cook just until they curl into loose Cs and turn opaque; tight Os mean they have gone rubbery.
Discard any mussels that remain closed, then finish with lemon zest, parsley and a squeeze of lemon; boiling after the herbs go in kills the summer brightness.

note: Serve in shallow bowls so the shellfish sits in broth rather than drowning in it.

name: Bahia Whole-Roasted Halloumi with Lime and Dendê Peppers
hook: Salty cheese, red oil, lime snap

steps.t: Heat the oven to 220°C and pat the halloumi dry all over; surface moisture makes it steam and split instead of roasting glossy.
Toss pepper and onion with olive oil, cumin, chilli and a pinch of salt in a small roasting dish, leaving a space in the centre; bury the cheese and it will stew in vegetable water.
Rub the halloumi with dendê oil and grated garlic, then set it whole in the centre; garlic left in clumps burns black before the cheese warms through.
Roast until the halloumi is swollen, lacquered at the edges and the peppers are soft with singed tips; pale cheese will squeak rather than yield.
Spoon hot red oil from the dish back over the block and return it briefly until the top blisters in small freckles; walk away now and it can toughen.
Finish with lime zest, lime juice, cassava flour and coriander while the dish is still hot; add the flour too early and it drinks the oil before reaching the table.
Score the halloumi into thick slices at the table so people can drag pieces through the pepper oil; slicing it cold loses the shared-plate drama.

note: Dendê is powerful; the olive oil keeps it fragrant rather than heavy.

name: Maple Celeriac Waldorf Slab
hook: Cold crunch under warm maple spice

steps.t: Shave the celeriac on a mandoline into wafer-thin sheets, then stack and cut into broad ribbons; if the pieces are thick, they will eat woody rather than silky-crisp.

Whisk soured cream, mayonnaise, maple syrup, cider vinegar, Dijon, allspice and a good pinch of salt until glossy; stop when it loosens to double-cream texture, as a stiff dressing clumps instead of coating.
Fold celeriac through the dressing with your hands until every ribbon is slick and pale; dry patches stay harsh and peppery.
Add celery, apple and cranberries, turning gently so the apple keeps its edges; rough mixing bruises it and makes the salad watery.
Leave the bowl at room temperature for 10 minutes, just until the celeriac bends without snapping; much longer and the crunch goes tired.
Spoon onto a chilled platter in one generous slab and shower with crushed crackers at the last second; add them early and they turn to paste.

note: A barely cooked-feeling winter salad built like American Waldorf, with comfort coming from maple, creaminess and spice rather than heat.

name: Chimichurri Halloumi Breakfast Salteado
hook: Squeaky cheese, blistered peppers, sharp herbs

steps.t: Pat the halloumi dry until the paper comes away almost clean; damp cubes steam and shed brine instead of catching in the pan.
Stir parsley, oregano, vinegar, garlic, chilli flakes, 1 tablespoon olive oil and a pinch of salt into a loose chimichurri; do not make it too early or the herbs darken.
Heat a wide frying pan or wok until a potato cut-side sizzles the instant it touches, then add the remaining oil; a lukewarm pan gives you oily potatoes.
Stir-fry potatoes for 4 minutes until the cut sides are crusty and gold; keep them moving only every 20 seconds, because constant stirring stops the crust forming.
Add pepper and onion and toss hard over high heat until the pepper skins blister and the onion tips char but still snap.
Add halloumi and smoked paprika, then stir-fry for 90 seconds until the cheese edges freckle brown; cook it longer and it tightens into rubber.
Take the pan off the heat, fold through half the chimichurri and pile over toast with the rest spooned on top; adding the herbs over flame kills their sharpness.

note: A fast breakfast salteado borrowing Argentine parrilla flavours without pretending halloumi is provoleta.

name: King Oyster Churrasco with Lime Farofa
hook: Steakhouse drama without the steak

steps.t: Slice the king oysters lengthways into 1 cm steaks and score one side in a shallow crosshatch; cut too deep and the steaks split when you turn them.
Mix olive oil, soy sauce, lime juice, garlic and cumin, then brush it over the mushrooms; drowning them in marinade makes them wet and reluctant to sear.
Heat a ridged griddle until a drop of water skips off fast, then lay the mushrooms scored-side down with space between them; crowding traps steam and erases the grill marks.
Griddle for 3 minutes, pressing lightly with a spatula until dark bars appear and the edges sag; if you move them early, the marks tear away.
Turn and griddle for 2 minutes more, just until juicy in the centre and bronzed outside; overcooking makes king oysters squeaky.
Melt butter in a small pan until it smells nutty, stir in cassava flour and cook until sandy and golden; pale farofa tastes dusty, burnt farofa tastes bitter.
Fold lime zest, coriander and chilli through the farofa off the heat, then spoon it around the mushroom steaks so it stays crisp rather than soaking underneath.

note: Serve on a wide platter with extra lime wedges for a churrasco-style centrepiece.

name: Crisp Beef Chapli Cucumber Plates
hook: Crackly beef, cool green crunch

steps.t: Squeeze the chopped tomato in your hand over the sink until it stops dripping; watery tomato makes the patties spit and fall apart.
Mix beef, onion, tomato, chillies, coriander, crushed coriander seeds, cumin, gram flour and 1 teaspoon salt with your fingers until tacky; undermixed mince crumbles at the edges.
Shape into 8 thin patties, about 8 cm wide, pressing a shallow dent in the centre; thick patties brown outside before the beef cooks through.
Heat oil in a wide frying pan over medium-high heat until a pinch of mixture crackles straight away; if the oil is quiet, the chapli soak it up.
Shallow fry 4 patties for 3 minutes on the first side until the rims are dark and crisp, then turn once only; repeated flipping breaks the crust.
Fry the second side for 3 minutes until the centre is piping hot and no pink beef remains; guessing by colour outside is unsafe because the spices brown quickly.
Repeat with the remaining patties, then rest them on a rack, not kitchen paper, so the undersides stay crackly.
Serve with cucumber ribbons, yoghurt and lemon wedges; pile the cucumber separately or its juices soften the chapli.

note: All the chapli kebab crunch, plated with cool cucumber so it lands as a summer dish rather than a heavy fry-up.

name: Pickled Mackerel Herb Cups
hook: Bright vinegar, oily fish, tangled herbs

ingredients.name: peppered smoked mackerel fillets, skin removed

steps.t: Toss carrot and mooli with rice vinegar, sugar and a pinch of salt until the strands shine; if the sugar sits grainy, the pickle tastes sharp in patches.
Leave the vegetables to pickle for 15 minutes, turning once, until they bend but still snap; longer turns them limp and watery.
Whisk fish sauce, lime juice, chilli and 2 tablespoons of the pickling liquid into a bright dressing; adding all the pickle liquor makes it too sweet and flat.
Break the smoked mackerel into large flakes with clean fingers, feeling for and removing any pin bones; tiny flakes disappear into the salad and make it look messy.
Drain the pickled vegetables well, pressing lightly, because excess brine will pool in the lettuce cups and dilute the dressing.
Dress the mackerel and pickles gently with half the sauce until just glossy; heavy mixing turns the oily fish pasty.
Arrange lettuce leaves on a shared platter, spoon in the mackerel mixture, then finish with mint, coriander, peanuts and the remaining dressing on the side so the leaves stay crisp.

note: Uses ready-smoked mackerel for safety and speed while keeping the Vietnamese balance of pickle, herbs, fish sauce and lime.

name: Achari Crackle Pork Strips
hook: Craggy edges, hot pickle spice, juicy pork

steps.t: Slice the pork across the grain into 1 cm strips and pat them dry until the paper comes away barely damp; wet meat throws water into the pan and the crust turns leathery.

Toss the pork with lemon juice, ginger-garlic paste, chilli, coriander, fennel, nigella and salt, then leave it while the oil heats; if the strips sit for ages, the salt draws out juice and the coating goes gluey.
