Fill lettuce leaves with cucumber batons and the smoky soybean mixture, then finish with sesame seeds and the remaining sauce; overfilling makes the cups split before the first bite.

note: Tofu and edamame keep it vegetable-led while giving a solid protein count for training days.

name: Ginger Caramel Steamed Egg Custard
hook: Barely set silk, warm ginger gloss

steps.t: Warm the milk with caster sugar, ginger, vanilla and salt until it steams at the edges but never bubbles; boiling milk gives the custard a cooked-skin taste.
Cover and steep off the heat until the ginger comes through clearly, then strain; leaving slices in the mix makes hot, fibrous pockets.
Beat the eggs just until no streaks remain, then whisk in the warm milk slowly; frothing hard traps bubbles that set into pockmarks.
Strain the custard into four heatproof bowls and skim off surface foam; any bubbles left on top become little craters after steaming.
Steam over the gentlest simmer, with the lid wrapped in a tea towel, until the centres wobble like soft jelly; hard boiling makes the eggs split and weep.
Rest the bowls off the heat while you melt brown sugar with lemon juice and 2 tbsp water to a thin amber syrup; take it too dark and the ginger custard will taste burnt.
Spoon the warm caramel over the custards and serve just warm; chilling firms them up, but warm is where the texture is at its silkiest.

note: Use a wide pan or steamer so the bowls sit level; tilted bowls set unevenly.

name: Coal-Grilled Mushroom Elote Tacos
hook: Charred caps, lime cream, chilli dust

steps.t: Light the coals and cook only when they are glowing with a grey ash coat; yellow flames lick the mushrooms with soot before they cook through.
Toss mushrooms with oil, smoked paprika, cumin and salt, rubbing the seasoning into the gills; dry spice left in the bowl means bland centres.
Grill the mushrooms in a basket or on skewers until they shrink, squeak less, and show dark charred edges; crowding them makes them steam and leak water.
Put the sweetcorn on a piece of foil at the cooler edge of the grill until it smells toasted and a few kernels bronze; leave it over direct heat and the sugars burn fast.
Mix soured cream with lime zest, half the juice and a pinch of salt until loose enough to drizzle; if it stays stiff, it drags the taco filling out with every bite.
Warm the tortillas briefly over the coals until floppy with a few toast marks; crisp tortillas crack the second you fold them.
Pile mushrooms and corn into the tortillas, then finish with lime cream, feta, coriander, chilli powder and the remaining lime juice; add the fresh bits last so they stay bright, not wilted.

note: A grill basket is useful but not essential; skewers stop small mushrooms dropping into the coals.

name: Charred Garlic-Lime Lamb with Tropeiro Bean Crumbs
hook: Smoke, lime and bean-rich winter crunch

ingredients.name: farinha de mandioca or coarse cassava flour

steps.t: Pat the lamb bone-dry, then rub with garlic, lime zest, cachaça, paprika, 1 tbsp oil and salt; wet meat steams on the griddle instead of charring, so the surface must feel tacky, not slick.
Put the bacon in a cold frying pan and cook until the fat runs clear and the edges look mahogany; if you rush it on high heat, the bacon scorches before it gives enough fat for the crumbs.
Add the onion to the bacon fat and cook until soft and sweet-smelling, then stir in the beans; stop before the beans collapse, or the crumbs turn pasty rather than nubbly.
Scatter in the cassava flour and stir until it smells nutty and looks sandy with glossy bean patches; pale flour tastes dusty, so give it time to toast.
Heat a ridged griddle until a drop of water snaps away, then oil the lamb lightly and lay it down without crowding; a crowded pan cools and leaves you with grey meat.
Griddle the lamb until blackened lines form and the edges bead with juices, turning once for medium-rare; keep flipping and you lose the crust that makes the dish.
Rest the lamb on a warm plate, then squeeze lime juice through the hot tropeiro crumbs and fold in parsley; cutting straight away spills the juices that should soak the crumbs.
Slice the lamb across the grain and spoon the bean crumbs beside it; slicing with the grain makes even tender lamb chew like rope.

note: A wintery Brazilian-style plate built around the comfort of feijão tropeiro and hard griddle char.

name: Lahori Crisp Masala Mackerel with Pink Onion Kachumber
hook: Crackly fish, hot spice, bright onion

ingredients.name: small red onion, very thinly sliced

steps.t: Mix yoghurt, lemon, ginger-garlic paste, chilli, coriander, ajwain and salt, then coat the mackerel flesh-side first; leaving thick yoghurt lumps makes the crust blister off in the oil.
Toss the onion with a pinch of salt and a squeeze of lemon from the bowl if there is any left; unsalted onion stays harsh instead of turning breakfast-sharp and pink.
Combine gram flour and rice flour on a plate, then press each fillet in firmly on both sides; a dusting that looks patchy gives patchy crunch.
Heat 1 cm oil in a wide pan until a pinch of flour fizzes immediately but does not blacken; oil that is too cool makes oily fish taste heavier and limp.
Lay the fillets skin-side down and fry without nudging until the rims turn deep orange and crisp; moving them early tears the skin and leaves the crust behind.
Turn once and fry the flesh side until the thickest part flakes cleanly and looks opaque; underdone mackerel tastes metallic, overdone mackerel goes dry at the edges.
Drain on a rack, not kitchen paper, then top with the salted onion and coriander; paper traps steam underneath and softens the crust you just made.

note: Serve with hot paratha or buttered toast if you want the full breakfast spread.

name: Gỏi Gà Jasmine Pickle Platter
hook: Cool chicken, sharp pickles, fragrant herbs

ingredients.name: daikon or mooli, cut into matchsticks

steps.t: Lower the chicken into barely simmering salted water and keep it at a lazy tremble; a rolling boil tightens the thighs and makes the shreds woolly.
Lift the chicken out and rest it until cool enough to handle; shredding it hot burns your fingers and squeezes out the juices you need for a glossy salad.
Stir rice vinegar with sugar and a pinch of salt until clear, then add carrot and daikon; if the sugar sits gritty at the bottom, the pickle tastes sharp in one bite and flat in the next.
Whisk fish sauce, lime juice, chilli, garlic and 2 tbsp of the pickling liquid into a dressing; taste it before dressing, because cabbage dulls seasoning fast.
Shred the chicken along the grain into generous ribbons, discarding any cartilage; chopped cubes look tidy but eat dry and do not catch the dressing.
Squeeze the pickles lightly, then toss cabbage, chicken and dressing with your hands until the cabbage bends but still squeaks; overworking bruises the herbs and floods the platter.
Fold through mint and coriander at the last moment, then pile onto a wide plate and finish with peanuts; adding herbs early turns them black and tired before guests sit down.

note: The platter can be built in stages: pickle and poach ahead, then dress just before serving.

name: Sicilian Prawn and Fennel Al Forno
hook: Sweet prawns, lemon air, tomato juices

ingredients.name: raw king prawns, peeled with tails left on
lemon, zested and cut into wedges

steps.t: Heat the oven to 220°C and put a shallow baking dish inside; starting cold makes the fennel leak water before it can sweeten at the edges.
Toss fennel, tomatoes, garlic, oregano, olive oil and salt in the hot dish, spreading everything in one layer; piled vegetables steam and taste boiled.
Pour in the wine when the tomato skins have wrinkled and the fennel tips are golden; adding wine too early washes away the light roasted flavour.
Pat the prawns dry, then tuck them among the vegetables in a single layer; wet or stacked prawns turn rubbery before they colour.
Mix breadcrumbs with lemon zest and a few drops of oil, scatter lightly, then bake until the prawns are pink and just opaque through the thickest curve; leave them longer and they bounce like rubber.
Rest the dish for 2 minutes so the tomato juices settle rather than scald the prawns further; serving straight from the oven keeps cooking the shellfish on the plate.
Finish with parsley and lemon wedges, scraping the thin pan juices over each serving; without the final acid, the sweet fennel can taste flat.

note: Use the widest dish you have: one shallow layer is what keeps this summery rather than soupy.

name: Dum Methi Paneer Handis
hook: Silky paneer, slow spice, fenugreek warmth

steps.t: Soak the cashews in hot water until soft, then blend with the yoghurt to a smooth cream; gritty cashews leave a sandy sauce no amount of simmering will fix.
Warm the ghee in a heavy pan and cook the onions slowly until deep gold and jammy at the edges; pale onions make the braise taste raw and harsh.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste, chilli powder and cumin until the oil stains red and the smell turns rounded; if the paste catches black, the whole handi tastes bitter.
Add tomatoes and salt, then cook until the sauce thickens and the ghee freckles the surface; stopping while it looks watery leaves the paneer floating in thin gravy.
Lower the heat and stir in the cashew-yoghurt cream a spoonful at a time; boiling it hard can split the yoghurt into grainy curds.

Fold in paneer, green chillies, garam masala and crushed fenugreek, then cover with a tight lid and braise on the gentlest heat; vigorous bubbling toughens paneer instead of letting it drink the sauce.
Rest covered off the heat before serving in small bowls; spooning it out immediately breaks the cubes and leaves the spice tasting separate.

note: Designed for a shared table: rich enough for small portions, best with naan pieces or little rotis.

name: Barely Warm Halloumi, Orange & Walnut Lahanosalata
hook: Salty squeak, sweet citrus, winter crunch

steps.t: Put the shredded cabbage in a wide bowl with the salt and squeeze it hard with your hands until it turns glossy and bends rather than snaps; skip this and the salad eats like coleslaw from the fridge.
Zest one orange into a small bowl, then cut both oranges into segments over the bowl so the juice lands in it; leaving the white pith on makes the whole plate bitter.
Whisk the olive oil, vinegar, honey and oregano into the orange juice until it looks cloudy and lightly thickened; if the honey sits in a blob, the dressing will taste sharp in patches.
Fold the dressing, orange segments, olives and walnuts through the cabbage, keeping a few pieces of orange and walnut back for the top; overmix now and the citrus breaks down into mush.

Warm a dry non-stick frying pan over medium heat, lay in the halloumi and turn it as soon as the surface feels hot and slightly supple, before it takes on a crust; cook it hard and you lose the barely-warmed squeak this dish needs.
Pile the cabbage salad into shallow bowls, tuck the warm halloumi through it and finish with the reserved orange and walnuts; plating the cheese separately makes it cool into rubbery slabs.

note: Best eaten straight away while the halloumi is warm and the cabbage still has crunch.

name: Turkish Skillet Peppers, Potatoes & Tomato Mint
hook: Charred peppers, jammy tomatoes, crisp potatoes

ingredients.name: waxy potatoes, cut into 1.5 cm cubes

steps.t: Boil the potato cubes in salted water until a knife goes in but the edges still hold square; take them to fluffy and they will collapse when they hit the wok.
Drain the potatoes very well and let them steam dry on a tray; wet potatoes lower the pan temperature and turn the breakfast into a stew.

Heat the oil in a wide frying pan or wok until it shimmers, then add the potatoes in one layer and leave them alone until the undersides are crisp and pale gold; stirring too early tears off the crust.
Add the onion and both peppers, then stir-fry hard until the pepper skins blister in spots and the onion tips char; a gentle heat gives you softness without that Turkish breakfast smoke.
Push everything to the sides, fry the tomato paste, pul biber and cumin in the bare oil until the paste darkens brick-red; if it stays raw, the pan will taste metallic.
Stir in the grated tomatoes and salt, tossing until the liquid clings to the potatoes instead of pooling under them; stop too soon and the plate will be watery.
Turn off the heat and fold through the parsley and mint so they wilt from the pan’s warmth; frying the herbs makes them dull and grassy.

note: Serve with bread, olives and strong tea if you want the full breakfast-table feeling.

name: Za’atar Griddled Tofu with Pomegranate Tahini
hook: Smoky edges, silk sauce, ruby crunch

steps.t: Slice the tofu into 8 slabs and press them between clean tea towels until the surface feels dry, not slippery; damp tofu steams and sticks before it ever griddles.
Mix the za’atar, 2 tbsp olive oil, lemon zest and half the salt, then rub it over both sides of the tofu; leaving dry spice on the surface makes it scorch in dusty patches.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice, garlic, pomegranate molasses, remaining salt and 3–4 tbsp cold water until it turns pale and pourable; stop while it is grainy and it will seize on the plate.
Heat a ridged griddle pan until a drop of water flicks away instantly, then oil it lightly; if the pan is only warm, the tofu will glue itself to the ridges.
Lay in the tofu and do not move it until dark grill lines form and the edges look drier and firmer; fussing with it early rips away the za’atar crust.
Turn the slabs with a thin spatula and griddle the second side until the centres are hot and the corners look lightly crisp; undercook them and the middle stays cold and bland.
Spoon tahini across a platter, stack on the tofu and scatter with pomegranate seeds, parsley and pine nuts; burying the tofu under sauce softens the griddled edges you worked for.

note: For a cleaner party service, make the tahini sauce a few hours ahead and griddle the tofu last minute.

name: Crisp Moroccan Lamb with Courgette Ribbons
hook: Spiced lamb, cool ribbons, lemon snap

ingredients.name: small red onion, grated and squeezed dry

steps.t: Mix the lamb, squeezed onion, ras el hanout, cumin, lemon zest, half the coriander, breadcrumbs and salt just until it holds together; kneading it like bread makes the lamb bouncy instead of tender.
Shape into 12 small, flat patties, pressing a shallow dent into each centre; round balls brown outside before the middle is safely cooked.
Toss the courgette ribbons and radishes with the lemon juice and a pinch of salt, then leave them to soften slightly; dressing them at the last second leaves the courgette stiff and raw-tasting.
Stir the yoghurt with the remaining coriander and a spoonful of the lemony juices from the courgettes; using thick yoghurt straight from the tub makes the plate heavy rather than summery.
Heat the olive oil in a wide frying pan until a breadcrumb sizzles immediately, then add the patties with space between them; crowding drops the heat and gives grey, greasy lamb.
Shallow fry until the undersides are deep brown and crisp at the edges, then turn once; flipping repeatedly breaks the crust and squeezes out the juices.
Cook the second side until the patties are firm, crisp and cooked through with no pink lamb remaining in the centre; guessing by colour outside is unsafe with mince.
Spread the yoghurt on plates, add the courgette ribbons and radishes, then sit the crisp lamb on top so it stays crunchy; putting hot lamb under the salad wilts everything.

note: Small patties keep this light; make them flat so the lamb cooks through before the crust darkens.

name: Escabeche Butter Beans with Roasted Pepper & Almonds
hook: Bright vinegar, creamy beans, smoky pepper

steps.t: Put the onion in a bowl with the sherry vinegar, sugar and half the salt, scrunching it until the slices turn glossy and pink at the edges; if you leave them untouched, they stay harsh and raw.
Warm the olive oil, garlic and bay leaves in a small pan until the garlic just turns pale straw at the edges; take it brown and the dressing will taste bitter.
Pull the pan off the heat and stir in the smoked paprika so it blooms in the hot oil without frying black; paprika burns fast and ruins the whole bowl.
Add the butter beans to the warm paprika oil and fold gently until they are coated and glossy; rough stirring splits their skins and turns the dressing cloudy.

Pour the beans and oil over the pickled onion, add the roasted peppers and let everything sit until the beans taste seasoned all the way through; serving immediately leaves vinegar on the outside and bland beans inside.
Remove the bay leaves, then fold in the parsley and most of the almonds; adding herbs while the beans are hot makes them dark and tired.
Spoon into a shallow sharing dish and finish with the remaining almonds and a thread of the dressing from the bowl; leaving the dressing behind wastes the best part for bread.

note: Serve at room temperature, not fridge-cold, so the olive oil tastes round rather than waxy.

name: Dijon Tarragon Chicken Gratin
hook: Creamy mustard edges, juicy chicken underneath

steps.t: Heat the oven to 220°C fan. Put the sliced potatoes in a large shallow baking dish with the oil and salt, then toss until every slice shines; dry patches stay leathery instead of turning tender.
Bake the potatoes until the top slices are just starting to curl and the edges look pale gold, otherwise the chicken will be ready before the potatoes are soft.
Whisk the mustard, cream, stock, vinegar, tarragon and garlic in a jug. Keep whisking until no mustard lumps cling to the sides, or the sauce bakes up spotty and sharp in places.
Nestle the chicken thighs between the potatoes in one layer, then pour the sauce over and around them. Do not stack the thighs; overlapped meat steams grey and cooks unevenly.
Scatter over the Gruyère and bake until the sauce bubbles hard at the edges and the chicken is fully cooked through with no pink in the thickest part.
Rest the dish until the bubbling calms and the cream tightens around the potatoes; serving it straight from the oven makes the sauce run across the plate.

note: Use a shallow ceramic or metal dish rather than a deep casserole so the potatoes cook quickly and the top gratins properly.

name: Key West Braised Conch with Buttered Grits
hook: Tender conch in a deep tomato tide

steps.t: Pat the conch dry and pound any thick pieces until they are floppy and even; chunky unpounded pieces tighten like rubber before the braise can soften them.
Warm the oil in a heavy casserole and cook the onion, celery and green pepper until the onion turns translucent and the pepper smells sweet, not raw and grassy.
Stir in the garlic and Old Bay until the pan smells toasty; if the garlic browns hard now it will taste bitter after the long braise.
Add the tomatoes, fish stock and conch, scraping the base until nothing catches. Bring to the quietest simmer, with only a bubble breaking here and there; a rolling boil toughens shellfish fibres.
Cover with the lid slightly ajar and braise until a fork slides through the conch with gentle pressure and the sauce is brick-red and glossy.
Cook the grits in salted simmering water according to the packet, whisking hard at the start so they do not clump into pebbles, then beat in the butter.
Stir lime juice into the conch off the heat and check the seasoning. Spoon it over the grits while both are loose; cold grits set firm and swallow the sauce.

note: Conch is the shellfish that rewards a true slow braise; do not swap in prawns, which only need minutes.

name: Chimichurri Halloumi Guiso
hook: Salty cheese, beans, green herb heat

steps.t: Brown the halloumi cubes in half the oil until the faces are deep gold and squeak when nudged; pale cubes will dissolve at the edges and make the stew salty but dull.
Lift the halloumi to a plate. Add the remaining oil, onion and red pepper to the pan and cook until the onion is soft and the pepper has slumped; rushing this leaves a harsh raw crunch in the stew.
Stir in the garlic, smoked paprika and cumin until the oil stains red and smells warm. Keep it moving, because scorched paprika turns dusty and bitter.
Add the beans, tomatoes and stock, then crush a spoonful of beans against the side of the pan; leaving them all whole makes the broth thin instead of stew-like.
Simmer uncovered until the liquid has thickened enough to leave a clean trail when you drag a spoon through the base.
Return the halloumi and simmer gently until hot all the way through. Do not boil hard now, or the cheese becomes springy and the bean skins split everywhere.
Stir the parsley with the vinegar, then fold most through the stew off the heat and spoon the rest on top; boiling the herbs kills the chimichurri brightness.

note: The beans and halloumi make this protein-heavy without meat; serve with a fried egg if your training day needs more.

name: Coconut Caramel Steamed Pudim
hook: Silky custard under dark caramel

steps.t: Put 100 g sugar and the water in a small pan and cook without stirring until the caramel is the colour of strong tea; stirring makes crystals, and pale caramel tastes only sweet.
Immediately pour the caramel into a 1 litre pudding basin or metal mould, tilting to coat the base. Use oven gloves, because the caramel stays dangerously hot and sticks to skin.
Blend the eggs, condensed milk, whole milk, coconut milk, vanilla, salt and remaining 60 g sugar until smooth but not foamy; too much foam leaves little holes in the pudim.
Strain the custard into the caramel-lined mould. Do not skip the sieve, as stringy egg white sets into pale flecks.

Cover the mould tightly with buttered foil, then set it on a trivet in a deep pan with simmering water halfway up the sides. Keep the water at a gentle tremble, not a boil, or the custard curdles at the edges.
Steam until the centre wobbles like set jelly and a knife comes out mostly clean, with no liquid custard running back into the cut.
Cool to room temperature, then chill until fully cold so the caramel loosens and the custard firms enough to unmould cleanly.
Run a thin knife around the edge and invert onto a lipped plate; using a flat plate wastes the caramel sauce when it floods out.

note: A lidded wok or stockpot works well as the steamer if the mould sits above the water, not in direct contact with the pan base.

name: Dhungar Masala Egg Rice
hook: Smoky eggs over spiced tomato rice

steps.t: Cook the rinsed rice in salted water until just tender, then drain well; wet rice turns the masala slack and claggy.
Boil the eggs until the yolks are set, then cool, peel and halve them. Do not leave soft centres for this dish, as the eggs will be handled and warmed again.
Heat the oil in a frying pan and cook the onion until the edges are tea-brown and frilly; pale onion tastes sweet and raw under the smoke.

Add the ginger-garlic paste, coriander, chilli powder and garam masala, stirring until the oil looks stained and the paste stops smelling sharp. If it sticks dry, splash in a spoon of water before it scorches.
Stir in the grated tomato and cook until it collapses into a thick masala and the oil starts to bead around the edges; watery tomato will make the rice break.
Fold in the rice, egg halves and fresh coriander gently, keeping the yolks intact; mashing them makes the pan chalky instead of glossy.

Heat the charcoal over a gas flame or with tongs under a grill until one edge glows red. Put it in a small heatproof cup set inside the pan, spoon the ghee onto the coal, cover at once and smoke until the aroma turns campfire-warm, not acrid.
Remove the cup and charcoal carefully with tongs, then fluff the rice from the edges inwards so the smoked fat perfumes everything without breaking up the eggs.

note: If you have no safe way to heat charcoal, skip the dhungar step rather than using treated briquettes or charcoal lighter fluid.

name: Steamed Winter Squash Bánh Cuốn
hook: Silky rolls with gingered winter sweetness

ingredients.name: rapeseed oil, plus extra for brushing
winter squash, peeled and coarsely grated

steps.t: Whisk the rice flour, tapioca starch, salt and warm water until completely smooth, then whisk in 1 tbsp oil. Rest the batter while you cook the filling; unrested batter tears instead of peeling into sheets.

Toss squash, cabbage, ginger and 1 tbsp oil in a wide pan with 3 tbsp water. Cover and steam-fry until the squash slumps and the cabbage turns glossy, not watery; if liquid pools, boil it off or the rolls will leak.
Season the filling with soy and rice vinegar, then spread it on a plate to steam off. Hot, wet filling makes the bánh cuốn split when rolled.
Bring a steamer to a steady simmer and stretch a clean, taut cotton cloth over the perforated tray, or use a lightly oiled flat steaming tray. Brush with oil; dry patches glue the rice sheet down.
Stir the batter, ladle on a thin layer and cover until it turns satin-matte with no chalky centre. Do not wait for browned edges; steamed rice sheets go rubbery if overcooked.
Lift the sheet with an oiled spatula, lay on a board, add a narrow line of filling and roll loosely. Tight rolling squeezes out the squash and makes the sheet burst.
Repeat, keeping finished rolls covered over gentle steam so they stay supple. Serve warm with coriander and fried shallots scattered over the top.

note: A warming Vietnamese-style vegetable roll: no tofu, egg or meat, just soft rice sheets and winter vegetables.

name: Coal-Grilled Borlotti Breakfast Farinata
hook: Smoky chickpea edges, soft beans beneath

steps.t: Whisk chickpea flour, water and salt until smooth, then skim off any foam. Rest the batter while the coals settle; cooking it straight away gives a sandy, raw-chickpea centre.
Light a charcoal grill and wait until the coals are grey with a steady medium-high heat, not flaming. Flames scorch the base before the farinata sets.
Put a 26 cm cast-iron pan on the grill for 5 minutes, then add 3 tbsp olive oil. The oil should shimmer; if the pan is only warm, the farinata sticks and turns pasty.
Stir rosemary and borlotti beans into the batter, pour it into the hot pan and close the grill lid. Cook until the rim is crisp and lace-brown and the middle has just stopped wobbling.
Toss tomatoes and onion with vinegar, 1 tbsp olive oil and a pinch of salt. Do this late so the tomatoes stay bright rather than collapsing into a wet salad.
Grill the bread beside the pan until striped and smoky at the edges; move it if it blackens before it dries and crisps.
Slide the farinata into wedges, top with the tomato onion mix and pecorino, and serve with the grilled bread while the edges still crackle.

note: Best cooked in a cast-iron pan over settled coals, giving the chickpea batter a breakfast-worthy smoky crust.

name: Keralan Lime-Cured Sea Bass with Curry Leaf Oil
hook: Cool citrus fish, warm spiced gloss

ingredients.name: sashimi-grade sea bass fillet, skinless and pin-boned

steps.t: Keep the sea bass fridge-cold and slice it across the grain into 5 mm pieces with a very sharp knife. Ragged warm fish looks dull and feels woolly, so chill the board if your kitchen is hot.

Stir lime juice, salt and sugar until dissolved, then spoon it over the fish in a shallow dish. Turn once until the edges turn pearly but the centre stays translucent; leaving it longer makes the fish chalky.

Meanwhile warm coconut oil in a small pan, add mustard seeds and curry leaves, and pull it off the heat as soon as the seeds crackle and the leaves turn glossy. Burnt curry leaves taste bitter, not smoky.
Pour the spiced oil into a cold bowl and let it cool to warm-room temperature. Hot oil will cook the fish in patches and tighten it unevenly.
Whisk coconut milk with the cooled curry leaf oil and green chilli. Taste before adding more salt, because the curing liquid already seasons the fish.
Lift the fish from the curing liquid and pat lightly on kitchen paper. Do not rinse it; rinsing washes away the lime perfume and leaves the surface watery.
Spoon the coconut dressing onto chilled plates, lay the fish over it, then finish with shallot, coriander and toasted coconut flakes. Serve immediately while the fish is cold and glossy.

note: Use only fish sold as suitable for raw eating by a trusted fishmonger, and keep it refrigerated until slicing.

name: Thai Basil Beef and Watermelon Wok Salad
hook: Seared beef, cold melon, basil heat

ingredients.name: beef rump steak, thinly sliced across the grain
palm sugar or light brown sugar
green beans, cut into 4 cm lengths

steps.t: Stir fish sauce, lime juice and sugar until dissolved, then toss 1 tbsp of it through the beef. Do not soak the beef; a wet marinade steams in the wok instead of searing.
Put watermelon and cucumber on a wide serving plate and keep it chilled. Warm melon turns flabby, and this dish needs the cold fruit against the hot beef.
Heat a wok until a drop of water vanishes on contact, then add 1 tbsp oil. If the wok is not smoking-hot, the beef will grey and leak juice.
Stir-fry half the beef in a single layer until the edges catch dark brown but the centres are still springy, then tip it onto the plate. Crowding the wok is the usual mistake here.
Repeat with the remaining oil and beef, then add garlic, chillies and green beans to the empty wok. Toss until the beans blister in spots but still squeak when bitten.
Return the beef and any resting juices to the wok with the remaining dressing. Toss only until everything shines; boiling the dressing makes it salty and heavy.
Spoon the hot stir-fry over the cold watermelon and cucumber, scatter with Thai basil and peanuts, and serve before the herbs wilt black.

note: Slice the beef thinly across the grain so the very short, fierce stir-fry keeps it tender.

name: Miso Mackerel Teppan Bites with Ponzu Daikon
hook: Crisp oily fish, sharp snowy daikon

ingredients.name: mackerel fillets, about 90 g each, pin-boned

steps.t: Pat the mackerel dry and cut each fillet into three chunky bites. If the skin is damp, it sticks to the griddle and tears before it crisps.
Mix miso, mirin, soy and rice vinegar, then brush it thinly over the flesh side only. A thick miso coat burns black before the oily fish cooks through.
Grate the daikon, squeeze it gently until snowy rather than dripping, then stir with yuzu juice and ponzu. Unsqueezed daikon floods the plate and softens the fish skin.
Heat a flat griddle or plancha over medium-high heat and wipe it with neutral oil. It should shimmer, not smoke hard; miso sugars scorch fast on an overheated plate.
Lay the mackerel skin-side down and press lightly for the first few seconds so the skin meets the metal. Cook until the skin is crisp and the sides turn opaque halfway up.
Turn the bites and cook the miso side just until glazed and the thickest piece flakes with gentle pressure. Do not keep flipping, or the glaze will smear and burn.
Arrange the mackerel on a shared plate with mounds of ponzu daikon, spring onions and sesame seeds. Eat while the skin still crackles against the cool daikon.

note: Made for a shared table: small griddled pieces, bright grated daikon, and enough savoury glaze for oily mackerel.

name: Whole-Roasted Za’atar Halloumi with Pomegranate Lentils
hook: Salty bronze crust, soft winter lentils

steps.t: Heat the oven to 220°C fan. Pat the halloumi very dry, then score the top in shallow diamonds; if the cuts go too deep the block opens out and dries instead of roasting whole.
Toss the onion and carrots with 1 tbsp olive oil, cumin and a pinch of salt in a roasting tin. Spread them in one layer; crowd them and they steam pale rather than catch at the tips.
Rub the halloumi with the remaining oil and za’atar, then sit it whole in the centre of the vegetables. Roast until the cheese is swollen and the vegetable edges are singed dark gold.
Stir the lentils and pomegranate molasses through the vegetables around the halloumi, keeping the cheese intact. If molasses lands thickly on the cheese it can scorch black before the lentils warm.
Return the tin to the oven until the lentils are hot and glossy and the halloumi crust is bronze with a little syrupy bubbling at the base.
Rest the tin for 3 minutes; cutting straight away sends the salty juices running across the lentils instead of staying in the cheese.
Finish with parsley, pomegranate seeds and a squeeze of lemon. Serve the halloumi in thick slabs over the lentils while the crust still squeaks.

note: Deeply savoury and wintry, with the halloumi kept as a proper centrepiece rather than cubes.

name: Cedar-Smoked Halloumi with Bessara and Harissa Butter
hook: Smoke, chilli butter, velvet beans

ingredients.name: tin broad beans or fava beans, drained

steps.t: Soak the cedar chips in water for 10 minutes, then drain well. Dry chips flare and wet dripping chips kill the smoke, so you want damp, not swimming.
Line the base of a wok or deep pan with foil, add the chips, set a rack above them and lay on the halloumi. Put the lid on tight; gaps let the smoke perfume your kitchen instead of the cheese.
Set the pan over medium-high heat until a thin stream of smoke appears, then smoke the halloumi until it smells woody and the surface turns slightly tacky.
Meanwhile simmer the beans with garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, 150 ml water and a pinch of salt until they crush easily against the side of the pan; undercooked skins make the bessara gritty.
Blend the beans with olive oil and lemon juice until smooth and loose enough to spoon. If it stands in peaks, beat in hot water a spoon at a time or it will eat heavily at breakfast.
Melt the butter with harissa in a small pan until it foams orange-red. Keep it gentle; burnt harissa tastes bitter rather than smoky.
Quickly sear the smoked halloumi in a hot dry pan until the ridges go chestnut brown, about a minute a side. Serve on the bessara with harissa butter and warm bread.

note: A proper weekend breakfast: smoky cheese, silky beans and heat that wakes you up without flattening you.

name: Saffron-Steamed Egg Cazuelitas with Piquillo Almond Crumb
hook: Silky custard under smoky red crunch

steps.t: Warm the milk just until steaming, then crumble in the saffron and leave it to stain deep gold. Boiling the milk dulls the saffron and can give the custard a cooked-milk skin.
Whisk the eggs with the salt, then whisk in the saffron milk. Do not beat in a froth; bubbles steam into little holes instead of a smooth Spanish-style custard.
Strain the mixture into four small cazuelas or ramekins. Skipping the sieve leaves strands of egg white that set rubbery around the edges.
Set the dishes in a wide pan on a folded tea towel and pour in hot water to halfway up the sides. Cover with a lid wrapped in a clean towel so condensation does not drip pockmarks into the tops.
Steam over low heat until the centres wobble like set cream, not liquid, and a knife at the edge comes out clean. Hard boiling makes the eggs puff, split and weep.
While they steam, toast the almonds in olive oil until they smell sweet and the palest pieces turn honey-coloured; take them too far and the paprika will taste burnt on contact.
Stir the piquillos, smoked paprika and sherry vinegar into the almonds, spoon over the custards, then finish with chives. Serve warm, when the tops are glossy and the crumb still crackles.

note: Impressive because it is quiet and precise: saffron, steam and a bright tapas-style finish.

name: Coal-Grilled Courgettes with Tomato Vierge and Basil Ash Salt
hook: Charred green ribbons, cool tomato oil

steps.t: Light the coals and let them burn down until they are grey-edged with no licking flames. Flames blacken courgette skins before the centres soften.
Salt the courgette slices lightly and leave them on a tray until beads of moisture appear, then pat dry. If they go on wet, they steam and stick to the bars.
Mix tomatoes, shallot, capers, olive oil, vinegar, fennel seeds and a little lemon zest. Let it sit while you grill; fridge-cold tomatoes taste flat and mute the basil.
Put a few basil leaves directly over the coals for a few seconds until brittle and dark, then crumble them with the flaky salt. Leave them too long and you get acrid dust, not a grassy ash note.
Grill the courgettes over the coals until bar marks are dark brown and the slices bend without collapsing. Move them if the edges shrivel faster than the centres soften.
Turn once and grill the second side until the pale flesh looks glossy and just translucent at the core. Constant flipping tears the slices and loses the clean stripes.
Lay the courgettes on a platter, spoon over the tomato vierge and finish with basil ash salt and lemon juice. Serve warm, not hot, so the tomato oil stays fresh.

note: Light, vegetable-led and built for summer: smoke from the coals, acidity from the vierge, no protein needed.

name: Chilled Cod Crudo with Celery, Hot Sauce and Potato Crisps
hook: Cold clean fish, diner-sharp crunch

ingredients.name: skinless white fish fillet, sold for raw consumption, very cold
celery, finely sliced with leaves kept

steps.t: Keep the fish in the coldest part of the fridge until the moment you cut it. Use only fish sold for raw consumption; ordinary fillets are not made safe by lemon juice.
Slice the fish across the grain into 5 mm pieces with a sharp knife. Sawing with a blunt blade warms and smears the flesh, so chill it again if it starts to look glossy-soft.
Whisk lemon juice, pickle brine, hot sauce, olive oil and salt until the dressing looks cloudy and unified. If the oil sits on top, the first bites taste greasy and the last bites too sharp.
Arrange the fish in a single layer on a chilled platter, then spoon over just enough dressing to shine. Piling slices traps warmth and turns the bottom pieces mushy.
Leave the fish for 2 minutes only, until the edges turn faintly opaque and the centres stay pearly. Longer curing makes white fish chalky rather than clean.
Scatter over celery, celery leaves, chilli and chives, then crush potato crisps over at the table so they crackle instead of softening in the dressing.

note: A shared small plate with American bar-snack energy: cold crudo, pickle brightness and crisp salty edges.

name: Crispy Gochujang Tofu with Scallion Sesame
hook: Crackly edges, sticky heat, cool spring onion

steps.t: Press the tofu between kitchen paper while you mix the sauce; if it goes into the pan wet, the coating turns gummy instead of crisp.
Whisk gochujang, soy, rice vinegar, honey and sesame oil with 2 tablespoons water until glossy and loose; if it sits in clumps, it will scorch before it coats.
Tear the tofu into bite-sized chunks and toss with cornflour until every torn face looks dusty; bare patches fry pale and soft.
Heat the oil in a wide frying pan until a pinch of cornflour fizzes at once, then fry the tofu in one layer; crowding drops the heat and gives you steamed tofu.
Turn the pieces until the corners are lace-gold and dry-sounding against the pan, then lift them to a plate; leave them too long after this and the small bits taste bitter.
Pour off all but a sheen of oil, bubble the sauce until it looks syrupy, then toss the tofu back through for 20 seconds only; longer softens the crust. Finish with spring onions and sesame.

note: Serve with microwave rice and cucumber for the fastest dinner.

name: Black-Vinegar Pickled Lamb with Cucumber Chilli Dressing
hook: Cold lamb, sharp vinegar, numbing chilli gloss

ingredients.name: boneless lamb shoulder, trimmed and cut into large chunks

steps.t: Put lamb in a pot, cover with cold water and bring to a boil; skim until the broth stops throwing up grey foam, or the pickle will taste woolly.
Add Shaoxing wine, ginger and star anise, then simmer very gently until a chopstick slides in with slight resistance; a hard boil tightens the lamb and clouds the stock.

Lift the lamb into a shallow container. Strain 300ml hot cooking liquor into a pan with soy, black vinegar, sugar and salt, then simmer until the sugar vanishes and the vinegar smells rounded, not raw.
Pour the hot pickling liquor over the lamb so it is mostly submerged, cool uncovered until it stops steaming, then cover and refrigerate; sealing it hot traps condensation and can sour the flavour.
Leave the lamb to pickle overnight, turning once if the top pieces are exposed; dry patches cure unevenly and taste flat.
Slice the chilled lamb across the grain into thin slabs; cutting with the grain makes even tender shoulder chew like string.
Toss cucumber with chilli oil and a spoonful of the pickling liquor, lay over the lamb, then finish with coriander and sesame; dress it just before serving or the cucumber floods the plate.

note: A weekend dish for cold platters, noodles or steamed buns.

name: Chipotle Black Bean Protein Cazuela
hook: Smoky beans baked under golden cheese

steps.t: Heat the oven to 200°C fan and use a deep baking dish, not a tray; a shallow dish dries the lentils before they soften.
In the dish, stir onion, pepper, black beans, lentils, quinoa, passata, hot stock, chipotle paste and cumin until the chipotle is fully dissolved; streaks of paste bake into harsh smoky pockets.
Cover the dish tightly with foil, crimping the edges so steam cannot escape; loose foil leaves crunchy quinoa around the sides.
Uncover and stir from the corners into the centre, scraping down any stuck grains; if you skip this, the edges overcook while the middle stays soupy.
Fold in the frozen sweetcorn, scatter over the cheddar and bake uncovered until the top blisters and the centre gives slow, thick bubbles.
Rest for 10 minutes before scooping; straight from the oven it looks loose, but the pulses finish drinking the sauce as it stands. Serve with lime wedges.

note: Good hot, better boxed for tomorrow after training.

name: Mastiha Steamed Egg Custards with Thyme Honey
hook: Silky custard, piney mastiha, warm honey

steps.t: Set four small heatproof cups in a wide lidded pan and pour in enough hot water to come halfway up their sides; too much water spits into the custard when it boils.
Warm the milk, cream, sugar and mastiha until the sugar dissolves and the milk smells lightly resinous; do not boil it, or the eggs will scramble on contact.
Whisk the eggs and vanilla just until smooth, then slowly whisk in the warm milk; frothy eggs make a bubbly, pocked surface instead of silk.
Strain the custard into the cups and skim off any foam with a spoon; those bubbles set into little craters.
Cover each cup with foil, lid the pan and steam over the gentlest simmer until the centres wobble like soft jelly; a rolling boil gives tough, honeycombed edges.
Lift the cups out and rest for 5 minutes, then spoon over thyme honey, pistachios and lemon zest; topping while they are boiling hot makes the honey run straight to the sides.

note: Serve warm or chilled; the texture is best the day it is made.

name: Turkish Tomato Mussel and Bulgur Stew
hook: Briny mussels, peppery tomato, soft bulgur

steps.t: Scrub the mussels and pull away the beards; discard any cracked ones, or any open mussels that do not close after a firm tap.
Soften onion in olive oil until it turns translucent at the edges, then add garlic; if the garlic browns now, the whole stew tastes burnt.
Stir in tomato paste and pul biber until the paste darkens to brick red and leaves rusty streaks on the pan; raw paste tastes tinny.
Add chopped tomatoes, bulgur and 250ml water, then simmer until the bulgur is swollen but still has a small bite; if it gets dry, splash in water before it catches.
Tip in the mussels, cover and simmer hard, shaking the pan once, until the shells have opened wide; keep the lid on or the mussels cook unevenly.
Discard any mussels that remain closed, squeeze in lemon and fold through dill; boiling after the dill goes in kills its clean aniseed lift.

note: Eat with bread for the tomato broth, or stretch with extra bulgur.

name: Chimichurri Mushroom Wok with Toasted Corn
hook: Smoke-edged mushrooms, sharp green sauce

ingredients.name: mixed mushrooms, torn into large pieces
small crusty rolls, split and toasted

steps.t: Pat the mushrooms and sweetcorn dry before you start; wet vegetables steam in the pan and you lose the smoky edges this dish needs.
Mix the garlic, parsley, vinegar, oregano, chilli flakes, 1 tbsp olive oil and a good pinch of salt in a bowl. If you add it to the hot pan later, the parsley turns dull and muddy.
Heat a wok or largest frying pan until a drop of water skitters away, then add 1 tbsp oil and the mushrooms. Spread them out; if they sit in a pile, they boil in their own juices.
Stir-fry hard until the mushroom edges are chestnut-brown and a little curled, not just beige and soft.
Add the red pepper and sweetcorn, then toss until the corn picks up golden blisters and the pepper is glossy but still has bite.
Take the pan off the heat, fold through half the chimichurri, and taste for salt. Keeping it on the flame now makes the garlic harsh.
Pile into toasted rolls or alongside them, spoon over the remaining chimichurri, and serve while the mushrooms still squeak at the edges.

note: Use a pan bigger than feels necessary; high heat only works when the vegetables have room.

name: Picanha Chapa Feast with Farofa Butter
hook: Salt-crusted beef, sandy cassava crunch

ingredients.name: picanha or rump cap, fat cap left on
limes, 1 zested and juiced, 1 cut into wedges

steps.t: Score the picanha fat cap in shallow diamonds, stopping before the meat. Cut too deep and the fat peels away on the griddle instead of basting the beef.
Rub the beef with the coarse salt and black pepper, then chill uncovered so the surface dries and the salt seasons beyond the outside.
Mix the onion, tomatoes, coriander, lime juice and olive oil for the vinagrete. Let it sit while the beef rests from the fridge; straight-from-cold salsa tastes sharp but flat.
Take the picanha out of the fridge and leave it at room temperature until the fat feels pliable, not fridge-hard, or the centre will lag behind the crust.
Heat a heavy griddle until faintly smoking. Put the beef fat-side down first and press gently; if the heat is shy, the fat renders greasy rather than crisp.
Griddle the meat side in broad faces, turning as each side forms a deep brown crust with tiny beads of juice on top. Pull it when the thickest part reaches 54°C for medium-rare.
Rest the beef on a warm plate; slicing early floods the board and leaves the meat dry.

Melt the butter with the garlic, stir in the cassava flour and lime zest, and cook until it smells nutty and feels like damp sand. Slice the picanha across the grain and serve with farofa, vinagrete and lime wedges.

note: A cast-iron griddle gives the closest indoor version of Brazilian chapa cooking.

name: Lahori Crisp Mackerel with Kachumber Yoghurt
hook: Crackly spice crust, cool cucumber snap

steps.t: Run your fingers over the mackerel and pull out any pin bones; finding them after frying ruins the crisp skin moment.
Mix lemon juice, ginger-garlic paste, cumin, coriander, chilli, turmeric and a firm pinch of salt, then coat the fish on both sides. Keep the coating thin; a thick paste burns before the fish cooks.
Dust the fillets with gram flour and shake off the excess. Flour clumps turn leathery in shallow oil instead of crisp.
Stir the yoghurt with cucumber, mint and a pinch of salt, then chill it. Warm yoghurt beside hot oily fish tastes heavy.
Heat the oil in a wide frying pan until a pinch of gram flour fizzes at once. If it sinks quietly, the fish will drink oil.
Fry the mackerel skin-side down until the edges look bronze and the skin feels rigid when nudged with a spatula.
Turn once and fry the flesh side until just opaque and flaking at the thickest point; repeated turning breaks oily fish apart.
Drain on a rack, not kitchen paper, then serve with the kachumber yoghurt while the crust is still crackly.

note: Mackerel brings plenty of protein and omega-3 fat; keep the oil hot so the meal stays sharp rather than greasy.

name: Cà Phê Steamed Caramel Flan
hook: Silky custard, bitter coffee caramel

steps.t: Put 60 g sugar in a small pan with 2 tbsp water and cook to a deep amber caramel. Stop before it smokes; burnt caramel makes the whole flan harsh.
Divide the caramel between four heatproof ramekins and swirl quickly to coat the bases. It sets fast, so hesitation leaves one ramekin with all the caramel.
Warm the milk with condensed milk, coffee, vanilla, salt and lime zest until steaming but not boiling. Boiling milk scrambles the eggs on contact.
Whisk the eggs, yolks and remaining 30 g sugar just until smooth, then slowly whisk in the warm milk mixture. Frothy eggs make bubbles in the finished custard.
Strain the custard into the ramekins. Skipping the sieve leaves streaks of egg white that set rubbery.
Cover each ramekin with foil and steam over a gentle simmer, not a rolling boil, until the centres wobble like soft jelly rather than slosh.
Lift the ramekins out and cool, then chill until fully cold; unmoulding warm flan makes it slump and split.
Run a thin knife around each edge, dip the base briefly in warm water, and turn out so the coffee caramel runs over the custard.

note: Gentle steam is the difference between satin custard and a pocked, eggy one.

name: Sicilian Lamb Mince Orzo Bake
hook: Tomato-stained orzo, crisp lamb edges

ingredients.name: pecorino or hard Italian cheese, grated

steps.t: Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Use a deep roasting dish that can take direct heat, or brown the mince in a frying pan first; pale mince bakes up woolly and bland.
Set the dish over medium heat, add the oil and lamb mince, and break it up until the little pieces have browned, crisp freckles. If you stir constantly, it steams grey.
Add the onion, garlic, oregano and chilli flakes, scraping the sticky lamb bits from the base. Leave those bits behind and the sauce loses its depth.
Stir in the orzo so every grain is shiny with lamb fat, then add the tomatoes and hot stock. Cold stock slows the bake and leaves chalky pasta in the centre.
Cover tightly with foil and bake until the orzo is nearly tender and the liquid has dropped below the surface.
Stir in the frozen peas, taste the sauce for salt, then scatter over the pecorino. Do not add peas at the start or they turn khaki and tired.
Bake uncovered until the top is bubbling, the corners are crusty, and the orzo underneath is creamy rather than soupy.
Rest for five minutes before serving; spooning it out straight away makes the pasta slide apart instead of sitting in glossy scoops.

note: Lamb mince gives the flavour of a Sunday ragù without the price or time of a joint.

name: Black Cardamom Winter Dal
hook: Velvet-dark, buttery, quietly smoky

steps.t: Melt the ghee in a heavy casserole over a medium-low heat, then cook the onions with the salt until they slump, turn walnut-brown at the edges and smell sweet; if they catch black, the whole dal will taste bitter.
Stir in the garlic and ginger until the raw sting disappears and the paste starts sticking to the spoon; do not rush this or the finished dal will taste sharp rather than deep.
Add the cumin, cracked black cardamom and chilli powder, stirring for a few breaths until the spices foam in the fat; if the pan is dry, splash in water so the spices bloom rather than scorch.
Tip in the lentils, kidney beans and passata, then add 500 ml water and scrape the base clean; anything left welded to the pot now will burn during the long braise.
Bring to a lazy bubble, lower the heat and braise uncovered, stirring often, until the beans look lacquered and the sauce leaves slow trails on the spoon.
Crush a few beans against the side of the pot to thicken the dal, then braise again until it moves like soft porridge, not soup; if it gets too tight, loosen with hot water rather than cold.
Stir in the cream and simmer gently until the colour softens to dark mink; boiling hard after the cream goes in can split the sauce and make it greasy.

note: Serve with rice or naan and a small sharp pickle to cut the richness.

name: Peppery Thai Morning Pork Stew
hook: Fragrant broth, soft pork, waking heat

ingredients.name: pork shoulder, cut into 3 cm chunks

steps.t: Pound the garlic, coriander roots and white pepper to a rough paste; leaving whole peppercorns behind gives harsh little bursts instead of warm breakfast heat.
Put the pork in a pan with 1.5 litres cold water and bring it up slowly, skimming the grey foam before it boils hard; if you let it roar early, the broth turns cloudy and greasy.
Stir in the pounded paste, ginger, fish sauce and soy, then simmer with the lid slightly ajar until the pork yields when pressed with a spoon but is not shredding.
Add the rinsed rice and daikon, stirring right down to the base so the grains do not weld themselves into a scorched mat.
Simmer gently until the rice blooms and thickens the broth into a loose stew, with the daikon translucent at the edges; add hot water if it starts looking like risotto.
Taste and adjust with more fish sauce only after the rice has thickened, because the broth concentrates as it cooks; seasoning too early makes it salty by the bowlful.
Ladle into warm bowls and finish with spring onions and lime; the lime goes on at the table so its brightness stays clean, not stewed.

note: Excellent with a soft-boiled egg or a spoon of chilli vinegar, though the stew stands on its own.

name: Sake-Miso Roast Whole Langoustines
hook: Sweet shells, burnished butter, sea-spray aroma

ingredients.name: whole raw langoustines, about 1.2 kg total
finely grated yuzu or lemon zest

steps.t: Heat the oven to 230°C and put a sturdy roasting tray inside; a cold tray steams the langoustines before the shells can roast fragrant.
Pat the langoustines dry, especially around the heads and claws; wet shells throw off water and dilute the miso butter into a salty puddle.
Beat the butter, miso, sake, mirin, zest and lemon juice until smooth; if the butter is fridge-hard, the paste will clump and slide off the shells.
Split each langoustine along the belly with kitchen scissors, keeping the shell and head intact, then smear a little miso butter into the cut side; forcing a knife through the back crushes the meat.
Lay the langoustines cut-side up on the hot tray and roast until the shells turn coral, the butter freckles and the tail meat is just opaque.
Rest for two minutes on the tray so the bubbling butter settles back into the shell; moving them immediately spills the best juices.
Scatter with spring onions and sesame, and serve with lemon wedges; squeeze lightly, as too much lemon flattens the sweet shellfish.

note: Buy lively-looking, sea-scented langoustines and cook them the day you bring them home.

name: Tea-Smoked Gochujang Halloumi with Peaches
hook: Cool fruit, smoky cheese, chilli gloss

steps.t: Soak the halloumi slices in cold water for 10 minutes, then pat them very dry; skipping this leaves them too salty, and wet cheese will not take smoke cleanly.
Line a wok or deep pan with foil and add the tea, rice and brown sugar, then set a rack above it; without the foil, the sugar burns onto the pan and taints the next thing you cook.
Put the halloumi on the rack, cover tightly and heat until a thin stream of smoke appears, then keep the heat low; thick, angry smoke makes the cheese acrid rather than gently smoky.
Smoke the halloumi with a window open or extractor on until the surface smells toasted and looks faintly honey-coloured; do not walk away, as the sugar mix can burn if overheated.
Whisk the gochujang, rice vinegar, honey and sesame oil to a glossy dressing; if it looks split, add a teaspoon of water so it coats instead of clinging in lumps.
Arrange the peaches, cucumber and herbs on a wide plate, keeping them loose; packing them down traps juice and turns the salad limp.
Brush the warm smoked halloumi with the gochujang gloss, lay it over the fruit and finish with sesame seeds; dress at the end so the cucumber stays crisp.

note: Use firm ripe peaches: fragrant but not so soft they collapse under the warm halloumi.

name: Ginger Pork Pearl Steamers
hook: Juicy pork wrapped in glossy rice

steps.t: Soak the glutinous rice in plenty of cold water until the grains turn chalky white at the centre; under-soaked rice stays hard on the outside of the pork.
Drain the rice well in a sieve and spread it on a tray; if it is dripping wet, it slides off the meatballs instead of sticking like pearls.

Mix the pork, shiitake, spring onions, ginger, soy, Shaoxing, sesame oil and cornflour in one direction until the mixture looks tacky and clings to the bowl; a loose mix leaks juices into the steamer.
Roll the pork into walnut-sized balls with damp hands, then roll each one through the soaked rice, pressing lightly so the grains stand up all over; squeezing hard makes dense, bouncy centres.
Line a steamer with pak choi leaves and leave space between the rice-coated balls; crowding them together glues the pearls into one slab.
Steam over firmly boiling water until the rice turns translucent and the pork is cooked through with clear juices, topping up the pan with boiling water if it runs low.
Rest the steamers for three minutes before lifting them out; straight from the steam, the rice coating is fragile and tears easily.

note: Serve with black vinegar and chilli oil alongside other small plates.

name: Coal-Griddled Ranchero Eggs
hook: Smoky yolks in blistered salsa

steps.t: Light a small bed of coals and set a cast-iron pan or plancha over the hottest patch; if the pan is only warm, the salsa will stew instead of catching smoke.
Put the tomatoes, onion and jalapeño directly on the grate, turning until skins blister black in spots and the tomato skins split; pull them before the tomatoes collapse through the bars.
Chop the charred vegetables roughly with salt, lime juice and most of the coriander; keep the juices, because a dry salsa scorches before the eggs set.
Brush the tortillas lightly with oil and grill until they puff and freckle, not until rigid; over-crisp tortillas crack under the eggs.
Oil the hot pan, pour in the salsa and let it hiss until the edge looks jammy and darker red; if you stir constantly, you lose the smoky crust.
Make four hollows, crack in the eggs, cover with a lid or foil and cook until whites turn opaque but yolks still wobble; leave them too long and the yolks go chalky.
Slide onto the tortillas and finish with cheese, coriander and a squeeze of lime; serve straight away before the tortillas steam soft underneath.

note: Fast enough for a weeknight if the coals are started in a chimney.

name: Aegean Weekend Pickle Salad
hook: Cold crunch, dill, lemon, salty sunshine

ingredients.name: unwaxed lemons, zest pared and juice squeezed

steps.t: Scrub a 1 litre jar and rinse it with boiling water, then let it air-dry; a greasy jar gives you dull flavours and mould-prone edges.
Toss cabbage, cucumber, fennel and onion with the salt in a wide bowl, squeezing until the cabbage turns glossy and releases a puddle; if it still feels squeaky, it will not pack under its own brine.
Mix in lemon zest, half the dill and oregano, then pack the vegetables hard into the jar so liquid rises above them; trapped air pockets make the top layer brown rather than bright.
Weight the vegetables under the brine, cover loosely and leave at cool room temperature until it smells lemony-sour, not harsh or rotten.
Open the jar over the sink because active brine can fizz; if the vegetables are not fully submerged, discard any dry discoloured pieces before continuing.
Drain just enough brine to make it salad-like, then fold through lemon juice, olive oil, vinegar and the remaining dill; adding oil earlier would block the brine from doing its work.
Chill before serving until the crunch tightens and the flavours taste clean rather than salty-hot from the jar.

note: A raw Greek-style pickle salad for making over a lazy weekend.

name: Istanbul Pepper-Flash Cod
hook: Lean fish, seared peppers, lemon heat

ingredients.name: cod loin, cut into 3 cm cubes

steps.t: Pat the cod very dry and season with salt, cumin and half the pul biber; wet fish drops the pan temperature and flakes before it sears.
Heat a wok or wide frying pan until a drop of water skitters away, then add the oil; if the oil smokes hard before the fish goes in, pull the pan off for a few seconds.
Lay in the cod with space between pieces and leave it untouched until the underside turns opaque with golden speckles; nudging early tears the cubes.
Flip the cod once, cook until just firm at the edges, then lift it to a plate; fully cooking it now means it will be dry after the final toss.
Throw onion and peppers into the same pan and stir-fry hard until the pepper skins wrinkle and the onion tips char; crowding or gentle heat makes them watery.
Return the cod with the remaining pul biber and toss only until the fish is hot and flakes in thick petals; rough stirring turns it into hash.
Finish with lemon juice and parsley off the heat, because boiling the lemon makes the whole pan taste metallic.

note: Serve with rice or salad depending on your training day.

name: Orange Blossom Steam Custard
hook: Silky wobble, honeyed citrus perfume

steps.t: Set a steamer over a gentle simmer, not a rolling boil; violent steam punches holes through the custard.
Warm the milk with sugar, salt and cardamom until the sugar dissolves and the milk feels hot but not scalding; boiling it gives the eggs a cooked edge before steaming.
Whisk the eggs just until no streaks remain, then slowly whisk in the warm milk; frothing hard traps bubbles that set as pockmarks.
Stir in orange blossom water and vanilla, then strain into four small heatproof cups; skipping the sieve leaves stringy egg bits at the base.
Cover each cup tightly with foil and steam gently until the centres tremble like soft jelly when nudged; uncovered cups drip and turn watery on top.
Lift the cups out and rest them until warm, because moving them straight to the fridge can crack the surface.
Spoon over honey and pistachios just before serving; add them earlier and the nuts lose their snap.

note: A Levantine-leaning steamed egg dessert with a soft, clean set.

name: Crisp Marrakesh Beef-Potato Pan
hook: Craggy beef edges, cumin, lemon

steps.t: Pile the grated potato and onion into a clean tea towel and wring until the liquid stops streaming; wet shreds steam and refuse to crisp.
Mix the squeezed vegetables with beef, garlic, cumin, paprika, cinnamon, egg, flour and salt until sticky; if the mix is loose, the patties shed bits into the oil.
Shape into nine thin rough patties, pressing ragged edges flat enough to touch the pan; thick centres stay grey while the outside burns.
Heat the oil in a wide frying pan until a potato shred sizzles immediately, then add patties without crowding; a crowded pan cools and gives you greasy softness.
Fry until the undersides are deep brown and craggy, then turn once with a thin spatula; flipping repeatedly knocks off the crust.
Fry the second side until the beef is cooked through and the potato edges look crisp and lace-brown; pale patches mean raw-tasting flour inside.
Drain on a rack, not kitchen paper, and squeeze over lemon while hot; paper traps steam and softens the crust you just made.

note: Cheap mince stretches well here because potato brings the crunch and bulk.

name: Smoky Mackerel Escabeche on Saffron Potatoes
hook: Warm vinegar, blue fish, crushed golden potatoes

steps.t: Put the potatoes in salted cold water with the saffron and bring to a steady boil; starting hot leaves the centres waxy while the edges collapse.
Simmer until a knife slides through with no chalky resistance, then drain and steam-dry in the colander so they crush fluffy rather than watery.
Salt the mackerel and fry skin-side down in 2 tablespoons of the oil until the skin tightens and goes lace-brown; move it too early and it tears.
Turn the fillets for 30 seconds only, then lift them to a shallow dish; overcooking makes the oily flesh woolly instead of silky.
In the same pan, soften onion, carrot and garlic with the bay until the onion is translucent at the edges, not browned, or the pickle will taste bitter.
Stir in paprika for a few seconds until smoky, add vinegar and the remaining oil, and bubble until the raw vinegar sting softens but the sauce still smells sharp.
Crush the hot potatoes with a fork, spoon the warm escabeche over the mackerel, and rest for 10 minutes so the fish drinks the dressing rather than shedding it.
Serve the glossy fish on the saffron potatoes with parsley scattered at the end; add it earlier and the winter warmth turns the herbs dull.

note: Best warm rather than piping hot, when the vinegar and mackerel fat settle into each other.

name: Comté Cloud Baked Eggs with Leeks
hook: Runny yolks under a nutty bronze crust

steps.t: Heat the oven to 190°C fan and butter a small baking dish; if the dish is too wide, the eggs spread thin and the yolks overcook before the cream bubbles.
Cook the leeks in butter with a pinch of salt until soft and glossy but still pale; browned leeks taste oniony and steal the sweetness.
Stir crème fraîche, Dijon, thyme and half the Comté into the leeks off the heat until loose and creamy; boiling it hard now can split the sauce.
Spoon the leek cream into the dish and make six clear hollows, because eggs cracked onto a flat surface slide together and cook unevenly.
Crack in the eggs, scatter over the remaining Comté, and bake until the whites are just set at the edges and the yolks still wobble under the cheese.
Rest for 3 minutes so the residual heat finishes the whites; serving straight away can leave a clear raw ring around the yolk.
Take it to the table with hot sourdough, scooping from the edge first where the cheese is bronzed and the cream is thickest.

note: For firmer yolks, add 2 minutes, but watch the whites rather than the clock.

name: Maple Bourbon Braised Lamb Shanks
hook: Sticky shanks with a glossy bourbon gravy

steps.t: Heat the oven to 160°C fan, season the shanks, dust lightly with flour, and shake off the excess; clumps of flour make a pasty sauce.
Brown the shanks in oil until each side has a dark chestnut crust; pale meat gives a thin gravy no matter how long it braises.
Lift out the lamb, then cook onion, celery and carrot in the same pot until the vegetables soften and the browned bits loosen from the base.
Add garlic and tomato paste and fry until the paste turns brick-red; if it stays raw, the sauce tastes metallic.
Pour in the bourbon and boil until the harsh alcohol smell disappears, scraping the base carefully so the glaze does not burn onto the pan.
Add stock, maple syrup and rosemary, return the shanks, cover tightly, and braise until the meat pulls back from the bone and yields to a spoon.
Uncover and braise for a final stretch until the sauce coats the back of a spoon; stopping while watery leaves the lamb impressive but the gravy forgettable.
Rest the shanks in the sauce for 10 minutes, then skim the orange fat slick before serving so the glaze tastes rich, not greasy.

note: Serve with mashed potatoes, buttered greens or cornbread to catch the sauce.

name: Summer Porotos with Corn and Chimichurri
hook: Brothy beans, sweet corn, sharp green oil

steps.t: Warm the oil and cook onion with a pinch of salt until it turns translucent and sweet; rushing this leaves a raw onion bite in a light stew.
Add the red pepper and cook until the corners soften but the pieces still hold their colour, because collapsed pepper makes the bowl feel heavy.
Stir in grated tomato and oregano and simmer until the tomato looks jammy and no longer foams pink around the spoon.
Add beans and stock, bring to a gentle simmer, and keep it below a hard boil so the beans stay whole instead of shedding skins.
Add the corn for the last few minutes only, cooking until the kernels brighten and taste milky; long simmering turns them dull and starchy.
Mix parsley, grated garlic, vinegar, lemon zest and lemon juice into a sharp chimichurri while the stew settles; adding it all to the pot would flatten the herbs.
Spoon the brothy porotos into shallow bowls and streak chimichurri over the top so every bite gets heat, acid and green freshness.

note: Good warm, but even better at room temperature with crusty bread and sliced tomatoes.

name: Cachaça Lime Roast Chicken with Farofa Crunch
hook: Citrus roast juices meet toasted cassava crumbs

ingredients.name: coriander, stalks chopped and leaves reserved

steps.t: Pat the chicken dry, then rub it all over and inside the cavity with salt, lime zest, lime juice, cachaça, garlic, coriander stalks and olive oil; wet skin steams instead of roasting.
Leave the chicken breast-side up for 20 minutes while the oven heats to 200°C fan, so the seasoning starts to bite without making the flesh cure.
Roast in a snug tray until the skin begins to bronze and the limey juices hiss at the edges rather than pool silently.
Baste once, lower the oven to 180°C fan, and keep roasting until the thickest thigh reaches 75°C or the juices run clear; guessing by colour alone is risky near the bone.
Rest the chicken on a board for 15 minutes, loosely covered; carving too soon sends the juices onto the board instead of into the meat.
While it rests, melt butter in a frying pan and stir in cassava flour and chilli flakes until sandy, golden and nutty-smelling; high heat scorches farofa before it crisps.
Stir spring onions and coriander leaves into the farofa off the heat, then spoon in a little roasting juice so it clumps lightly rather than turning greasy.
Carve the chicken into small shared pieces and pile with lime wedges, farofa and the remaining roasting juices for dragging through the crumbs.

note: Set it out with pickles, black beans or sliced avocado so everyone can build small plates.

name: Lahori Crisp Masala Prawns
hook: Crackly edges, lemon heat, sweet prawns

steps.t: Pat the prawns very dry with kitchen paper; if they go into the flour damp and glossy, the coating turns pasty instead of crisp.
Mix gram flour, rice flour, chilli, turmeric, ajwain, lemon zest and a good pinch of salt in a bowl, breaking up any gram flour lumps before they become gritty clumps on the prawns.
Stir in the ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice and just enough water to make a thick batter that drags off the spoon slowly; a runny batter slides into the oil and leaves the prawns bare.
Fold in the prawns until every curve is coated, then leave them while the oil heats; do not leave raw prawns sitting warm for longer than this short pause.
Heat the oil in a wide frying pan until a drop of batter sizzles hard and rises straight away; if the oil is sleepy, the coating drinks grease before it crisps.
Shallow-fry the prawns in one loose layer, turning once, until the ridges are deep gold and the prawns are opaque right through; crowding the pan steams them rubbery.
Drain on a rack, not paper, then scatter with coriander and a last squeeze of lemon; paper traps steam underneath and softens the crust you just made.

note: Serve with sliced red onion and cucumber if you want a sharper weeknight plate.

name: Steamed Halloumi Bánh Cuốn Parcels
hook: Silky rice folds, salty molten filling

ingredients.name: neutral oil, plus extra for brushing

steps.t: Whisk rice flour, tapioca starch, warm water, 1 tablespoon oil and a pinch of salt until smooth, then rest it until the chalky smell softens; unripened batter tears as it steams.
Cover the shiitakes with boiling water until springy, then squeeze them hard and chop finely; wet mushrooms flood the filling and make the parcels slip apart.

Cook the shallots in 1 tablespoon oil until their edges turn honey-gold, then stir in mushrooms, halloumi and spring onions just until the halloumi warms and squeaks; fully melting it now makes the filling greasy.
Stir fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, chilli and 3 tablespoons water into a sharp dipping sauce; if the sugar sits undissolved, every spoonful tastes uneven.
Set a taut cloth or lightly oiled metal tray over a steamer at a lively simmer, then brush with oil; dry fabric or bare metal grips the rice sheet like glue.
Whisk the batter again, ladle on a thin film, cover and steam until the sheet turns translucent and lifts at the edge; if it still looks milky, it will rip when folded.
Spoon on a line of halloumi filling, fold the sheet over itself and slide it to an oiled plate; stack without oil and the parcels weld together before lunch.
Repeat, keeping the steamer bubbling and the batter stirred, then serve warm with the lime-chilli sauce; weak steam gives thick, gummy sheets instead of silk.

note: This is a slow, satisfying project dish: the first sheet is usually the cook’s snack.

name: Tuscan Ember Pork with Bean Salsa
hook: Lean smoke, rosemary, bright beans

steps.t: Rub the pork with 1 tablespoon olive oil, garlic, rosemary, fennel, lemon zest, salt and black pepper; miss the silver skin and it tightens on the grill like elastic.
Light the coals and wait until they are ashed over with no tall flames; flames lick soot onto lean pork before the centre has a chance to cook.
Stir beans, tomatoes, rocket, balsamic, lemon juice and the remaining olive oil together, seasoning firmly; underseasoned beans taste flat beside grilled meat.
Grill the pork over the hot side of the coals, turning as each face gets dark bar marks and releases cleanly; if it sticks, it is not ready to turn.
Move the pork to the cooler side, lid down if you have one, until it feels springy but not hard and reaches 63°C in the thickest part; guessing with pork is how you get either risk or sawdust.
Rest the pork on a warm plate so the juices settle; slice straight from the grill and they run out onto the board.
Slice thickly across the grain and pile beside the bean salsa, spooning over any resting juices; cutting with the grain makes even tenderloin chew stringy.

note: Built for protein without heaviness: lean pork, beans and a sharp salad finish.

name: Kesar Elaichi Steamed Egg Custard
hook: Saffron silk under bitter caramel

steps.t: Warm the milk with saffron and cardamom until it steams at the edge, then take it off the heat; boiling milk dulls the saffron and can scramble the eggs later.
Melt the sugar in a small pan to a deep amber caramel and pour it into a 1 litre heatproof bowl, tilting fast; pale caramel tastes merely sweet, but burnt black caramel turns harsh.
Whisk eggs gently with condensed milk and rosewater, then slowly whisk in the warm saffron milk; hard whisking fills the custard with bubbles that set as holes.
Strain the custard over the set caramel; skip this and tiny egg threads spoil the smooth, steamed texture.
Cover the bowl tightly with foil and set it in a steamer over a calm simmer; a violent boil rattles the custard into a grainy split.
Steam until the edges are set and the centre wobbles like soft jelly, not liquid milk; an under-set custard collapses when turned out.
Cool, then chill until fully cold so the caramel loosens into sauce; unmoulding warm custard usually breaks the dome.
Run a thin knife around the edge, invert onto a plate and scatter with pistachios; forcing it without loosening leaves the best caramel stuck in the bowl.

note: A make-ahead finish with the familiar comfort of Indian bakery caramel custard.

name: Snow Day Halloumi Wedge Salad
hook: Cold crunch, hot maple-buttered cheese

steps.t: Cut the iceberg through the core into two thick wedges and chill them while you cook; if you slice away the core, the leaves slump apart on the plate.
Whisk soured cream, mayonnaise, cider vinegar, Dijon and plenty of black pepper until pourable; if it sits like paste, loosen with a teaspoon of cold water or it will clag in one spot.
Set a non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat and lay in the halloumi dry; move it too soon and the golden crust tears off before it has formed.
Cook the halloumi until the underside is deep honey-gold and the edges puff slightly, then turn once and colour the second side.
Drop in the butter and maple syrup, swirl until foaming, and spoon it over the cheese for a glossy coat; boil it hard for too long and the syrup turns bitter.
Spoon dressing over the cold wedges, tuck the hot halloumi against them, then finish with pecans, chives and smoked paprika so every forkful gets crunch rather than a bare lettuce core.

note: Barely cooked comfort: the lettuce stays raw and icy while the cheese gets a quick hot glaze.

name: Mackerel Chimichurri Breakfast Revuelto
hook: Crisp fish, sharp herbs, soft eggs

steps.t: Stir parsley, oregano, vinegar, garlic, chilli flakes and a pinch of salt into a loose chimichurri; if you add it to the pan too early, the herbs go khaki and flat.
Pat the mackerel very dry and cut into chunky strips; damp skin steams instead of spitting into the crisp flakes you want.
Heat a wide frying pan or wok until a drop of water skitters away, then add the oil, potatoes and red onion; a crowded or timid pan gives you greasy potato rubble.
Stir-fry hard until the potato corners blister brown and the onion edges char in spots.
Add the mackerel skin-side down where possible and toss only as it firms; constant stirring breaks it into oily crumbs before the flesh has set.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt, pour them around the fish, and fold just until glossy curds cling to the potatoes; take them dry and the whole breakfast eats chalky.
Pull off the heat and spoon over the chimichurri, letting the vinegar cut the rich fish rather than cooking its brightness away.

note: Use cooked leftover potatoes to keep this genuinely fast at breakfast.

name: Moqueca-Glazed Cauliflower Steaks
hook: Coconut gloss and smoky lime edges

steps.t: Slice the cauliflower through the stalk into four 2 cm steaks, keeping the core attached; trim it away and the florets scatter before they reach the griddle.
Whisk coconut milk, tomato purée, lime juice, paprika, cumin and salt into a peach-coloured glaze; taste now, because a bland glaze stays bland once charred.
Brush the steaks with oil and set them on a very hot griddle pan; if the pan is only warm, the cauliflower leaks water and tastes boiled.
Griddle until dark bars appear and the underside smells nutty, then turn carefully with a wide spatula.
Brush the seared side thickly with the coconut glaze, cook until the second side is barred, then turn once more to lacquer the glaze until sticky at the ridges, not burnt black.
Warm the diced pepper and spring onions on a cooler corner of the griddle just until glossy; take them too far and you lose the fresh moqueca crunch.
Plate the steaks with the peppers, coriander and cashews, spooning over any remaining warm glaze so the charred grooves catch the coconut sauce.

note: Dendê gives the most Brazilian colour and aroma, but olive oil keeps it accessible.

name: Lahori Crisp Cod Kachumber
hook: Crackly fish, cool lemoned crunch

steps.t: Salt the cod lightly and rub with lemon zest, then leave it while you make the salad; if the fish is wet when battered, the coating slides off in the oil.
Toss cucumber, tomato and red onion with half the lemon juice and a pinch of salt; deseed the tomatoes or the kachumber floods the crisp fish.

Mix gram flour, rice flour, coriander, ajwain, chilli, turmeric and salt, then whisk in enough cold water and the remaining lemon juice to make a batter like single cream; too thick gives a doughy shell.
Heat 1 cm oil in a frying pan until a drip of batter rises straight away with tiny bubbles, not violent smoke.
Pat the cod dry, coat each piece thinly, and lay it away from you into the oil; dropping it in from height splashes hot oil and knocks off the batter.
