Shallow fry until the crust is sandy-gold and crisp at the corners, turning once so the fish cooks through without drying.
Drain on a rack, not kitchen paper, and serve with the lemony kachumber; paper traps steam underneath and softens the best side.

note: Cod loin stays neat, but haddock or pollock also work if cut thick.

name: Pickled Oyster Mushroom Gỏi
hook: Tangled mushrooms, bright chilli-lime snap

steps.t: Pour boiling water over the torn oyster mushrooms, leave until just wilted and flexible, then drain hard; skip the squeeze and the pickle turns watery instead of snappy.
Warm rice vinegar with sugar and salt just until dissolved, then pour it over the mushrooms; boiling them in the brine makes them rubbery.
Let the mushrooms pickle until they taste sharp all the way through the thickest strips.
Drain the mushrooms, reserving two tablespoons of pickling liquid, and squeeze gently; leave them swimming and the dressing will taste thin.
Whisk the reserved pickling liquid with lime juice and soy sauce, then toss with carrot, cucumber and chilli; dressing the herbs now bruises them black.
Fold in the mushrooms, mint and coriander at the last moment so the leaves stay lifted and the mushroom strands remain distinct.
Scatter with crushed peanuts on a wide plate; pile it in a deep bowl and the bright dressing hides at the bottom.

note: A clean, make-ahead small plate: pickle the mushrooms earlier, dress just before serving.

name: Miso-Butter Griddled Cod with Savoy Rice
hook: Miso butter warmth, crackling cod edges

steps.t: Mix the miso, mirin, butter, soy and ginger to a smooth paste; if it stays lumpy, the butter will scorch in patches instead of glazing the fish.
Pat the cod very dry, then coat it lightly with half the miso butter and leave it while you sort the rice; wet fish steams and tears on the griddle.
Fold the cabbage and most of the spring onions through the hot rice, cover, and let the leaves slump until glossy and sweet-edged; if the rice is lukewarm, the cabbage will taste raw and squeaky.
Heat a ridged griddle until a drop of water snaps away, then oil it thinly; too much oil smokes before the cod has a chance to mark.
Lay the cod down and do not prod it until the ridges are dark gold and the edges turn opaque; moving it early leaves half the crust welded to the pan.
Turn the fish with a thin spatula, brush with the remaining miso butter, and cook until the flakes just separate under gentle pressure; pushed past this point, cod turns woolly.
Spoon the cabbage rice into warm bowls, sit the cod on top, and scatter over the remaining spring onion while the butter is still bubbling.

note: A cast-iron griddle gives the best wintery char, but a heavy frying pan also works.

name: Kimchi-Crisp Oyster Mushroom Breakfast Jeon
hook: Crisp edges, kimchi steam, morning sesame

steps.t: Squeeze the kimchi over a bowl and keep the juice; if it goes in dripping wet, the batter loosens and the jeon fry leathery instead of crisp.
Whisk the eggs, flour, potato starch, gochujang, soy, sesame oil and 2 tablespoons of kimchi juice until just smooth; over-whisking makes the pancake bouncy rather than tender.
Fold in the mushrooms, kimchi and spring onions until every strip is lightly coated; bare mushroom patches spit in the oil and never crisp properly.
Heat half the oil in a wide frying pan until a fleck of batter sizzles immediately, then spread in two loose pancakes; crowding them traps steam underneath.
Fry until the undersides are lace-brown and the centres look set rather than glossy; flipping too soon breaks the mushroom web apart.
Turn, add the remaining oil around the edges, and fry until the second side scratches when nudged with a spatula; without the extra oil, the edges stay soft.
Stir the rice vinegar with a splash of soy for dipping, then eat the jeon hot while the crust is still audible.

note: Good breakfast jeon should feel more mushroom than batter, with kimchi doing the seasoning.

name: Chinkiang-Pickled Beef with Sichuan Chilli Gloss
hook: Cool beef, black vinegar, numbing gloss

ingredients.name: cucumber, deseeded and cut into ribbons

steps.t: Salt the bavette lightly and pat it dry; any surface moisture boils on the pan and gives you grey beef instead of a clean sear.
Toss the cucumber and daikon with 50 ml vinegar and the sugar, then leave until bendy and sharp; if you skip this wait, the vegetables taste watery beside the beef.
Heat the oil in a heavy pan until shimmering, then sear the steak hard on both sides until a dark crust forms and the thickest part reaches at least 57°C; a pale crust tastes flat once chilled.
Rest the beef on a board until the juices settle; slicing straight away floods the dressing and leaves the meat dry.
Whisk the remaining vinegar with soy, chilli oil, Sichuan pepper and garlic until glossy and brick-red; if the garlic sits in clumps, it bites harshly in one mouthful.
Slice the beef thinly across the grain, looking for short fibres rather than long strings; cut with the grain and even tender bavette chews like rope.
Drain the pickles well, arrange them with the beef, spoon over the chilli gloss, and finish with coriander and sesame just before serving so the herbs stay lifted.

note: Serve cool, not fridge-cold, so the black vinegar and beef fat taste rounded rather than muted.

name: Lime-Baked Mackerel Veracruz Tray
hook: Bright lime, soft tomatoes, clean mackerel

steps.t: Heat the oven to 220°C and choose a shallow baking dish that holds everything in one layer; a crowded dish stews the fish and dulls the summer sharpness.
Toss the tomatoes, courgette, red onion, jalapeño, olives, oregano, lime zest and olive oil in the dish until shiny; dry patches catch before the tomatoes burst.
Bake the vegetables until the tomato skins wrinkle and the onion tips go purple-brown; if they are still raw when the fish goes in, the mackerel will overcook waiting for them.
Season the mackerel, lay it skin-side up on the hot vegetables, and spoon a little oily tomato juice over the flesh; burying the skin makes it flabby.
Bake until the skin tightens, the flesh turns opaque at the thick end and flakes with a nudge; mackerel goes chalky fast once the flakes gape wide open.
Squeeze over the lime juice and rest for a minute in the dish so the juices taste joined rather than raw and separate.
Scatter with coriander and serve straight from the baking dish, keeping the fillets on top so they do not break into the tomatoes.

note: This is deliberately light: oily fish, acid, herbs and vegetables rather than a heavy sauce.

name: Slow-Braised Tofu Stifado with Kalamata Olives
hook: Silky tofu in cinnamon tomato depth

steps.t: Wrap the tofu in a clean tea towel and press gently until the surface feels dry, not cracked; wet tofu sheds water into the braise and tastes bland in the middle.
Cut the tofu into chunky rectangles and brown them in half the oil until the edges are biscuit-coloured; pale tofu will stay spongey no matter how good the sauce is.
Lift out the tofu, add the shallots and remaining oil, and cook until the cut sides are amber and starting to soften; rushing this leaves the stifado sharp and oniony.
Add the garlic for just long enough to smell sweet, then pour in the wine and scrape up the browned bits; burnt garlic turns the whole pot bitter.
Stir in the passata, cinnamon, bay leaves, olives and vinegar, then nestle the tofu back in so it is mostly covered; pieces left high and dry toughen at the corners.
Cover and braise on a low heat until the shallots slump and the sauce clings thickly to a spoon; a hard boil breaks the tofu and makes the oil split harshly.
Uncover for the final thickening until small red oil beads show at the edges, then remove the cinnamon and bay; leaving the cinnamon in too long makes it taste dusty.
Finish with parsley and serve warm in the centre of the table, where the sauce can be dragged through bread or spooned beside other meze.

note: It eats best warm rather than piping hot, when the tofu has absorbed the stifado perfume.

name: Quick Lamb Türlü with Pepper Butter
hook: Silky lamb stew, bright pul biber warmth

ingredients.name: lamb leg steak, trimmed and cut into 2 cm pieces

steps.t: Heat the oil in a wide saucepan until it shimmers, then spread the lamb in one layer. Let it catch at the edges before stirring; if you crowd or fuss it, the lamb steams grey and tastes boiled.
Add the onion and green pepper with a pinch of salt. Cook until the onion collapses and the pepper skin looks glossy; if they stay crunchy now, the stew will taste raw and separate.
Stir in the garlic, tomato paste and pul biber until the paste darkens to brick-red and leaves rusty streaks on the pan. Do not let the garlic go brown, or the whole pot turns bitter.
Add the potatoes, chopped tomatoes and hot stock, scraping the base clean. The liquid should just lap around the potatoes, not drown them, or you will get soup instead of türlü.
Simmer with the lid slightly ajar until the potatoes crush easily against the side and the lamb has lost its springy bite. Keep it at a lazy bubble; a hard boil tightens lean lamb fast.
Rest off the heat for 3 minutes, then fold through the parsley. Taste for salt only at the end, because the sauce concentrates as it sits.

note: Cutting the lamb small is what makes this weeknight-fast without pretending stewing cuts cook in minutes.

name: Whole-Roasted Chickpea Kibbeh Pumpkin
hook: Crackly pumpkin, spiced chickpeas, lemony tahini

steps.t: Cover the chickpeas with plenty of cold water the night before. Use a bowl much bigger than seems sensible; if they swell above the waterline, the centres stay chalky no matter how long you cook them.

Drain the chickpeas, simmer in fresh unsalted water until creamy inside, then cook the lentils in a second pan until tender but still holding their skins. Salt both only near the end, or old pulses can toughen.
Cut a neat lid from the pumpkin and scrape out every string and seed. Leave the walls thick and even; gouge them thin and the pumpkin slumps before the filling is hot.

Fry the onions in the olive oil until sweet and golden at the edges, then add garlic, baharat and tomato paste. Cook until the paste smells roasted, not tinny, because this is the backbone of the stuffing.
Mix the chickpeas, lentils, bulgur and onion spice paste while the pulses are hot. Add enough pulse cooking water to make it damp and spoonable; a dry filling steals moisture from the pumpkin.
Pack the filling into the pumpkin without ramming it tight, replace the lid, rub the skin with oil and salt, and set it on a tray. If it is overfilled, the bulgur expands and forces the lid off.

Roast at 180°C until the skin is blistered, the base feels soft when pressed with a spoon, and a knife slides through the shoulder with no hard ring. Rest before cutting, or the slices collapse into mash.

Whisk tahini with lemon juice, salt and splashes of cold water until pale and pourable, then spoon it over wedges with parsley. Add the water slowly; too much at once makes the sauce split and grainy.

note: A proper weekend centrepiece: soaking, simmering, stuffing and whole roasting all matter.

name: Tea-Smoked Chermoula Chicken with Carrot Lentils
hook: Clean smoke, sharp herbs, steady protein

steps.t: Flatten the thick end of each chicken breast slightly, then coat with coriander, garlic, lemon zest, cumin, paprika, olive oil and salt. If the breasts stay domed, the thin ends dry out before the middle is safe.
Line a wok or deep pan with two layers of foil, then add the tea, rice and sugar in a flat mound. Keep the smoking mix on the foil, not loose in the pan, or the burnt sugar is miserable to clean.

Set a small rack or foil balls above the smoking mix, add the chicken, cover tightly and put over medium-high heat until wisps of smoke appear. Do not lift the lid for a peek; you lose the smoke in one breath.

Lower the heat to medium and smoke-cook until the chicken is firm, opaque and 74°C in the thickest part. If it is short of temperature, finish it covered for a few more minutes rather than serving risky pink meat.
Move the chicken to a board and rest it so the juices settle instead of flooding the lentils. Slice too soon and even well-cooked breast eats dry.
Warm the lentils with the grated carrots, lemon juice and a pinch of salt just until the carrots soften at the edges. Boil them hard and the lentils burst into sludge.
Slice the smoked chicken across the grain and lay it over the carrot lentils, spooning over any resting juices. Cut with the grain and the breast feels stringy however carefully you cooked it.

note: The tea smoke gives real aroma; the thermometer keeps the lean chicken gym-meal safe and juicy.

name: Seville Orange Tocino Steam Pots
hook: Glossy caramel, orange, trembling yolk custard

steps.t: Put 70 g of the sugar in a small pan with 2 tablespoons of the water and cook to a deep amber caramel. Stop before it smokes; pale caramel tastes flat, burnt caramel bullies the custard.
Divide the caramel between four heatproof ramekins, tilting to coat the bases. Work carefully but quickly, because once it sets in a thick lump it will not melt evenly under the custard.

Simmer the remaining sugar and water with the orange zest and cinnamon until the syrup looks clear and lightly glossy, then cool until warm, not hot. Pouring boiling syrup onto eggs gives sweet scrambled egg.
Whisk the yolks, whole egg and salt just until smooth, then trickle in the warm syrup while stirring. Avoid frothing it; bubbles set as pockmarks instead of that Spanish glassy surface.
Strain into the caramel-lined ramekins and cover each tightly with foil. Straining is not fussy here: it catches chalazae and zest that would spoil the silk.
Steam gently in a covered pan, with water halfway up the ramekins, until the edges are set and the centres tremble like soft jelly. A rolling boil makes honeycomb holes and rubbery sides.
Cool for 20 minutes, then chill until cold before turning out. Unmould warm and the caramel runs thin while the custard slumps.

note: This is a steamed egg dessert, closer to tocino de cielo than a dairy custard.

name: Coal-Grilled Halloumi Niçoise Baguettes
hook: Salty squeak, charred bread, tomato juices

steps.t: Light the coals and wait until they are ashed over with no licking flames. Grill halloumi over flames and it soots before the middle softens.
Mix the tomatoes, red onion, white beans, olives, vinegar, olive oil and Dijon with a pinch of salt. Let it sit while the grill settles; skip this pause and the bread misses the tomato juices.
Pat the halloumi dry. Wet brine on the surface stops browning and makes the cheese stick to the bars.
Grill the baguette cut-side down until the ridges turn dark gold and the edges rasp when tapped. Take it too far and the sandwich shatters instead of soaking up dressing.
Grill the halloumi over the coals until striped and bulging at the sides, then turn once only. Keep flipping and it tears, leaks, and loses its squeak.
Spoon the tomato-bean mixture over the charred baguette halves, making sure the juices hit the hot crumb. If the filling sits only on the crust, every bite slides off.
Lay the grilled halloumi on top and tear over basil. Eat straight away; once halloumi cools, it firms back into a salty eraser.

note: Niçoise pantry flavours make a cheap coal-grilled halloumi meal feel intentional, not like emergency toast.

name: Tuscan Beef Orzo al Forno
hook: Molten mozzarella over tomato-rich beef

steps.t: Heat the oven to 220°C fan. Put the oil, beef and onion in a deep ovenproof dish or roasting tin over a medium hob heat; break the mince up small, because big clumps bake into dry nuggets.
Cook until the beef loses its raw red colour and the onion turns glossy at the edges; if there is watery juice still pooling, keep going or the orzo will taste boiled rather than baked.
Stir in the garlic and orzo for a minute, scraping the base so the grains get shiny; skip this and the pasta can stick in a starchy mat.
Add passata, hot stock, oregano and a good pinch of salt, then stir right into the corners. The liquid should sit just above the orzo; dry corners become crunchy before the middle cooks.
Scatter over mozzarella and parmesan, cover tightly with foil and bake until the sauce is bubbling hard around the edges.
Remove the foil and bake until the cheese blisters in golden patches and the orzo is tender with a little bite; if it looks dry before then, splash in hot water around the edge, not over the cheese.
Rest for 5 minutes so the sauce settles back around the pasta, then tear over basil; serving straight away makes it soupy on the plate.

note: Use a wide dish rather than a narrow casserole so the orzo cooks evenly and the top browns quickly.

name: Malabar Tamarind Mackerel Braise
hook: Dark spice oil, soft sour fish

steps.t: Rub the mackerel with 1 teaspoon turmeric and 1 teaspoon salt, then chill while the masala cooks; leaving it at room temperature for a long braise is both unsafe and makes the fish smell strong.
Warm the coconut oil in a heavy shallow pan, add onions and cook slowly until they are deep gold and sticky, not pale. Pale onions give a raw sweetness that will not disappear later.

Add garlic, ginger and curry leaves; fry until the garlic edges turn biscuit-coloured and the leaves crackle. If the garlic goes dark brown, pull it off the heat because it will taste bitter through the whole sauce.
Stir in chilli powder, coriander and the remaining turmeric with a splash of water; cook until the spice paste separates from the oil in rusty streaks, or the braise will taste dusty.
Add coconut milk, tamarind paste, 200 ml water and the remaining salt. Simmer uncovered, barely bubbling, until the oil floats in red beads on top and the sauce tastes rounded rather than sharp.

Slide in the chilled mackerel skin-side up, spoon sauce over it, cover and braise on the lowest heat until the thickest pieces flake when nudged but still look glossy inside; a hard boil will curl and toughen the fillets.
Turn off the heat and rest covered so the fish drinks in the sour coconut sauce without breaking apart under a spoon.

note: Best with steamed rice and something crisp, such as sliced cucumber or red onion with lime.

name: Red Curry Tofu Edamame Stew
hook: Lean heat with coconut-lime depth

steps.t: Press the tofu between kitchen paper while you prep the vegetables, then cut into chunky cubes; wet tofu dilutes the curry and breaks when stirred.
Heat the oil in a wide saucepan and fry the curry paste until it darkens slightly and smells roasted, not raw and sharp.
Whisk in a spoonful of coconut milk first to loosen the paste smoothly; dumping in all the liquid at once leaves red flecks that never quite dissolve.
Add the remaining coconut milk, stock, soy sauce and sugar, then bring to a steady simmer with small bubbles at the rim, not a rolling boil that splits the coconut milk.
Add tofu and edamame, then simmer until the tofu has swollen slightly and the beans are hot through; stir with a folding motion so the tofu stays in cubes.
Add mangetout and red pepper and cook just until the greens turn bright and squeak faintly between your teeth; if they sag olive-green, the stew loses its fresh snap.
Turn off the heat, stir in lime juice and herbs, then taste for salt; boiling after the lime goes in flattens the clean citrus edge.

note: Serve as-is for a lower-carb bowl, or add jasmine rice if you need more fuel after training.

name: Matcha Caramel Mushi Pudding
hook: Wobbly custard, bitter caramel silk

steps.t: Set four heatproof ramekins in a steamer basket or a deep lidded pan with a rack. Keep the water below the rack; if it touches the ramekins, the custard heats too aggressively and turns grainy.

Cook 80 g sugar with the water in a small pan until it turns deep amber and smells like toasted nuts, then divide between the ramekins. Stop before it smokes black, because burnt caramel dominates the delicate custard.
Warm the milk until steaming at the edge, then whisk matcha with a splash of it in a bowl before adding the rest; dry matcha tipped straight into milk forms bitter green lumps.
Whisk eggs, 45 g sugar, vanilla and salt gently until combined, not frothy. Foam makes holes across the top instead of a mirror-smooth pudding.
Pour the warm matcha milk into the eggs slowly, whisking all the time, then strain into a jug and fill the ramekins; straining catches chalazae and any matcha specks that would set as flecks.
Cover each ramekin with foil and steam over the gentlest simmer until the edges are set and the centres wobble like soft jelly; a rattling boil gives bubbles and a rubbery rim.
Cool for 10 minutes, then chill until cold. Run a thin knife round each pudding and invert; unmoulding warm makes the custard slump and tear.

note: The caramel will loosen as the puddings chill, giving you a glossy sauce when turned out.

name: Smoked Gochujang Lentil Bap
hook: Tea smoke, sticky chilli lentils

steps.t: Line the base of a wok or deep saucepan with two layers of foil, then add the tea leaves and uncooked rice. Do not use a non-stick pan for this; the dry heat can damage the coating.

Put the drained lentils in a metal sieve or small heatproof colander that fits above the tea mixture, then cover tightly with a lid or foil. Wet lentils drip and put the smoke out, so pat them dry if they look shiny.
Heat on medium-high until you see a thin curl of smoke, then smoke the lentils until they smell like roasted tea rather than ash. Too much heat gives acrid smoke that clings unpleasantly.
Turn off the heat and let the pan stand covered before opening near an extractor or window; lifting the lid straight away dumps smoke into the room and gives weaker lentils.

Stir gochujang, soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, garlic and sesame oil in a frying pan with 3 tablespoons water, then warm until glossy and loose; if it boils dry, the chilli paste catches and tastes scorched.
Fold in the smoked lentils and simmer until they are sticky and red, with sauce clinging to the skins rather than puddling underneath.
Spoon hot rice into bowls, top with the lentils, spring onions and sesame seeds. Keep the fresh onion on top; cooking it into the sauce dulls the cheap, sharp lift that makes the bowl work.

note: Canned lentils make this very low-cost; rinse them well so the smoke and gochujang taste clean.

name: Ginger Lap Cheong Steamed Chicken
hook: Silky chicken, sweet smoke, winter ginger

ingredients.name: bone-in chicken thighs, chopped through the bone or left whole
fresh ginger, cut into fine matchsticks

steps.t: Rinse the rice until the water is only slightly cloudy, then cook it with 420 ml water; if you skip the rinse the starch makes a gummy bed instead of separate grains.
Mix chicken with soy, Shaoxing, oyster sauce, ginger, cornflour and sesame oil until every surface looks glossy; dry patches steam up flat and under-seasoned.
Spread the chicken in one shallow heatproof dish, skin side up where possible, and tuck lap cheong slices between the pieces; piling it high leaves the middle steaming slowly and unevenly.

Set over a hard-simmering wok or pan with 4 cm water, cover tightly and steam until the juices run clear and the thickest piece reaches 75°C; a weak simmer gives you rubbery skin before the meat is safe.
Turn off the heat and rest covered so the juices settle into the sauce; lifting the lid straight away lets the fragrant steam escape and the meat tightens.
Scatter with spring onions and spoon the ginger-sausage juices over bowls of rice; leave the juices in the dish and you lose the whole comfort of it.

note: Bone-in pieces give the deepest winter brothiness, but boneless thighs work if cut large and steamed a little less.

name: Coal-Blistered Nopal Breakfast Tlayudas
hook: Charred cactus, beans, bright morning crunch

ingredients.name: large corn tortillas or small tlayudas

steps.t: Light a charcoal grill and wait until the coals are grey and glowing, not flaming; flames scorch the tortillas before the vegetables get their smoky sweetness.
Grill the nopales and corn, turning often, until the cactus turns olive green with black freckles and the corn kernels blister in patches; pull them too early and the cactus stays squeaky and wet.
Rest the nopales for a minute, then slice them into strips and cut the corn from the cobs; slicing while they are dripping hot makes the juices flood the board instead of staying in the strips.
Warm the refried beans in a small pan or grill-safe pot until loose and steaming; cold beans tear the crisp tortilla when you try to spread them.
Toast the tortillas over the coals until they stiffen and smell nutty, flipping before the edges curl into ash; if they go black all over they taste bitter, not toasted.

Spread each tortilla with beans, then pile on nopales, corn, avocado, radish, queso fresco, coriander, salsa macha and lime; overload the centre only and every bite after the first tastes like plain tortilla.

note: If nopales are hard to find, use thick courgette planks; it becomes less classic but still vegetable-led and coal-bright.

name: Halloumi Peach Crudo with Olive-Leaf Oil
hook: Salty slices, cold peach, green perfume

steps.t: Put the halloumi in a bowl and cover with just-boiled water for 5 minutes; this softens the salt and squeak, while boiling it hard makes the edges rubbery.
Whisk olive oil with lemon zest, 1 tablespoon lemon juice, honey and oregano until it looks glossy; undissolved honey sinks and gives one sticky mouthful instead of balance.
Slice peaches into thin wedges and cucumber into ribbons, stopping at the watery seed core; the core dilutes the dressing and makes the platter slump.
Drain the halloumi, pat it dry, then shave or slice it as thinly as you can; wet cheese repels the oil and thick slabs eat like a packed lunch, not crudo.
Arrange halloumi, peach and cucumber loosely on a chilled platter, tucking air between the pieces; pressing everything flat makes it sweat and look tired.
Spoon over the dressing, then scatter olives, capers and torn mint; dress too early and the peaches bleed juice into the salt before guests see the shine.

note: Use the ripest fragrant fruit you can find; this dish is built on contrast rather than cooking.

name: Sumac Pork Tava with Cucumber Herbs
hook: Hot pork, cool herbs, lemony snap

ingredients.name: pork tenderloin, sliced into thin strips
flat-leaf parsley and mint, roughly chopped

steps.t: Toss the pork with 1 tablespoon oil, sumac, pul biber, cumin and a good pinch of salt; seasoning after frying leaves the strips tasting dusty on the outside and plain inside.
Heat a wide wok or heavy frying pan until a drop of water skitters away instantly; if the pan is only warm the pork stews and turns grey.
Stir-fry half the pork in a single loose layer until the edges catch bronze and the centre is just cooked through; crowding the pan drops the heat and squeezes out juice.
Lift out the first batch and repeat with the rest, adding a film of oil only if the pan looks dry; too much oil makes the spices muddy rather than toasted.
Throw in the pepper and onion and stir-fry until the onion tips char but the pepper still bends with a snap; cook them soft and the plate loses its summer lift.
Return the pork with any resting juices, squeeze over lemon and toss for a few seconds until shiny; leaving it on the heat after the lemon goes in toughens the meat.
Serve on warm flatbreads with cucumber and a heavy shower of parsley and mint; bury the herbs underneath and they wilt before they cool the pork.

note: Pork is not traditional in many Turkish kitchens, but the tava-style high-heat method and seasonings suit a lean summer plate.

name: Za’atar Griddled Egg Coins
hook: Crisp-edged eggs for tearing and sharing

ingredients.name: olive oil, plus extra for the griddle

steps.t: Whisk eggs with yoghurt, za’atar, spring onions, parsley and a pinch of salt until no streaks of yoghurt remain; lumps scorch on the griddle and leave sour white spots.
Stir tahini with lemon juice, 1 tablespoon olive oil and enough cold water to make a spoonable sauce; add the water slowly or it seizes into a paste before it loosens.
Heat a flat griddle or heavy non-stick pan until hot, then wipe it with oil so it shines but does not pool; puddles fry ragged edges instead of neat coins.
Spoon small rounds of egg mixture onto the griddle and leave them alone until the rims set and turn lace-gold; fussing early smears them into scrambled egg.
Flip each coin once and cook until just firm in the centre; overcooking makes them bouncy, and undercooking leaves raw egg on a shared plate.
Repeat with the remaining mixture, re-oiling lightly between batches when the surface looks dry; a dry griddle grabs the herbs and tears the coins.
Pile the warm egg coins on a platter with tahini sauce, Aleppo pepper and torn pitta; stacking them too long under cover steams away the crisp edges.

note: Serve beside olives, tomatoes and pickles so people can build bites straight from the platter.

name: Moqueca-Roasted Whole Tofu with Dendê Pumpkin
hook: Coconut warmth, crisp edges, velvet sauce

ingredients.name: extra-firm tofu, kept as one block
pumpkin or squash, peeled and cut into 3 cm chunks

steps.t: Heat the oven to 220°C. Pat the tofu very dry, then score the top in a shallow diamond pattern; if it goes in wet, it steams and never gets those chewy roasted corners.

Toss pumpkin, pepper and onion with half the dendê, smoked paprika and salt in a roasting tin, spreading them out so the pieces touch metal; if they pile up, they collapse into stew before the tofu roasts.
Nestle the whole tofu block in the centre, rub with the remaining dendê and salt, then roast until the tofu edges are tawny and the pumpkin is starting to blister.
Stir garlic, tomatoes and coconut milk around the tofu, not over it, scraping the sticky orange bits from the tin; covering the top now softens the crust you worked for.
Return to the oven until the sauce bubbles thickly at the edges and leaves a trail when dragged with a spoon.
Finish with lime zest, lime juice and coriander, then rest for 5 minutes; cutting straight away makes the tofu shed its juices into the sauce instead of staying custardy inside.

note: Serve in thick slices with the coconut tomato sauce spooned around, not over, the crisp top.

name: Dhungar Lahori Chana with Ginger-Fried Bread
hook: Coal smoke, soft chickpeas, bright ginger

ingredients.name: ginger, half grated and half cut into matchsticks

steps.t: Cook the onion in 2 tbsp ghee with a pinch of salt until it turns deep golden at the edges; pale onion leaves the chana sweet and flat, while black specks make it bitter.
Add garlic, grated ginger, coriander, cumin and chilli, stirring until the fat stains brick-red and the raw garlic smell disappears; dry spices burn fast, so splash in chickpea liquid if they catch.
Add chickpeas, garam masala and 200 ml reserved chickpea liquid, then mash a quarter of the chickpeas against the pan; if you skip the mash, the gravy stays watery instead of clinging to bread.
Simmer until the chana looks glossy and thick enough to mound on a spoon, seasoning hard because breakfast pulses need salt to wake them up.

Meanwhile toast the bread in the remaining ghee with the ginger matchsticks until the edges are crisp and the ginger is straw-gold; too fierce a heat scorches the ginger before the bread warms through.

Heat the charcoal over a gas flame or with tongs under a grill until ashy and glowing, then set it in a small foil cup inside the chana pan, drizzle on a few drops of ghee, cover immediately and smoke briefly; leave it too long and the chickpeas taste like an ashtray.
Remove the charcoal cup carefully, stir once, and serve the smoky chana over the ginger-fried bread with lemon for squeezing.

note: Do the smoking step with ventilation and use natural charcoal only, never treated barbecue briquettes.

name: Steamed Mung Bean Bánh Bèo with Scallion Oil
hook: Silky cups, golden crumble, sharp dressing

ingredients.name: split yellow mung beans, soaked for at least 2 hours

steps.t: Drain the soaked mung beans, cover with fresh water and simmer until they squash easily between finger and thumb; undercooked beans stay gritty and ruin the soft contrast.
Drain very well, then mash with a pinch of salt into a fluffy yellow crumble; if it is wet, steam it uncovered for a minute to drive off moisture or it will paste onto the cakes.
Whisk rice flour, tapioca starch, warm water and 0.5 tsp salt until smooth, then rest so the starch hydrates; skipping the rest gives rubbery edges and chalky centres.
Heat a steamer and warm small shallow bowls or saucers inside it, then brush them lightly with oil; cold cups make the batter set unevenly and stick in sad patches.
Stir the batter right down to the bottom, pour a thin layer into each hot cup, and steam until the cakes turn translucent with a small dimple in the centre.
Warm the oil until shimmering, pour it over the spring onions and a pinch of salt, and stop there; frying them brown turns the scallion oil harsh instead of sweet and green.

Mix soy sauce, lime juice, sugar, chilli and 3 tbsp water until bright and balanced, then top each cake with mung bean crumble, scallion oil, fried shallots and mint just before serving so the crunch survives the steam.

note: Use small saucers or dipping bowls for the prettiest guest-table presentation.

name: Salmoriglio Coal-Grilled Chicken with Fennel Peach Salad
hook: Smoke-kissed chicken, lemon herbs, cool crunch

steps.t: Light the charcoal and let it burn until the coals are mostly grey with no licking flames; flame-grilling chicken thighs paints them black outside before the centre is safe.
Mix lemon zest, half the lemon juice, 2 tbsp olive oil, garlic, oregano, fennel seeds and salt, then coat the chicken; do not leave it sitting for hours in lemon or the surface turns woolly.
Set the chicken over medium-hot coals and grill until the underside releases cleanly with dark bar marks; if it sticks, it is not ready to turn and will tear.
Turn and cook the second side until the thickest piece reaches 74°C or the juices run clear with no pinkness; guessing is how summer chicken gets served unsafe.
Move the chicken to a cooler edge of the grill, spoon over a little lemon-herb oil, and rest until the juices settle instead of flooding the board.
Toss fennel and peaches with the remaining lemon juice, olive oil and a pinch of salt until the fennel softens slightly but still snaps; overdressing early makes the salad limp.
Slice the chicken across the grain and plate with rocket, the fennel peach salad and parsley, spooning over any resting juices for a clean salmoriglio finish.

note: Chicken thighs stay juicier than breast over coals while still eating light with the raw fennel salad.

name: Kokum-Lime Barely Poached Prawn Chaat
hook: Cool prawns, tart kokum, crisp sev

steps.t: Soak the kokum in 80 ml just-boiled water until the liquid turns deep pink and sharply sour; using it dry gives leathery bites instead of a clean tang.
Bring a pan of well-salted water to a bare simmer, not a rolling boil; violent bubbles toughen prawns before the centres warm through.
Add the prawns and poach until they curl into loose Cs and turn opaque all the way through, then lift them straight into a bowl of iced water; tight Os mean they have gone rubbery.
Drain the prawns thoroughly and pat dry, because watery shellfish dilutes the lime and makes the sev sag immediately.
Strain the kokum liquid and mix with lime juice, mustard oil, chaat masala, cumin and chilli; taste for salt now, as chaat should hit sour, salty and warm before it meets the prawns.
Fold prawns, onion, cucumber and coriander through the dressing and let them sit just until the edges taste seasoned; leaving them too long in acid firms the prawns like overcooked ceviche.
Spoon onto a shared plate and scatter sev at the last second so it crackles rather than turning into noodles.

note: Use very fresh prawns, keep them chilled, and cook them fully to opaque while preserving a barely poached texture.

name: Crisp Chermoula Carrot Fritters
hook: Frilly edges, warm spice, lemon snap

steps.t: Toss the grated carrot and courgette with a good pinch of salt, then squeeze hard in a clean tea towel until the bundle feels dry and squeaky; if it still drips, the fritters steam instead of crisping.
Mix the squeezed vegetables with flour, cornflour, coriander, preserved lemon, garlic, cumin and paprika until every strand is lightly dusty; stop before it turns pasty, or the centres cook up gummy.
Heat the oil in a wide frying pan until a stray shred sizzles the second it lands; if the oil is quiet the fritters drink it, and if it smokes the spices scorch bitter.
Press the mixture into 6 thin fritters and fry in two batches, leaving space between them so the steam can escape; crowding gives you soft pancakes with pale edges.
Flip when the undersides are deep gold with lace-brown rims, then fry the second side until the fritters feel firm when nudged; turn too early and they split.
Drain on a rack, not kitchen paper, and squeeze over lemon at the table; paper traps steam underneath and steals the crunch you just made.

note: A fast vegetable dinner that eats best straight from the pan.

name: Weekend Hake Escabeche with Orange Olive Dressing
hook: Cool vinegar, silky fish, briny olives

steps.t: Sprinkle the hake evenly with the salt and chill uncovered; this firms the flakes so they survive the pickle, while skipping it leaves the fish woolly and fragile.

Rinse the fish quickly and pat it very dry, then warm half the oil in a frying pan and cook the fillets just until opaque at the thickest point; wet fish spits, and raw centres are not safe to pickle cold.
Lift the hake into a shallow glass or ceramic dish in one layer; piling hot fillets on top of each other breaks them before the vinegar can season them.
In the same pan, soften the onion, carrot, garlic and bay until the onion bends without browning; browned garlic turns harsh once vinegar hits it.
Stir in the paprika for a few seconds, then add the sherry vinegar and remaining oil and bring it to a bare simmer; boil it hard and the marinade tastes sharp rather than rounded.
Pour the hot escabeche over the fish, cool until no steam rises, cover and refrigerate for 24 hours; cover it while hot and condensation dilutes the pickle.
To serve, spoon the fish and vegetables onto plates and dress with orange zest, orange segments, torn olives and parsley; adding the dressing a day early muddies the bright citrus finish.

note: Serve cool, not fridge-cold, with bread to catch the escabeche oil.

name: Dijon Chicken, Mushroom and Lentil Bake
hook: Earthy mushrooms, lean chicken, molten Gruyère

ingredients.name: chicken breast, cut into large chunks

steps.t: Heat the oven to 210°C and set a wide ovenproof dish over a medium-high hob; if the dish is small, use a tray instead, because crowded mushrooms leak and stew.
Oil and season the chicken, then sear it in the dish until the outside turns opaque with a few golden patches, not cooked through; fully cooking it now makes it dry after baking.
Add the mushrooms and shallots and cook until the mushrooms give up their water and the pan sounds like frying again; if you move on while it is watery, the bake turns thin.
Stir in the garlic for one minute, then fold through the lentils, Dijon, stock, crème fraîche and thyme until the sauce is beige and glossy; unmixed mustard leaves hot, salty pockets.

Nestle the chicken pieces back through the lentils, scatter over the Gruyère and bake until the top freckles brown and the chicken is cooked through; pale cheese usually means the middle is still only warm.
Rest the dish until the sauce stops bubbling at the edges, then serve in deep bowls; spooning it out immediately makes the creamy sauce run instead of clinging.

note: Built for meal prep: it reheats gently without losing much texture.

name: Maple Pecan Steamed Custard Cups
hook: Silky maple wobble, salty pecan crunch

steps.t: Set a steamer over a low simmer and wrap the lid in a clean tea towel; dripping condensation pits the custard tops and a rolling boil makes them bubbly.
Warm the milk, cream, maple syrup and brown sugar until the sugar dissolves and the pan feels hot but not scalding; boiling it scrambles the eggs on contact.
Whisk the eggs and vanilla just until loose, keeping the whisk low; frothy eggs steam into a spongy texture instead of a satin one.
Pour the warm dairy into the eggs slowly while whisking, then strain into four ramekins; straining catches chalazae and any accidental curds before they set.
Cover each ramekin with foil and steam gently until the edges are set and the centre gives a slow wobble, not a liquid ripple; fierce steam leaves tunnels through the custard.
Toast the pecans in a dry pan until they smell buttery and darken at the edges; take them too far and their bitterness cuts straight through the maple.
Rest the custards for 5 minutes, then finish with pecans and flaky salt; topping them straight from the steamer makes the nuts soften in the surface steam.

note: Serve warm for comfort, or chill for a firmer spoonful.

name: Sardine Chimichurri Potato Guiso
hook: Potato-thick stew with bright sardine oil

steps.t: Open the sardines and spoon 2 tablespoons of their oil into a saucepan; throwing the oil away loses the cheap richness that carries the stew.
Cook the onion and green pepper in the sardine oil until soft and shiny, not browned hard; burnt pepper makes the whole pot taste tired.
Add the garlic, cumin, paprika and oregano and stir until the spices smell warm; leave them dry too long and the paprika catches black.
Tip in the potatoes, tomatoes and water, then scrape the base of the pan so no spice paste is stuck there; stuck spices scorch during the simmer.
Simmer with the lid half on until the potatoes crush easily against the side of the pan and the tomato broth looks thicker; if the potato is still sharp-edged, the stew will taste watery.
Fold in the sardines in large pieces and warm them through gently; hard boiling breaks them into gritty flakes and pushes the fishiness forward.
Stir in the vinegar and parsley off the heat, then let the guiso sit briefly before serving; boiling the fresh finish dulls the chimichurri bite.

note: Good with plain rice, but filling enough without it.

name: Winter Mushroom Stifado with Chestnuts
hook: Dark wine, sweet onions, forest mushrooms

ingredients.name: mixed mushrooms, torn into large pieces
pearl onions or small shallots, peeled

steps.t: Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a wide casserole and fry the mushrooms in two batches until their cut faces go nut-brown and the pan sounds dry; crowd them and they will boil grey instead of building flavour.
Add the remaining oil and the onions to the same pan, turning them until patchily golden; if the heat is too fierce the outside scorches before the centres soften.
Stir in the garlic, tomato purée, bay and cinnamon until the purée darkens to brick red; leaving it raw makes the braise taste tinny.
Pour in the wine and scrape hard at the base until the sticky bits dissolve; if you skip this, the sauce tastes thin and the pan may catch later.
Return the mushrooms with the stock, vinegar and a good pinch of salt, then bring to a bare simmer; a hard boil breaks the mushrooms down and muddies the sauce.
Cover with the lid slightly ajar and braise until the onions yield to a spoon and the sauce is glossy, not watery.
Fold in the chestnuts for the final few minutes, then rest off the heat until the oil settles in little red pools; add parsley at the end or it turns khaki.

note: Serve with orzo, mashed potato or thick bread for dragging through the sauce.

name: Aleppo Halloumi Breakfast Stew
hook: Squeaky cheese in peppery tomato warmth

ingredients.name: green Turkish pepper or mild green chilli, sliced

steps.t: Pat the halloumi dry and sear it in 1 tbsp oil until the edges blister gold; wet cheese spits and steams, so dry it properly before it hits the pan.
Lift the halloumi out, add the remaining oil, onion and peppers, and cook until the onion slumps and the peppers smell sweet; undercooked pepper stays squeaky and sharp in the finished stew.
Stir in the garlic and pul biber for a short sizzle until the oil stains red; let the garlic brown and it will turn bitter before the tomatoes arrive.
Add the tomatoes, rinse the tin with 100 ml water and pour that in too, then simmer until the sauce looks thick enough to leave a trail when stirred.
Return the halloumi and simmer gently so it warms through without tightening into rubber; a rolling boil makes the cubes tough.
Make two hollows, crack in the eggs, cover and cook until the whites are set but the yolks still tremble; if the sauce is boiling hard, the bottoms overcook before the tops set.
Melt the butter with a pinch more pul biber, spoon it over the eggs, then finish with herbs; add the herbs earlier and their brightness disappears.

note: Put the pan in the middle of the table with warm flatbreads and strong tea.

name: Sumac Roast Whole Mackerel with Tahini Herbs
hook: Crisp skin, lemon steam, silk tahini

steps.t: Heat the oven to 220°C fan and line a roasting tray with baking paper; a cool oven gives oily fish time to leak fat before the skin crisps.
Slash each mackerel three times on both sides to the bone, then rub with olive oil, sumac, cumin and salt; shallow slashes leave the seasoning sitting on the skin, not in the flesh.
Stuff the bellies with lemon slices, sliced garlic and a handful of herbs, but do not overfill them or the fish roast unevenly and gape open.
Roast until the skin is blistered and the flesh at the backbone turns opaque and lifts cleanly; if it still clings glassily to the bone, give it longer.
Whisk tahini with lemon juice, crushed garlic, pomegranate molasses, salt and enough cold water to make it pour like double cream; add the water slowly or the sauce will split into chalky clumps.
Rest the fish on the tray so the juices settle instead of flooding the platter; moving them straight away tears the hot skin.
Slide the whole fish onto a platter, spoon over tahini, scatter the remaining herbs and pine nuts, and serve at once while the skin still crackles.

note: Ask the fishmonger to gut the mackerel, but roast them whole for the theatre.

name: Tea-Smoked Tofu with Courgette Chermoula
hook: Cool ribbons, warm smoke, citrus bite

ingredients.name: firm tofu, pressed and sliced into 1 cm slabs

steps.t: Brush the tofu with soy sauce and leave it while you prepare everything else; if the surface is wet rather than tacky, the smoke will taste flat and the tofu will steam.
Line a wok or deep pan tightly with foil, add the tea, rice and sugar, then set a rack above it; gaps in the foil leave tarry smoke on the pan and make washing up miserable.
Put the tofu on the rack, cover with a tight lid or foil, and heat until wisps of smoke appear, then keep the heat steady; too much heat burns the sugar and turns the smoke acrid.
Turn off the heat and let the tofu sit covered so the smoke settles into the slabs; lifting the lid straight away wastes the perfume and fills the kitchen.
Whisk olive oil, lemon juice, cumin, smoked paprika, coriander and a pinch of salt into a loose chermoula; if it tastes dusty, it needs more lemon, not more oil.
Toss the courgette ribbons with half the chermoula just until glossy; salt them too early and they collapse into wet strands.
Slice the smoked tofu, plate it with the courgettes and orange, then spoon over the remaining chermoula; burying the tofu under salad hides the smoke you worked for.

note: Use a pan with good ventilation and keep the smoking time controlled for a clean, gentle smoke.

name: Sherry-Steamed Lamb Albóndigas with Almond Picada
hook: Tender lamb, nutty sauce, paprika steam

steps.t: Mix lamb, breadcrumbs, egg, half the garlic, paprika, cumin and salt with your fingertips until just combined; kneading it like dough makes the albóndigas bouncy instead of tender.
Roll into 20 small balls with lightly oiled hands; uneven sizes cook at different speeds, which is awkward on a tapas table.
Bring the sherry and stock to a simmer in a wide pan fitted with a steamer basket, keeping the liquid below the basket; if the meatballs sit in liquid, they poach rather than steam.
Arrange the lamb balls in one layer, cover tightly and steam until firm, juicy and cooked through with no pink centre; stack them and the lower ones squash before they set.

Meanwhile pound or blitz almonds, parsley, remaining garlic, vinegar, olive oil and a spoonful of the steaming liquor into a coarse picada; take it completely smooth and you lose the tapas-bar texture.
Lift the albóndigas to a warm dish, then boil the steaming liquor until it tastes rounded rather than boozy; leaving raw sherry sharpness will fight the lamb.
Spoon the reduced liquor over the meatballs and dot with almond picada; sauce them too early and the crustless steamed surface drinks up everything before serving.

note: Serve with cocktail sticks, olives and little glasses of cold fino.

name: Warm Vietnamese Pickled Egg Congee
hook: Sharp yolks over soft winter rice

steps.t: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then put it in a saucepan with the stock. If you skip the rinse, the congee turns gluey rather than softly creamy.

Bring to a lively simmer, then turn the heat low and cook with the lid slightly ajar, stirring often, until the grains burst and the spoon leaves a brief trail. If the base catches, it will taste dusty and scorched all the way through.
Meanwhile lower the eggs into boiling water and cook until the yolks are jammy, not chalky. Cool under running water and peel gently; cracked whites take up too much pickle and taste harsh.

Stir together the vinegar, fish sauce and sugar until dissolved. Halve the eggs and spoon over half the dressing; toss the carrot and cucumber in the rest. If the sugar sits undissolved, the pickle tastes sharp in patches.
Loosen the congee with a splash of hot water if it has tightened; it should slump from the ladle, not stand in a mound. Taste before salting because the stock and fish sauce do most of the work.
Bowl the congee while steaming, then add the pickled eggs, dressed vegetables, spring onions, crispy shallots and chilli oil. Keep the pickles on top so their snap is not swallowed by the heat.

note: A winter bowl with the brightness of đồ chua and the comfort of rice porridge.

name: Pork Salsiccia Breakfast Strata
hook: Golden bread, fennel pork, molten middle

steps.t: Heat the oven to 190°C. Oil a medium baking dish and scatter in the torn ciabatta; if the bread is sliced too neatly, it compacts instead of making crisp peaks.
Fry the sausage meat in the olive oil, breaking it into hazelnut-sized pieces, until the fat runs clear and the edges are bronze. Pale pork will leak into the custard and make the bake greasy.
Add the fennel and rosemary to the pan for a minute, just until the fennel smells sweet. Do not cook it soft now or it vanishes in the oven.
Whisk the eggs, milk, mascarpone and half the parmesan until mostly smooth; a few mascarpone flecks are fine, but unbroken egg white bakes into rubbery streaks.
Tip the sausage, fennel and tomatoes over the bread, then pour the custard evenly into the corners. Press the bread down once so it drinks, but leave some tips exposed for crunch.

Scatter over the remaining parmesan and bake until the centre has a gentle wobble and the top is deep gold with tomato juices bubbling at the edges. If you pull it while liquid ripples, the middle will collapse on serving.
Rest for 8 minutes before spooning out. Cutting straight away sends the custard flooding across the dish instead of setting around the pork.

note: Built for a slow morning: all the pleasure of a cooked breakfast in one bubbling dish.

name: Malabar Coconut-Braised Cod with Curry Leaves
hook: Silky fish in fragrant gold sauce

ingredients.name: thick cod loin, cut into 4 portions

steps.t: Salt the cod and leave it in the fridge while you start the sauce. This short cure firms the flakes; unsalted fish sheds water and thins the braise.
Warm the oil in a wide lidded pan and add the mustard seeds. When they pop like tiny knocks, add the curry leaves; if the oil is not hot enough, the spices taste flat rather than nutty.
Add the onions and cook until soft, sweet and tea-gold at the edges. Rush this and the sauce will taste raw no matter how much coconut you add.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, turmeric and chilli for a minute until the paste stains the onions bright ochre. Let it catch hard and the turmeric turns bitter.
Pour in the coconut milk with 150 ml water and simmer gently until glossy and lightly thickened. It should blip, not boil hard, or the coconut can split and look grainy.
Nestle in the cod, spoon sauce over the tops, cover and braise on the lowest heat until the fish flakes in thick petals when nudged. Vigorous boiling breaks the loins into crumbs.
Lift the fish to a warm platter, sharpen the sauce with lime juice, then spoon it over. Add the lime off the heat so the sauce stays smooth and perfumed.

note: Serve with lemon rice or appams for a guest-worthy centrepiece without last-minute panic.

name: Summer Het Tom Mushroom Stew
hook: Lemongrass broth, mushrooms, clean heat

steps.t: Bring the stock to a simmer with the lemongrass, lime leaves and galangal. Keep it covered so the citrus oils stay in the pot, not in the kitchen air.
Add the mushrooms and simmer until they relax and darken but still have bounce. A rolling boil makes them squeaky and pushes their aroma out of the broth.
Add the baby corn, tomato, soy sauce, palm sugar and chilli. The tomato should slump at the edges but not dissolve, or the broth turns muddy.
Taste the broth before adding lime; it should be savoury and lightly sweet because sourness will sharpen everything. If it is weak now, lime will only make it thin and tart.
Turn off the heat, stir in the lime juice and rest for a minute. Boiling lime juice dulls its perfume and leaves only acidity.
Ladle into shallow bowls, leaving the galangal, lemongrass and lime leaves behind if you like, then finish with coriander. Serve hot but not scalding so the herbs taste green.

note: Inspired by tom het: broth-forward, bright and intentionally light.

name: Miso Roast Beef Tataki Platter
hook: Rosy beef, salty crust, sharp dips

ingredients.name: whole beef fillet tail or small sirloin centre-cut

steps.t: Take the beef out of the fridge 30 minutes before cooking and pat it completely dry. Wet beef steams before it roasts, so the miso crust slides instead of searing.
Heat the oven to 220°C. Mix the miso, soy, mirin, sesame oil, garlic and half the ginger into a smooth paste; lumps of miso scorch into salty spots.
Rub the beef with neutral oil, then smear the miso paste thinly all over. Keep the layer even because thick patches burn before the centre warms.

Roast on a rack until the outside is dark lacquered and the centre reaches 50–52°C for rare, or 55°C for medium-rare. Guessing by colour alone is risky with a whole joint; use a probe if you have one.
Rest the beef uncovered until the juices settle and the surface stops sizzling. Foil traps steam and softens the crust you worked to build.
Slice thinly across the grain with a sharp knife. If the slices look stringy, turn the beef and cut the other way so each piece eats tender.
Arrange on a shared platter with spring onions, sesame seeds, remaining ginger and lemon wedges. Add the lemon at the table so the beef stays glossy, not grey at the edges.

note: A roast handled like tataki: whole, rosy, sliceable and made for passing round.

name: Thai Basil Halloumi Wok Crackle
hook: Hot wok basil, squeaky golden cheese

ingredients.name: green beans, cut into short lengths

steps.t: Pat the halloumi very dry before it goes near the wok; wet cubes spit, steam and turn rubbery instead of taking on little bronze blisters.
Mix oyster sauce, soy, lime juice and sugar in a cup. Have it beside the hob, because once the wok is hot you will not have time to hunt for bottles.
Heat the wok until a drop of water skips across it, then add the oil and halloumi. Stir-fry until the corners are golden and the cheese squeaks against the spoon; a lukewarm wok makes it leak brine.
Lift the halloumi to a plate, leaving the oil behind. Add garlic and chilli for a few seconds only, until sharp and fragrant; if the garlic goes chestnut brown here, the whole dish will taste bitter.
Throw in beans and pepper and toss hard over the highest heat until the beans turn glossy and bright with tiny scorched spots. If they slump and puddle, your pan is crowded or not hot enough.

Return the halloumi, pour in the sauce and toss until it clings in a shiny coat rather than pooling at the bottom. Fold through the basil off the heat so it wilts green, not black, and serve with hot jasmine rice.

note: Halloumi brings the salt, so taste before adding any extra soy.

name: Miso-Koji Pork Okonomiyaki Stack
hook: Smoky griddle pork under lacquered sauce

steps.t: Rub the pork belly with shio koji and half the miso, then chill it in a shallow dish. Do not leave thick clumps of miso on the meat; they scorch before the fat has rendered.
Whisk the flour with the cold dashi and remaining miso until just smooth, then rest it. If you beat it like pancake batter, the finished okonomiyaki turns bready instead of tender.
Fold eggs, cabbage, spring onions and pickled ginger into the rested batter just before cooking. The cabbage should look lightly dressed, not drowned; a soupy bowl will spread and refuse to flip.
Heat a flat griddle or heavy frying pan to medium and oil it lightly. Lay on a quarter of the pork in overlapping strips until the fat starts to go translucent and the edges curl.
Spoon a quarter of the cabbage batter over the pork and nudge it into a thick round. Keep the heat moderate; too fierce and the pork blackens while the cabbage stays raw in the middle.
Flip with two spatulas when the underside feels set and releases in one piece. Cook the second side until the centre springs back rather than squelching under the spatula.
Repeat with the remaining portions, wiping away burnt miso flecks between rounds. Those little black bits taste harsh if you drag them into the next pancake.
Brush each stack with okonomiyaki sauce and stripe with mayonnaise while hot, so the sauces gloss and settle into the ridges. Serve straight from the griddle before the crisp pork softens.

note: Make four smaller okonomiyaki rather than one heroic slab; they cook through cleanly and flip without drama.

name: Crisp Kimchi Egg-Tofu Jeon
hook: Frilly-edged eggs with kimchi heat

steps.t: Wrap the tofu in kitchen paper and press until it feels damp rather than dripping. Watery tofu thins the egg mix and stops the jeon forming crisp edges.
Beat the eggs with potato starch, gochugaru and 1 tablespoon soy sauce until no white starch pockets remain. Those dry pockets fry into chalky lumps.
Crumble in the tofu, kimchi and spring onions. Stir firmly but stop before the tofu disappears; small curds give the pancakes bite and protein-rich heft.
Heat half the oil in a wide frying pan over medium-high heat until it shimmers, then spoon in small pancakes. Leave space between them, because touching edges steam instead of frilling.
Fry until the rims turn lace-brown and the top looks mostly set, then flip once. If you flip while the centre is still loose, the egg tears and drinks oil.
Cook the second side until crisp freckles show and the middle no longer wobbles. Eggs should be fully set, not glossy, for a gym-box meal that travels safely.
Toss the spinach in the hot pan with the remaining soy sauce just until it slumps and shines; cook it longer and it throws out water onto the crisp jeon. Finish with sesame seeds.

note: For meal prep, cool the jeon on a rack before boxing so the undersides stay crisp.

name: Hong Kong Ginger Milk Steamed Egg Custards
hook: Soft ginger silk, barely set

steps.t: Warm the milk with rock sugar and ginger until the sugar dissolves and the milk smells gently spicy. Do not boil it hard, or the ginger turns harsh and the milk skins over.
Take the pan off the heat, add mandarin zest and let the milk stand until warm, not hot. Hot milk scrambles the eggs on contact.
Beat the eggs lightly in a jug, then strain in the ginger milk and stir without frothing. Bubbles leave pockmarks, so keep the whisk below the surface.
Strain the custard into four small bowls and skim off any foam. Cover each bowl tightly with foil; uncovered custards catch drips and turn watery on top.
Set the bowls in a steamer over the gentlest steady steam, not a furious boil. Steam until the edges are set and the centres tremble like soft jelly.
Rest the custards off the heat before uncovering, so the set finishes softly instead of cracking from a rush of steam. Sprinkle with black sesame and serve warm.

note: If your steamer runs hot, prop the lid slightly open with a chopstick to keep the texture silken.

name: Veracruz Hake, Bean and Rice Bake
hook: Tomato rice, flaky fish, student-proof

ingredients.name: frozen hake fillets, thawed and patted dry

steps.t: Heat the oven to 200°C fan and choose a deep baking dish that can be covered tightly. A shallow tray dries the rice before the grains soften.

Stir rice, tomatoes, black beans, sweetcorn, onion, garlic, chipotle, cumin and the crumbled stock cube in the dish with 350 ml boiling water. The liquid should just cover the rice; dry corners stay hard.
Cover tightly with foil, crimping the edges so steam cannot escape. Bake until the rice has swollen and there is still a little tomato liquid visible between the grains.
Stir the rice from the edges into the centre, then lay the patted-dry hake on top and spoon a little tomato rice over each fillet. Wet fish waters down the bake, so blot it properly first.
Cover again and bake until the fish turns opaque and flakes when pressed with a fork. If the centre still looks glassy, it needs longer.
Uncover for the last few minutes so the top loses its wet look and the tomato edges darken slightly. Do not blast it until crusty, or the hake will go cottony.
Squeeze over lime and scatter coriander at the table. Taste the rice before salting; the stock cube and chipotle usually do enough.

note: Thaw the hake overnight in the fridge, or in a sealed bag under cold running water if you forgot.

name: Gochujang Crisp Mackerel with Sesame Cucumber
hook: Hot lacquered fish, cold crunch

steps.t: Pat the mackerel very dry, especially the skin side; damp fish spits hard in the pan and the coating slides off instead of crisping.
Dust the fillets all over with cornflour and shake off the excess; clumps scorch before the fish cooks and taste chalky.
Mix gochujang, soy, vinegar, honey and sesame oil in a bowl until glossy; if it looks split, keep stirring or it will hit the fish in salty patches.
Heat the neutral oil in a frying pan until a pinch of cornflour fizzes at once, then lay in the mackerel skin-side down; crowding the pan steams the skin, so cook in two goes if needed.
Fry until the skin is crackly and the edges turn deep bronze, then turn once and cook the flesh side just until opaque; flipping early tears the skin away.
Lift the fish out, pour off all but a slick of oil, then bubble the sauce for a few seconds until it darkens and coats the spoon; over-reduce it and the chilli paste turns bitter.
Brush the sauce over the crisp fish and serve with cucumber and spring onions; saucing too early softens the crust you worked for.

note: Serve with microwave rice if you want this to land fully as a weeknight dinner.

name: Eight-Treasure Steamed Tofu Parcels
hook: Silken tofu, deep savoury treasure

steps.t: Cover the dried shiitakes with hot water and soak until floppy right through; if the centres stay leathery, they will never steam tender inside the parcels.
Drain the tofu, wrap it in a clean tea towel and weight it gently; press too hard and it cracks, press too little and the filling turns watery.
Finely dice the soaked mushrooms, bamboo shoots, carrot and water chestnuts, keeping everything pea-sized or smaller; big chunks split the tofu when you fold it.
Mash 200 g of the tofu with soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, ginger, cornflour and sesame oil, then fold in the diced vegetables; the mixture should hold together softly, not slump like soup.
Cut the remaining tofu into thick squares, hollow each one slightly with a teaspoon and mound in the filling; scrape too close to the base and steam will burst the parcel open.
Set the parcels on a heatproof plate, pour stock around not over them, and steam over a steady simmer until the tops look set and glossy; a raging boil rattles the tofu into rubble.
Spoon the savoury steaming juices back over the parcels and rest for a minute before lifting; moving them immediately is when they collapse.

note: A slow, careful dim-sum-style project with simple supermarket ingredients.

name: Coal-Grilled Adobo Lamb with Lime Beans
hook: Smoke, char, lean strength

steps.t: Stir chipotle paste, cumin, oregano, lime zest, half the lime juice, olive oil and salt into a thick adobo; if it is runny, it drips into the coals instead of clinging to the lamb.
Coat the lamb steaks and leave them while the barbecue comes ready; grilling fridge-cold lamb gives you burnt edges before the centre warms.
Light the coals and wait until they are ashed over with no tall flames; flames lick the marinade black and bitter before the meat cooks.
Grill the lamb over the hottest part until dark char freckles appear, then turn once and cook to 63°C in the thickest part; constant flipping stops a proper crust forming.
Move the lamb to a board and rest it so the juices settle; slice straight away and the protein you paid for runs across the board.
Toss black beans with tomatoes, coriander, red onion and the remaining lime juice; season after mixing, because beans hide salt until they sit for a moment.
Slice the lamb across the grain and pile it beside the beans; cutting with the grain makes even lean lamb chew like rope.

note: Around 50 g protein per serving, depending on the lamb cut.

name: Masticha Steamed Egg Custard with Honey Figs
hook: Quivering custard, pine-sweet honey

steps.t: Warm the milk with lemon peel, salt and crushed masticha until steaming but not boiling; if it boils, the masticha turns medicinal and the milk tastes cooked.
Whisk eggs with 50 g honey and caster sugar just until smooth, not foamy; foam becomes pockmarks on the custard surface.
Pour the warm milk into the eggs in a thin stream while whisking, then strain into four small bowls; skip straining and you will get white egg threads in the set custard.
Cover each bowl tightly with foil and set in a steamer over the gentlest simmer; uncovered bowls drip with condensation and turn watery on top.
Steam until the custards wobble like soft jelly at the centre, not liquid underneath; hard boiling makes them split into sweet scrambled egg.
Rest the bowls off the heat, still covered, so the carry-over heat finishes the centre; uncovering at once lets the tops wrinkle and dry.
Spoon over figs, walnuts and the remaining honey just before serving; add them earlier and the fruit bleeds syrup into the custard.

note: Serve warm or chilled; both suit the floral masticha.

name: Tavuk Saç Kavurma with Pepper Rice
hook: Fast smoky chicken, buttery peppers

steps.t: Slice the chicken thinly and pat it dry; wet strips dump liquid into the pan and you get boiled chicken instead of kavurma edges.
Heat the widest frying pan you have until the oil shimmers, then add the chicken in one loose layer; if it piles up, cook it in batches or it will stew.
Stir-fry until the chicken loses its raw shine and catches golden at the tips; stop while it is pale and the final dish tastes flat.
Add onion and green pepper, tossing hard over high heat until the pepper skins blister in spots; gentle heat makes them soft and sweet without smoke.
Stir in garlic, tomato paste, pul biber, cumin and salt, scraping until the paste stains the oil brick-red; if the paste stays in lumps, every bite tastes different.
Fold in cooked rice and butter, pressing the rice briefly against the hot pan so it picks up chicken fat and pepper char; cold clods left unbroken stay bland inside.
Serve as soon as the rice is hot and glossy; leaving it in the pan dries the chicken and glues the rice to the bottom.

note: Best with leftover rice, which fries cleanly instead of turning mushy.

name: Riviera Coal-Socca with Mustardy Lentils
hook: Smoky chickpea edges, sharp green lentils

steps.t: Light a small chimney of charcoal and tip it into one tight, even bed; cooking over tall flames scorches the socca before the middle sets.
Whisk chickpea flour, water, 2 tbsp olive oil and 1/2 tsp salt until it pours like single cream; dry pockets of flour turn into bitter little pellets on the grill.
Toss lentils, tomatoes, garlic, mustard, lemon juice, parsley and 1 tbsp olive oil; if you dress them late, the lentils taste flat instead of soaking up the sharpness.
Set a 26 cm cast-iron pan over the coals until a drop of batter hisses on contact; a lukewarm pan gives you a rubbery pancake, not lace-brown edges.
Oil the pan with the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, pour in the batter and close the grill lid until the top is set and the rim is crisp and nutty-smelling.
Slide the socca onto a board, spoon over the mustardy lentils and finish with lemon zest; leaving it in the pan makes the crisp underside steam soft.

note: Best cooked in a heavy pan directly over hot coals, not over a weak barbecue flame.

name: Chesapeake Oyster Icebox with Bloody Mary Granita
hook: Briny oysters, peppered tomato snow

steps.t: Buy oysters from a reputable fishmonger, keep them cupped-side down on ice and discard any that are cracked, open and not closing, or smell muddy; raw shellfish gives no second chances.
Stir tomato juice, vodka, horseradish, Worcestershire, 1 tbsp lemon juice and celery salt, then pour into a shallow metal tray; a deep bowl freezes solid at the edges and slushy in the middle.
Freeze the tray, scrape every hour with a fork until it becomes dry red crystals; if you leave it untouched, you get a hard block instead of granita.
Mix shallot, cider vinegar and remaining lemon juice, then chill; chunky shallot or warm vinegar bullies the oyster liquor.
Scrub the oyster shells under cold running water and set up a folded towel, oyster knife and iced tray; a slipping shell is how hands get cut.
Shuck each oyster flat-side up, cutting the top muscle and keeping the liquor in the cupped shell; tipping the shell away throws out the clean sea flavour you paid for.
Nestle oysters into crushed ice, spoon on a little granita and serve mignonette and saltines alongside; topping them too early melts the granita into tomato water.

note: Serve raw oysters only to guests comfortable eating raw shellfish; keep them cold throughout.

name: Rosario Chimichurri Prawn Wok
hook: Seared prawns, green herb bite

steps.t: Pat the prawns very dry and season them; wet prawns dump water into the wok and turn from seared to squeaky.
Stir parsley, oregano, vinegar, 1 tbsp olive oil, chilli flakes and half the garlic into a rough chimichurri; blending it smooth makes it taste grassy and dull.
Heat a wok or wide frying pan until the first wisp of smoke appears, then add the remaining oil; if the pan is merely warm, the vegetables stew.
Stir-fry pepper and onion hard until the onion edges char and the pepper still snaps; soft peppers make the whole bowl feel canteen-sad.
Add prawns and remaining garlic, tossing constantly until the prawns curl into loose C-shapes and turn opaque; tight rings mean they have gone rubbery.
Fold in the white beans just until hot and glossy, then pull the pan off the heat; overworking them splits the skins and muddies the sauce.
Spoon over the chimichurri and squeeze lemon at the table; cooking the herbs in the wok kills the bright Argentine bite.

note: High protein without heaviness: prawns and beans carry the meal, oil stays measured.

name: Steamed Lime Quindim Cups
hook: Glossy yolk custard, coconut chew

ingredients.name: unsalted butter, melted, plus extra for moulds

steps.t: Butter six small ramekins heavily and dust the bases with a little of the sugar; a bare patch grabs the custard and tears the glossy top.
Soak the coconut in coconut milk, lime zest and salt until it looks plump rather than dusty; dry coconut floats up in hard clumps.
Pass the yolks and whole egg through a sieve into a bowl, scraping gently; forcing the membrane through leaves chewy yellow threads.
Stir in the remaining sugar, melted butter and soaked coconut without whisking foam into it; bubbles make the quindim pitted instead of glassy.
Divide between ramekins, cover each with foil and set in a steamer over a gentle simmer; a rolling boil rattles the cups and curdles the edges.
Steam until the centres wobble like set jelly and a knife comes out clean near the rim; taking them off while liquid means they slump when turned out.
Cool for 15 minutes, loosen the sides and unmould while just warm; fully cold butter sets hard and glues the custard in place.

note: Quindim is sweet by design, so serve small and cold or just warm.

name: Lahori Pork Keema Aloo Tikkis
hook: Crisp potato shells, hot spiced pork

steps.t: Boil the potatoes in salted water until a knife slides through with no crunch; undercooked centres leave hard flecks that split the tikkis.
Drain, steam-dry in the hot pan, then mash until fluffy; wet mash drinks oil and turns greasy before it crisps.
Fry onion in 1 tbsp oil until the edges are golden, then add ginger-garlic paste, chilli and spices; adding spices to a dry pan makes them dusty and bitter.
Add pork mince and cook, breaking it small, until no pink remains and the pan smells roasted rather than raw; pale clumps leak fat into the potato.
Mix the spiced pork into the mash, cool until handleable, then shape six squat patties; shaping while hot makes them crack at the edges.
Dust each patty in flour, dip lightly in egg and shake off drips; a thick egg coat blisters away from the potato instead of sealing it.
Shallow fry in the remaining oil over medium-high heat until both sides are deep amber and crisp; too low a heat makes oily tikkis, too high burns the flour before the middle is hot.
Drain on a rack and serve with cold yoghurt; stacking them on kitchen paper traps steam and softens the crust.

note: Pakistani street-snack spicing, using inexpensive pork mince for the brief.

name: Sumac Prawn Freekeh Skillet
hook: Smoky prawns over buttery green wheat

ingredients.name: raw king prawns, peeled and deveined

steps.t: Rinse the freekeh until the water runs less dusty, then put it in a small pan with the stock. If you skip the rinse, the grains cook up muddy rather than nutty.
Simmer uncovered until the grains are tender with a little bite and the liquid has mostly tucked itself in; stir near the end so the bottom does not catch and taste scorched.
Pat the prawns very dry, then toss with olive oil, cumin, 1 tsp sumac, garlic and a pinch of salt. Wet prawns steam on the griddle instead of taking on char.
Heat a ridged griddle or heavy frying pan until a drop of water jumps away at once. Lay the prawns down with space between them; crowding drops the heat and makes them rubbery.
Cook the prawns until the undersides show dark griddle bars and the flesh has turned opaque halfway up, then turn once and cook just until curled and pearly all through.
Beat the butter through the hot freekeh until glossy, then fold in lemon juice to taste. Too much lemon before the butter will make it taste sharp rather than round.
Spoon the freekeh into warm bowls, add yoghurt, prawns, pine nuts, parsley and the remaining sumac. Serve at once, because prawns toughen as they sit on hot grain.

note: A wintery Levantine bowl built on smoke, sour sumac and warm grains.

name: Crisp Harissa Egg Msemen
hook: Flaky edges, molten yolk, red heat

steps.t: Stir the harissa, cumin and drained tomatoes together. If the tomatoes are watery, the msemen will soak and fry leathery instead of crisp.
Warm 2 tbsp oil in a frying pan over medium heat, then lay in one msemen. It should sizzle gently; if it roars, the outside burns before the centre warms.
Spread half the harissa tomato over the middle, leaving a crisp border, then crack in an egg. Keep the yolk centred or it runs to the edge and overcooks.
Shallow fry until the underside is deeply golden and the white is mostly set at the edges. Spoon hot oil over the white, not the yolk, so it firms without turning chalky.
Scatter over half the feta, fold two corners loosely towards the middle if the bread allows, and lift out when the edges sound scratchy against the spatula.
Repeat with the second msemen, adding the remaining oil if the pan looks dry; dry frying gives pale, tough patches rather than blistered layers.
Finish with honey, coriander and a squeeze of lemon. Eat immediately, while the underside still shatters and the yolk is runny.

note: Use msemen from a Moroccan bakery if you can; good frozen ones work well.

name: Sherry-Pickled Pork Tonnato
hook: Silky pork, bright vinegar, briny cream

steps.t: Trim the pork fillet of silver skin; leave it on and the slices curl with a chewy strip down one side.
Bring the sherry, vinegar, bay, paprika, orange zest, half the orange juice and a pinch of salt to a simmer in a narrow pan. If the pan is too wide, the pork will sit half-exposed and cook unevenly.
Lower in the pork, cover and poach at a lazy tremble until the centre reaches 63°C. Boiling makes the outside tight before the middle is ready.
Lift the pork into a shallow dish, pour over the hot pickling liquor and rest until barely warm, turning once. Cutting now spills the juices instead of keeping the meat silky.
Blend mayonnaise, anchovies, capers, remaining orange juice and olive oil into a smooth dressing. If it tastes flat, add a spoon of the pickling liquor rather than more salt.
Slice the pork thinly across the grain. Thick slices eat like roast meat; thin ones take the vinegar and dressing properly.
Lay rocket on a platter, drape over the pork, spoon on the anchovy dressing and scatter extra capers. Dress at the last minute or the leaves collapse under the warm acidity.

note: A Spanish-leaning party plate inspired by escabeche and tonnato.

name: Courgette Goat’s Cheese Clafoutis
hook: Custardy, green, barely golden edges

steps.t: Heat the oven to 190°C. Oil a shallow baking dish; a deep dish gives a pale, wet middle before the top colours.
Toss courgette slices with olive oil and salt, then spread them in the dish. If they are piled thickly, they steam and water down the custard.
Bake the courgettes until they look glossy and just softened at the edges, not browned to crisps.
Whisk eggs, milk, flour, mustard, lemon zest and a pinch of salt until smooth. Lumps of flour bake into little paste pockets, so scrape the bowl well.
Stir in chives and basil, then pour the batter around the courgettes. Do not pour from a height or the vegetables float to one end.
Dot with goat’s cheese and bake until the centre has a gentle wobble and the rim is puffed with light gold freckles. If it is firm all over, it has gone rubbery.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving warm or room temperature; slice too soon and the custard slumps rather than setting cleanly.

note: Serve with dressed leaves and cold white wine for a light plate.

name: Bourbon-Braised Carrots with White Cheddar Grits
