hook: Sweet smoke over creamy corn

ingredients.name: small carrots, scrubbed and halved lengthways

steps.t: Heat the oil in a wide sauté pan and put the carrots cut-side down. Let them take a chestnut-brown line; if you keep moving them, they taste boiled later.
Add the onion and cook until it softens and catches amber at the tips. Pale onion will not give the braise enough backbone.
Pour in the bourbon off the heat, then return the pan and simmer until the raw alcohol smell fades. Adding it over a flame is unsafe, and leaving it raw tastes harsh.
Add stock, maple syrup, smoked paprika and salt. Cover and braise at a low bubble until a knife slides into the thick end of a carrot with only slight resistance.
Uncover and reduce the liquor until it coats the carrots like shiny syrup. Stop before the pan looks dry, or the maple catches and turns bitter.
Meanwhile, simmer milk with 300 ml water and a pinch of salt, then whisk in the grits in a steady rain. Dump them in at once and they clump no matter how hard you stir.
Cook the grits, stirring often, until they lose their gritty bite and fall in slow ribbons from the spoon.
Beat in cheddar and butter, spoon onto a warm platter, then pile the carrots and onion on top with chopped jalapeños. Serve straight away, before the grits tighten.

note: Vegetable-led, generous and built for passing round the table.

name: Lahori Crisp Masala Chicken
hook: Craggy edges, lime, chilli heat

ingredients.name: boneless chicken thigh fillets, cut into 3 cm pieces

steps.t: Stir yoghurt, ginger-garlic paste, chilli, cumin, coriander, garam masala and 1 tsp salt in a bowl until brick-red; if the spices sit in dry clumps they will scorch on the chicken.
Add the chicken and turn every piece through the marinade, then leave it while the pan heats; skipping this short rest gives you pale patches instead of a proper masala crust.
Sprinkle over the gram flour and toss until the chicken looks shaggy and barely damp, not pasty; too much loose flour will fall off and burn in the oil.
Heat the oil in a wide frying pan over medium-high heat until a pinch of batter fizzes at once; if the oil is quiet, the coating drinks grease before it crisps.
Lay in the chicken with space between pieces and fry until the undersides are deep orange with dark crisp freckles; crowding the pan steams the coating soft.
Turn and fry the second side until the pieces feel firm and the coating is craggy, then check the thickest piece is piping hot through; undercooked thigh will still look glossy inside.
Drain on kitchen paper for one minute, then squeeze over lime just before eating; lime too early softens the crisp edges.

note: Use thigh rather than breast for a juicier weeknight fry.

name: Saigon Pickled Prawn Glass Noodle Salad
hook: Cool prawns, sharp herbs, glossy dressing

steps.t: Toss carrot and daikon with 1 tsp salt, scrunch until they squeak and start to weep, then rest; if you skip the salting, the pickle turns watery and bland later.
Rinse the vegetables briefly and squeeze hard until they feel springy, not wet; excess brine will flatten the dressing.
Warm the vinegar with sugar and 60 ml water just until dissolved, pour over the vegetables and chill until bendy and bright; boiling the pickle drives off its clean sharpness.
Poach the prawns in gently simmering salted water until they curl and turn opaque, then lift them straight into iced water; a rolling boil makes them rubbery before the centres cook.
Peel and devein the prawns once cold, keeping them whole; leaving grit in the back seam spoils the clean sweet bite.
Soak the glass noodles in boiling water until clear and supple, then drain and rinse cold; if they stay hot they clump into a sticky mat.
Mix fish sauce, lime juice, chilli and 2 tbsp of the pickle liquid, then taste for salty-sour balance before dressing; if it tastes harsh alone, it will taste harsher on the noodles.
Tumble noodles, pickles, prawns and herbs with the dressing, finish with peanuts, and serve cool; dressing too early makes the herbs blacken and collapse.

note: Most of the time is hands-off pickling, so it suits a long weekend prep session.

name: Sicilian Halloumi Lentil Traybake
hook: Salty slabs, tomatoes, gym-friendly heft

steps.t: Heat the oven to 220°C fan and put a large baking dish in to warm; starting in a cold dish makes the tomatoes stew instead of blister.
In the hot dish, stir lentils, tomatoes, onion, olive oil, tomato purée, oregano, chilli flakes and 100 ml water until the purée has disappeared; streaks of purée catch and taste metallic.
Bake until the tomatoes split and the onion tips char at the edges, giving the dish a saucy base rather than a watery one.
Stir in the spinach until just wilted and glossy; leaving it piled on top dries the leaves into papery flakes.
Lay the halloumi slabs over the lentils, leaving small gaps for steam to escape; a sealed blanket of cheese traps moisture and stops browning.
Bake again until the halloumi is swollen with bronze patches and the lentils bubble thickly around it; pull it too soon and the cheese tastes squeaky and raw-edged.
Finish with lemon zest, lemon juice and torn basil while hot; adding basil before baking turns its fragrance dull and cabbagey.

note: High protein from halloumi and lentils, with everything cooked in one baking dish.

name: Saffron Steamed Egg Mishti Cups
hook: Silky custard, cardamom, saffron warmth

steps.t: Rub four small heatproof cups with a thin film of ghee; thick smears melt into greasy pools on the custard surface.
Warm the milk with saffron until steaming and golden at the edges, then take it off the heat; boiling milk can scramble the eggs when mixed.
Whisk eggs, condensed milk, sugar and cardamom only until smooth, not foamy; too much froth leaves little pockmarks after steaming.
Pour the warm milk slowly into the eggs while whisking, then strain into a jug; unstrained chalazae and spice clumps break the silkiness.
Divide between cups and cover each tightly with foil, crimping the edges; loose covers let drips fall in and crater the tops.
Steam over a low, steady simmer until the custards tremble as one piece when nudged; fierce steam makes them bubble and turn grainy.
Rest covered for 10 minutes, then chill or serve barely warm with pistachios; unmoulding straight away tears the soft sides.

note: A gentle steamed dessert, closer to mishti doi softness than baked flan.

name: Bangkok Tomato Egg Stew
hook: Jammy eggs in sour-sweet broth

ingredients.name: green beans, cut into short lengths

steps.t: Boil the eggs, then cool under running water until you can handle them; peeling hot eggs tears the whites and they break up in the stew.
Peel the eggs and halve them lengthways with a wet knife; a dry blade drags the yolk into ragged crumbs.
Heat the oil in a saucepan and fry the garlic and curry paste until the oil stains orange and smells roasted; if the paste stays raw, the stew tastes dusty.
Add tomatoes, water, fish sauce and sugar, scraping the base so no paste burns underneath; burnt curry paste turns bitter fast.
Simmer until the tomatoes darken and the broth thickens enough to coat a spoon lightly; if it is still watery, the eggs will taste separate from the stew.
Add green beans and simmer until bright green with a slight snap; overcooked beans go khaki and squeak rather than crunch.
Nestle in the egg halves, spoon broth over them and warm gently without stirring hard; rough boiling knocks the yolks out into the sauce.
Turn off the heat and add lime juice and coriander; boiling lime makes the stew taste flat instead of sharp.

note: Cheap, filling and built from store-cupboard tins plus eggs.

name: Saffron Malai Paneer with Charred Clementines
hook: Creamy saffron warmth, paneer kept cloud-soft

ingredients.name: clementines, peeled and sliced into thick rounds

steps.t: Warm the cream just until it steams at the edge, then stir in the saffron and salt. Do not boil it, or the cream tastes cooked and the saffron turns flat rather than honeyed.
Whisk the yoghurt into the saffron cream until smooth, then fold in the paneer gently. If you beat it hard, the paneer breaks and the dish loses its soft, generous cubes.
Heat a dry frying pan until a clementine slice hisses on contact, then sear the rounds on one side until the cut faces show dark freckles. Move them before they collapse and leak juice everywhere.

Melt the ghee in a small pan and add the ginger, garam masala and chilli powder. Let it foam until the ginger smells warm and nutty; if the spices go mahogany, they have burnt and will make the cream bitter.
Pour the hot spiced ghee over the paneer and fold only twice or three times. The aim is barely warmed paneer, not simmered paneer, so stop before the cubes tighten and squeak.
Spoon into a shallow bowl, tuck in the charred clementines, and scatter over almonds and coriander. Serve at once, while the cream is warm and the paneer still tastes milky.

note: Best with hot naan or saffron rice; the paneer should never reach a simmer.

name: Holy Basil Breakfast Mushrooms with Crispy Egg Rice
hook: Smoky mushrooms, runny yolks, lime bite

ingredients.name: mixed mushrooms, torn into large pieces

steps.t: Break the cold rice up with your fingers before the wok goes on. If it goes in as a brick, it steams instead of catching into crisp little edges.
Mix the fish sauce, soy and sugar in a small bowl so the seasoning is ready. High-heat stir-frying gives you no time to hunt for bottles without scorching the garlic.
Heat a wok until a drop of water skitters away, then add 1 tablespoon oil and the mushrooms. Spread them out and leave them until their edges blister and the wet smell turns roasted.
Add the garlic and chillies and toss hard for a few seconds, just until the garlic smells sweet. If it browns before the sauce goes in, it will taste harsh at breakfast.
Splash in the sauce and keep tossing until the mushrooms are glossy and almost dry. Fold through the Thai basil off the heat so it wilts green, not black.
In a separate hot frying pan, add the remaining oil, press in the rice and fry until the underside is crisp and pale gold. Do not stir constantly, or you will never get the breakfast crunch.
Fry the eggs until the whites are set and frilly but the yolks still wobble. Serve the mushrooms over the crispy rice with the eggs and lime wedges.

note: Use the widest pan you own if you do not have a wok; crowding makes mushrooms watery.

name: Miso-Maple Tsukune Skewers with Sesame Tare
hook: Glossy skewers with charcoal-bar sweetness

steps.t: Soak 8 bamboo skewers in water if using them, otherwise they scorch before the chicken cooks. Metal skewers can go straight in.

Mix the chicken, spring onions, ginger, miso, panko and egg with clean hands until the mixture turns sticky and clings to the bowl. Stop there; overworking makes the skewers bouncy rather than tender.

Shape the mixture into 8 long ovals around the skewers, wetting your hands lightly so the chicken smooths instead of smearing. Keep them even in thickness or the tips will dry before the centres are safe.
Simmer the soy sauce, mirin and maple syrup in a small pan until it looks syrupy and coats the back of a spoon. If it reduces to tar, loosen it with a splash of water before glazing.
Heat a ridged griddle pan until it is properly hot, then oil it lightly and lay on the skewers. Cook until deep grill lines appear and the meat releases without tearing.
Turn the skewers and continue griddling, brushing with tare only once the outside has set. Sugary glaze added too early burns before the chicken reaches 75°C in the centre.
Brush once more off the heat, sprinkle with sesame seeds and rest for 3 minutes. Cutting immediately lets the juices run out and dulls the glossy finish.

note: A probe thermometer is the neatest way to keep the chicken juicy and safely cooked.

name: Sesame-Crisp Prawns with Pear Muchim
hook: Crackly prawns, cold crunch, clean heat

steps.t: Pat the prawns very dry with kitchen paper and season with half the salt. If they go into the starch damp, the coating turns paste-like and slides off in the oil.
Toss the cucumber and pear with rice vinegar, gochugaru, sesame oil, spring onions and the remaining salt. Chill it while you fry, so the salad stays snappy against the hot prawns.
Whisk the egg white until loose and foamy, then coat the prawns lightly. You want a thin tacky film, not a thick batter that hides the shellfish.
Mix the potato starch and sesame seeds, then press the prawns through it and shake off the excess. Loose starch burns in the pan and makes the oil taste dusty.
Heat the oil in a wide frying pan until a pinch of starch fizzes immediately. Add the prawns in one layer; crowding drops the heat and gives you limp, steamed prawns.
Shallow fry until the coating is pale gold and the prawns are opaque with a tight C-shape, turning once. If they curl into hard little O-shapes, they have gone too far.
Drain on a rack, not kitchen paper, so the undersides stay crisp. Plate with the chilled pear muchim and eat while the sesame crust still crackles.

note: Use raw prawns, not pre-cooked ones; pre-cooked prawns toughen before the crust crisps.

name: Sichuan Pickled Halloumi with Celery and Chilli Oil
hook: Salty squeak, numbing chilli, sharp vinegar

ingredients.name: celery sticks, thinly sliced on the diagonal
cucumber, deseeded and cut into batons
fresh ginger, cut into fine matchsticks

steps.t: Rinse the halloumi batons briefly under cold water, then pat them completely dry. Skip this and the finished plate can taste more salty than pickled.
Whisk the black vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, Sichuan pepper, chilli oil, sesame oil and ginger until the sugar dissolves. Undissolved sugar leaves gritty sweet spots rather than a clean dressing.
Fold the halloumi through half the dressing and leave it to pickle until the edges taste sharp but the centre still squeaks. Much longer makes the cheese rubbery and overly sour.
Toss the celery and cucumber with the remaining dressing just before serving. Dress them too early and they slump, losing the cold crunch that makes the plate work.
Lift the halloumi from its marinade with a slotted spoon and mix gently with the dressed vegetables. Pouring in every drop makes the shared plate soupy.
Scatter with peanuts and shredded spring onions, spoon over a little extra chilli sediment, and serve cool. The contrast should be crisp, sharp and numbing, not fridge-cold and muted.

note: This is a liangban-style cold plate; no cooking is needed, just careful salting and dressing.

name: Smoky Madrid Steamed Beef Albóndigas
hook: Paprika steam, tender winter meatballs

ingredients.name: waxy potatoes, cut into 3 cm chunks

steps.t: Put the mince, breadcrumbs, egg, half the garlic, 1 tsp paprika, half the parsley and the salt in a bowl. Mix with your fingertips just until it clings; kneading it like dough makes the albóndigas bouncy instead of soft.
Roll into 20 walnut-sized balls with damp hands. Keep them loose and rounded; compressed meatballs steam up tight and dry in the centre.
In a wide pan that fits a steamer insert, warm the olive oil and gently sizzle the remaining garlic and paprika until the oil turns brick-red. If the garlic goes brown, the whole broth tastes bitter.

Add the stock, passata, potatoes and chickpeas, then bring to a steady simmer. Set the steamer insert above it, making sure the liquid does not touch the basket or the beef will boil rather than steam.

Lay in the meatballs with small gaps between them, cover tightly and steam until they feel springy and there is no pink centre when one is split. The lid must stay shut; lifting it repeatedly drops the heat and leaves the middle undercooked.
Lift the albóndigas out, then simmer the potatoes and chickpeas uncovered until the sauce coats a spoon in a smoky red film. If it is still watery, the plate will eat thin instead of comforting.
Spoon the potatoes, chickpeas and broth into warm bowls, sit the steamed beef on top and finish with the remaining parsley.

note: Minced beef must be cooked through; split one meatball to check before serving.

name: Brittany Coal-Grilled Mackerel Tartines
hook: Smoke, buttered toast, sharp cornichons

steps.t: Light the coals and wait until they are glowing with a thin grey coat, not flaming. Flames scorch oily mackerel skin before the flesh has warmed through.
Mash the butter with Dijon, cornichons, shallot, capers, lemon zest and parsley. Taste for sharpness now; once it is on hot toast you cannot fix a flat butter.
Pat the mackerel very dry, oil the skin lightly and season with salt. Wet skin welds itself to the grill and tears away the best crisp bit.
Toast the bread over the edge of the coals until the ridges are dark gold and the middle is still chewy. If it goes brittle, the fish juices will just run off.
Lay the mackerel skin-side down over the hottest clean bars and leave it alone until the edges fizz and the skin releases with a nudge. Moving it early is what makes it stick.
Turn for the final kiss of heat, just until the flesh turns opaque and flakes in thick, glossy pieces. Overcooked mackerel tastes metallic and dry.
Spread the warm toast thickly with the mustard-cornichon butter, top with mackerel and squeeze over lemon before eating.

note: Best cooked outdoors over settled coals; a very hot ridged grill pan works if the weather wins.

name: Maine Halibut Crudo with Buttermilk Ranch Oil
hook: Cold silk, citrus snap, green heat

ingredients.name: sashimi-grade halibut fillet, skinless and pin-boned

steps.t: Put four plates in the fridge and keep the halibut cold until the moment you slice. Warm raw fish softens and smears under the knife instead of cutting cleanly.
Segment the grapefruit over a bowl, catching the juice, then squeeze in the lemon. Pick out any pips; one bitter pip can spoil the neat citrus bite.
Stir the buttermilk with 2 tbsp grapefruit-lemon juice, the olive oil, dill, chives and half the salt. It should taste like sharp ranch dressing; if it tastes milky, add a few more drops of citrus.
Slice the halibut across the grain into 5 mm pieces with one long pull of a sharp knife. Sawing raggedly bruises the fish and makes an expensive plate look tired.
Lay the fish on the chilled plates in a single layer, then spoon over just enough dressing to gloss it. Drowning it hides the clean sweetness of the halibut.
Scatter with grapefruit segments, jalapeño, celery and the remaining salt. Let it stand briefly until the edges turn faintly pearly but the centre stays translucent.
Crush potato crisps over the top at the table so they crackle; adding them early turns them limp.

note: Use fish sold specifically for raw eating by a trusted fishmonger, keep it refrigerated and serve the same day.

name: Mendoza Wok-Seared Lamb with Peach Chimichurri
hook: Charred lamb, cool herbs, juicy peach

ingredients.name: lean lamb leg steaks, sliced into thin strips
spring onions, cut into 4 cm lengths

steps.t: Toss the lamb with half the salt, 1 tbsp olive oil and the garlic. Leave it while you cut the vegetables; salting it too far ahead pulls out moisture and stops the strips charring.
Stir the peach with parsley, oregano, vinegar, chilli flakes, the remaining olive oil and a pinch of salt. Keep it chunky; puréeing it makes a sweet sauce instead of a fresh chimichurri.
Heat a wok or heavy frying pan until a drop of water skitters and vanishes. If the pan is only moderately hot, the lamb will stew in its juices.
Add the lamb in one layer and sear hard until the underside has dark, smoky freckles, then toss once. Crowding the pan turns the meat grey, so cook in two batches if needed.
Lift the lamb to a plate while it is still a little pink inside. Leaving it in the pan while the vegetables cook makes lean lamb tough.
Add the courgette, pepper and spring onions to the same pan and stir-fry until blistered at the edges but still bright. If they collapse, the summer feel is gone.
Return the lamb and any juices for a final toss, then plate immediately with the peach chimichurri spooned over the top.

note: Slice lamb against the grain so it stays tender through the fierce heat.

name: Bahia Griddled Black-Eyed Bean Cakes
hook: Crisp bean cakes, lime, chilli

ingredients.name: cooked black-eyed beans, drained and patted dry

steps.t: Mash the black-eyed beans roughly with a fork so some split and some stay whole. A smooth paste cooks heavy; whole beans alone will not hold together.

Squeeze the grated onion in your hand over the sink, then mix it into the beans with garlic, cassava flour, egg, half the chilli, half the coriander, lime zest and salt. Skipping the squeeze makes the cakes slump on the griddle.
Shape the mixture into 12 small patties, pressing the edges firmly so they do not crack. If the mix feels wet, dust in a little more cassava flour rather than adding more egg.
Mix the tomatoes with lime juice, remaining chilli and coriander. Salt it only lightly; too much salt pulls out tomato water and floods the platter.
Heat a flat griddle or heavy frying pan until a little oil shimmers in a thin sheet. If the oil sits dull and still, the bean cakes will drink it before they crisp.
Griddle the cakes in batches until the undersides form deep golden crusts and release cleanly. Turn them too soon and the crust stays stuck to the pan.
Flip and cook the second side until the centres feel hot and firm when pressed, not soft and pasty.
Serve on a shared platter with the tomato-lime relish and spoonfuls of coconut yoghurt for cooling swipes.

note: Tinned black-eyed beans work well here; drying them on kitchen paper is the difference between crisp and mushy.

name: Smoked Kimchi Squash Juk with Sesame Greens
hook: Breakfast porridge with a woodsmoke edge

ingredients.name: butternut squash, peeled and diced small

steps.t: Put the smoking chips on foil in the base of a lidded wok or deep pan, set a small rack above, and line the rack with baking paper; without the paper, softened squash can sag through and taste acrid where it touches metal.

Add the diced squash to the paper, clamp on the lid and heat until a thin stream of smoke appears, then smoke gently; if the smoke billows white, lower the heat or the squash will taste like a bonfire.
Tip rice, smoked squash, stock and gochujang into a heavy saucepan, stirring to dissolve the paste fully; lumps of gochujang sink and scorch before the rice has thickened.
Simmer, stirring often, until the grains burst and the porridge falls from the spoon in soft ribbons rather than watery drips.
Stir in the chopped kimchi and cook just until hot; boiling it hard for ages flattens its bright sour crunch into cabbage mush.
Fold in the greens and sesame oil until the leaves wilt glossy and dark; leave them too long and they turn khaki and stringy.
Ladle into bowls and finish with spring onions and sesame seeds, serving while it still ripples; juk thickens fast as it sits, so loosen with hot stock if it stands.

note: Choose vegan kimchi if avoiding seafood-based kimchi paste.

name: Steamed Lotus-Leaf Mushroom Rice with Black Vinegar Soy
hook: Fragrant parcels, glossy mushrooms, theatre

ingredients.name: glutinous rice, soaked 4 hours and drained

steps.t: Soak the dried shiitake in 300 ml boiling water until bendy, then squeeze and slice them, keeping the soaking liquor; pour slowly and stop before the gritty last spoonful reaches the bowl.
Pour boiling water over the lotus leaves until pliable, then rinse both sides; dry leaves crack when folded and leak the mushroom juices into the steamer.
Stir-fry the fresh mushrooms in 1 tbsp spring onion oil until they squeak less and their edges bronze; if you crowd the pan, they steam early and the parcel tastes flat.
Mix rice with fresh mushrooms, shiitake, 220 ml shiitake liquor, both soy sauces, vinegar, Shaoxing, ginger and sugar; every grain should look tea-stained, or the centre will season unevenly.
Line two shallow bowls with lotus leaves, divide the rice mixture between them and fold into tight parcels seam-side down; loose folds let condensation drip in and make the rice woolly.
Steam hard over plenty of water until the rice is sticky and translucent at the edges, topping up the steamer with boiling water if needed so it never runs dry.
Rest the parcels off the heat before opening at the table, then drizzle with the remaining spring onion oil; opening immediately lets the perfume vanish before guests smell it.

note: If lotus leaves are unavailable, use baking paper inside a bamboo steamer, though the aroma will be milder.

name: Coal-Grilled Lime Carne Asada with Cucumber Radish Salad
hook: Smoke, lime, cool crunch

steps.t: Light the coals and let them burn until covered in grey ash with a fierce red core; cooking over black flames coats the beef in soot before the centre warms.
Mix lime juice, olive oil, garlic, cumin, chipotle and salt, then coat the steak for 15 minutes only; a long lime soak makes the surface woolly instead of cleanly charred.
Toss cucumber, radishes, red onion and half the coriander with a spoonful of the marinade from before it touched the beef, not from the meat bowl; used raw-meat marinade is not safe on salad.
Pat the steak dry and grill close to the coals until the edges char in freckles and the meat releases without tearing; wet steak steams and sticks.
Turn and grill the second side until springy with a little give for medium-rare, or longer if preferred; dragging it around the grate tears off the crust you built.
Rest the beef on a warm plate so the juices settle into the fibres; slicing straight away floods the board and leaves the steak dry.
Slice thinly across the grain and serve over the cucumber-radish salad with remaining coriander and lime wedges; cutting with the grain makes even tender skirt steak chew like rope.

note: Use a hot griddle pan if coals are not possible, but the smoke will be gentler.

name: Aegean Citrus-Cured Mackerel with Oregano Olive Oil
hook: Silky fish, sharp lemon, green oil

ingredients.name: previously frozen sashimi-grade mackerel fillets, skin removed

steps.t: Check the mackerel is labelled previously frozen and suitable for raw eating, then keep it chilled while you work; citrus firms fish but does not make unsafe fish safe.
Run your fingertips down the fillets and pull any pin bones with tweezers; leaving them in ruins the silky mezze texture with sharp surprises.
Slice the fish on a slight angle into 5 mm pieces and lay them in one layer on a cold plate; stacking the slices cures the outside while the hidden pieces stay oily and dull.
Whisk lemon juice, orange juice, lemon zest and salt until the salt dissolves, then spoon it over the fish; grains of undissolved salt make harsh specks rather than an even cure.
Leave until the edges turn opaque but the centres still look glossy and coral-pink; if it goes chalk-white all the way through, you have left it too long.

Lift the fish from most of the citrus, then dress with olive oil, oregano, capers, red onion, cucumber and parsley; drowning it in the curing liquid makes the oil slide off and tastes sharp rather than bright.
Serve immediately as a shared plate with bread or crisp potatoes; oily fish warms quickly, and once warm its clean sea flavour turns heavy.

note: Ask a fishmonger for mackerel intended for raw preparations, or use properly frozen fillets thawed overnight in the fridge.

name: Patagonian White Fish Chupín
hook: Tomato-rich broth, flaky fish, olive bite

ingredients.name: firm white fish fillets, such as hake or cod

steps.t: Slice the potatoes 5 mm thick, cut the onion and pepper into strips, and pat the fish dry; thicker potatoes stay hard after the fish is already flaking.
Warm the oil in a wide pan and soften the onion and pepper until glossy and slumped, not browned; rushing this leaves the stew tasting sharp and raw.
Stir in the garlic and paprika for 30 seconds, then add passata, stock, potatoes and a good pinch of salt; if the paprika scorches, the whole broth turns bitter.
Simmer with the lid slightly open until the potato edges yield to a knife; a hard boil breaks the slices and makes the sauce gluey.
Season the fish, nestle it into the broth and simmer gently until the flakes just separate; a rolling boil will tear the fillets into cottony bits.
Fold in the olives and parsley, then spoon from the edge of the pan rather than stirring hard; rough stirring now turns a clean stew into fish mash.

note: Add lemon at the table if your olives are mild; the stew should finish briny and bright.

name: Bahian Whole-Roasted Portobellos with Lime Farofa
hook: Deep roasted caps, bright sandy crunch

steps.t: Wipe the mushrooms clean and trim only the dry stem tips, keeping the caps whole; washing them under the tap loads them with water and they roast flabby.
Whisk coconut milk, dendê, lime zest and juice, grated garlic, chopped chilli, sugar and salt; without enough salt the big caps taste seasoned only on the surface.
Coat the mushrooms, sit them gill-side up in a snug dish and marinate, turning once; a short soak gives you roasted mushrooms with sauce, not mushrooms seasoned through.
Heat the oven to 200°C and spread the mushrooms whole on a lined tray with space between them; crowding traps steam and stops the caps becoming meaty.
Roast with a spoonful of marinade in each cap until the mushrooms sag and leak dark juices; if the tray is swimming, tip off excess liquid or they will braise.
Baste with the sticky tray juices and roast again until the rims look lacquered and slightly curled; skipping the baste leaves dry edges and bland centres.
Melt the butter, stir in cassava flour and cook until it looks like pale golden beach sand; high heat takes it from nutty to scorched in seconds.
Fold spring onions, coriander and crushed cashews into the farofa, then serve it over the roasted caps; covering the farofa too early makes the crunch turn damp.

note: Dendê is distinctive and worth buying for the weekend-project feel; use olive oil only if you cannot find it.

name: Dhungar Smoked Beef Boti Bowl
hook: Charcoal smoke, lean beef, sharp cucumber

steps.t: Cut the beef across the grain into 2 cm pieces and pat them very dry; wet beef drops its juices and stews before it browns.
Mix yoghurt, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, tandoori masala and salt, then coat the beef; if the yoghurt sits in clumps, those patches taste chalky after cooking.
Heat the oil in a heavy pan until shimmering and spread the beef in one layer; piling it up cools the pan and gives grey meat with no boti char.
Sear, turning the pieces, until the edges are dark red-brown and the largest piece reaches 63°C, then rest it; guessing by colour can leave a cold centre.
Put the cooked beef in a lidded pan, set a small metal bowl in the middle, add glowing charcoal and spoon ghee onto the coal; if the coal touches the food it tastes sooty.
Cover immediately and smoke near an open window or extractor until the beef smells like a tandoor, not a bonfire; over-smoking makes lean beef taste ashy.
Toss cucumber, red onion and coriander with lemon, warm the rice, and bowl everything without trapping the salad under hot beef; heat kills the crunch you need against the smoke.

note: Use only plain lumpwood charcoal, not treated barbecue briquettes, and smoke after the beef is fully cooked.

name: Vietnamese Coffee Steamed Flan
hook: Silky custard, bitter caramel, coffee drift

steps.t: Cook the sugar and water in a small pan until the caramel is deep copper, then divide between ramekins; pale caramel tastes flat, while smoking black caramel turns harsh.
Warm the milk, condensed milk, vanilla and salt until steaming at the edges; boiling milk scrambles the eggs as soon as it hits them.
Whisk the eggs and yolk gently, then pour in the warm milk mixture slowly; beating in froth gives the finished flan a pocked, bubbly top.
Strain the custard into the caramel-lined ramekins and cover each with foil; skipping the sieve leaves stringy egg bits, and uncovered cups catch watery lid drips.
Steam over the lowest steady heat until the centres wobble like soft jelly; a fierce boil makes honeycomb holes instead of silk.
Lift the ramekins out and leave them still on the worktop; moving hot custard around is how fine cracks become splits.
Chill thoroughly, loosen the edges, unmould and spoon the strong coffee around the caramel; unmoulding warm flan makes it slump instead of stand glossy.

note: The coffee is poured on at the end so the custard stays clean and the finish tastes distinctly Vietnamese.

name: Coal-Grilled Tofu Panzanella
hook: Smoky tofu, torn bread, tomato juices

steps.t: Light the charcoal and wait until the coals are ashy with no black patches; grilling over raw-looking coals gives acrid smoke and sticky grates.
Press the tofu between towels with a pan on top, then cut it into thick planks; wet or thin tofu steams, tears and falls through the bars.
Mix grated garlic, olive oil, vinegar, oregano, lemon zest, lemon juice and salt, then brush some over the tofu; dry tofu grabs the grate before it gets grill marks.
Tear the ciabatta, chunk the tomatoes, slice the onion and basil, and toss them with most of the dressing; tiny bread cubes turn to paste instead of soaking up tomato juice.
Grill the tofu and sliced courgette over the coals until dark bars appear and the tofu releases easily; forcing it early leaves the crust welded to the grill.
Toast the torn bread briefly on the cooler edge, then fold it through the tomatoes with the courgette; leaving bread over the heat too long makes croutons, not panzanella.
Top with the grilled tofu and rest the salad before eating; skipping the rest means dry bread and tomato juice left sadly in the bowl.

note: Built for a student barbecue: cheap tofu, stale bread and the ripest tomatoes you can find.

name: Chipotle Pork Tray Enchilada Bake
hook: Saucy, smoky, cheese-crisped at the edges

ingredients.name: corn tortillas, torn into rough pieces

steps.t: Heat the oven to 220°C, or 200°C fan. In a medium baking dish, mix the passata, chipotle paste and onion, then pinch in the pork mince and break it up thoroughly; big lumps stay bland in the middle and cook unevenly.
Cover the dish tightly with foil and bake until the sauce is bubbling hard around the edges and the pork has turned opaque, not pink.
Stir firmly, scraping the corners where mince hides. If you still see any pink pork, return it to the oven for a few minutes before adding anything else.
Stir in the black beans, sweetcorn and torn tortillas, pushing the tortilla pieces under the sauce; dry exposed pieces turn leathery rather than soft and saucy.
Scatter over the cheddar and bake uncovered until the cheese is freckled golden and the sauce is puffing through the tortilla edges.
Rest briefly, then finish with lime juice and coriander. Cut it too soon and the bake slumps into the dish instead of holding saucy layers.

note: Use a dish large enough for a shallow bake; crowding makes the tortillas stodgy.

name: Stifado-Braised Eggs with Caramel Pearl Onions
hook: Jammy eggs in sweet-spiced onion gravy

steps.t: Cover the pearl onions with boiling water, then drain and slip off the skins. Trim only the whiskery end; cut too deep and the onions unravel during the long braise.
Heat the oven to 150°C, or 130°C fan. Warm the olive oil in a heavy casserole and cook the onions gently until glossy with amber patches; high heat scorches the outside before the centres turn sweet.
Add the garlic, oregano, bay and cinnamon, stirring just until the garlic smells mellow. If it browns here, the whole sauce will carry that bitter edge for hours.
Pour in the wine and vinegar and simmer until the sharp alcohol smell softens and the liquid is reduced by about half.

Add the tomatoes, season, cover with a lid and braise in the oven until the onions are spoon-soft and the sauce is dark brick-red. Check once; if the edges look dry, splash in water before it catches.
Set the casserole over a low hob. Make eight shallow wells, crack each egg into a cup, then slide it in; cracking straight into the stew risks shell and broken yolks you cannot rescue.
Cover and simmer gently until the whites are opaque and the yolks still tremble. Rest, then crumble over feta and parsley; boiling hard makes rubbery whites and chalky yolks.

note: The braise can be made a day ahead; add the eggs only when you are ready to eat.

name: Antep Lentil, Chickpea & Spinach Güveç
hook: Hearty legumes, peppery warmth, lemon lift

steps.t: Rinse the lentils until the water runs mostly clear. Skipping this leaves dusty starch in the pot and the stew tastes flat rather than cleanly earthy.
In a wide saucepan, cook the onion and peppers in the olive oil until the peppers slump and the onion smells sweet; if they still squeak against the spoon, the finished stew will taste raw.
Stir in the garlic, tomato paste, pepper paste and pul biber until the oil turns rusty red. Let the pastes fry, but not blacken; burnt pepper paste goes harsh fast.
Add the lentils and vegetable stock, bring to a simmer, then cook until the lentils are tender but still holding their shape.
Stir in the chickpeas and simmer until the broth thickens around them. Add them earlier and they split; add them later and they taste like a tin dropped into stew.
Fold in the spinach by handfuls until just wilted, then finish with lemon juice. If the spinach boils for long, it turns khaki and drags the whole pot down.

note: This lands around the gym-meal brief through legumes rather than animal protein: sturdy, filling and still vegetable-led.

name: Rosewater Steamed Egg Custards with Date Molasses
hook: Silky rose custard, glossy with dates

steps.t: Set a steaming rack in a wide saucepan with about 3 cm water and bring it to a bare simmer. A rolling boil rattles the ramekins and makes pocked, bubbly custard.
Warm the milk with the sugar, cardamom, orange zest and salt until steaming at the edges, not boiling. Boiled milk tightens the eggs too quickly later.
Whisk the eggs in a jug, then pour in the hot milk slowly while whisking all the time. Dump it in quickly and you will make sweet scrambled egg.
Strain the custard, stir in the rosewater, then divide between four ramekins and cover each with foil; unstrained zest and egg threads spoil the silkiness.
Steam with the lid on until the edges are set and the centres wobble like soft jelly. If the water boils hard, lower the heat immediately or the custards will honeycomb.
Lift out and rest so the centres finish gently, then spoon over date molasses and scatter with pistachios just before serving.

note: Serve warm for a soft finish, or chill if you prefer a firmer set.

name: Tea-Smoked Mushroom Chermoula Couscous
hook: Woodsy smoke, bright herbs, fluffy couscous

steps.t: Open a window and line an old lidded wok or deep pot with two layers of foil. Put the tea, rice and sugar in the centre; gaps in the foil let caramelised sugar weld itself to the pan.
Toss the mushrooms with half the olive oil, ras el hanout, garlic and lemon zest. Set them on a rack or metal steamer above the tea mix; if they touch it, they taste acrid rather than smoked.
Put the lid on tightly and heat until thin wisps of smoke smell toasty, then lower to medium and smoke until the mushrooms turn tan and tender.
Turn off the heat and let the pot sit before opening the lid away from your face. Opening early fills the room with smoke and leaves the mushrooms underflavoured.
Meanwhile, put the couscous and chickpeas in a bowl, pour over the hot stock, cover and leave until the grains have swollen. Too much liquid makes couscous paste, not fluff.
Fluff the couscous with a fork, then fold in parsley, lemon juice and the remaining olive oil. Pile the smoked mushrooms on top with any smoky juices from the rack.

note: Use a cheap stainless-steel pot if you can; avoid non-stick for smoking over high heat.

name: Smoky Cider-Braised Paneer Pot
hook: Maple smoke, soft roots, squeaky golden paneer

steps.t: Pat the paneer very dry and season it. If it goes into the pan damp, it steams and tears instead of forming a golden crust.
Heat the oil in a heavy casserole and brown the paneer on two sides until the edges are honey-gold and lightly blistered; lift it out before it toughens.
Add the onion to the same pan and cook until soft, sweet and amber at the tips. If it catches black now, the whole braise will taste bitter.
Stir in the garlic, mushrooms and smoked paprika until the mushrooms look glossy and the paprika smells warm, not dusty.
Add the sweet potatoes, cider, tomatoes and maple syrup. Scrape the base clean, because any stuck brown bits left behind will scorch during the long cook.
Cover and braise gently until the sweet potatoes yield to a spoon but still hold their shape; a rolling boil will break them into paste.
Return the paneer with the greens and cook uncovered until the greens slump and the sauce clings thickly. Finish with cider vinegar so the pot tastes deep, not heavy.

note: Serve in deep bowls with cornbread or buttered toast.

name: Chimichurri Lentil Morning Guiso
hook: Herby steam, soft lentils, bright vinegar heat

steps.t: Soften the onion and pepper in the oil until the pepper turns silky and the onion loses its raw bite; rush this and the stew tastes sharp rather than breakfast-warm.
Stir in garlic, paprika and cumin for a minute, just until fragrant. If the spices darken to brick-brown, pull the pan off the heat before they turn acrid.
Add lentils, potatoes and stock, then bring to a quiet simmer. Boiling hard splits the lentils before the centres are creamy.
Simmer with the lid slightly ajar until the potatoes are tender and the lentils are soft but not collapsed.
Crush a few potato pieces against the side of the pan to thicken the broth; do not blend it smooth, because guiso should still eat like a stew.
Mix parsley, oregano and vinegar in a bowl with a spoonful of hot stew liquor to wake the herbs without cooking them grey.
Spoon the chimichurri-style dressing through the stew just before serving, so the top smells grassy and sharp rather than flat.

note: Good with toast, mate or strong coffee.

name: Bahia Whole-Roasted Squash with Eggs
hook: A golden centrepiece with coconut-silk eggs

ingredients.name: small whole kabocha or crown prince squash, about 1.4 kg

steps.t: Heat the oven to 200°C. Cut a neat lid from the squash and scoop out every seed and string; stray fibres make the filling watery and bitter.
Rub the squash inside and out with oil and salt, then roast it with the lid beside it until a knife slides through the thickest wall with only slight resistance.
Meanwhile cook the onion in a small pan until soft and glossy. If it browns hard, it will bully the coconut instead of sweetening it.
Add garlic, chilli and tomato purée, stirring until the purée darkens slightly and stops smelling tinny.
Stir in coconut milk and lime juice, then simmer until it coats the back of a spoon; a runny sauce will drown the eggs rather than cradle them.
Pour the sauce into the hot squash, crack in the eggs and return it to the oven uncovered until the whites are set and the yolks still wobble when the squash is nudged.
Rest for five minutes, then scatter coriander and cashews over the top. Cutting straight away makes the eggs spill before guests see the centre.

note: Carry it to the table whole, then spoon out wedges with the coconut eggs.

name: Dhungar-Smoked Courgette Kachumber
hook: Cool crunch under a whisper of smoke

steps.t: Salt the courgette ribbons lightly and leave them until they bend without snapping; skip this and they taste raw and squeak against the cucumber.
Pat the courgettes dry, then toss with cucumber, tomatoes, onion, chilli, chaat masala and lemon juice. Excess surface water will dilute the smoke and dressing.
Nestle a small heatproof metal bowl in the salad and have a tight lid ready. If the lid does not seal, the smoke escapes before flavouring the vegetables.
Heat the charcoal over a gas flame or with a blowtorch until one side glows red and ashy; black unlit coal gives a harsh paraffin taste.
Place the hot charcoal in the little bowl, spoon the oil over it and immediately cover the salad. Do not touch the coal or let it contact the vegetables.
Uncover, remove the charcoal bowl and toss in mint and coriander. Add the soft herbs only now, or they bruise dark and lose their lift.
Taste for lemon and salt just before serving, because tomatoes release juice as they sit and can make the plate go flat.

note: Serve chilled or cool, not fridge-cold, with thin roti or on its own.

name: Ginger-Lime Steamed Cod Cups
hook: Clean steam, bright lime, tender flakes

ingredients.name: cod loin or other firm white fish, cut into 8 pieces
fresh ginger, cut into fine matchsticks

steps.t: Check the fish for bones and pat it dry. Wet pieces slide around and steam unevenly, leaving some flakes woolly and others raw-looking.
Stir fish sauce, lime juice and sugar until the sugar dissolves; gritty sugar on the fish burns salty rather than seasoning cleanly.
Line a steamer with pak choi leaves and set a piece of fish on each leaf. Leave gaps for steam, because a crowded steamer cooks from the edges only.
Spoon over the dressing and scatter ginger on top, keeping the chilli and herbs back so they stay vivid.
Steam over steadily boiling water until the fish turns opaque and flakes with gentle pressure, but still looks juicy at the centre.
Lift the cups out carefully, keeping the cooking juices in the leaves; tipping them loses the best sauce.
Finish with spring onion, chilli, peanuts and coriander just before the platter hits the table, so every bite has crunch and clean heat.

note: Set out with extra lime wedges and small spoons for the juices.

name: Pul Biber Tofu Saç Sizzle
hook: Peppery tofu with smoky lemon edges

ingredients.name: red pepper, cut into thin strips
green pepper, cut into thin strips

steps.t: Tear the tofu into thumb-sized chunks and press hard between clean tea towels until the surface feels dry; wet tofu steams and will never take on those ragged browned edges.
Heat your widest frying pan or wok until a drop of water skitters away, then add the oil and tofu in one layer; if the pan is only warm or crowded, the tofu will leak and turn spongy.
Fry hard, turning every minute or so, until the tofu corners are deep gold and slightly crisp, then lift it to a plate; stopping at pale beige means the sauce will taste flat.
Throw the peppers and onion into the same hot pan and keep them moving until the edges blister but the centres still snap; if they slump and go watery, the heat is too low.
Add the garlic, pul biber, tomato paste and salt, scraping the paste across the pan until it darkens brick-red; raw tomato paste leaves a tinny taste.
Return the tofu with the sumac and lemon juice, toss hard for a final glossy coating, then take it off the heat as soon as the pan smells smoky-citrus rather than sharp.
Scatter with parsley and serve immediately; leave it in the pan and the tofu softens under its own steam.

note: Good with rice, flatbread or a quick cucumber yoghurt.

name: Aleppo Lamb Arayes Project
hook: Crisp bread, spiced lamb, smoky yoghurt

ingredients.name: large Lebanese flatbreads or thin pitas
lemon, zested and cut into wedges

steps.t: Squeeze the grated onion in your fist until it stops dripping, then mix it with the lamb, parsley, garlic, baharat, Aleppo pepper, pine nuts, lemon zest and salt; watery onion makes the bread split and steam.
Knead the mixture with cold hands until it turns tacky and clings to the bowl, then cover and chill overnight; loose mince falls out of the bread on the griddle.
Split each flatbread into pockets or halve thin pitas, then spread the lamb inside in a thin, even layer right to the edges; a thick centre stays raw while the bread burns.
Brush both sides lightly with olive oil and press the breads flat with your palms; dry patches scorch black before the lamb fat has a chance to baste the crumb.
Heat a cast-iron griddle over medium heat until steadily hot, not smoking, and cook the arayes in batches under a weighted pan until the bread is bronze and the lamb juices hiss at the seams.
Flip and cook the second side until the bread sounds crisp when tapped and the lamb is fully cooked through; if you rush this, the centre stays pink and unsafe.
Rest the arayes on a rack for 5 minutes, then cut into wedges; stacking them on a plate traps steam and ruins the crackle.
Serve with thick yoghurt and lemon wedges, dragging the hot cut edges through the cold yoghurt.

note: The overnight chill is what makes this feel like a proper weekend project.

name: Chermoula Lentil-Chickpea Crisps
hook: Golden pulse cakes with green heat

steps.t: Spread the lentils and chickpeas on kitchen paper and pat them dry until they look matte; damp pulses make the cakes burst and spit in the oil.
Mash two thirds of the pulses with the eggs, gram flour, harissa, spices, lemon zest and salt, leaving some chickpeas whole for bite; blending everything smooth gives you paste, not crisp cakes.
Fold in half the fresh coriander, then rest the mixture until the gram flour hydrates and the bowl no longer looks wet at the edges.
Shape 9 squat cakes with oiled hands, pressing the sides firm; loose, tall cakes crack before the crust sets.

Heat the oil in a wide frying pan until a crumb sizzles instantly, then shallow fry the cakes without crowding until the undersides are mahogany-gold and crisp enough to slide a spatula under cleanly.
Turn once and fry the other side to the same hard crust; fiddling with them early tears off the protein-rich crust you worked for.
Stir the yoghurt with lemon juice and the remaining coriander, then spoon it beside the hot crisps; pouring yoghurt over the top softens them fast.

note: Around 28 g protein per serving, depending on your yoghurt and egg size.

name: Seville Orange Steamed Flan
hook: Silky custard under bitter caramel

steps.t: Put 90 g sugar and the water in a small pan and cook without stirring until the syrup turns dark amber and smells just bitter; stirring crystallises it into grit.
Immediately divide the caramel between six ramekins, tilting to coat the bases before it sets; wait too long and it hardens in the pan.
Warm the milk with the orange zest until steaming but not boiling, then take it off the heat; boiled milk gives the flan a cooked, skin-on flavour.
Whisk the eggs, yolks, remaining sugar, sherry and salt just until smooth, then slowly whisk in the warm milk; frothing it hard leaves bubbles in the finished custard.
Strain into the ramekins and cover each tightly with foil, because stray steam droplets pit the surface.
Set the ramekins in a wide lidded pan on a folded tea towel, pour in hot water halfway up the sides, cover and steam at the barest simmer until the centres wobble like set jelly, not liquid.
Cool, then chill until fully cold; unmoulding warm flan makes the custard slump and the caramel run thin.
Run a knife around each edge and invert onto plates, letting the caramel flood over the top.

note: Use sweet oranges if Seville oranges are out of season; add a tiny extra strip of zest for bitterness.

name: Normandy Mussel Potato Gratin
hook: Creamy potatoes, briny mussels, crisp top

ingredients.name: floury potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
frozen cooked mussel meat, thawed and patted dry

steps.t: Heat the oven to 200°C fan and butter a medium baking dish; an ungreased dish welds the bottom potato layer on like glue.
Toss the potato slices, leek, garlic, thyme, salt and pepper directly in the dish, separating any stuck potato slices; clumps cook hard in the middle.
Whisk the cream, milk and Dijon until smooth, then pour it over the potatoes and press everything level; dry potato tips scorch before the centre softens.
Cover the dish tightly with foil and bake until a knife slides through the centre with only slight resistance; loose foil lets the liquid evaporate before the potatoes cook.
Fold the thawed mussels gently through the top half of the potatoes, not the bottom, so they warm through without turning rubbery from overbaking.
Scatter over the cheese and dot with butter, then bake uncovered until the top is bubbling and freckled brown at the ridges.
Rest for 8 minutes before spooning out; serve too soon and the cream runs across the plate instead of clinging to the potatoes.

note: Frozen cooked mussels keep this cheap and avoid any shell-scrubbing in a student kitchen.

name: Harissa-Crisped Chakchouka Eggs
hook: Runny yolks, crackling spiced edges

steps.t: Warm the oil in a wide frying pan over medium-high heat, then fry the onion and pepper until the onion is glossy and the pepper corners start to blister; if they only sweat, the eggs will taste flat rather than fried.
Stir in the harissa and cumin for 30 seconds, just until the oil turns brick-red; take it further and the chilli catches bitterly on the pan.
Add the tomatoes and a pinch of salt, then bubble hard until the sauce is thick enough to leave a clean trail when you drag a spoon through it; watery sauce stops the egg edges crisping.
Make four shallow hollows and crack in the eggs, spacing them apart so the whites hit hot oily sauce instead of steaming in one puddle.
Spoon a little red oil from the edges over the whites, then fry until the white rims turn lace-brown and the yolks still wobble; too low a heat gives rubbery whites with no crisp bits.
Splash with lemon juice, scatter with coriander, and serve straight from the pan with warmed flatbreads; wait too long and the yolks set from the pan heat.

note: For less heat, use half the harissa and add a pinch of smoked paprika.

name: Azafrán Steamed Vegetable Terrine
hook: Silky vegetables, saffron-sweet steam

ingredients.name: large aubergines, sliced lengthways 5 mm thick

steps.t: Salt the aubergine and courgette slices lightly and leave them in a colander until beads of moisture appear; skip this and the terrine slumps into vegetable water when sliced.
Meanwhile blacken the peppers directly over a gas flame or under a very hot grill until the skins blister all over, then cover in a bowl; if the skins are only tanned, they cling and tear the flesh.
Peel and seed the peppers, then cut into broad strips; rinse the aubergine and courgette quickly and pat every slice dry, because wet vegetables steam unevenly and taste washed out.
Warm the olive oil with saffron, smoked paprika, vinegar and a pinch of salt until fragrant but not frying; burnt paprika gives the whole terrine a dusty bitterness.
Line a loaf tin with baking parchment and layer potatoes, onion, aubergine, pepper and courgette, brushing each layer with saffron oil and pressing flat; loose layers leave gaps that crumble later.
Cover tightly with foil and steam over steadily simmering water until a skewer slides through the centre potatoes without crunch; boiling the pan dry will scorch the tin and ruin the perfume.
Weight the covered terrine with tins and chill until firm, then unmould and slice with a sharp knife; cutting it warm turns careful layers into a heap.
Finish with almonds, parsley and a few drops of sherry vinegar just before serving so the nuts stay crisp against the soft vegetables.

note: This is best made ahead; the slicing improves after an overnight chill.

name: Coal-Grilled Cod aux Herbes
hook: Clean smoke, lemon, firm flakes

ingredients.name: cod loin fillets, about 180 g each

steps.t: Light the coals and wait until they are covered in grey ash with no licking flames; flames scorch cod before the centre firms.
Pat the cod very dry, then rub with olive oil, Dijon, lemon zest, garlic, salt and pepper; damp fish glues itself to the bars and tears when you turn it.
Toss the lentils with half the lemon juice, a pinch of salt and most of the herbs, then set aside so they taste bright rather than canteen-dull.

Oil the grill bars, lay the cod on the hottest clean section, and do not move it until the underside releases and shows clear dark grill lines; fiddling early leaves half the fish welded to the grate.
Turn with a wide fish slice and grill the second side until the flakes separate under gentle pressure but the middle still looks pearly, not chalk-white.
At the same time, grill the green beans in a perforated tray until blistered and squeaky-tender; if they go limp, they have steamed instead of grilled.
Plate lentils, beans and cod, then finish with the remaining lemon juice and herbs; add the acid at the end or it dulls the green herbs while the fish rests.

note: If using thinner fillets, shorten the grilling by about a minute per side.

name: Maple Steamed Custard Cups
hook: Wobbly satin under maple gloss

steps.t: Heat the milk with the brown sugar, salt and cinnamon until steaming at the edges, not boiling; boiled milk gives the custard a cooked-skin flavour.
Whisk the eggs just until smooth, then slowly whisk in the hot milk; pour too fast and you will scramble the eggs into sweet strands.
Stir in the vanilla and half the maple syrup, then strain into four ramekins; straining catches chalazae and bubbles that would spoil the satin texture.
Cover each ramekin tightly with foil and set in a steamer over barely simmering water; a rolling boil makes pitted, rubbery custard.
Steam until the custards wobble as one soft piece and a knife near the edge comes out clean; if the centre is liquid, it will collapse under the syrup.
Lift out carefully, cool for 15 minutes, then chill until fully cold; serving warm hides the maple and makes the texture loose.
Spoon over the remaining maple syrup and scatter pecans on top just before serving; add nuts early and they soften into leathery bits.

note: Use real maple syrup here; pancake syrup turns one-note and sticky.

name: Chimichurri Beef Pan Fideos
hook: Seared beef, garlicky noodle crunch

steps.t: Cover the noodles with boiling water until just bendy, then drain and rinse cold; fully soft noodles turn to paste when they hit the wok.
Mix garlic, vinegar, parsley, oregano, chilli flakes, a pinch of salt and one tablespoon of oil into a rough chimichurri; if you cook all the herbs, you lose the sharp Argentine lift.
Heat a wok or large frying pan until a drop of water skitters away, then add the remaining oil; a merely warm pan stews the cheap steak grey.
Spread the beef in a single layer and leave it alone until the edges brown hard, then toss once; constant stirring stops the sear forming.
Add onion and green pepper and stir-fry until the pepper blisters but still snaps; cook it limp and the whole pan tastes like takeaway leftovers.
Add the drained noodles and stir-fry hard until some strands catch golden and crisp on the pan; if the pan is crowded, pause between tosses so steam can escape.
Take off the heat, fold through the chimichurri, and serve immediately; heating the vinegar-herb sauce too long makes it muddy instead of bright.

note: Slice the beef across the grain as thinly as you can; it makes budget steak eat tender.

name: Black Vinegar Pickled Soybeans with Sesame Savoy
hook: Black vinegar warmth, sesame gloss, cabbage crunch

steps.t: Warm the soybeans in a small pan of water until they steam, then drain hard; if they go into the pickle cold and wet, the dressing tastes thin instead of clinging.
Simmer the black vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, ginger and garlic until the sugar disappears and the raw garlic smell softens; do not boil it fiercely or the vinegar turns harsh.
Pour the hot pickle over the warm soybeans and fold gently until every bean is lacquered; stir roughly and the skins split into a mash.
Leave the beans to stand, turning once, until they taste sharp all the way through rather than just sour on the surface.
Wilt the Savoy in a wide pan with a splash of water until the ribs bend but still squeak; overcook it and the whole bowl smells sulphurous.
Whisk sesame paste with 2 tablespoons of the bean pickling liquid, then fold in the chilli oil; add the liquid slowly or the paste seizes into chalky lumps.
Pile cabbage into bowls, spoon over the pickled soybeans and finish with spring onions and sesame seeds; serve warm, because fridge-cold beans mute the vinegar and chilli.

note: A kettle of hot water beside the hob makes loosening the sesame dressing easy if it tightens.

name: One-Dish Halloumi Ranchero Breakfast Bake
hook: Crisp cheese, runny yolks, smoky beans

ingredients.name: corn tortillas, torn into rough pieces

steps.t: Heat the oven to 200°C fan and put a deep baking dish on a tray; skipping the tray is how bubbling tomato ends up burning onto the oven floor.
Toss onion, pepper and olive oil in the dish, then bake until the onion tips curl and the pepper smells sweet; if they stay raw, the sauce tastes watery.
Stir in chipotle paste, black beans and chopped tomatoes, scraping the corners well; unmixed chipotle gives someone a bitter, fiery mouthful.
Fold torn tortillas through the beans so some sit proud and some sink; bury them all and you lose the crisp edges that make this worth waking for.
Lay halloumi over the top and bake until the sauce is burping at the edges and the cheese has bronze freckles; pull it too soon and the halloumi stays rubbery-pale.
Make four hollows, crack in the eggs and bake until the whites are just set but the yolks still tremble; leave them until firm and breakfast turns heavy.
Scatter coriander over the dish and serve with lime and avocado; add the lime at the table, because baking it dulls the clean sharpness.

note: For milder plates, use 1 tablespoon chipotle paste and add 1 teaspoon smoked paprika.

name: Kokkinisto Octopus with Fennel and Kalamata Olives
hook: Silky octopus in glossy red wine

ingredients.name: lemon, zested and cut into wedges

steps.t: Pat the octopus dry and cut the head and tentacles into large serving pieces; small pieces tighten before they tenderise and look mean on a guest platter.
Soften onions and fennel in olive oil until glossy and collapsed, not brown; rush this stage and the braise tastes sharp rather than sweet.
Add garlic and tomato purée and stir until the purée darkens to brick red; if it stays raw-red, the sauce keeps a tinny edge.
Pour in the red wine and simmer until the steam smells fruity rather than alcoholic; trapping raw wine under the lid makes the octopus taste boozy.
Add passata, cinnamon, bay and octopus, then bring to the gentlest blip; a rolling boil makes the outside fibrous before the centre gives way.
Cover and braise on low until a skewer slides into the thickest tentacle with almost no push; stop at chewy and no amount of garnish will save it.
Stir in olives and simmer uncovered until the sauce coats a spoon in a shiny red layer; leave it loose and it floods the platter.
Rest off the heat, then finish with lemon zest, fennel fronds and lemon wedges; adding zest while boiling drives off its perfume.

note: Do not salt at the start: octopus and olives usually season the sauce enough as it reduces.

name: Summer Halloumi Türlü with Minted Tomato Broth
hook: Bright courgettes, squeaky cheese, tomato steam

steps.t: Soften onion and green pepper in olive oil until the onion is translucent and the pepper loses its raw snap; browning them makes the stew taste heavy, not summery.
Stir in tomato paste and pul biber until the oil stains orange; if the paste is left in a lump, it tastes metallic later.
Add grated tomatoes and simmer until the foam settles and the colour deepens; watery raw tomato will not carry the halloumi.
Add green beans with 100 ml water, cover and simmer until they bend but still look green; boil them hard and they turn khaki before the courgette arrives.
Fold in courgettes and halloumi, keeping the simmer lazy; fierce bubbling breaks the courgettes and makes the cheese tough at the edges.
Taste before salting, then add lemon juice and half the mint; halloumi is salty, so seasoning early can push the broth over the line.
Spoon into shallow bowls and finish with the remaining mint; deep bowls trap steam and carry on cooking the vegetables to softness.

note: Serve just warm rather than piping hot, with crusty bread for the tomato broth.

name: Whole Za’atar Pork Fillet with Pomegranate Tahini
hook: Pink-centred slices, sharp ruby onions

steps.t: Heat the oven to 220°C fan and trim any silver skin from the pork without cutting into the meat; leave it on and it shrinks into a tough strap.
Mix za’atar, olive oil, garlic, lemon zest and pomegranate molasses, then rub it over the whole fillets; patchy coating gives burnt sweet spots and bland slices.
Toss sliced onions with lemon juice and sumac and scrunch until glossy; if you do not bruise them, they stay harsh and papery.
Sear the pork in an ovenproof pan until the paste smells toasted and the underside releases easily; move it too soon and the crust tears off.
Roast the fillets whole until the centre reaches 63°C, then lift them to a board; guessing by colour risks dry pork or unsafe undercooking.
Rest the pork loosely covered so the juices settle; slice straight away and the platter fills with juice instead of the meat staying succulent.
Whisk tahini with the remaining lemon juice and enough cold water to make a spoonable sauce; add water all at once and it can split grainy.
Slice the pork thickly and serve with tahini, sumac onions, parsley, pomegranate seeds and warm flatbreads; thin slices cool fast and lose their rosy centre.

note: This is Levantine-spiced rather than traditional; it belongs beside pickles, olives and salads on a mezze-style table.

name: Dendê-Griddled Mackerel with Black Bean Farofa
hook: Bronzed fish, smoky beans, winter warmth

steps.t: Rub the mackerel with dendê, smoked paprika, lime zest and a firm pinch of salt; keep it skin-side up so the cure does not draw too much water into the flesh and make the skin slack.
Melt the butter in a frying pan, add the onion and cook until it folds and turns jammy at the edges; if it is still sharp and purple, the farofa will taste raw.
Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the black beans and a splash of water; crush a spoonful against the pan so the beans cling to the cassava instead of rolling loose.
Stir in the cassava flour and toast until it smells nutty and looks like damp sand, not pale dust; take it too far and it will taste bitter rather than cosy.
Heat a ridged griddle until a drop of water skitters away, then lay the mackerel skin-side down and press for the first few seconds; without that contact the skin steams instead of blistering.
Turn the fish only when the skin releases and the edges are lace-brown, then cook the flesh side briefly until just opaque; if white beads flood out, it has gone dry.
Finish the farofa with lime juice and coriander, spoon it onto warm plates and sit the mackerel on top so the crisp skin stays proud of the beans.

note: Dendê is strong and warming; a little gives the dish its Brazilian winter glow.

name: Lahori Crisp Pork Cutlets with Masala Eggs
hook: Crackling crumbs, spiced yolks, hot tea

steps.t: Bash the pork steaks between baking paper to 1 cm thick; leave thick ridges and the coating will burn before the centre is safely cooked.
Mix yoghurt, ginger-garlic paste, cumin, chilli, garam masala and salt, then coat the pork and let it sit while you set up the pan; do not leave it swimming or the crust will slide off.
Stir the gram flour and panko together, lift each cutlet from the marinade, and press crumbs hard into both sides until no wet patches show.
Heat the oil in a wide frying pan until a breadcrumb fizzes steadily, not violently; if the oil is lazy the cutlets drink it, if it smokes the spices scorch.
Shallow fry the pork until the underside is deep golden and crisp, then turn once and cook the second side; check the thickest point is piping hot with clear juices before resting.
Pour off all but a spoon of oil, add the tomato and a pinch of chilli, and cook until it collapses into a glossy masala; watery tomato makes the eggs taste thin.
Crack in the eggs, spoon masala oil over the whites until set with soft yolks, then serve beside the crisp cutlets and hot bread before steam softens the crust.

note: This is a Pakistani-spiced breakfast built around pork for the brief, not a traditional everyday Pakistani dish.

name: Saigon Pickled Lamb Herb Platter
hook: Sharp pickles, rosy lamb, fragrant leaves

ingredients.name: daikon or mooli, cut into matchsticks

steps.t: Toss carrot and daikon with rice vinegar, sugar and a pinch of salt, scrunching until the sticks bend slightly; if they stay rigid, they will taste like garnish rather than pickle.
Mix fish sauce, lime juice, chilli, lemongrass and 2 tablespoons of the pickle liquor to make a dressing that tastes bright and salty; if it tastes flat now, the lamb will mute it further.
Pat the lamb completely dry and salt it just before cooking; damp meat boils at the surface and never gets the sweet grilled smell you need.
Heat the oil in a heavy pan until shimmering, then sear the lamb on all sides until the outside is mahogany and the centre still has spring when pressed.
Rest the lamb on a board so the juices settle; cut too soon and the platter floods, washing the dressing off the herbs.
Slice the lamb thinly across the grain, then spoon over half the dressing while it is warm so the edges drink it in without cooking grey.
Drain the pickles, fold them with the herbs, arrange with the lamb, then finish with peanuts and the remaining dressing just before serving so the leaves stay lifted.

note: Serve as a centrepiece with rice crackers or lettuce cups for guests to build their own bites.

name: Sicilian Chickpea and Courgette Teglia
hook: Sunlit beans, lemon, crisp crumbs

steps.t: Heat the oven to 210°C fan and choose a shallow baking dish where the chickpeas sit mostly in one layer; crowd them deep and they stew instead of turning lightly crisp.
In the dish, toss chickpeas, courgettes, tomatoes, onion, garlic, capers, lemon zest, olive oil, salt and black pepper until everything shines.
Spread the mixture out with the tomato cut sides facing up where you can; buried tomatoes dump juice underneath and make the base soggy.
Bake until the courgette edges wrinkle, chickpeas tan at the corners and the onion tips catch a little colour.
Scatter over the breadcrumbs and return to the oven until they turn sandy-gold and dry to the touch; pale crumbs taste bready, dark crumbs dominate the lemon.
Rest the teglia for 5 minutes so the chickpeas absorb the tomato juices rather than leaking them across the plate.
Squeeze over lemon juice, tear on basil and serve warm or room temperature; add the basil earlier and it will blacken in the heat.

note: A light one-dish bake that eats well with salad, grilled bread or chilled white wine.

name: Malabar Slow-Braised Chicken Pepper Fry
hook: Soft chicken, black pepper, glossy onions

steps.t: Salt the chicken well and leave it while you slice the onions; seasoning only at the end leaves the meat bland under a spicy sauce.
Warm the coconut oil in a heavy casserole, add the onions and cook until they slump to deep gold and sweeten; stop at pale yellow and the braise will taste harsh.
Add garlic, ginger, black pepper, coriander, turmeric and curry leaves, stirring until the raw garlic smell disappears; dry spices left sitting on the base will scorch and turn dusty.
Nestle in the chicken and turn it through the onion masala until every piece is stained yellow-brown; bare patches will braise pale and taste separate from the sauce.
Pour in coconut milk, tamarind and 100 ml water, bring to a quiet simmer, then cover and braise until the meat pulls easily from the bone but is not collapsing into strings.
Uncover and simmer briskly until the sauce reduces to a glossy cling rather than a soup; if you rush this over fierce heat, the coconut can split and oil out.
Rest for 5 minutes, scatter with fresh coriander, and serve in small bowls with toothpicks or soft appams so the table can share without wrestling bones.

note: Best as part of a spread with pickles, flatbreads and something crisp.

name: Ember Mushroom Taleggio Piadine
hook: Smoke, gloss, molten cheese

steps.t: Light a small chimney of charcoal and wait until the top coals are ash-grey, not black; if you cook on sooty coals the mushrooms taste acrid instead of smoky.
Toss the mushrooms with olive oil, garlic, balsamic, lemon zest, chilli and salt; coat them lightly rather than soaking them, because dripping oil will flare and scorch the edges.
Grill the mushrooms in a single layer over hot coals until the cut faces go deep bronze and the caps slump; crowding them steams them and you lose the charcoal bite.
Move the mushrooms to the cooler edge, splash with lemon juice and parsley, then taste for salt; if you season only at the end, the thick portobellos stay bland inside.
Warm each piadina on the grate until flexible and faintly blistered, then turn once; leave it too long and it cracks before the cheese melts.
Fill the piadine with Taleggio, hot mushrooms and rocket, fold, then return briefly to the cooler side until the cheese droops; direct fierce heat will leak the filling into the coals.

note: Use a chimney starter to keep this genuinely weeknight-fast.

name: Mustard Scallop Papdi Chaat
hook: Cool scallops, sharp tamarind crunch

steps.t: Rub flour, ghee, ajwain and a pinch of salt together, then add just enough water to make a firm dough; a soft dough drinks oil and gives leathery papdi.
Rest the dough covered until it feels relaxed rather than springy; roll too soon and it snaps back into thick crackers.
Roll the dough thin, prick all over and cut into rough diamonds; missing the pricks makes the papdi balloon instead of frying flat and crisp.
Fry the papdi at 170°C until the bubbles shrink and the edges turn biscuit-gold; too cool makes greasy crackers, too hot browns them before the centre dries.
Blitz coriander, mint, green chilli, mustard seeds, a spoon of yoghurt and salt to a coarse green chutney; over-blitzing warms the herbs and turns the flavour muddy.

Slice each scallop horizontally into two coins, simmer in salted water until the surfaces turn opaque and the centres are just warm, then drain and chill fast; do not serve them glassy-raw, and do not boil them rubbery.
Layer papdi, yoghurt, mustard herb chutney, tamarind, scallops, red onion and chaat masala at the last minute; building early turns the crisp base soggy.

note: The papdi and chutneys can be made a day ahead; cook the scallops on the day.

name: Flame-Hit Mackerel Pad Krapao
hook: Peppery basil, crisp-skinned fish

ingredients.name: green beans, cut into short lengths

steps.t: Cut the mackerel into 3 cm pieces and dust the skin side with cornflour; wet fish sticks and tears, so pat it dry before it touches the wok.
Stir fish sauce and oyster sauce with 2 tablespoons water; if you pour thick sauces straight into a smoking wok, they catch before coating the fish.
Heat the wok until a wisp of smoke appears, add oil, then lay the mackerel skin-side down until the skin grips and turns crisp at the edges; move it early and it shreds.
Lift the fish out, add beans, garlic and chillies, and stir-fry until the beans blister in spots but still squeak; low heat makes them dull and watery.
Return the mackerel with the sauce and toss only until glossy and hot; rough stirring breaks oily fish into flakes instead of keeping chunky pieces.
Tear in Thai basil off the heat and squeeze over lime; cooking the basil hard turns it black and medicinal.
Serve over hot jasmine rice, spooning the wok juices over the top; cold rice drags down the aroma and makes the fish taste oily.

note: Pin-boning matters here because the fish is cooked quickly and eaten in big pieces.

name: Silken Matcha Kuromitsu Purin
hook: Wobbling custard, smoky black sugar

steps.t: Simmer muscovado sugar with 50 ml water until glossy and syrupy, then divide between four heatproof cups; take it too far and it tastes burnt rather than kuromitsu-dark.
Warm milk, cream and caster sugar until steaming but not boiling, then whisk in sifted matcha; boiling milk cooks the eggs on contact and leaves green speckles.
Beat eggs and yolks gently, pour in the warm matcha milk in a thin stream, then stop as soon as blended; frothing now gives a bubbly, pocked custard.
Strain the custard twice into the cups and skim off surface bubbles; skipping this is why purin turns grainy around the rim.
Steam the cups covered over the lowest simmer until the centres wobble like soft jelly, not liquid; hard boiling makes tunnels and a scrambled edge.
Cool, then chill until fully set and cold through; unmoulding warm purin slumps and leaks syrup everywhere.
Run a thin knife around each cup and invert onto plates; forcing it out without loosening tears the custard skin.

note: A folded tea towel under the lid catches drips so the tops stay smooth.

name: Crisp Kimchi Lamb Jeon
hook: Craggy edges, spicy lamb

steps.t: Fry the lamb mince in a dry pan until the fat runs and no pink remains, breaking it small; adding raw mince to the batter risks undercooked pockets inside crisp pancakes.
Stir kimchi, cabbage, gochujang, soy, garlic and spring onions into the hot lamb so the cabbage just wilts; if it stays stiff, the jeon will split when flipped.
Whisk flour, egg and cold water to a loose batter, then fold in the lamb mixture; overmixing wakes the gluten and makes chewy pancakes.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a frying pan until a drop of batter sizzles instantly; lukewarm oil soaks in and gives heavy, greasy jeon.
Spoon in two pancakes and press them thin so the edges turn ragged; thick middles stay stodgy before the outside crisps.
Fry until the underside is deep golden and rigid enough to lift, then flip once; flipping early tears the crust and spills the lamb.
Drain on a rack, scatter sesame seeds over the hot tops and eat straight away; stacking them on a plate traps steam and softens the crunch.

note: Use the fattier supermarket lamb mince here; it seasons the whole pancake cheaply.

name: Coconut Tamarind Mussel & Prawn Stew
hook: Bright broth, sweet shellfish, soft heat

steps.t: Rinse the mussels in cold water, pulling off any beards; throw away cracked ones or any that stay open after a firm tap, because they will not become safe or pleasant in the pot.

Put a wide saucepan on medium heat and fry the curry paste with 2 tablespoons of the thick coconut cream from the tin until it darkens slightly and smells roasted; if it still smells raw and sharp, the stew will taste flat.
Stir in the remaining coconut milk, tamarind, fish sauce and tomatoes, then bring to a lively simmer; do not let it boil hard or the coconut can split and turn oily.
Add the mussels, cover tightly and simmer until most shells spring open and the tomatoes slump into the broth; keep the lid shut or the shellfish will steam unevenly.
Add the prawns and pak choi, re-cover and simmer just until the prawns curl and turn opaque; if they go tight and rubbery, they have gone too far.
Discard any mussels that remain closed, squeeze in lime, and taste for salty-sour balance before scattering with coriander; skipping this last adjustment leaves the coconut heavy.

note: Serve with jasmine rice if you want a fuller dinner; the kcal estimate is for the stew only.

name: Whole Miso-Maple Halloumi with Charred Negi
hook: Bronzed edges, salty centre, smoky onions

steps.t: Soak the whole halloumi block in a bowl of cold water to pull back some salt; if you skip this, the miso glaze can push it into harshness.
Pat the block very dry and score the top in shallow 5 mm cuts, stopping well before the base; cut too deep and the cheese will split open instead of roasting as one piece.
