Whisk miso, mirin, maple syrup, soy, vinegar, sesame oil and ginger until glossy, then coat the halloumi all over and sit it in a small roasting dish; dry patches will roast pale rather than lacquered.
Leave it to marinate in the fridge, turning once halfway so the underside is not bland and rubbery.
Heat the oven to 210°C fan, then roast the halloumi until the glaze bubbles dark at the edges and the scored top opens slightly; pull it before black blisters taste bitter.
Lay the spring onions beside the cheese for the final stretch, turning them when the tips char and the middles soften; if they stay rigid, they will eat raw and sulphurous.
Rest the halloumi for 5 minutes, spoon the sticky tray glaze over it, and finish with sesame seeds; slicing immediately makes the hot centre squeak and shed its glaze.

note: A slow, salty-sweet centrepiece for rice, pickles and a quiet weekend table.

name: Gochujang-Smoked Pork Tenderloin Lettuce Bowls
hook: Lean smoke, chilli glaze, cold crunch

steps.t: Mix gochujang, doenjang, soy, honey, garlic, ginger, vinegar and sesame oil into a thick paste; if it is not fully mixed, the chilli catches in bitter clumps on the smoker.
Coat the pork tenderloins all over and leave them while you light a small charcoal fire with a handful of soaked wood chips; cold meat straight on smoke cooks unevenly.
Set the barbecue for indirect heat at about 120–140°C, with the coals on one side and a drip tray on the other; if the meat sits over direct coals, the sugar burns before the centre is safe.
Smoke the pork away from the coals, lid closed, until the outside is brick-red and the thickest part reads 63–65°C on a probe; guessing by colour alone is risky with pork.
Move the pork briefly over the hot side to set the glaze until it looks tacky and lightly charred at the ridges; leave it too long and the honey turns acrid.
Rest under loose foil so the juices settle instead of flooding the board when sliced.
Slice across the grain into thick coins and serve in lettuce leaves with cucumber and kimchi; cutting with the grain makes even tenderloin feel stringy.

note: Built around lean tenderloin for a high-protein plate without a heavy sauce.

name: Silken Osmanthus Steamed Egg Custard
hook: Wobbly, floral, barely sweet silk

steps.t: Warm the milk, water, sugar and ginger until the sugar dissolves and the liquid smells gently spicy; do not boil it, or hot dairy can curdle the eggs later.
Take the pan off the heat, stir in the osmanthus, and let it steep until the perfume is clear but not grassy.
Beat the eggs in a bowl just until no streaks remain; whisking in lots of foam leaves bubbles and pockmarks in the finished custard.
Strain the warm milk into the eggs slowly, stirring all the time, then strain again into four small heatproof bowls; any unstrained egg threads set into chewy flecks.
Cover each bowl with foil and steam over a low, steady simmer until the custards tremble like soft jelly at the centre; fierce steam makes cratered, rubbery tops.
Turn off the heat and let the covered bowls sit in the steamer so the centres finish gently without overcooking at the edges.
Top with goji berries while warm, then serve warm or chilled; adding them before steaming stains the surface and sinks them into the custard.

note: Use a shallow steam rather than a roaring boil for the smoothest set.

name: Silken Avgolemono Hake with Dill Oil
hook: Lemony steam, velvet broth, pearly fish

ingredients.name: previously frozen skinless hake or cod fillet
waxy potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced

steps.t: Cut the fish into 4 cm pieces and salt it lightly; if the pieces are ragged, they will overcook at the edges before the centre turns silky.
Simmer the stock, potatoes and leek in a wide pan until the potato slices bend easily but do not collapse; hard potato will make the finished bowl feel thin and unfinished.
Stir the garlic into the hot broth for the last minute, just until it smells sweet rather than raw; scorched garlic will bully the lemon.
Whisk the eggs and lemon juice in a bowl until completely smooth, then ladle in hot stock slowly while whisking; rush this and you get scrambled egg threads instead of velvet.
Turn the pan to its lowest heat, slide in the fish, and pour the tempered egg-lemon mixture around it; boiling now will toughen the fish and split the avgolemono.
Cover and barely poach until the fish flakes when pressed but still looks moist and pearly in the centre; leave it longer and it turns chalky.
Mix the olive oil with dill and spoon it over the bowls at the table; adding the dill too early dulls its winter-green snap.

note: Use fish that has been commercially frozen, and cook it gently until just opaque if serving to anyone pregnant, elderly or immunocompromised.

name: Sucuk-Sizzled Menemen Eggs
hook: Peppery eggs with blistered tomato edges

steps.t: Beat the eggs with the salt just until no clear streaks remain; over-whisking makes the curds foamy instead of lush.
Heat a wide frying pan until a drop of water skips, then add the oil, butter and sucuk; if the pan is timid, the sausage leaks grease without crisping.
Stir-fry the sucuk until the rims curl and stain the fat brick-red, then lift a few slices out for the top; miss this cue and the dish tastes boiled.
Throw in the onion and peppers and keep them moving over high heat until the pepper skins blister in spots but still squeak under the spoon.
Add the grated tomato and pul biber and fry hard until the tomato thickens into glossy streaks and no watery puddle follows the spoon.
Pour in the eggs and fold fast from the edges to the centre, stopping when the curds are glossy and softly set; wait until they look dry and they will eat rubbery.
Scatter with parsley and the reserved crisp sucuk, then serve straight from the pan before the eggs tighten.

note: Have bread ready before the eggs go in; the final minute moves quickly.

name: Pomegranate Baharat Beef Skewers
hook: Charred beef, glossy molasses, cool tahini

ingredients.name: beef sirloin or rump, cut into 3 cm cubes

steps.t: Toss the beef with pomegranate molasses, baharat, garlic, half the lemon juice, half the oil and salt; coat every face or the bare patches will scorch blandly.
Leave the beef at room temperature while you make the sauce, but do not park it in a warm spot; cold cubes seize on the griddle and cook unevenly.
Whisk tahini, yoghurt, remaining lemon juice and a splash of water to a spoonable sauce; if it looks grainy, keep whisking with drops of water until it turns satin-smooth.
Thread beef and red onion petals onto skewers, leaving tiny gaps; packed meat steams and never gets the restaurant-style crust.
Heat a ridged griddle until it smokes lightly, oil it, then lay on the skewers; if there is no fierce sizzle, take them off and wait.
Griddle, turning on each face, until the edges are lacquered and char-speckled while the centre still gives slightly under tongs.
Rest the skewers on a warm plate so the juices settle; cut immediately and the board gets the sauce instead of your guests.
Spoon tahini yoghurt on a platter, add skewers, mint and pine nuts, then flick over any resting juices for shine.

note: Metal skewers give the strongest heat transfer; soak wooden ones first if that is what you have.

name: Sherry Escabeche Tofu with Smoked Almonds
hook: Cool vinegar, paprika oil, almond crunch

steps.t: Press the tofu between plates until it sheds its spare water; skip this and the pickle tastes diluted instead of bright.
Cut the tofu into thick dominoes and lay them in a shallow dish in one layer; stacked pieces pickle patchily.
Warm olive oil, garlic and bay in a small pan until the garlic turns pale gold at the edges; dark garlic makes the escabeche bitter.
Take the pan off the heat, then stir in sherry vinegar, smoked paprika, sugar and salt; adding paprika over fierce heat burns its sweetness in seconds.
Pour the warm escabeche over the tofu and piquillo peppers, spooning it across every piece so no dry corners remain.
Leave to pickle until the tofu edges taste tangy and the centre is seasoned but still creamy.
Lift the tofu onto a sharing plate, dress with a little of the escabeche oil, and scatter over smoked almonds, parsley and orange zest; too much liquid on the plate drowns the crunch.

note: Serve cool, not fridge-cold, so the olive oil tastes rounded rather than waxy.

name: Dijon Lamb & White Bean Gratin
hook: Mustardy lamb under crisp herb crumbs

steps.t: Heat the oven to 220°C fan. Put the lamb mince and olive oil in a small baking dish, then break the meat into walnut-sized pieces; if you leave it in a block, the centre steams grey instead of roasting.
Bake on the top shelf until the lamb edges are browned and the fat is sizzling in the corners of the dish.
Stir in the onion, garlic, beans, tomatoes, Dijon mustard and stock, scraping the browned lamb from the base; if the mustard sits in clumps, the sauce tastes sharp in patches.
Return to the oven until the tomatoes slump and the stock bubbles thickly around the beans, not as a watery pool.
Mix the breadcrumbs with parsley and a pinch of salt, scatter evenly over the dish, then press down only lightly; compacted crumbs turn heavy rather than crisp.
Bake until the crumbs are lace-golden and the bean mixture is bubbling up at the edges.
Rest for 3 minutes before serving, so the sauce settles around the beans rather than running across the plate.

note: Use a shallow dish so the lamb browns quickly and the topping crisps.

name: Molasses-Braised Pot Beans
hook: Deep brown beans with smoky sweetness

ingredients.name: dried navy beans or haricot beans

steps.t: Rinse the beans and pick out any small stones; skipping this is how grit ends up in an otherwise soft pot.
Cover the beans with plenty of water, bring to a hard boil, then turn off the heat and leave them to swell until the skins look smooth rather than wrinkled.
Heat the oven to 150°C fan. In a heavy casserole, cook the onion in oil until soft and golden at the edges; pale onion makes the final beans taste flat.
Stir in the garlic, tomato purée, molasses, vinegar, mustard and smoked paprika until the purée darkens and sticks slightly to the pan; if it burns black, scrape it out and start that bit again.
Drain the beans, add them with the bay leaf and hot water, then bring to a simmer on the hob; cold liquid delays the braise and toughens the timing.
Cover and bake until the beans squash easily against the side of the pot but still hold their shape.
Uncover, stir in salt to taste, and bake until the top looks glossy and the liquid clings like gravy, not soup.
Rest for 20 minutes before serving; straight from the oven, the sauce is loose and the heat masks the molasses depth.

note: Salt after the main braise so older beans soften reliably.

name: Chimichurri Chicken & Lentil Guiso
hook: Lean chicken in a bright green stew

ingredients.name: skinless chicken breast, cut into large chunks

steps.t: Season the chicken well. Heat the oil in a wide pot and sear the pieces just until the outside turns opaque with a few golden patches; cooking them through now makes them stringy later.
Lift the chicken to a plate, then add the onion and pepper to the same pot. Cook until the onion is soft and the pepper smells sweet, not raw and grassy.
Stir in the garlic, cumin and smoked paprika for a short sizzle; if the spices sit dry on the base, add a splash of stock before they scorch.
Add the lentils and stock, bring to a steady simmer, then skim any grey foam so the stew tastes clean.
Simmer until the lentils are almost tender with a tiny chalky dot in the centre; fully soft lentils at this point will collapse before the chicken finishes.
Return the chicken and any juices to the pot, then simmer gently until the thickest piece is cooked through and no pink remains inside.
Stir the vinegar and parsley together, fold through the stew off the heat, and taste for salt; boiling the herbs dulls the chimichurri lift.

note: For meal prep, keep extra parsley-vinegar dressing separate and add after reheating.

name: Coconut Quindim Steam Cups
hook: Glossy custard with a coconut chew

ingredients.name: butter, melted, plus extra for greasing

steps.t: Butter six small metal or ceramic moulds thoroughly, especially the bases; missed spots tear the glossy tops when you turn them out.
Whisk the yolks, whole eggs and sugar gently until smooth, not foamy; too much air gives the custard pockmarks instead of a glassy surface.
Stir in the coconut milk, desiccated coconut, melted butter, vanilla and salt, then leave the mixture until the coconut looks hydrated and no longer dusty.
Strain the liquid part through a sieve into a jug, pressing lightly, then stir the coconut left in the sieve back in; this catches eggy strings without losing the chew.
Divide between the moulds and cover each tightly with foil. Set them in a steamer over gently bubbling water; a fierce boil splashes water into the custards.
Steam until the edges are set and the centres wobble like soft jelly, with no liquid sloshing under the foil.
Cool for 20 minutes, then chill until firm enough to unmould cleanly.
Run a thin knife around each cup and invert onto plates; if they resist, warm the base briefly with your hands rather than digging into the custard.

note: They can be steamed a day ahead and kept covered in the fridge.

name: Dhungar Paneer & Chickpea Karahi
hook: Smoky paneer in a tangy tomato pan

steps.t: Heat the oil in a frying pan and brown the paneer on two sides until it has honey-coloured patches; if you keep moving it, it rubs and crumbles instead of crusting.
Lift the paneer out, add the onion, and cook until the edges are deep golden and the middle is soft; pale onion leaves the karahi tasting boiled.
Add the garlic, ginger, cumin, garam masala and chilli powder with a splash of water, stirring until the raw garlic smell disappears; dry spices burn bitter in seconds.
Add the tomatoes and a pinch of salt, then cook hard until the oil separates in small orange beads and the tomatoes no longer look watery.
Stir in the chickpeas and paneer with 100 ml water, simmering until the sauce grips the cubes rather than sliding off them.
Meanwhile, heat the charcoal directly over a gas flame with tongs, or under a grill, until one edge glows red; do not use treated barbecue briquettes or anything with lighter fluid.

Set a small foil cup on top of the curry, place the hot charcoal inside, add the ghee, and immediately cover the pan. Leave it just long enough for a campfire aroma; longer makes the paneer taste ashy.
Remove the charcoal cup carefully, stir once, and serve with rice or flatbread.

note: If you have no charcoal, finish with smoked salt, but the dhungar smoke is the point.

name: Crispy Gochujang Beef Ribbons
hook: Crackly beef, sticky chilli glaze

ingredients.name: thin-cut beef steak, sliced into ribbons

steps.t: Toss the beef with the soy sauce, then work in the potato starch until every ribbon looks dry and dusty; wet patches turn gluey and fry soft instead of crisp.
Stir the gochujang, honey, rice vinegar and sesame oil in a bowl until smooth; if you add it straight to the pan unmixed, the chilli paste catches before the honey melts.
Heat the oil in a wide frying pan until a pinch of starch sizzles sharply on contact; if the oil only murmurs, the beef will drink it and turn heavy.
Shallow fry the beef in two batches, spreading the ribbons apart, until the edges are craggy and deep mahogany; crowding the pan steams the coating off.
Lift the beef to kitchen paper and let it sit for a minute so the crust firms; piling it in a bowl while dripping traps steam and softens the crackle.
Pour off all but a slick of oil, add the sauce and bubble until it looks glossy and leaves a trail through the pan; take it too far and the honey turns bitter.
Return the beef, toss for just long enough to lacquer it, then finish with spring onions and sesame seeds; lingering in the sauce makes the crust chewy.

note: Serve with hot rice and cucumber for a complete weeknight plate.

name: Shanghai Black-Vinegar Pickled Mackerel
hook: Silky fish, sharp ginger gloss

steps.t: Rub the mackerel with salt and Shaoxing wine, then chill it uncovered; this tightens the flesh, while skipping it leaves the fish flabby under the pickle.
Pat the fillets very dry, especially along the skin; surface moisture spits in the oil and stops the skin setting cleanly.
Heat the neutral oil in a non-stick pan and fry the mackerel skin-side down until the skin is taut and blistered, then turn briefly to seal the flesh; undercooked fish will collapse in the jar.
Simmer the vinegar, soy, sugar, ginger, spring onions and star anise until the sugar dissolves and the steam smells rounded rather than raw; a cold brine tastes harsh and thin.
Pack the hot fish into a clean container and pour over the hot pickle to cover; if pieces sit above the liquid, they dry and taste metallic.
Cool quickly, cover and refrigerate for two days so the vinegar reaches the centre; eating it the same day gives sharp edges and bland flesh.
Lift the fish out, spoon over a little pickle and dress with chilli oil and fresh slivers of ginger if you like; drowning it hides the mackerel’s clean oiliness.

note: This is cooked before pickling, so it is safe for a weekend make-ahead cold dish.

name: Chipotle Tofu Enchilada Protein Bake
hook: Smoky slabs under bubbling cheese

steps.t: Heat the oven to 210°C fan and use a deep baking dish; a shallow tray dries the sauce before the tofu heats through.
Crumble the tofu into chunky curds with your hands and blot with kitchen paper; if it goes in dripping wet, the bake tastes steamed rather than roasted.
Mix passata, chipotle paste and cumin directly in the dish until brick-red and even; streaks of paste give random bitter-hot mouthfuls.
Fold in the tofu, black beans, sweetcorn, torn tortillas and half the onion, making sure the tortilla pieces are coated; dry corners bake into tough chips.
Scatter over the cheese and remaining onion, then bake until the sauce bubbles hard at the edges and the cheese has bronze freckles.
Rest the bake until the bubbling drops to a gentle sigh; cutting immediately makes the sauce run and the layers slump.
Finish with coriander and a squeeze of lime; adding them before baking turns the herbs dull and the lime bitter.

note: Black beans and tofu keep the protein high without making the bake heavy.

name: Mastiha Steamed Honey Egg Custards
hook: Quivering custard, piney honey perfume

steps.t: Set a steamer over barely simmering water and wrap the lid in a clean tea towel; fierce steam or dripping condensation leaves pitted, watery custards.
Warm the milk with sugar, honey, mastiha, vanilla and salt until steaming but not boiling; boiling milk scrambles the eggs the moment it hits them.
Whisk the eggs just until loosened, not frothy, then slowly pour in the warm milk while whisking; foam bakes into bubbles and a sudden pour makes sweet scrambled egg.
Strain the custard into four small heatproof bowls; unstrained chalazae and mastiha specks set as rubbery flecks.
Cover each bowl with foil and steam gently until the centres wobble like soft jelly, not liquid milk.
Turn off the heat and leave the bowls in the closed steamer so the custard finishes softly; lifting them straight out can shock the surface into cracks.
Serve warm or cool with pistachios and an extra thread of honey; heavy toppings sink if the custard is still loose.

note: Mastiha is potent, so keep it restrained for a clean Greek finish.

name: Bulgur Mercimek Nohut Yahnisi
hook: Tomato-rich pulses, lemon-bright warmth

steps.t: Soften the onion in olive oil over a medium heat until it smells sweet and the edges turn translucent; rushing it leaves harsh raw onion in the finished stew.
Stir in the tomato paste and pul biber and cook until the paste darkens to rusty red; if it stays bright, the stew tastes tinny.
Add the rinsed lentils, chickpeas, bulgur and stock, scraping the base so the tomato paste dissolves; stuck paste scorches as the stew thickens.
Simmer with the lid ajar, stirring often, until the lentils collapse and the bulgur is tender with a slight chew; unattended bulgur catches at the bottom.
Adjust with a splash of water if it stands like porridge; the right texture is spoonable and glossy, not sliceable.
Squeeze in lemon and rest the stew off the heat so the pulses settle and thicken evenly; boiling after the lemon dulls its lift.
Finish with parsley and a final pinch of pul biber; adding parsley early turns it khaki and flat.

note: Made from cupboard pulses, this keeps well and reheats with a little water.

name: Za’atar Clementine Roast Chicken with Freekeh Drippings
hook: Bronzed skin, citrus steam, spiced gravy

steps.t: Take the chicken out of the fridge 30 minutes before roasting; a fridge-cold bird tightens in the oven and cooks unevenly at the thigh joint.

Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Rub the chicken all over with za’atar, allspice, salt and 3 tbsp olive oil, getting into the leg creases; if the spice sits in dry clumps, it will scorch rather than perfume the skin.

Tip the freekeh, onions, garlic, stock and 1 tbsp olive oil into a deep roasting tin. Set the chicken on top and tuck the clementines around it, cut-side up; if the grain is not fully wet, the top layer will stay hard.

Roast for 70 minutes, basting the breast twice with the orange-gold pan juices, until the skin is mahogany and the thickest part of the thigh reads 74°C; stop early and the joints will be pink, go too long and the breast dries out.
Lift the chicken to a warm board and rest it uncovered for 15 minutes; covering it traps steam and softens the skin you worked for.
Stir pomegranate molasses through the freekeh and return the tin to the oven for 8 minutes, until the grains are swollen and glossy rather than soupy.
Carve the chicken, squeeze over the roasted clementines, scatter with parsley and spoon the sticky freekeh drippings beside it.

note: Use a thermometer at the thigh for confidence; whole chickens vary more than timings do.

name: Smoked Mackerel Chermoula Breakfast Hash
hook: Crisp potatoes, smoky flakes, runny yolks

ingredients.name: waxy potatoes, cut into 2 cm cubes
preserved lemon quarter, flesh discarded, rind finely chopped

steps.t: Simmer the potatoes in salted water until a knife slides in but the corners still hold; overcook them now and they will collapse into mash in the pan.
Drain well and let them steam dry in the colander for 3 minutes, shaking once; wet potatoes spit in oil and refuse to crisp.
Heat the olive oil in a wide frying pan and fry the potatoes until the cut faces turn deep golden and sound dry against the pan.

Add the red pepper, cumin, paprika, harissa and preserved lemon, then cook until the pepper softens and the spices smell warm rather than dusty; if the pan looks dry, splash in a spoon of water before the paprika burns.
Flake in the smoked mackerel in large pieces and fold gently; stir hard and the fish disappears into salty shreds.
Make two hollows, crack in the eggs, cover the pan and cook until the whites are just set and the yolks still wobble under the lid.
Finish with coriander and lemon juice, tasting before adding more salt because smoked mackerel and preserved lemon already bring plenty.

note: Best eaten straight from the pan with warm khobz or toast.

name: Saffron-Steam Halloumi Piquillo Parcels
hook: Salty cheese, saffron vapour, almond crunch

ingredients.name: lemon, zested and cut into wedges

steps.t: Soak the saffron in the fino sherry for 10 minutes; adding dry threads straight to the parcel leaves expensive red specks with little aroma.
Lay out four large sheets of baking parchment and divide the piquillos and courgette between them, keeping the pile low and central so steam can circulate rather than pool at one end.
Set two halloumi slices on each pile, dust with smoked paprika and a very small pinch of salt; heavy salting makes halloumi harsh, especially as it warms.
Spoon over the saffron sherry and olive oil, then fold each parcel with tight crimped edges; loose folds leak the saffron liquor into the steamer.
Steam the parcels over briskly simmering water until they puff and smell of sherry, saffron and warm peppers; if the water is boiling violently, it can splash into the parcels and dilute the sauce.
Rest the parcels for 2 minutes before opening, keeping faces away from the first burst of steam.
Serve opened at the table with almonds, lemon zest, parsley and lemon wedges, spooning the golden juices back over the cheese before they soak into the paper.

note: This is about softening halloumi, not melting it; it should be tender and squeaky, with a fragrant liquor.

name: Charcoal Pork Paillards with Tarragon Peaches
hook: Smoke-kissed pork, juicy peach, mustard bite

ingredients.name: ripe peaches, stoned and cut into wedges

steps.t: Light the barbecue and let the coals turn grey with a few red cores; flames lick soot onto lean pork before the centre cooks.
Slice the pork fillet on a slant into 8 pieces, then flatten each between baking paper to about 8 mm; uneven paillards give you dry edges and underdone middles.
Whisk Dijon, olive oil, vinegar, honey, salt and pepper, then coat the pork lightly; a thick mustard layer burns bitter over coals.
Grill the peach wedges first until they have dark stripes and just start to slump, then move them to a platter; if they collapse completely, the salad turns jammy.
Grill the pork over direct coals until the edges tighten and the underside releases cleanly, then turn once and cook until just firm with clear juices.
Rest the pork for 5 minutes on the peach platter so the juices settle into the dressing rather than run across the board.
Toss rocket, tarragon and shallot through the warm peaches, lay the pork on top and spoon over any mustardy juices from the platter.

note: Pork fillet is lean; keep the pieces thin and the fire hot so it stays tender.

name: Everything Salmon Crudo with Rye Crisps
hook: Cold salmon, onion snap, sesame crunch

ingredients.name: sashimi-grade salmon fillet, previously frozen, skinless and pin-boned
small red onion, very thinly sliced

steps.t: Keep the salmon chilled until the last moment and work on a clean board; warm raw fish smears under the knife and is not worth the risk.
Stir the sour cream with horseradish and a pinch of salt, then chill it while you slice; if it sits warm, the clean bite turns heavy.
Slice the salmon across the grain into 5 mm pieces with one long pull of a sharp knife; sawing ragged edges makes the platter look tired.
Arrange the salmon on a cold plate in a single layer, leaving small gaps so the dressing hits each slice rather than pooling at the rim.
Whisk lemon juice, sesame oil and capers, then spoon it over the fish just before serving; dress too early and the lemon cures the surface chalky.
Scatter with red onion, chives and everything seasoning, using your fingers from height so the sesame and poppy seeds spread evenly instead of clumping.
Serve immediately with rye crackers and horseradish cream for building small bites at the table.

note: Buy salmon sold for raw eating from a trusted fishmonger and keep it refrigerated until plating.

name: Chimichurri Wok Verduras
hook: Charred edges, sharp herbs, weeknight speed

steps.t: Mix parsley, oregano, vinegar, chilli flakes, garlic, 1 tbsp oil and a pinch of salt in a bowl; if you add the herbs to the pan later, they scorch and turn dusty.
Heat a wok or largest frying pan until a drop of water skitters and vanishes; a merely warm pan makes the vegetables leak and stew.
Add 1 tbsp oil, then the onion and pepper. Stir-fry hard until the onion edges blister purple-brown but the centres still look glossy.
Add the courgette in one layer as much as possible. Leave it alone briefly, then toss; moving it constantly stops the cut sides catching colour.
Tip in the sweetcorn and keep the heat fierce until some kernels freckle dark gold and the pan smells toasted, not watery.
Pull the pan off the heat, scrape in the chimichurri and toss for 20 seconds; cooking it hard kills the parsley brightness.
Taste for salt and vinegar, then plate immediately while the courgette still has snap; sitting in the wok makes it collapse.

note: Serve with crusty bread or quick rice if you want it more filling, but keep the vegetables the lead.

name: Banana-Leaf Moqueca Griddled Hake
hook: Coconut-slick fish with smoky lime edges

steps.t: Stir coconut milk, lime juice, garlic, 1 tbsp dendê and salt together, then coat the hake. Chill it covered; leaving fish in a sharp marinade all day makes the flakes chalky, so keep it to 1 hour.
Warm the banana leaves over a dry hob flame or hot pan until flexible and glossy; cold leaves split and dump the marinade on the griddle.
Melt the butter in a frying pan, add cassava flour and stir until it smells nutty and looks like damp sand with golden specks; pale farofa tastes raw and squeaky.
Lay onion and pepper on each banana leaf, place the drained hake on top, spoon over a little marinade and fold into snug parcels; loose parcels steam weakly and the fish dries at the edges.
Heat a heavy griddle until properly hot, then set the parcels seam-side down. You want a faint leaf char smell, not black smoke.
Griddle the parcels, turning once, until the leaf is browned in patches and the hake flakes at the thickest point with gentle pressure.
Rest the parcels off the heat so the coconut juices settle; opening at once sends the sauce across the board.
Open at the table, drizzle with the remaining dendê, scatter coriander over and spoon farofa alongside before it softens.

note: Banana leaf gives the weekend drama; baking paper works, but you lose the grassy smoke.

name: Lahori Crisp Mushroom Besan Cutlets
hook: Crunchy caps, chilli heat, cooling mint

steps.t: Pat the mushrooms very dry, especially under the caps; trapped moisture blows holes in the coating and makes the oil spit.
Whisk gram flour, eggs, cumin, coriander, chilli, ajwain, 0.5 tsp salt and 3 tbsp water into a thick batter that drops slowly from the whisk; thin batter slides off and fries bare patches.
Stir yoghurt with mint, lemon juice and the remaining salt, then chill it; warm yoghurt tastes flat next to the hot crust.
Heat the oil in a wide frying pan until a drip of batter bubbles at once and floats; if it sinks, the cutlets drink oil before they crisp.
Dip each mushroom fully in batter, let the excess trail off, then lay it cap-side down in the oil. Do not crowd the pan or the crust steams soft.
Shallow fry until the underside is deep golden and rigid enough to lift without tearing, then turn once; fiddling early strips the besan shell away.
Fry the second side until crisp at the rim and the mushroom feels juicy but not floppy when pressed.
Drain on a rack, not kitchen paper, and eat with the mint yoghurt; paper traps steam and softens the crunch you just built.

note: Eggs, gram flour and yoghurt push the protein up while keeping the mushroom centre savoury and moist.

name: Cà Phê Steamed Egg Caramel
hook: Silky custard, bitter coffee caramel

steps.t: Put 70 g sugar and the coffee in a small pan and cook until the bubbles slow and the caramel smells roasty; taking it pale makes it sugary, taking it black makes the whole custard harsh.
Divide the caramel between four heatproof ramekins and swirl quickly to cover the bases; it sets fast, and scraping it later makes lumps.
Warm the milk with condensed milk until steaming but not boiling; boiling milk scrambles the eggs on contact.
Whisk eggs, yolks, remaining sugar, vanilla and salt just until smooth, then slowly whisk in the warm milk. Do not whip foam in, or the custard steams with bubbles.
Strain the custard into the ramekins, cover each tightly with foil and set in a steamer over a gentle simmer; hard boiling gives pocked, rubbery sides.
Steam until the edges are set and the centres wobble like soft jelly when nudged.
Lift out, uncover and cool, then chill until fully cold; unmoulding warm custard breaks it at the caramel line.
Run a thin knife round each ramekin and invert onto plates, letting the coffee caramel flood over the top.

note: A gentle simmer is the difference between satin and sponge.

name: Sardine Tomato Riso al Forno
hook: Crisp top, oily fish, sweet tomato

ingredients.name: sardines in olive oil, about 120 g each

steps.t: Heat the oven to 200°C fan and oil a medium baking dish; an unheated oven stretches the bake and leaves the rice chalky.
Tip rice, tomatoes, onion, garlic, oregano, chilli, salt and hot stock into the dish, then stir until the rice is evenly spread; dry mounds of rice stay hard.
Cover the dish tightly with foil and bake until the liquid is bubbling at the edges and the rice is almost tender, with a little bite in the middle.
Flake the sardines into large pieces, keeping some of their oil, and fold them through gently; smashing them to paste makes the whole bake taste muddy.
Mix breadcrumbs, cheese and 1 tbsp sardine oil or olive oil, then scatter over the top; dry crumbs brown in patches and taste dusty.
Return uncovered to the oven until the top is crisp gold and tomato bubbles push up around the sides.
Rest for 5 minutes before spooning out; serving straight away makes it slump and burn mouths while the rice finishes absorbing sauce.

note: Tinned sardines keep it cheap, rich and properly Italian in spirit.

name: Black Cardamom Braised Tofu Makhani
hook: Smoke, butter and tomato-soaked tofu

ingredients.name: firm tofu, pressed and cut into large cubes

steps.t: Warm the ghee in a heavy pan and sear the tofu on two broad sides until it has tawny patches; if you keep moving it, the cubes tear before they build a skin.
Lift out the tofu, add the onions and cook until they collapse into sticky bronze strands; pale onions leave the sauce sharp and thin.
Stir in ginger, garlic, black cardamom, garam masala and chilli powder until the pan smells smoky and sweet; if the spices catch black, they will make the whole braise bitter.
Pour in the passata, rinse the carton with 100 ml water and add it, scraping the base clean; any browned spice left stuck underneath will scorch during the long simmer.
Return the tofu, cover with the lid slightly ajar and braise gently until the sauce darkens to brick-red and clings to the spoon; a hard boil makes the tofu rubbery and splits the tomato.
Stir in the cream, kasuri methi and salt, then simmer uncovered until glossy orange fat freckles the edge; if you rush this, it tastes like cream poured over tomatoes.
Rest off the heat for 10 minutes before serving, because straight from the hob the tofu has not finished drinking in the sauce.

note: Best with naan or steamed basmati and a spoonful of lime pickle.

name: Morning Market Coconut Pumpkin Stew
hook: Golden broth, herbs, soft pumpkin

ingredients.name: pumpkin or squash, peeled and cut into chunks
palm sugar or light brown sugar

steps.t: Fry the curry paste in the oil until it darkens and beads of red oil appear; if it only warms through, the stew tastes dusty rather than rounded.
Whisk in a splash of coconut milk first, then the rest, so the paste loosens smoothly; dumping it all in at once leaves gritty red flecks.
Add the stock, pumpkin, soy sauce and sugar, then simmer until a knife slides into the pumpkin but the edges still hold their shape; overcooked pumpkin turns the broth baby-food thick.
Add the green beans and tomatoes and simmer until the beans squeak less but stay bright; if they go khaki, the whole bowl tastes tired.
Turn off the heat and sharpen with lime juice a little at a time; boiling lime juice flattens its perfume and makes the coconut taste heavy.
Spoon hot rice into bowls, ladle the stew around it and tear herbs over the top; chopping the herbs too early bruises them black on a warm morning.

note: Breakfast-friendly because it is gentle, brothy and filling without feeling heavy.

name: Whole-Roasted Miso Kabocha with Adzuki-Sesame Crumble
hook: A burnished squash centrepiece with crunch

ingredients.name: kabocha or small crown prince squash

steps.t: Heat the oven to 190°C and scrub the squash well, because the skin becomes part of the dish and grit has nowhere to hide.
Cut a neat lid around the stalk, scoop out the seeds and rub the inside with a pinch of salt; if the cavity stays wet and stringy, the filling steams rather than roasts.
Whisk miso, mirin, soy and rapeseed oil, then brush the squash inside and out until it looks lacquered; thick unmixed miso burns in salty patches.
Set the squash and lid on a lined tray and roast until the skin is glossy, the sides yield to a skewer and the base is soft but not collapsing; under-roast it and guests fight the knife.
Meanwhile toast panko and sesame seeds in a dry pan until the crumbs are deep gold and smell nutty; pale crumbs disappear against the beans, but dark brown sesame tastes acrid.
Fold adzuki beans with rice vinegar, sesame oil, spring onions and half the crumb, keeping the beans mostly whole; mashing them makes the centre heavy and dull.
Spoon the adzuki mixture into the roasted squash, return it to the oven until the filling is hot at the centre, then finish with the remaining crumble; serving it lukewarm blunts the miso aroma.

note: Bring it to the table whole, then cut into wedges like a savoury cake.

name: Tea-Smoked Chicken with Cucumber Naengchae
hook: Cool cucumber under smoky sliced chicken

steps.t: Put the chicken in a pan, cover with cold water and bring just to a tremble; a rolling boil tightens the meat before it cooks through.
Simmer gently until the thickest part reaches 74°C or the juices run clear with no pinkness, then rest it on a rack; smoking undercooked chicken is unsafe, and slicing hot chicken leaks it dry.
Line a wok or deep pan with foil, add tea, rice and brown sugar, then set a rack above it; without foil, the sugar welds itself to the pan.
Heat until the mixture smokes steadily, add the cooked chicken, cover tightly and smoke until the outside turns pale amber; too long gives a bitter ashtray edge.
Toss cucumbers with vinegar, gochugaru, sesame oil, soy and honey until glossy; salting them far ahead dumps water into the dressing and makes the plate limp.
Slice the chicken across the grain into thin pieces, because long fibres make even juicy breast feel stringy.
Pile the cucumber on a chilled plate, lay over the smoked chicken and finish with spring onions and sesame seeds; if you dress the plate too early, the cucumbers flood it.

note: Serve cool rather than fridge-cold so the smoke and sesame still come through.

name: Steamed Clams with Black Bean-Ginger Sizzled Oil
hook: Briny shells, sizzling garlic, glossy sauce

ingredients.name: fermented black beans, rinsed and chopped

steps.t: Rinse the clams in several changes of cold water and discard any cracked ones or open shells that do not close when tapped; bad shellfish cannot be rescued by sauce.
Set a steamer over fast-boiling water and spread the clams in a shallow heatproof dish; piling them deep makes the bottom ones overcook before the top ones open.
Scatter over black beans, garlic and ginger, then spoon on Shaoxing wine, soy and sugar; clumps of black bean give harsh salty bites.
Steam until the shells spring open and the liquor is bubbling around them; keep the lid shut or the steam drops and the clams toughen while you wait.
Remove the dish and discard any clams that remain closed, because forcing them open is not worth the risk.
Top with spring onions and chilli, heat the oil until it shimmers, then pour it over the aromatics so they hiss and perfume the shellfish; lukewarm oil just makes everything greasy.
Spoon the black bean juices back over the shells and serve at once; if they sit, the clams shrink and the sauce turns too salty.

note: Set out cocktail sticks or small forks and plenty of napkins for the table.

name: Coal-Grilled Tajín Halloumi Tacos
hook: Smoke, lime, squeaky salty cheese

steps.t: Light the coals and wait until they are glowing with a thin grey ash; if you cook over flames, the halloumi scorches before the centre softens.
Toss the halloumi with olive oil and Tajín, coating the edges as well as the faces; dry patches stick hard to the grill bars.
Mash the avocado with half the lime juice and a pinch of salt until chunky, not smooth; overworked avocado goes pasty and dull.
Mix the cabbage, sweetcorn, coriander and remaining lime juice, then squeeze it once with your hands; if it sits unseasoned, the taco tastes flat and watery.
Stir the yoghurt with chipotle paste and a pinch of salt; taste it now, because once the tacos are built you cannot fix a bland sauce.
Grill the halloumi for 90 seconds per side, until the ridges are deep bronze and the cheese bends without collapsing; move it too early and it tears.
Warm the tortillas on the grill for 20 seconds a side, just until floppy with a few toasted freckles; leave them longer and they turn brittle.
Build each tortilla with avocado, cabbage, grilled halloumi and chipotle yoghurt, then serve at once while the cheese is still squeaky.

note: Paneer also works, but salt it lightly and grill a little longer because it does not bring halloumi’s brine.

name: Santorini Tomato-Water Scallop Crudo
hook: Cold scallops, briny tomato clarity

ingredients.name: small red onion, very thinly sliced

steps.t: The day before, mix the tomatoes with the salt, then tip them into a muslin-lined sieve over a bowl; pressing makes the water cloudy, so let gravity do the work.
Chill the dripping tomato water for 12–15 hours until you have a clear, fragrant bowlful; if it smells fermented rather than fresh, do not use it.
Toss the red onion with the vinegar and set aside until it turns glossy pink; raw onion left untreated will bully the scallops.
Check the scallops are labelled suitable for raw eating, smell clean and sweet, and keep them cold until the last moment; citrus does not make unsafe shellfish safe.
Slice each scallop into three coins with a sharp knife, wiping the blade if it drags; ragged slices warm up quickly and lose their clean texture.
Season the tomato water with lemon zest, a little lemon juice, olive oil and oregano, whisking until it looks lightly pearled; too much lemon will turn the scallops chalky.
Spoon cucumber, olives and pickled onion into cold shallow bowls, lay the scallops on top, and pour the tomato water around rather than over them so they stay glossy.
Finish with dill and crushed barley rusk right before serving; add the crumbs early and they swell into paste.

note: This is a project because the tomato water needs an overnight drip, not because the final assembly is difficult.

name: İzmir Egg-White Sucuk Skillet
hook: Peppery eggs with gym-day bite

ingredients.name: spring onions, cut into 3 cm lengths
low-fat süzme yoghurt or thick Greek yoghurt

steps.t: Put a wide frying pan or wok over high heat until a drop of water skitters away; if the pan is only warm, the eggs stew instead of catching in soft curds.
Add the oil and sucuk, then stir-fry until the slices curl and leak red fat at the edges; stop before they blacken, because burnt sucuk tastes bitter fast.
Throw in the peppers and spring onions and keep them moving until blistered in spots but still crisp; overcrowding or gentle heat makes them limp and wet.
Push everything aside, fry the tomato paste and pul biber in the red oil until the paste darkens by a shade; raw paste leaves a tinny taste.
Beat the egg whites with the whole eggs and a pinch of salt, then pour them into the pan in one go; adding them slowly gives rubbery streaks.
Stir-fry with broad folds until the eggs are just set and still shiny in the creases; if they look dry in the pan, they will be tougher on the plate.
Take the pan off the heat, dot with yoghurt and parsley, and eat immediately; yoghurt added over heat splits and turns grainy.

note: High heat and a wide pan are the difference between a lively Turkish-style scramble and a damp omelette.

name: Orange Blossom Steamed Labneh Custards
hook: Silken wobble, honeyed flower perfume

steps.t: Whisk the eggs and sugar just until the sugar loosens, not until foamy; trapped bubbles steam into little holes instead of a smooth custard.
Warm the milk until it feels hot but not boiling, then whisk it slowly into the eggs; pour too fast and you scramble the base.
Whisk in the labneh, orange blossom water, cardamom and salt until smooth, then strain into a jug; unstrained labneh leaves tiny curds in the finished custard.
Divide between four small heatproof bowls and cover each tightly with foil; uncovered bowls collect drips from the lid and turn watery on top.
Set the bowls in a steamer over gently simmering water, not a rolling boil, and steam until the centres wobble like set jelly; fierce steam makes the edges spongy.
Lift the bowls out and rest for 10 minutes, still covered, so the heat finishes the centres; peel the foil off straight away and the surface wrinkles.
Chill until cold and softly set; serving warm makes the orange blossom taste harsh and the texture loose.
Warm the honey with lemon juice until runny, spoon it over the custards, and finish with pistachios; add nuts too early and they lose their snap.

note: Orange blossom water varies hugely, so measure rather than free-pour.

name: Chermoula-Crisp Hake Flatbreads
hook: Crackly fish, cumin-green sauce

ingredients.name: frozen hake fillets, defrosted and patted dry

steps.t: Pat the hake very dry and cut it into fat fingers; wet fish spits in the pan and steams under the coating.
Mix lemon zest, half the lemon juice, cumin, paprika, garlic, coriander and a pinch of salt into a rough chermoula; if it tastes shy now, the fish will too.
Rub half the chermoula over the hake and leave it while you set up the coating; marinating for ages in lemon makes cheap white fish mushy.
Mix the flour and semolina, then coat each piece of fish firmly and shake off the excess; clumps fall into the oil and burn black.
Heat the oil in a frying pan until a pinch of coating fizzes instantly; if the oil is dull, the crust drinks it and turns greasy.
Shallow fry the fish for 2 minutes per side, until the crust is sandy-gold and crisp and the flakes split easily; crowd the pan and the coating softens.
Stir the carrot with the remaining lemon juice and a pinch of salt, and mix the yoghurt with the remaining chermoula; undressed carrot tastes like homework.
Warm the flatbreads, pile in carrot, crisp hake and chermoula yoghurt, then eat while the edges still crackle.

note: Pollock or basa fillets work too; the semolina keeps the crust crisp even on budget frozen fish.

name: Hanoi Winter Mắm Chưng Pork Pot
hook: Steam-soft pork under golden egg

steps.t: Soak the wood ear mushrooms and glass noodles in just-boiled water until floppy; if the centres still feel wiry, they will stay squeaky in the finished steam pot.
Start the jasmine rice with 450 ml water so it can rest while the pork steams; if you leave it until the end, the custard sits around and weeps.
Drain well, snip the noodles short and chop the mushrooms finely; long strands pull the pork apart instead of letting it slice cleanly.

Mix pork, shallots, garlic, ginger, fish sauce, sugar, pepper, four whole eggs and the white from the fifth egg until the mince turns sticky; if it looks loose and separate, the custard will set patchily.
Spoon into a shallow heatproof dish no deeper than 4 cm and level the top; a deep mound overcooks at the edges before the middle is safe and set.
Steam over a steady simmer until the surface feels springy and the juices at the centre run clear with no pink pork; a violent boil makes the egg honeycomb and tough.
Beat the reserved yolk, brush it over the top and steam uncovered until matte-gold; if you cover it again, condensation freckles the surface with water marks.
Rest for five minutes, then spoon over rice with spring onions; cutting straight away sends the savoury juices across the board instead of back into the pork.

note: A heatproof ceramic or metal dish that fits inside your steamer works best.

name: Tuscan Coal-Grilled Mushroom Breakfast Slabs
hook: Smoky mushrooms, yolk-soaked toast

steps.t: Light the charcoal and cook it down to ash-grey coals with no tall flames; flames lick the mushrooms with soot before they have time to sweeten.
Toss the dry mushrooms with 45 ml oil, garlic, rosemary and salt; rinsed or wet mushrooms steam in their own puddle instead of taking on coal smoke.
Grill the mushrooms in a single layer until the cut sides go chestnut and the edges curl; if you keep moving them, they never build that breakfast crust.
Brush the sourdough with the remaining oil and grill until the ridges are dark and crisp; pale toast collapses once yolk and mushroom juices hit it.
Set a cast-iron pan on the grill and fry the eggs until the whites are fully set and the yolks still wobble; a lukewarm pan makes rubbery whites with oily edges.
Pile mushrooms on the toast, crown with eggs, then finish with lemon zest, a squeeze of juice, pecorino and parsley; lemon added earlier makes the mushrooms leak and lose their char.

note: Porcini are lovely here, but chestnut, oyster and portobello mushrooms give a more realistic supermarket mix.

name: Udaipur Jewel Kachumber
hook: Cold crunch, scarlet tamarind sparkle

steps.t: Whisk lime juice, tamarind, chaat masala, cumin and green chilli until smooth; dry spice clumps taste dusty and hit the tongue in one harsh patch.
Slice the red onion very thinly and soak it in cold water; without the soak it shouts over the beetroot and pomegranate.
Shave beetroot, cucumber and radishes into thin coins or ribbons; thick pieces eat like a raw vegetable platter, not a polished kachumber.
Pat the cucumber and radishes dry with kitchen paper; surface water dilutes the tamarind and leaves a pink puddle on the platter.
Drain the onion and toss the vegetables with the dressing only when you are ready to serve; dressed too early, the beetroot stains everything flat red and the crunch fades.
Spread shallowly on a wide platter and scatter pomegranate, coriander and mint over the top; a deep bowl hides the jewels and leaves the bottom soggy.

note: Use a mandoline if you have one, with the guard every time.

name: Miso-Butter Teppan Mushrooms with Ponzu Scallions
hook: Browned caps, glossy miso butter

ingredients.name: mixed mushrooms, such as shiitake, oyster and king oyster

steps.t: Mix miso, soy sauce and mirin into a smooth paste; miso lumps make salty spots that scorch on the griddle.
Tear the mushrooms into large pieces and keep them dry; tiny or rinsed pieces leak water and turn grey instead of meaty.
Heat a flat griddle until a water droplet dances across it; if it sits and steams, the first batch will steam too.
Oil the griddle, lay mushrooms in a single layer and press them down until the undersides turn chestnut; fussing with them stops the crust forming.
Turn the mushrooms and add butter around the edges so it foams and smells nutty; adding butter at the start burns it before the mushrooms brown.
Spoon over the miso paste and toss until every piece is glossy; more than half a minute makes the mirin sugars catch and taste bitter.
Slide onto a plate, then add ponzu, spring onions, sesame and shichimi; ponzu poured onto the hot griddle flashes away before it can brighten the mushrooms.

note: Serve with cocktail sticks or small forks so people can graze while the mushrooms are still hot.

name: Lahori Crisp Chana Tikki
hook: Golden edges, cumin heat, lemon snap

steps.t: Tip the chickpeas into a bowl and crush with a fork until half paste and half rubble; if you leave them whole, the tikkis split in the pan.
Mix in onion, chilli, coriander, cumin, garam masala, gram flour, half the lemon juice and salt; squeeze a handful and check it holds rather than crumbles dry.
Shape into 6 squat patties, pressing the edges firmly smooth; ragged edges burn before the centres warm through.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat until a crumb of mixture sizzles straight away; if the oil is only warm, the patties drink it and turn heavy.
Fry the patties without crowding until the undersides are deep golden with crisp lace-brown rims, then turn once only so they do not break.
Cook the second side until crisp and hot through, then lift onto kitchen paper; leaving them in the pan after crisping makes the crust soften.
Stir yoghurt with the remaining lemon juice and a pinch of salt, then spoon it over or alongside the tikkis while they are still crackly.

note: Fast tinned chickpeas make this weeknight-friendly; gram flour is the small insurance policy against collapse.

name: Hanoi Lotus Leaf Steamed Chicken
hook: Fragrant rice, silky chicken, herbal steam

steps.t: Soak the glutinous rice in cold water for 1 hour; skipping this gives hard chalky grains no matter how long you steam it.
Soak the lotus leaves in hot water until pliable and tea-scented, then rinse both sides well because grit hides in the folds.
Cut chicken thighs into large bite-sized pieces and mix with fish sauce, soy, sugar, ginger and sesame oil; coat every piece or some will taste flat after steaming.
Drain the rice until it stops dripping, then toss it with the mushrooms and half the spring onions; wet rice clumps into a dense brick.
Line a steamer basket with the softened lotus leaves, glossy side up, add rice, then chicken on top, and fold the leaves over tightly so the steam perfumes instead of washing the filling.
Steam over steadily boiling water, topping up the pan if needed, until the rice is tender and the chicken is piping hot with clear juices; a lazy simmer leaves the centre stubbornly raw.
Rest the parcel off the heat so the rice settles, then open carefully away from your face and finish with coriander and the remaining spring onions.

note: Use a wide steamer so the parcel sits in one even layer; thick mounds cook unevenly.

name: Calabrian Coal-Grilled Prawns with Lemon Beans
hook: Charred shells, chilli oil, clean protein

steps.t: Light the coals and wait until they are covered in grey ash with no licking flames; flames scorch the shells before the prawns cook.
Pat the prawns very dry, then toss with half the oil, garlic, chilli, lemon zest, salt and pepper; wet shells steam and never pick up that sweet char.
Warm the beans gently with a splash of water, lemon juice and a pinch of salt until creamy at the edges but not collapsing into mash.
Spread the prawns on the grill in a single layer and do not move them until the shells turn coral and show black pinstripes from the bars.
Turn the prawns and grill until the flesh is opaque at the thickest part; pull them late and they tighten into rubber.
Fold parsley and the remaining olive oil through the beans, then pile over rocket so the leaves just wilt rather than slump.
Serve the prawns on top with extra lemon; keep the shells on for flavour, but peel at the table so the juices stay with the meal.

note: For gym-friendly eating, this keeps the fat moderate and the protein high without losing the coal-grilled flavour.

name: Saffron Elaichi Steamed Egg Bhapa
hook: Soft custard, cardamom warmth, saffron gloss

steps.t: Warm 50 ml milk with saffron and crushed cardamom until steaming, then take it off the heat; boiling drives off the perfume and leaves flat sweetness.
Whisk eggs, condensed milk, sugar and the remaining milk gently until smooth; beating hard traps bubbles that steam into pockmarks.
Strain the egg mixture into a jug, then stir in the saffron milk; any unstrained egg threads set into chewy flecks.
Grease a heatproof dish with ghee and pour in the custard, skimming off surface foam so the top sets satin-smooth.
Cover the dish tightly with foil and steam over a low, steady simmer; fierce boiling rattles the custard and makes it split around the edges.
Check that the centre wobbles like set jelly, not liquid milk, then rest covered off the heat so carry-over warmth finishes it gently.
Chill until cool, scatter with pistachios, and slice with a wet knife so the custard cuts clean rather than tearing.

note: This is closest in spirit to bhapa doi, but egg-led and steamed into a firmer dessert custard.

name: Bangkok Crackling Pork Basil Rice
hook: Hot wok pork, basil snap, salty crunch

steps.t: Break up the cooked rice with damp fingers before the wok goes on; clumps stay cold inside and make the pork overcook while you fight them.
Stir fish sauce, soy sauce and sugar in a small cup so it can hit the wok at once; measuring later means the garlic burns while you hesitate.
Heat the wok until a thread of oil shimmers and smokes lightly, then add oil, garlic and chilli; if the wok is timid, everything sweats instead of frying.
Add pork mince and press it into the hot metal, then break it up once the underside has browned in little crisp freckles.
Pour in the sauce and toss hard until it smells salty-sweet and the pork is glossy, not sitting in a puddle.
Add the rice and stir-fry until the grains are hot, separate and stained with pork juices; stop too soon and the bowl tastes like leftovers with topping.
Turn off the heat, fold through Thai basil until just wilted, and serve with lime; cooking basil hard turns it black and medicinal.

note: Day-old rice is best, but a microwave pouch works when the budget and timetable are tight.

name: Sherry-Pickled Mushrooms on Smoky Patatas
hook: Hot vinegar, velvet potatoes, winter smoke

ingredients.name: mixed mushrooms, torn or thickly sliced

steps.t: Boil the potatoes in well-salted water until a knife slides through without crunch; if they are underdone, the mash will turn gluey before it turns comforting.
Drain the potatoes, let them steam dry for 2 minutes, then mash with 2 tbsp olive oil and enough hot cooking water to make a loose, spoonable purée; wet potatoes make it thin and tired.
Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a wide frying pan until it shimmers, then add the mushrooms in one layer; crowding them makes them leak water instead of taking on bronze edges.
Cook the mushrooms until the rims wrinkle and the undersides are chestnut-brown, then add garlic and smoked paprika for the last minute; burnt paprika tastes bitter, so keep it moving.
Whisk sherry vinegar, honey, mustard, 1 tbsp olive oil and a pinch of salt, pour it over the hot mushrooms, and bubble until the vinegar smell softens but still catches the nose.
Spoon the warm patatas into shallow bowls, pile the glossy pickled mushrooms on top, and finish with almonds and parsley; add the nuts at the end or they soften in the dressing.

note: Best with a glass of fino or a bitter winter salad.

name: Cassoulet Breakfast Beans with Baked Eggs
hook: Crackling crumbs, creamy beans, golden yolks

steps.t: Heat the oven to 200°C fan with a medium baking dish inside; a cold dish delays the bake and leaves the egg whites snotty at the edges.
Soften onion and carrot in olive oil in an ovenproof pan until the onion turns translucent and sweet-smelling, not brown; scorched onion will dominate the beans.
Stir in garlic, thyme and tomato purée until the purée darkens to brick red; if it stays raw and bright, the finished dish tastes tinny.
Add beans and stock, simmer until the liquid looks creamy and just coats a spoon; too much liquid means the eggs sink and boil rather than bake.
Tip into the hot baking dish if needed, make four deep hollows, and crack in the eggs; shallow hollows let the whites run thin and overcook before the yolks set.
Mix breadcrumbs with melted butter and parsley, scatter around the eggs, then bake until crumbs are crisp and whites are just opaque with wobbling yolks.
Rest for 2 minutes before serving; cutting in immediately makes the yolks flood the beans instead of saucing each spoonful.

note: Use leftover cooked beans if you have them; keep the total cooked weight around 480 g.

name: Cider-Braised Salmon with Maple Mustard Onions
hook: Silky salmon, sweet onions, glossy cider

steps.t: Heat the oven to 130°C fan and salt the salmon all over; a fierce oven tightens the fish and pushes out white albumen.
In a wide lidded casserole, cook onions and celery in oil until the onions slump and turn pale gold at the edges; rushing this leaves them squeaky and sharp under the fish.
Add garlic for 1 minute, then pour in cider and scrape the base clean; any browned onion stuck underneath will burn during the braise.
Stir in stock, maple syrup and mustard, bring to the gentlest simmer, then slide in the salmon; boiling liquid will shred the flakes before the centre cooks.
Cover and braise in the oven until the salmon flakes in thick, glossy plates and is just cooked through at the thickest point.
Lift the salmon to a warm platter, whisk butter into the onions and juices until shiny, then taste for salt; adding butter before reducing makes the sauce greasy.
Spoon the maple mustard onions over the salmon, scatter with dill, and serve with lemon wedges; lemon goes last or it dulls the cider sweetness.

note: Bring the casserole to the table whole if your platter is not big enough; it looks generous either way.

name: Summer Chimichurri Tofu Carbonada
hook: Bright herbs, soft squash, clean broth

ingredients.name: firm tofu, pressed and cut into cubes
ripe tomatoes, grated or finely chopped

steps.t: Pat the tofu dry until the paper comes away barely damp; wet tofu clouds the stew and tastes steamed rather than clean.
Warm the olive oil in a wide pan and soften onion and red pepper until glossy and flexible, not browned; dark edges make this summer stew taste heavy.
Add garlic, cumin and paprika, stirring until the spices smell warm and earthy; leave them still and paprika catches fast.
Stir in tomatoes and simmer until they collapse into a loose red sauce with small oily bubbles at the edge; raw tomato keeps the broth watery.
Add tofu, courgette, sweetcorn and stock, then simmer gently until the courgette is tender but still green at the rim; a hard boil breaks the tofu into crumbs.
Turn off the heat and fold in chimichurri; boiling the herbs turns them khaki and flattens the vinegar bite.
Serve warm, not piping hot, with extra chimichurri spooned over; the flavours open up as the steam settles.

note: For a colder plate, let it stand 20 minutes and serve with crusty bread.

name: Cachaça-Lime Whole Roast Lamb Leg with Farofa
hook: Crisp fat, lime perfume, toasted crumbs

steps.t: Heat the oven to 220°C fan and bring the lamb out of the fridge while you make the rub; roasting fridge-cold meat gives you a grey band before the centre warms.
Mix garlic, lime zest, half the lime juice, cachaça, olive oil, salt, pepper and cumin, then rub it into every crease of the lamb; patches left bare taste flat once sliced thin.
Set the lamb in a roasting tin and roast until the outside starts to spit and the fat takes small golden blisters; without this hot start, the surface stays leathery.
Lower the oven to 170°C fan and roast until the thickest part is rosy and the juices run pink, basting with the tin juices twice; dry lamb is usually unbasted lamb.
Rest the whole leg loosely covered for 25 minutes; carve too soon and the juices run across the board instead of staying in the meat.
While it rests, melt butter in a frying pan, add red onion, then stir in cassava flour until it smells nutty and feels sandy, not dusty; pale farofa tastes raw.
Finish the farofa with coriander and the remaining lime juice, then carve the lamb into thin shared slices; thick slabs overpower small plates.

note: Serve with pickled chillies, orange wedges and cold beer for a proper shared table.

name: Hamsi Domates Yahni
hook: Silky anchovies in peppery tomato oil

ingredients.name: fresh anchovies or sardine fillets, pin-boned

steps.t: Warm the olive oil in a wide shallow pan, then soften the onion and green pepper with a pinch of salt until the onion turns floppy and translucent; if it catches brown now, the stew will taste harsh instead of sweet.
Add the garlic, pul biber and cumin and stir until the oil stains brick-red and smells toasted; do not let the garlic freckle dark brown or it will dominate the fish.
Pour in the tomatoes, rinse the tin with a splash of water and add that too, then simmer briskly until the sauce looks glossy and thick enough to leave a trail from the spoon.
Lay the anchovy or sardine fillets over the sauce in one layer, skin-side up where possible, and spoon a little sauce over them; piling them up makes the lower fish overcook before the top is done.
Cover and simmer gently until the fish has just turned opaque and flakes with a nudge; a rolling boil will break the oily fish into woolly shreds.
Finish with lemon juice and parsley off the heat, then rest for a minute so the oil rises in orange pools rather than serving it watery straight from the boil.

note: Serve with crusty bread or quick bulgur to catch the tomato oil.

name: Za’atar Roast Tofu Makloubeh
hook: Crisp tofu crown, spiced rice beneath

ingredients.name: extra-firm tofu, left as one block

steps.t: Wrap the tofu block in a clean tea towel, weight it with a heavy pan, and press until the towel is wet to the touch; if you skip this, the roast steams inside and never forms a savoury crust.
Mix olive oil, za’atar, pomegranate molasses and salt, then coat the whole tofu block and let it sit while the oven heats; a dry patch stays pale and tastes beany.
Roast the tofu on a lined tray until the corners are firm and the surface looks dark-speckled and leathery, not wet; move it gently, as tearing the crust now loses the best texture.
Roast the aubergine and cauliflower on a separate tray until the aubergine edges collapse and the cauliflower tips char lightly; under-roasted vegetables turn the rice pot soggy.

Layer the roasted vegetables in a deep ovenproof pot, scatter over the rinsed rice, allspice and cinnamon, then pour in hot stock until it just covers the rice; too much liquid makes makloubeh slump instead of unmould.
Cover tightly and bake until the rice has absorbed the stock and the grains at the edge stand separate; if steam escapes, top up with a small splash of boiling water rather than stirring.
Rest the covered pot, then invert it onto a platter in one confident motion and set the whole roasted tofu on top; rushing the rest makes the rice crack apart.
Finish with pine nuts and torn mint so the hot spice gets a fresh lift instead of tasting heavy.

note: A weekend centrepiece inspired by makloubeh, with the tofu roasted whole as the crown.

name: Smoked Lamb Kefta Chermoula Bowl
hook: Charred smoke, lean spice, bright herbs

steps.t: Light the barbecue for indirect cooking and add a small handful of soaked wood chips once the coals are ashed over; thick white smoke tastes acrid, so wait for it to thin and smell sweet.
Mix lamb, squeezed onion, half the garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, coriander and salt until sticky enough to cling to your fingers; loose mixing makes crumbly kefta that fall through the grill.
Shape into eight short logs around skewers or into thick patties, pressing out cracks; cracks widen over heat and leak fat onto the coals.
Smoke the kefta on the cooler side with the lid down until they feel springy and reach 70°C in the centre; guessing by colour is unreliable with smoked paprika and lamb.
Move the kefta briefly over the hot coals until the ridges char and the fat hisses; leave them too long and lean lamb dries before it browns.
Cover couscous with its volume of boiling water, salt and olive oil, then stand until the grains swell and separate with a fork; stirring early turns it claggy.
Fold chickpeas, lemon zest, lemon juice and chopped herbs through the couscous, then season the yoghurt with the remaining garlic and a pinch of salt; bland base makes the smoky meat feel heavy.
Serve the kefta over the chickpea couscous with yoghurt spooned alongside, resting the meat for a few minutes so the juices stay in the lamb rather than flooding the bowl.

note: Built for protein without feeling like punishment: lamb, chickpeas and yoghurt carry the meal.

name: Azahar Steamed Egg Custards
hook: Wobbly silk with orange-blossom caramel

steps.t: Cook 70 g sugar with the water in a small pan until it turns deep amber and smells like toasted honey; pull it while still pale and the caramel will taste flat, take it too dark and it turns bitter.
Divide the caramel between four heatproof ramekins and tilt quickly to coat the bases; it sets fast, so slow pouring leaves thick bitter islands.
Warm the milk with orange zest until steaming at the edges, then switch off and let it infuse; boiling the milk hard gives the custard a cooked dairy taste.
Whisk whole eggs, yolks, remaining sugar, orange blossom water and salt just until smooth, not foamy; foam becomes pockmarks on the finished custard.
Strain the warm milk into the eggs in a steady stream while whisking, then strain again into a jug; any zest or egg strand left behind spoils the silk.
Pour into the ramekins, cover each with foil, and steam over barely simmering water until the centres tremble like soft jelly; fierce steam makes bubbles and a rubbery edge.
Cool, then chill until fully cold so the caramel loosens into sauce instead of sticking to the ramekin.
Run a thin knife round each custard and invert onto plates, pausing before lifting the ramekin so the caramel can slide down the sides.

note: A Spanish-style flan perfumed with azahar, gentle enough to finish a meal.

name: Charcoal Poulet Moutarde Baguette
hook: Mustard smoke tucked into crusty bread

steps.t: Light a small bed of coals and wait until they are grey with a steady orange glow; cooking over flames scorches the mustard before the chicken is safe inside.
Mix Dijon, oil, vinegar, garlic, thyme, salt and pepper, then coat the chicken thighs thoroughly; bare patches stick to the grill and taste flat.
Grill the thighs over the coals, turning when the underside releases easily and has dark bars rather than torn meat; forcing them early leaves the best crust behind.
Move any pieces that flare up to the cooler edge and cook until the thickest part reaches 74°C; chicken thighs forgive heat, but undercooked chicken is unsafe.
Rest the chicken on a board while you split and briefly toast the baguette cut-side down; skip the rest and the juices soak the bread before you bite.
Stir yoghurt with a spoonful of the leftover mustard mix only if it has not touched raw chicken; if it has, use fresh mustard, because raw chicken marinade is not safe as a sauce.
Slice the chicken, pile it into the baguette with cornichons, salad leaves and the yoghurt sauce, pressing lightly so the sharp pickles cut through the smoke instead of sliding out.

note: Cheap, smoky and built from supermarket basics; thighs stay juicier than breast over coals.

name: Miso Butter Winter Okonomiyaki Omelette
hook: Buttery miso edges, soft steaming cabbage

steps.t: Whisk the eggs, flour, miso and soy with 3 tbsp cold water until only tiny flour freckles remain; leave big lumps and the centre cooks pasty.
Fold in the cabbage and leek with your hands so every strand is glossed; if the vegetables sit in a dry pile, the omelette will scorch before it softens.
Heat a heavy frying pan or flat griddle over medium heat and melt half the butter until it foams quietly, not browns; too hot gives bitter miso before the inside sets.
Spoon in two thick rounds and press them to about 2 cm deep; cook until the edges look lace-brown and the top has lost its wet shine.
Slide a wide spatula fully underneath, flip in one calm move and add the remaining butter around the sides; a hesitant flip tears the soft cabbage middle.
Cook until the second side is deeply golden and the omelette springs back when pressed, not squelches.
Finish with spring onions and nori, then serve straight from the griddle while the butter is still hissing.

note: Good with Japanese mayonnaise or a little extra soy, but it is rich enough without either.

name: Crisp Gochugaru Halloumi Jeon
hook: Salty crisp cheese, sharp kimchi warmth

steps.t: Pat the halloumi very dry with kitchen paper; surface brine makes the coating slide off and spits in the oil.
Put the flour on a plate, then beat the egg with gochugaru and half the spring onions in a shallow bowl; if the egg is not loose, it clumps instead of forming a thin crust.
Dust each halloumi slice in flour, shake until it looks only faintly powdered, then dip in the egg; a heavy flour coat turns leathery.
Heat the oil in a frying pan until a dropped spring onion slice fizzes at once; if it sinks silently, the cheese will drink oil before crisping.
Shallow fry the halloumi in one layer until the underside is copper-gold and rigid at the edges, then turn once only.
Cook the second side until crisp, then drain on a rack rather than paper so steam does not soften the crust.
Stir kimchi, soy and honey together, spoon beside the hot jeon and scatter with sesame seeds and the remaining spring onions.

note: Serve with rice or a fried egg if you want a larger breakfast.

name: Black Vinegar Pickled Cod with Ginger Oil
hook: Silky fish, black vinegar sparkle

ingredients.name: skinless cod loin or hake fillet
fresh ginger, cut into fine matchsticks

steps.t: Salt the fish and set it on a heatproof plate with the Shaoxing wine; the salt firms it lightly, but piling it thickly will cure the outside unevenly.
Steam the fish gently until the flakes turn opaque and just separate under a chopstick; hard boiling makes the loin split and look ragged.
Lift the fish from its juices and cool until warm, not cold; dressing straight from the steamer makes the pickle taste flat and cooked.
Mix rice vinegar, black vinegar, sugar and soy until the sugar is gone, then spoon half over the fish; undissolved sugar leaves gritty sweet patches.
Tuck the cucumber around the fish and spoon over the rest of the vinegar mix; leave until the surface looks glossy and lightly stained tea-brown, not chalky.
Pile ginger and spring onions on top, heat the neutral oil until it shimmers, then pour it over them so they hiss; lukewarm oil leaves raw ginger harsh.
Finish with chilli oil and serve at room temperature, spooning the sharp dressing back over the flakes just before it reaches the table.

note: Use thick white fish pieces rather than thin tail ends; they stay elegant after steaming and pickling.

name: Salsa Verde Mushroom Calabacita Bake
hook: Green salsa steam, sweet corn crunch

ingredients.name: corn tortillas, torn into rough pieces

steps.t: Heat the oven to 220°C and put the mushrooms, courgettes and olive oil in a wide baking dish; crowding them in a small dish traps water and turns the bake soupy.
Bake until the mushrooms have shrunk and the courgette edges start to tan, with little puddles of juice at the corners.
Stir in the sweetcorn, tomatoes, salsa verde and torn tortillas so some tortilla pieces stay on top; bury them all and you lose the crisp edges.
Return to the oven until the salsa bubbles hard around the sides and the exposed tortilla tips curl and toast.
Scatter over the cheese and bake just until it softens and catches in spots; too long and it dries into salty crumbs.
Squeeze over lime and shower with coriander at the table, when the bubbling has calmed enough not to wilt the herbs instantly.

note: A wide ceramic or metal dish gives the lightest result because the vegetables roast before they stew.

name: Orange Olive Kokkinisto Beef
hook: Sticky beef, orange-scented tomato gravy

ingredients.name: beef shin or chuck, cut into large chunks

steps.t: Season the beef and brown it in the olive oil in batches until the edges are dark mahogany; if the pan is crowded, the meat steams grey and the sauce tastes thin.
Lower the heat and cook the onions in the same pan until soft, sweet and amber at the tips; rushing this leaves the braise sharp.
Add the garlic for the last minute only, stirring until it smells warm; scorched garlic will bitter the whole pot.
Pour in the wine and scrape the base until the sticky brown patches dissolve; leave them behind and you waste the deepest flavour.
Add passata, stock, cinnamon, bay, orange peel and oregano, then return the beef and bring to the gentlest blip, not a rolling boil.
Cover and braise on a low hob or in a 150°C oven until a spoon can press the beef apart and the sauce clings red to the meat.
Stir in the olives and simmer uncovered until the gravy is glossy and no longer watery; add them earlier and they dominate with salt.
Rest for 10 minutes, remove the cinnamon and orange peel, then serve in a shallow dish for spooning onto bread or potatoes.

note: Best warm rather than scorching hot, with lemony greens, feta and plenty of bread around it.

name: Fireside Oyster Pan Roast
hook: Briny oysters in velvet winter heat

steps.t: Check the oysters for shell grit with clean fingers and keep them cold; if they sit out while you cook, they lose their clean snap and turn slack.
Melt the butter in a small heavy pan and soften the shallot and celery until glossy, not brown; browned celery makes the cream taste muddy.
Stir in the tomato purée and paprika until the paste darkens to brick red; if it stays raw-looking, the broth will taste tinny.
Pour in the sherry and bubble until the harsh alcohol smell goes and the pan sounds syrupy; stop too early and it will bite through the cream.
Add the oyster liquor, cream and Worcestershire, then bring just to a lazy simmer; a rolling boil will split the cream and toughen the oysters later.
Slide in the oysters and heat only until their edges curl and their centres still look plump and glossy; if they shrink tight, they have gone rubbery.
Spoon into warm bowls with the toast tucked alongside, making sure the oysters are half-submerged so the last mouthful stays hot.

note: Buy oysters from a reputable fishmonger and keep them refrigerated until cooking.

name: Porteño Pork Gramajo
hook: Crisp potatoes, smoky pork, soft yolk

ingredients.name: pork shoulder or loin, cut into thin strips

steps.t: Rinse the potato matchsticks until the water runs clearer, then dry them hard in a tea towel; wet potatoes steam and never get that café-style crackle.
Toss the pork with cumin, paprika and a good pinch of salt, spreading the strips out; clumps hit the pan cold and stew instead of searing.
Heat half the oil in a wide frying pan until it shimmers, then stir-fry the potatoes until the tips blister and the middles are tender; if the pan is crowded, do it in two runs.
Lift the potatoes out, add the remaining oil, and stir-fry the pork over high heat until the edges catch brown and no pink remains inside; pale pork means the heat was too timid.
Add the onion and pepper and keep everything moving until the onion bends but still has bite; let it collapse and the whole breakfast turns sweet and heavy.
Return the potatoes, pour in the eggs, and fold just until the curds are glossy and barely set; dry scrambled egg kills the richness you want.
Finish with chimichurri and parsley off the heat, so the herbs smell green rather than fried.

note: For safe pork, slice thinly and cook until fully opaque with browned edges.

name: Cachaça Pork Lombo with Pineapple Farofa
hook: Charred pork, boozy glaze, golden crunch

steps.t: Pat the pork dry, then season with salt; surface moisture is the enemy of griddle marks and makes the meat taste boiled.
Mix cachaça, lime juice, garlic and brown sugar for the glaze, stirring until the sugar mostly dissolves; undissolved sugar burns in bitter spots.
Heat a ridged griddle until a drop of water spits away instantly, then oil the pork lightly, not the pan; a slick pan smokes before the meat sears.
