Griddle the pork until dark bars form and the steaks release without tearing, then turn and repeat; forcing them early leaves the crust glued to the ridges.
Brush with the cachaça glaze for the final minute on each side, letting it bubble sticky rather than blacken; glaze from the start and the sugar scorches before the pork cooks.
Rest the pork on a warm plate while you make the farofa; cutting straight away sends the juices across the board.
Melt the butter in a frying pan, toss in pineapple until the edges caramelise, then stir through cassava flour until sandy and golden; pale farofa tastes dusty, burnt farofa tastes acrid.
Slice the pork across the grain and serve over the pineapple farofa with coriander and lime wedges.

note: Pork loin is lean, so resting matters as much as the sear.

name: Crispy Masala Egg Kachumber
hook: Frilled eggs, cool cucumber, sharp lime

steps.t: Boil the eggs until the yolks are set but still golden, then cool under running water; soft centres are awkward to slice and can spit in the oil.
Peel and halve the eggs lengthways, wiping the knife between cuts; ragged whites shed their coating in the pan.
Mix gram flour, turmeric, chilli, cumin, salt and enough water to make a thin paste that coats a spoon; too thick and it fries doughy, too thin and it slides off.
Toss cucumber, tomato, onion, lime juice and a pinch of salt in a bowl, then leave it crisp and bright; make it too early and the vegetables flood the plate.
Heat the oil in a frying pan until a drip of batter fizzes at once, then dip the cut side of each egg in batter and lay it down gently; cold oil gives greasy eggs.
Shallow fry until the batter forms a crisp ochre skirt around the yolk side, then briefly turn to kiss the rounded side; over-frying makes the whites bouncy.
Drain on kitchen paper and plate over the kachumber with torn mint, keeping the crisp sides facing up so they do not soften.

note: Use fully cooked eggs for clean slicing and safer shallow frying.

name: Lime-Pickled Kohlrabi Đồ Chua
hook: Cold crunch with chilli-lime sparkle

ingredients.name: kohlrabi, peeled and cut into matchsticks

steps.t: Toss kohlrabi and carrot with the salt and scrunch once or twice; skip this and the pickle tastes watery rather than snappy.
Leave the vegetables until they bend without breaking and a little liquid pools underneath; if they are still stiff, the dressing will sit on the surface.
Rinse quickly and squeeze dry by handfuls; leave salt clinging and the final plate will taste harsh, squeeze too hard and you lose the crunch.
Whisk rice vinegar, lime juice, sugar, chilli and garlic until the sugar disappears; gritty sugar makes the dressing taste unfinished.
Dress the vegetables and toss with your hands so every matchstick shines; dry patches taste raw beside the pickled ones.
Chill briefly until cold and lively, not limp; hours in the dressing soften the kohlrabi too far for a small-plate crunch.
Scatter with peanuts and herbs just before serving, or they darken and lose their fragrance.

note: Vegetable-led and fish-sauce-free, built for sharing alongside richer plates.

name: Chermoula-Crisp Pork Schnitzels
hook: Citrus spice under shattering golden crumbs

ingredients.name: lemon, zested and cut into wedges

steps.t: Put each pork steak between two sheets of baking paper and bash to about 7 mm thick; if you leave thick ridges, the crumb burns before the pork cooks through.
Rub the pork with chermoula and lemon zest, then leave it while you set up the coating; do not drown it in paste or the crumbs slide off in the pan.

Mix flour with a pinch of salt, beat the egg in a second bowl, and stir panko with cumin and paprika in a third. Coat pork in flour, egg, then crumbs, pressing firmly so there are no bald wet patches.
Heat the oil in a wide frying pan until a breadcrumb dropped in fizzes at once; if the oil only sighs, the schnitzels soak it up and turn heavy.
Shallow fry the pork until the underside is deep gold and the edges look dry and crisp, then turn once and cook the second side the same way.
Drain on kitchen paper for 1 minute, season while hot, then serve with salad leaves and lemon wedges; stacking them traps steam and softens the crust.

note: Fast enough for a weeknight, with Moroccan chermoula doing the heavy lifting.

name: Escabeche Eggs with Saffron Peppers
hook: Silky yolks in sharp golden oil

steps.t: Lower the eggs into simmering water and cook until the yolks are just set with a darker, fudgy centre; boiling hard makes rubbery whites that pickle unevenly.
Chill the eggs in cold water, peel carefully, and halve any that have torn whites for tasting rather than the jar; ragged eggs cloud the dressing.
Char the peppers over a gas flame or under a fierce grill until the skins are black and blistered all over; pale patches cling bitterly and are awkward to peel.
Cover the peppers for 10 minutes, then peel, deseed and slice into ribbons; rinsing them under the tap washes away the smoky juices you want in the escabeche.
Warm olive oil with garlic, bay, saffron and paprika until the garlic just turns straw-coloured; if it browns, the whole pickle tastes harsh.
Stir in sherry vinegar, onion and a pinch of salt, bring just to a tremble, then pour over the eggs and peppers in a non-reactive dish; a rolling boil toughens the egg surfaces.
Cover and refrigerate for 24 hours, turning once if the eggs are not submerged, then dress with parsley and a spoon of the saffron oil to serve.

note: A weekend make-ahead tapa: the waiting is the point.

name: Steamed Bourbon Custard Puddings
hook: Warm vanilla wobble with caramel steam

steps.t: Butter four small heatproof ramekins and put a spoon of brown sugar in the bottom of each; ungreased sides make the custard tear if you turn it out.
Warm milk, cream, caster sugar and salt until steaming but not bubbling; boiling milk scrambles the eggs the moment it lands.
Whisk eggs, vanilla and bourbon just until smooth, then slowly whisk in the hot milk; frothing hard traps bubbles that set as little tunnels.
Strain the custard into a jug and divide between the ramekins; skipping the sieve leaves stringy egg bits on an otherwise satin pudding.
Cover each ramekin tightly with foil and set in a wide pan on a folded tea towel. Pour in hot water halfway up the sides; too much water can splash into the custard as it steams.
Cover the pan and steam gently until the edges are set and the centres wobble like soft jelly, topping up with hot water if the pan gets low.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving warm, either in the pots or loosened with a small knife; rushing them makes the caramel bottom spill thin rather than glaze.

note: An American-style steamed custard with a bourbon caramel bottom.

name: Mate Mushroom Locro
hook: Smoky corn stew for small budgets

steps.t: Heat the oil in a large saucepan and fry the mushrooms with a pinch of salt until they give off liquid and then start to squeak and brown; stopping while they are wet makes a flat, boiled stew.
Add onion, carrot and red pepper and cook until the onion turns translucent at the edges; if the vegetables catch now, the paprika tastes scorched later.
Stir in garlic, tomato purée, smoked paprika and oregano until the pan smells sweet and smoky; dry spices left in a hot pan for too long go dusty and bitter.
Add sweetcorn, butter beans and stock, scraping the base clean so the browned mushroom bits dissolve into the broth; stuck bits become black flecks instead of flavour.
Simmer uncovered until the carrot is tender and the broth has thickened around the beans, not boiled violently into mush.
Crush a ladleful of beans and corn against the side of the pan and stir it back in; blending the whole pot makes it heavy and baby-food smooth.
Taste for salt and serve in deep bowls, with extra oregano if you have it; under-seasoning is obvious because corn and beans are naturally sweet.

note: A student-friendly nod to Argentine locro, built from tins and mushrooms.

name: Snow-Day Steamed Lamb with Daikon
hook: Brothy, gingery lamb for bitter nights

ingredients.name: boneless lamb shoulder, cut into 4cm chunks
daikon, peeled and cut into thick half-moons
rock sugar or light brown sugar

steps.t: Soak the dried shiitake in 300ml just-boiled water until leathery-soft; if you rush this, the centres stay woody and the soaking liquor will taste thin.
Put the lamb in a heatproof bowl, cover with boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain and rinse off the grey scum; skip this and the finished broth turns muddy and lanolin-heavy.

Mix the lamb with soy, Shaoxing, sugar, ginger, spring onions, star anise and Sichuan peppercorns, then tuck in the mushrooms and 250ml of their strained soaking liquor; keep grit from the bottom of the jug out or it will crunch between your teeth.

Set the bowl in a steamer over a steady, not raging, boil and cover tightly; steam until the lamb yields when pressed with a spoon, topping up the pan before it runs dry or the sauce will scorch underneath.
Lift the lid away from you, add the daikon, and spoon hot broth over the pieces; if the daikon sits dry on top, it cooks woolly rather than juicy.
Steam again until the daikon is glassy at the edges and a chopstick slides through without cracking it apart.
Skim off any heavy surface fat, stir through sesame oil, and rest 5 minutes before serving; straight from the steamer it tastes flat, but the salt and ginger settle as it cools slightly.

note: Serve in deep bowls with steamed rice and chilli oil on the side.

name: Ember Huevos Rancheros with Charred Salsa
hook: Smoke, yolk and salsa at sunrise

steps.t: Light a small charcoal barbecue and wait until the coals are ash-grey with no tall flames; flames scorch the tortillas before the eggs have even begun to set.

Grill the tomatoes, onion, jalapeños and unpeeled garlic directly over the coals until the skins blister black in patches and the tomatoes slump; pull them too early and the salsa tastes raw and watery.

Peel the garlic, chop everything with a good pinch of salt and half the lime juice, then let the salsa sit; blending it smooth loses the smoky little charred bits that make the dish worth lighting coals for.
Warm a cast-iron frying pan on the grill grate with the oil until it shimmers but does not smoke hard; a cold pan glues the eggs down, while a smoking one gives bitter whites.
Crack in the eggs and cook with the lid down until the whites are just opaque and the yolks still tremble when the pan is nudged.
Slide the tortillas onto the grate for the last minute, turning once until they puff in spots; leave them longer and they turn brittle instead of bendy.
Spoon warm black beans onto the tortillas, add the ember-fried eggs, charred salsa, cheese, coriander and a squeeze of lime; serve at once, because the tortillas toughen as they cool.

note: If your barbecue grate is wide, use a perforated grill tray for the vegetables.

name: Aegean Sea Bass Crudo with Olive Snow
hook: Silky fish, lemon, frozen olive brine

ingredients.name: skinless sea bass fillet, pin-boned, previously frozen and suitable for raw eating

steps.t: Freeze the pitted olives for at least 2 hours if they are not already frozen; soft olives smear on the grater instead of falling like salty black snow.
Chill the serving plates and keep the fish cold while you work; warm fish slices raggedly and loses its clean, sweet smell.
Slice the sea bass across the grain into thin, even pieces with one long pull of a sharp knife; sawing leaves furry edges that catch too much lemon.
Lay the fish in a single layer on the cold plates, then season with sea salt, oregano and finely grated lemon zest; stacking the slices makes the bottom ones cure while the top ones stay bland.
Spoon over lemon juice and olive oil, then wait just until the edges turn faintly pearl-white while the centres stay glossy.
Shave cucumber into ribbons, scatter over capers and dill, then grate the frozen olives over the top at the table; add the olive snow early and it melts into dark puddles.

note: Buy fish specifically sold for raw eating, or use fish that has been commercially frozen to parasite-safe standards.

name: Bodrum Prawn Sac with Lemon Mint
hook: Fast prawns, bright herbs, sea air

ingredients.name: raw king prawns, peeled and deveined

steps.t: Pat the prawns very dry and salt them lightly; wet prawns boil in their own juice and never get that sweet, snappy edge.
Heat a wide sac, wok or heavy frying pan until a drop of water skitters away instantly; if the pan is only warm, the tomatoes collapse before the prawns sear.
Add the oil and green pepper, tossing until the pepper blisters in green-brown freckles but still bends rather than flops.
Add the garlic, pul biber and cumin and stir for a few seconds until the garlic smells sweet; let it go bronze and it will taste harsh through the whole plate.
Throw in the prawns in one layer and stir-fry hard until they curl into loose Cs and turn opaque almost to the centre.
Add the tomatoes and cook just until their cut sides shine and leak a spoonful of juice; burst them completely and the dish becomes a sauce, not a summer stir-fry.
Finish off the heat with lemon zest, a squeeze of juice, parsley and mint, then tip onto a cool platter so the prawns stop cooking before they turn tight.

note: Have bread ready for the lemony pan juices, but keep the prawns the centre of the plate.

name: Za’atar-Griddled Halloumi with Pomegranate
hook: Squeaky cheese, hot herbs, ruby crunch

steps.t: Pat the halloumi dry, then rub it with 1 tablespoon olive oil and the za’atar; if the cheese is wet, the herbs slide off and burn in the pan.
Stir the yoghurt with lemon zest, a squeeze of juice and the cucumber, then spread it thinly on a platter; a thick mound makes the hot halloumi sweat and slide.
Heat a ridged griddle until you can hold your palm above it for only a second; a lukewarm griddle melts the halloumi slowly and gives no stripes.
Lay on the halloumi slices with space between them and griddle until the undersides show dark bars and the edges soften but do not slump.
Turn once and cook the second side just until the cheese puffs slightly in the middle; keep flipping and it toughens into salty rubber.

Move the halloumi straight onto the yoghurt, drizzle with pomegranate molasses and the remaining olive oil, then scatter over pomegranate seeds, mint and sesame; wait too long and the cheese loses its squeak.

note: Set it down with warm flatbread, olives and chopped salad for a proper mezze spread.

name: Ligurian Lemon Cod Traybake
hook: Flaky fish, jammy tomatoes, olive-oil potatoes

ingredients.name: lemon, zested and cut into wedges

steps.t: Heat the oven to 220°C. Put the sliced potatoes, onion, tomatoes, olives, capers, oregano, olive oil, lemon zest and salt in a shallow baking dish; if the potatoes sit in a heap, they steam instead of catching at the edges.
Toss hard with your hands until everything shines with oil, then spread into one thin layer. Tuck the lemon wedges cut-side up so their juice roasts rather than floods the dish.
Bake until the potato edges look blistered and the tomatoes are beginning to slump, not just warm and shiny.
Pat the cod dry, nestle it on top, and spoon a little hot tray juice over it. Wet fish leaks water and turns the tray soupy, so do not skip the paper towel.
Return to the oven until the cod flakes in thick petals when pressed at the fattest point; if it looks translucent in the centre, give it another minute rather than serving it glassy.
Squeeze over the roasted lemon wedges and rest for 2 minutes so the fish finishes gently instead of breaking apart on the plates.

note: Use hake or pollock if cod is expensive; keep the fillets thick so they do not dry out.

name: Lucknowi Dum Mushroom Korma
hook: Deep onion sweetness, velvet cashew gravy

ingredients.name: king oyster mushrooms, torn into thick strips

steps.t: Cook the onions in the ghee over medium-low heat, stirring often, until they collapse into a bronze, sticky mass. Stop at tan and the korma tastes raw-sweet; push to black flecks and it will taste bitter.

Lift out a third of the onions for finishing. Blend the rest with the drained cashews, yoghurt, turmeric, chilli, half the salt and 100 ml water until completely smooth; grainy cashew paste never turns silky later.
In the same heavy casserole, fry the garlic-ginger paste for a minute until it smells rounded rather than sharp. If it catches on a dry base, splash in water, not more ghee.
Add the mushrooms and remaining salt, then cook until they throw off liquid and that liquid reduces to a glossy coating. If you braise before this point, the sauce turns thin and grey.
Stir in the cashew-yoghurt sauce and garam masala, scraping the base clean. Bring only to a lazy bubble; a hard boil can split the yoghurt.
Cover tightly with a lid, then seal the rim with foil. Braise in a 140°C oven until the mushrooms are spoon-tender and the gravy is beige-gold and settled, not foamy.
Crush in the fenugreek leaves, fold through the reserved onions, and rest uncovered for 10 minutes so the fat rises slightly and the seasoning comes into focus.

note: Best with naan or basmati rice, but the korma itself is the slow weekend centrepiece.

name: Isan Tamarind Beef Stew
hook: Lean beef, sour broth, chilli warmth

ingredients.name: lean beef shin, trimmed and cut into 4 cm chunks

steps.t: Put the beef and stock in a heavy pot and bring slowly to a tremble, skimming off the grey foam. Boil hard now and the broth clouds before the beef has softened.
Stir in the curry paste, lemongrass and lime leaves, then keep the stew at a gentle simmer with only small bubbles breaking the surface.
Cover partly and cook until a piece of beef gives when pressed with a spoon but does not shred into fibres; if it is still springy, it needs more time, not more heat.
Stir in the tamarind paste and fish sauce. Add them after the beef softens, because early acidity can make lean shin tighten up.
Rinse the rice until the water is less cloudy, then cook it in 300 ml water with a pinch of salt; too much water makes a heavy bowl rather than a gym-friendly base.
Add the mushrooms and green beans to the stew and simmer until the beans are bright green with a slight snap. If they go olive and floppy, they have eaten the freshness of the broth.
Discard the lemongrass and lime leaves, tear in the basil, and serve over rice with lime wedges. The final squeeze should sharpen the stew, not make it taste like limeade.

note: Approximate protein is 48 g per serving, depending on the trim of the beef.

name: Tokyo Caramel Mushi Pudding
hook: Wobbling custard, bittersweet lacquered caramel

steps.t: Put 50 g sugar and the water in a small pan and cook without stirring until the syrup turns the colour of polished copper. Pale caramel tastes flat; dark smoke means it has gone bitter.
Divide the caramel between four heatproof ramekins, tilting quickly to coat the bases before it sets into thick glassy puddles.
Warm the milk, cream, remaining sugar, vanilla and salt until steaming but not bubbling. If it boils, cool it first or it will scramble the eggs on contact.
Whisk the eggs and yolks just until even, not frothy. Pour in the warm milk mixture slowly while whisking; foam bakes into pockmarks instead of a satin top.
Strain the custard into a jug, then fill the ramekins. Cover each with foil so condensation does not drip and crater the surface.
Set the ramekins in a steamer over barely simmering water and steam until the edges are set but the centres wobble like soft jelly. A fierce boil makes honeycomb holes.
Cool for 15 minutes, then chill until cold. Run a thin knife round each pudding and invert; forcing it out warm makes the custard slump and split.

note: A low, steady steam is the whole trick; the custard should finish smooth, not bubbly.

name: Gochujang Smoked Tofu Bokkeumbap
hook: Crisp tofu, sticky chilli rice

ingredients.name: smoked tofu, patted dry and diced

steps.t: Break up the cold rice with damp fingers before the pan goes on. Clumped rice stays clumped, and you will crush the tofu trying to fix it later.
Stir the gochujang, soy sauce, sugar and 1 tbsp kimchi juice in a cup until smooth; straight paste hits the hot pan in salty red lumps.
Heat the rapeseed oil in a wide frying pan and add the smoked tofu in one layer. Fry until the corners turn chestnut and dry-looking, not just warm and beige.
Add the kimchi and the white parts of the spring onions, then fry until the kimchi smells roasted and the wet hiss has mostly stopped. If it stays watery, the rice will steam.
Add the rice and press it across the pan so the grains pick up orange edges. Stir too constantly and you get hot rice salad rather than bokkeumbap.
Pour over the gochujang sauce and toss until every grain is stained red and the base of the pan looks glossy, not saucy.
Take off the heat, fold in the sesame oil, sesame seeds and green spring onion tops. Add sesame oil earlier and its nutty smell burns off.

note: Smoked tofu gives the savoury depth cheaply, without needing meat or a smoker.

name: Cachaça-Molasses Whole Picanha
hook: Charred fat, dark gravy, winter warmth

ingredients.name: whole picanha, fat cap left on

steps.t: Heat the oven to 220°C. Score the picanha fat in a shallow diamond pattern; do not cut into the meat or the roast leaks juice instead of self-basting.

Rub the beef all over with salt, pepper, garlic, cachaça, molasses and olive oil. Push seasoning into the fat cuts, but leave no wet clumps of garlic on top because they burn bitter before the beef roasts.
Lay the onions in a roasting tin with the bay leaf and sit the picanha on top, fat side up. Roast until the fat cap blisters and takes on dark mahogany patches, not just pale gold.

Turn the oven down to 160°C, pour the stock and orange juice around the beef, and roast until the centre reaches 54°C for medium-rare. If the liquid dries out, the onions scorch and the gravy tastes ashy, so add a splash of water if needed.
Lift the beef to a board and rest loosely covered until the juices settle; slicing straight away floods the board and leaves the centre dry.
Simmer the roasting juices with the softened onions, scraping up the sticky base, until glossy enough to coat a spoon. If it tastes flat, add a pinch of salt before adding more molasses.
Slice the picanha across the grain into thick rosy slabs, spoon over the blackened onion gravy, and finish with orange zest for lift.

note: Serve with rice, farofa or greens; the fat cap is meant to be generous and crisp-edged.

name: Dhungar Masala Mushrooms on Paratha
hook: Smoky mushrooms, runny yolk, hot bread

steps.t: Cook the onion in 1 tablespoon ghee over medium heat until the edges are tea-brown and sweet; stop at pale and the masala tastes raw, push further and it turns bitter.
Add ginger-garlic paste, cumin and chilli, stirring until the sharp raw smell disappears. Keep it moving because the paste catches on the pan before it looks burnt.
Add the tomato and cook until it collapses into a jammy base and the ghee shows at the edge; watery tomato will steam the mushrooms instead of coating them.

Tip in the mushrooms and salt well. Fry hard until they give up their liquid, then reabsorb it and turn glossy with browned corners; if the pan is crowded, cook a minute longer rather than serving them squeaky.

Stir in garam masala, then make a small foil cup in the pan. Put the charcoal on a gas flame or under a grill until glowing red, place it in the cup, spoon on 1 teaspoon ghee and cover immediately; if the lid is loose, the smoke perfumes the kitchen, not the mushrooms.

Remove the charcoal cup carefully and discard it. Fry the eggs in the remaining ghee until the whites are set and the yolks still wobble; underdone whites make the plate slippery, overdone yolks lose the sauce.
Warm the parathas until flaky, pile on the smoked mushrooms, crown with eggs and coriander, and eat while the bread is still crisp at the edges.

note: Use a heatproof pan and lid for the dhungar smoke, and never leave the glowing charcoal unattended.

name: Banana-Leaf Steamed Silken Tofu
hook: Perfumed parcels with bright chilli dressing

steps.t: Soften the banana leaves by passing them over a low flame or dipping them in hot water until flexible; use them stiff and they split as soon as you fold the parcels.
Cut the tofu into four thick slabs and blot gently with kitchen paper. Pressing hard breaks the custardy texture, but leaving it wet dilutes the dressing.
Lay each tofu slab on banana leaf with shiitake and half the spring onions on top. Fold into neat parcels seam-side down; loose folds let steam drip in and wash away the mushroom juices.
Steam the parcels over briskly simmering water until the leaves darken and smell grassy, and the tofu is hot all the way through. Do not let the pan boil dry or the leaf turns acrid.
Whisk soy sauce, fish sauce, lime juice, sugar and chilli until the sugar dissolves. Taste for a clean salty-sour snap; gritty sugar sinks to the bottom and makes the last spoonful harsh.
Open the parcels at the table or just before serving, keeping the tofu intact. Spoon over the dressing while hot so it runs into the mushroom layer rather than sitting on top.
Finish with peanuts, herbs and the remaining spring onions. Add the herbs last, because steam wilts them from fragrant to dull in seconds.

note: The drama is in opening the leaf parcels; prepare them ahead and steam when guests sit down.

name: Coal-Grilled Lamb Spiedini with Fennel
hook: Smoke-kissed lamb, lemony crunch

ingredients.name: lamb leg steaks, trimmed and cut into 3 cm cubes

steps.t: Toss the lamb with 1 tablespoon olive oil, lemon zest, garlic, rosemary, fennel seeds, salt and pepper. Coat it lightly rather than drowning it, because oily marinade drips onto coals and gives a sooty taste.
Leave the lamb to season while you light the charcoal. Cook over coals only when they are glowing and filmed with grey ash; flames lick the outside black while the middle stays cold.
Thread the lamb onto soaked skewers with a little space between pieces. Pack them tight and the sides steam instead of taking on char.
Grill the spiedini over direct heat, turning as each face develops crisp brown edges and tiny fat flares. Move them aside if flames rise; burnt rosemary tastes medicinal.
Rest the skewers on a warm plate so the juices thicken inside the meat; cut one open too soon and the pink centre bleeds onto the salad.
Toss fennel, rocket and tomatoes with lemon juice, remaining olive oil and a pinch of salt. Dress at the last moment, because salted fennel softens fast and loses its snap.
Set the lamb over the salad and shave pecorino across the top. Serve warm, not piping hot, so the rocket stays lively.

note: For even cooking, choose lamb leg rather than shoulder; it grills quickly and stays neat on skewers.

name: Kokum-Cured Mackerel Bhel
hook: Cold oily fish, crackling sev, tamarind heat

ingredients.name: sashimi-grade mackerel fillets, previously frozen, skin removed

steps.t: Keep the mackerel chilled while you work and slice it into thin pieces with a clean sharp knife. Ragged cuts warm up in your hands and feel greasy instead of silky.
Stir kokum syrup, lime juice, ginger and salt in a cold bowl until sharp and balanced. If the salt is not dissolved now, it lands in harsh little bursts on the fish.
Fold the mackerel through the kokum cure and chill until the surface turns slightly opaque but the centre stays glossy. Leave it too long and the oily fish firms up like overcooked tuna.
Heat mustard oil until it shimmers, add mustard seeds and cover until they pop. If the seeds stay silent, the oil is too cool and they taste dusty; if they blacken, start again.
Let the spiced oil cool until just warm, then stir in the green chilli. Pouring smoking-hot oil onto the cured fish would cook it unevenly and bring out a metallic flavour.
Just before serving, mix onion, puffed rice, sev and coriander in a wide bowl. Do not do this early: the crunch collapses as soon as it meets moisture.
Lay the cured mackerel over the bhel, spoon the mustard-chilli oil around it, and serve immediately for scooping in small shared bites.

note: Buy mackerel sold for raw consumption and keep it refrigerated; this dish is not suitable for anyone avoiding raw fish.

name: Black Sea Sardine Breakfast Stew
hook: Tomato steam, pepper oil, bright fish

steps.t: Heat the oil in a shallow pan and soften the onion and pepper with a pinch of salt until the onion bends easily; if it browns hard now, the stew tastes fried rather than breakfast-soft.
Add the garlic and pul biber, stirring until the oil turns brick-red; leave it too long and the chilli flakes turn dusty and harsh.
Tip in the grated tomatoes and water, then simmer until the surface bubbles lazily and the sauce no longer tastes raw; if it is still sharp and foamy, the fish will taste separate from it.
Season the sardine fillets lightly, slide them into the sauce skin-side up, and keep the pan at a bare simmer; boiling makes oily fish curl tight and go metallic.
Cover and cook until the sardines have just turned opaque through the thickest part; if you wait for them to flake apart, they are already dry.
Squeeze in lemon and scatter over dill off the heat; herbs boiled in the stew lose the clean, seaside smell you want at breakfast.
Spoon into warm bowls with toast for dragging through the peppery oil, checking for stray bones as you serve.

note: Fresh sardines are best, but small mackerel fillets work in the same timing if they are thin.

name: Whole-Roasted Za’atar Portobellos with Lemon Tahini
hook: Meaty caps under glossy sesame rain

steps.t: Heat the oven to 220°C and line a heavy tray; a thin tray buckles and tips mushroom juices into one corner where they burn.
Wipe the mushrooms clean and trim only the dry stem ends, keeping the caps whole; washing them under the tap loads them with water and stops the edges roasting.
Mix olive oil, za’atar, garlic, pomegranate molasses and salt, then rub it over and under each cap; bare undersides steam pale instead of turning savoury and dark.
Roast gill-side up until the caps slump slightly and the juices collect in the centres; pull them before they collapse completely or they will leak all over the platter.
Whisk tahini with lemon juice, cold water and a pinch of salt until it turns pale and pourable; if it seizes, keep whisking in water a spoonful at a time rather than adding oil.
Spoon the roasting juices back over the mushrooms and return them to the oven until the rims look lacquered and lightly crisped.
Arrange the whole caps on a platter, drizzle with lemon tahini, then finish with pine nuts, mint and sesame; dressing too early hides the glossy roasted surface.

note: Use mushrooms of similar size so the platter looks deliberate and they cook together.

name: Smoked Chermoula Beef with Orange Cucumber Salad
hook: Cool crunch beneath warm spice smoke

ingredients.name: lean beef rump steak, about 3 cm thick

steps.t: Rub the beef with olive oil, ras el hanout, cumin and salt, then leave it out while you prepare the salad; fridge-cold steak cooks grey at the edge before the centre warms.
Toss orange segments, cucumber, red onion, half the lemon juice and a pinch of salt, then chill; salting it too heavily now pulls out a puddle and makes the plate watery.
Line a wok or deep pan with foil, add the oak chips, set a rack above them and have a tight lid ready; gaps in the lid leak smoke into the kitchen instead of seasoning the beef.
Sear the beef in a very hot frying pan until a deep brown crust forms on both broad sides; if the crust is beige, the smoke will taste raw and sooty rather than rounded.
Move the beef to the rack, cover tightly, and smoke over medium heat until the centre reaches 55°C for medium-rare or 60°C for medium; guessing by colour is unreliable once smoke darkens the surface.
Rest the beef on a board so the juices settle; slicing immediately floods the salad and leaves the meat dry.
Slice thinly across the grain, toss herbs through the salad, and finish with the remaining lemon juice; cutting with the grain makes even tender rump chew like string.

note: Ventilate well when smoking indoors, and keep the pan covered until the chips stop smoking.

name: Sherry-Steamed Mackerel Pintxos with Pickled Pepper Oil
hook: Silvery fish, sharp peppers, warm bread

ingredients.name: roasted red peppers from a jar, sliced

steps.t: Pour the sherry into a wide pan with the bay leaf and lemon peel, then bring it to a gentle steam; if it boils hard, the alcohol smell turns sharp and the fish tightens.
Season the mackerel and lay the fillets skin-side up in a steamer basket or on a heatproof plate above the sherry; sitting in the liquid poaches them and washes away the oil-rich flavour.
Cover and steam until the thickest part just flakes under a fingertip but still looks glossy; fully matte mackerel is overcooked and tastes bitter at the skin.
Lift the fish out carefully and peel away any skin that has loosened; dragging it with tongs breaks the fillets into untidy scraps before they reach the bread.
Warm the olive oil with smoked paprika off direct heat until it stains red and smells sweet; frying paprika fiercely makes it acrid in seconds.
Stir the peppers, sherry vinegar, olives and parsley into the paprika oil; adding vinegar while the oil is screaming hot spits and dulls the pepper’s brightness.
Break the steamed mackerel into large flakes over the toasts, spoon on the pickled pepper oil, and serve while the bread is still crisp; assemble too early and the pintxos slump.

note: Set the components out separately for a shared table, then build the toasts as people eat.

name: Gochujang-Crisp Mushroom Bap
hook: Crackly mushrooms, sticky chilli rice

ingredients.name: oyster mushrooms, torn into thumb-sized strips

steps.t: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then cook it with 270 ml water. If you skip the rinse, the bowl eats stodgy rather than glossy.
Toss the torn mushrooms with cornflour and a pinch of salt until every frill looks dusty. Bare patches turn leathery instead of crisp.
Heat the neutral oil in a wide frying pan until a pinch of cornflour fizzes straight away. Fry the mushrooms in two batches, leaving gaps; crowding traps steam and gives you squeaky mushrooms.
Turn the mushrooms when the undersides are lace-brown and rigid, then fry the other side until the edges rattle against the tongs. Drain on kitchen paper, not in a heap, or the crust softens.
Pour off all but 1 tablespoon oil, lower the heat, then stir in gochujang, soy, vinegar, honey and sesame oil until shiny and bubbling. Keep it moving; gochujang catches fast and turns bitter.
Return the mushrooms and fold just until glazed, keeping some crisp corners visible. If you simmer them in the sauce, you undo the frying.
Spoon rice into bowls, pile over the chilli-crisp mushrooms, and finish with spring onions and sesame seeds.

note: Best cooked in a wide pan so the mushrooms fry rather than stew.

name: Lotus Leaf Ginger Beef Buns
hook: Cloud-soft buns, deep ginger beef

ingredients.name: plain flour, plus extra for dusting
beef shin, cut into 3 cm pieces

steps.t: Mix flour, yeast, sugar and warm water into a shaggy dough, then knead until smooth and slightly bouncy. If the dough stays rough, the steamed buns split instead of puffing evenly.
Cover and leave in a warm place until doubled and full of small bubbles under the surface. Under-proved dough steams up tight and heavy.
Meanwhile put the beef shin, soy, Shaoxing, ginger and 250 ml water in a lidded pan; simmer gently until the meat pulls apart with a spoon. A hard boil tightens the beef before the collagen melts.
Shred the beef, then reduce any liquid to a sticky glaze and stir in spring onions, oyster sauce and sesame oil. The filling should look moist, not wet, or it will burst the buns.
Divide the dough into 12 pieces, roll each into a round with a thicker centre, add beef filling, then pleat closed and set on baking paper. Thin centres tear when the steam pressure rises.
Rest the shaped buns until puffy and a fingertip dent springs back slowly. Steam too soon and the dough stays dense around the filling.
Steam over briskly simmering water with space between buns until swollen and matte. Do not let boiling water touch them, or the bottoms turn gummy.
Turn off the heat and leave the lid closed for 3 minutes before lifting it. Opening at once can make the buns wrinkle and collapse.

note: A proper weekend project: slow beef, risen dough, and a final steam.

name: Coal-Grilled Sardine Tlayudas
hook: Smoky fish, lime, shattering tortilla

ingredients.name: limes, 1 juiced and 1 cut into wedges

steps.t: Light the coals and wait until they are ashed over with a steady medium-high heat. Flames lick oily fish and make it taste sooty rather than smoky.
Pat the sardines very dry, then rub with olive oil, cumin, smoked paprika, lime juice and salt. Wet skin welds itself to the grill bars.
Mash the black beans with a pinch of salt and a splash of hot water until spreadable. If they are stiff, they drag and tear the tortilla.
Grill the tortillas briefly until blistered and rigid at the edges, then move them to the cooler side. Leave them too long over the hot coals and they scorch before they crisp.
Grill the sardines over direct heat, turning once when the skin releases easily and shows dark grill stripes. Forcing them early leaves half the skin behind.
Spread beans over the crisp tortillas, then top with cabbage, avocado, sardines, coriander and jalapeño. Keep the cabbage raw; it is the crunch that stops the oily fish feeling heavy.
Serve with lime wedges and eat straight away while the tortilla still snaps.

note: High protein from sardines and beans, with enough fat to feel satisfying after training.

name: Mastiha Steamed Egg Custards
hook: Silky custard, piney Greek perfume

ingredients.name: mastiha crystals, crushed with a little sugar

steps.t: Warm the milk, cream, lemon zest and crushed mastiha until steaming at the edge, not boiling. Boiling drives the perfume off and can make the dairy taste cooked.
Whisk the eggs and caster sugar just until combined, keeping the whisk low. Froth becomes bubbles on the finished custard.
Pour the warm dairy into the eggs in a thin stream while whisking, then strain into a jug. Skip straining and little egg threads show up in the silk.
Divide between four small heatproof bowls and skim off surface bubbles with a spoon. Any foam left on top sets as a pocked skin.
Cover each bowl tightly with foil and steam over the gentlest simmer. A rattling boil overheats the eggs and makes the custard weep.
Check for a soft wobble like barely set jelly; the centre should not slosh. If it is liquid, steam in short bursts rather than blasting it.
Rest for 10 minutes, then spoon over honey and pistachios. Serving it straight from the steamer makes the texture seem loose and too hot to taste the mastiha.

note: A Greek-leaning steamed dessert with mastiha, honey and pistachio.

name: Isot Lamb Bulgur Skillet
hook: Peppery lamb, nutty bulgur heat

steps.t: Cover the bulgur with boiling water by 1 cm, add salt, cover and leave until swollen but still nutty. Too much water makes it porridge-like when it hits the pan.
Heat a large frying pan or wok until a drop of water skitters away, then add the oil. If the pan is only warm, the lamb leaks grey juice instead of frying.
Add the lamb mince in small clumps and leave it untouched until the underside forms dark, crisp freckles. Stir too soon and you lose the cheap mince’s best texture.
Add onion and green pepper, then stir-fry hard until the onion edges char in spots and the pepper stays bright. Soft, wet vegetables make the whole pan taste flat.
Stir in tomato paste, isot pepper and cumin, smearing the paste on the hot pan until it darkens brick-red. Raw paste tastes tinny and sweet in the finished dish.
Fluff the bulgur and toss it through the lamb over high heat until the grains are stained red and separate. If it clumps, break it up with the back of the spoon before it steams.
Fold through parsley off the heat and squeeze over lemon at the table. Cooking the parsley kills the fresh lift this thrifty pan needs.

note: Uses a small amount of lamb mince stretched with bulgur for a student-friendly price.

name: Ginger-Pickle Halloumi Bún Chả Bowl
hook: Hot squeaky cheese, sharp winter crunch

steps.t: Toss the carrot and cabbage with the rice vinegar, sugar and a pinch of salt, then scrunch hard until the cabbage starts to squeak and wilt; if you just stir it, the pickle stays stiff and tastes raw.
Cover the vermicelli with boiling water and set a timer; drain when the strands are bendy but still springy, because over-soaked noodles turn into a claggy mat under the dressing.
Stir fish sauce, lime juice, grated ginger, chilli and 3 tbsp warm water into the pickle bowl juices; taste for salty-sharp balance now, as the noodles will mute it later.
Pat the halloumi dry until the kitchen paper stops shining; wet cheese steams and refuses to take on those burnished edges.
Fry the halloumi in hot oil in a non-stick pan until the undersides are deep golden with crisp freckles, then turn once; moving it early tears the crust off.
Divide noodles between warm bowls, spoon over most of the ginger dressing, then pile on pickle, herbs and hot halloumi; leaving the cheese until last keeps it squeaky rather than rubbery.
Finish with the remaining dressing from the pickle bowl and eat straight away, while the contrast is hot, cold, soft and crunchy.

note: A cosy winter bún-style bowl: bright, dressed vegetables against salty grilled halloumi.

name: Saffron Dum Egg Korma
hook: Silky eggs under a perfumed lid

ingredients.name: saffron threads soaked in 2 tbsp warm milk

steps.t: Lower the eggs into simmering water and cook to a jammy set, then chill in cold water; if you boil them violently, the whites go rubbery before the sauce ever sees them.
Peel the eggs and cut two shallow slashes in each, stopping well before the yolk; deep cuts leak yolk and make the korma grainy.
Cook the onions in ghee over a low heat until they turn soft gold and sweet at the edges; rushing this over high heat gives you scorched bitterness instead of body.
Add garlic, ginger, coriander, garam masala and turmeric, stirring until the raw smell disappears and the fat looks stained; dry spices burn fast, so loosen with a spoon of water if they catch.
Blend the drained cashews with the yoghurt until completely smooth, then stir it into the pan off the heat first; adding cold yoghurt to fierce heat makes it split into flecks.
Return to a bare simmer, add saffron milk, salt and the eggs, then cover and braise gently until the sauce thickens to a velvet coat and stains the egg slashes yellow.
Rest covered for 10 minutes before serving, then spoon sauce over the eggs and finish with coriander; skipping the rest leaves the eggs bland in the middle.

note: A slow, elegant egg korma for a table that expects something special.

name: Miso-Roasted Whole Sea Bream with Yuzu Radish
hook: Lacquered skin, pearly flakes, clean bite

ingredients.name: whole sea bream, scaled and gutted
daikon or breakfast radishes, very thinly sliced

steps.t: Heat the oven to 220°C fan and line a roasting tray with baking paper; miso sugars weld themselves to bare metal if you skip the liner.
Pat the bream very dry inside and out, then slash the thickest part three times on each side; wet skin steams, and unslashed flesh cooks unevenly near the backbone.
Mix miso, mirin, soy, sake, sugar and oil into a loose paste, then brush a thin coat over the fish, including inside the cuts; a thick layer burns before the flesh cooks.
Roast until the glaze is chestnut in patches and the flesh lifts from the backbone in moist flakes, not glassy resistance; check at the shoulder, the slowest part.
While the fish roasts, toss radish with yuzu juice and a pinch of salt until the slices soften at the rims; dressing too early makes them limp, but not dressing at all leaves them harsh.
Rest the fish for 5 minutes on the tray, because carving straight from the oven tears the flakes and spills the juices.
Slide the whole bream onto a platter, scatter with spring onions and sesame, and serve with the yuzu radish for lifting bites from the shared table.

note: Designed for izakaya-style small plates: one whole fish to pick at together.

name: Bangkok Basil Chicken with Lime-Fish Sauce Crackle
hook: Basil heat, glossy chicken, fast rice

ingredients.name: green beans, cut into 2 cm pieces

steps.t: Stir the fish sauce, soy, oyster sauce, sugar and 15 ml water together before the pan goes on; if you start measuring over a smoking wok, the chicken will overcook while you panic.
Crush the garlic and chillies to a rough, wet rubble, not a paste; a paste burns black before the chicken has time to brown.
Heat the wok until a drop of water skitters away, then add the oil, chilli-garlic mix and green beans; stir-fry until the garlic smells sharp and the beans turn glossy emerald, not wrinkled.
Add the chicken mince and spread it hard against the metal, then break it up only once the underside has caught pale golden edges; constant stirring makes it boil and taste flat.
Pour in the sauce and toss until it clings in shiny patches and the chicken is fully cooked with no pink pieces hiding in the folds; stop before the sauce disappears into salt.
Kill the heat, fold through the basil until just wilted, and squeeze lime over at the table with hot jasmine rice; cooking basil hard turns it muddy and medicinal.

note: Use chicken thigh mince for juiciness; breast mince works but needs a splash more water in the sauce.

name: Osaka Scallop Okonomiyaki with Browned Nori Butter
hook: Sea-sweet scallops under lacquered savoury batter

ingredients.name: raw king scallops, side muscles removed and halved horizontally

steps.t: Soak the kombu in 450 ml cold water until the water tastes faintly of the sea; rushing this gives you hot water with seaweed floating in it, not dashi.
Warm the kombu water until tiny bubbles gather at the edge, lift out the kombu, add bonito, then turn off the heat; boiling the bonito makes the stock harsh and dusty.
Strain and cool 250 ml dashi, then whisk it with flour, eggs and finely grated nagaimo until stretchy and pourable; hot dashi scrambles the eggs into specks.
Rest the batter in the fridge so the flour hydrates and the pancake holds together instead of slumping apart on the griddle.
Fold in the cabbage with a wide spoon just before cooking; crushing it early floods the bowl and leaves the centre gummy.
Oil a flat griddle over medium heat, mound four thick pancakes, and press the scallops into the tops in a single layer; buried scallops steam grey before the batter sets.
Cook covered until the rims look dry and the underside is chestnut-speckled, then flip decisively and cook until the scallops are pearly opaque and firm at the edges.
Brush with okonomi sauce, stripe with mayonnaise, then spoon over butter foamed to hazelnut-brown with nori; pale butter tastes greasy, black butter bullies the scallops.

note: This is a slow, satisfying griddle project: make the dashi properly and the rest is calm assembly.

name: Gochujang-Crisp Halloumi with Edamame Sesame Slaw
hook: Crisp squeaky slabs, chilli glaze, clean crunch

steps.t: Pat the halloumi bone-dry, especially the cut faces; wet cheese spits in the oil and sheds its crust in sheets.
Whisk gochujang, soy, vinegar, honey, garlic and sesame oil until smooth and brick-red; lumps of paste catch on one slice and leave the rest under-seasoned.
Toss cabbage and edamame with one spoonful of the sauce only, keeping it crunchy; drowning the slaw now makes a salty puddle under the fried cheese.
Dip halloumi in egg white, then press into cornflour until every edge feels dry and velvety; bare corners leak brine and turn leathery instead of crisp.
Heat 5 mm oil in a wide pan until a pinch of cornflour fizzes at once, then shallow fry the halloumi without crowding until the bottoms are lace-gold.
Turn once and fry the second side until rigid at the edges and squeaky when nudged; flipping back and forth knocks off the fragile crust.
Drain on a rack, brush with the remaining gochujang glaze, and serve over the edamame slaw while the crust still crackles; stacking the slices traps steam and softens them.

note: Halloumi brings the protein and salt; the vinegar-heavy glaze keeps the plate from feeling heavy after training.

name: Silken Ginger Milk Steamed Egg Custards
hook: Quivering custard with warm ginger gloss

steps.t: Warm the milk with 55 g sugar and half the ginger until steaming but not bubbling; boiling milk forms a skin that breaks the custard's silkiness.
Leave the milk to infuse, then strain and cool until just warm to the finger; hot milk will curdle the eggs into sweet scrambled flecks.
Beat the eggs gently, not frothily, then stir in the ginger milk and pass everything through a fine sieve; bubbles and stringy egg white become pockmarks after steaming.
Divide between four heatproof bowls, cover each tightly with foil, and set in a steamer over a low, steady simmer; uncovered bowls collect dripping water and turn cratered.
Steam until the custards wobble as one soft piece, like set jelly, with no liquid ring at the edge; fierce steam makes them honeycombed and rubbery.
Simmer the remaining sugar, ginger, goji berries and 60 ml water to a light syrup, spoon it over the warm custards, and finish with sesame; a thick syrup masks the delicate egg.

note: Serve warm for the smoothest texture, or chill and add the syrup just before eating.

name: One-Dish Chilaquiles Egg Bake with Black Beans
hook: Runny eggs, smoky beans, no washing-up

steps.t: Heat the oven to 200°C and put the oil, onion and garlic in a small baking dish; the onion needs a head start or it stays raw-sweet under the tomatoes.
Bake until the onion edges look translucent and the garlic smells mellow, not sharp; if the garlic goes dark now, it will taste bitter through the whole dish.
Stir in tomatoes, black beans, cumin, paprika and a pinch of salt, scraping the sticky onion from the corners; dry spice left on the dish burns instead of seasoning the sauce.
Bake until the sauce bubbles thickly and a spoon dragged through leaves a brief trail; watery sauce turns the tortilla chips to paste.
Fold in half the tortilla chips, scatter the rest on top, then make four deep hollows and crack in the eggs; shallow hollows let the whites slide off and cook unevenly.
Scatter cheddar around, not over, the yolks and bake until the whites are fully set and the yolks still tremble if you like them soft; under-set whites are unpleasant and unsafe.
Finish with coriander and lime at the table, eating straight from the dish once it stops spitting; cutting in too soon burns mouths and breaks the eggs.

note: Use whatever supermarket tortilla chips are cheapest; the broken bits are perfect for thickening the bake.

name: Charred Lentil Kibbeh with Brown Butter Onions
hook: Smoke, spice, and soft winter depth

steps.t: Rinse the lentils until the water runs mostly clear, then simmer with 650 ml water and a good pinch of salt until they collapse into a thick orange porridge; if you leave them soupy, the kibbeh will slump on the griddle.
Take the pan off the heat, stir in the bulgur, cover tightly and let it swell until the grains are tender and the mixture holds a spoon track; uncovering too early leaves hard, gritty flecks.

Meanwhile cook the onions in the butter and olive oil over medium heat until deep gold with brown, frizzled edges; stop at pale beige and you miss the sweetness, push them black and the whole dish tastes bitter.
Stir cumin, allspice, chilli and tomato purée into the lentil-bulgur mixture, then fold in half the onions and parsley; taste now, because bland pulses stay bland once charred.
With damp hands, shape the mixture into 8 squat ovals about 2 cm thick; make them too tall and the outside scorches before the centre warms through.
Heat a ridged griddle until a drop of water skips, oil it lightly, then griddle the ovals until dark bars form and the edges firm up; moving them early tears the crust off.
Serve hot with the remaining brown butter onions spooned over and lemon wedges alongside, so the sharp juice cuts the winter richness.

note: A bowl of thick yoghurt beside this is lovely, but the dish stands on its own.

name: Crisp Harissa Bean Beghrir with Fried Egg Herbs
hook: Crackly edges, yolk, morning heat

ingredients.name: tin cannellini beans, drained and patted dry

steps.t: Mash half the beans in a bowl and leave the rest whole, then stir in gram flour, harissa, cumin, baking powder, spring onions, half the coriander, 180 ml water and salt; if the beans are wet from the tin, the batter turns gluey instead of crisp.
Rest the batter until it thickens to a spoonable paste with visible whole beans suspended through it; frying straight away makes the middles taste floury.
Heat 3 tbsp olive oil in a wide frying pan until it shimmers, then spoon in four small cakes and flatten them gently; overcrowding drops the heat and gives you greasy pancakes.
Shallow fry until the undersides are deep chestnut and the rims look dry and bubbled, then turn once; flip too soon and the crust stays welded to the pan.
Cook the second side until crisp and firm when pressed, then drain on kitchen paper while you fry the remaining cakes with a little more oil if the pan looks dry.
In the same pan, fry the eggs in the remaining oil until the whites are lacy and set but the yolks still wobble; if the oil is timid, you get rubbery whites with no crisp skirt.
Serve the bean cakes with yoghurt, fried eggs, lemon juice and the remaining coriander scattered over, while the edges still crackle.

note: For breakfast, make the batter the night before and keep it covered in the fridge.

name: Manzanilla Pickled Prawns with Orange and Fennel
hook: Cold, briny, citrus-bright elegance

ingredients.name: orange, zest pared and flesh segmented
small fennel bulb, very thinly sliced
small red onion, very thinly sliced

steps.t: Bring a pan of salted water to a steady simmer and cook the prawns just until they curl and turn opaque; boiling hard makes them tight and squeaky.
Lift the prawns into a bowl of iced water, then drain well and pat dry; leaving them wet dilutes the pickle and makes the dressing taste flat.
Warm the olive oil with garlic, smoked paprika and bay until the garlic just whispers at the edges; if it browns, the paprika turns dusty and bitter.
Add the manzanilla, sherry vinegar, orange zest, red onion and a pinch of salt, then bring only to a brief simmer to soften the onion without cooking away the wine aroma.
Pour the warm pickle over the prawns and leave until cool and glossy; putting them in the fridge hot traps steam and toughens the shellfish.
Fold through fennel and orange segments, then chill until the prawns taste seasoned all the way through; under-pickled prawns taste like salad with vinegar on top.
Spoon onto a shallow platter, finish with parsley and a thread of the pickling oil, keeping the orange and fennel visible for the guest-table drama.

note: Serve with crisp bread or salted crisps to catch the sherry oil.

name: Summer Halloumi Tian with Courgette, Tomato and Thyme
hook: Salty edges, soft Provençal sweetness

steps.t: Heat the oven to 200°C fan and rub a shallow baking dish with a little olive oil; a deep dish steams the vegetables instead of letting their edges roast.
Whisk garlic, vinegar, mustard, thyme, remaining olive oil and black pepper into a loose dressing; go easy on salt because the halloumi will season the whole dish.
Layer tomato, courgette, red onion and halloumi upright in tight rows, spooning the dressing between the layers; loose piles collapse and leave watery gaps.
Bake until the tomatoes sag, the courgettes are tender at the centre and the halloumi edges turn golden; if the vegetables still look glossy and raw, the flavour will be thin.
Scatter breadcrumbs over the top and bake again until they are crisp and sandy-gold, not pale and soft.
Rest the tian until the bubbling juices settle back into the vegetables; cutting straight in floods the plate.
Tear over basil and serve warm or just above room temperature, with the salty halloumi balanced by the sweet tomato juices.

note: This is best in a wide ceramic or metal dish where everything sits in one layer.

name: Cider-Braised Pork Cheeks with Mustard Pickle Relish
hook: Sticky pork, sharp crunch, open table

steps.t: Heat the oven to 150°C fan, season the pork cheeks and dust lightly with flour; a heavy coat muddies the sauce instead of helping it gloss.
Brown the cheeks in hot oil until they have a dark crust on both broad sides, working in batches; crowd the pot and they boil grey before they ever caramelise.
Lower the heat and cook the onions in the same pot until soft, sticky and amber at the tips, scraping up the brown bits before they burn.
Stir in garlic, then add cider and let it bubble until the sharp raw alcohol smell softens; skipping this leaves the braise tasting thin and beery.
Add stock, mustard, maple syrup and Worcestershire, return the pork to the pot, cover and braise in the oven until a spoon can press into a cheek with almost no resistance.
Uncover and cook until the sauce is glossy and clings to the pork rather than running like stock; if the cheeks are exposed too early, they dry at the edges.
Chop pickles with parsley and a spoon of their brine, then serve the pork cheeks in small pieces with sauce and relish, so every rich bite gets a sharp snap.

note: Put out small rolls, lettuce cups or cornbread wedges and let everyone build bites at the table.

name: Dijon Coal-Grilled Tofu à la Tarragon
hook: Smoke, mustard and soft herb butter

steps.t: Light a half chimney of charcoal and let it ash over while you prep; if the coals are still black and smoking, the tofu will taste sooty rather than grilled.
Slice the tofu into 8 slabs and press hard between kitchen paper until the surface feels almost suede-dry; damp tofu sticks to the bars and steams instead of taking smoke.
Stir the Dijon, olive oil, lemon juice, honey, garlic and salt into a glossy paste, then coat the tofu and courgette lightly; thick clumps of mustard scorch before the middle warms through.

Spread the coals in an even layer, oil the grill bars, and lay on the tofu and courgette; leave them alone until the tofu edges look dry and the courgette has dark railway lines, or they will tear when lifted.
Turn with a thin spatula and grill the second side until the tofu feels springy and the courgette bends without snapping; if flames lick up, move the pieces aside before the honey blackens.
Melt the butter at the cooler edge of the grill or in a small pan, stir in the tarragon, then spoon it over the plated tofu; boiling the herb butter hard drives off the soft aniseed perfume.

note: Use the firmest tofu you can find; silken or soft tofu will collapse on the grill.

name: Buenos Aires Triple-Pulse Chimichurri Salteado
hook: Charred beans under sharp green chimichurri

steps.t: Rinse the pulses, drain hard, then spread them on a clean tea towel until the skins look matte; wet beans burst in the pan and turn the salteado pasty.
Stir the parsley, garlic, red wine vinegar, chilli flakes, half the olive oil and a pinch of the salt into a loose chimichurri; chopping it too fine makes it muddy rather than bright.
Heat a wok or wide cast-iron pan until a drop of water skitters away immediately; if the pan is only warm, the pulses will stew before they char.
Add the remaining oil, then stir-fry the onion and red pepper until the pepper skin blisters in spots but the strips still have snap.
Add the chickpeas, black beans, lentils, smoked paprika and remaining salt, then toss hard until the chickpeas split at the edges and the lentils stop leaving moisture on the pan.
Take the pan off the heat and fold through half the chimichurri; adding it over full heat dulls the parsley and turns the garlic harsh.
Pile into bowls and spoon over the remaining chimichurri so each bite gets both charred pulse and sharp herb sauce.

note: For gym prep, cool it quickly and reheat in a very hot pan so the beans regain their dry edges.

name: Bahia Steamed Coconut Quindim
hook: Glossy gold custard, coconut chew

steps.t: Butter six small ramekins thoroughly, including the bottom corners, then dust each with a little of the sugar; missed patches grip the custard and ruin the glossy unmould.
Soak the desiccated coconut in the coconut milk until it swells and softens; dry coconut steals moisture from the custard while it steams.
Gently whisk the yolks, whole egg, remaining sugar, lime zest and salt just until smooth, not foamy; bubbles rise as pockmarks on the finished quindim.
Stir in the soaked coconut milk mixture, then pass the liquid part through a sieve while nudging the coconut through last; skipping this leaves stringy egg bits in a dessert that should cut cleanly.
Fill the ramekins, cover each tightly with foil, and set them on a rack over barely simmering water; a rolling boil rattles the cups and makes the custard honeycombed.
Steam with the lid on until the edges are set, the tops are glossy, and the centres wobble like soft jelly rather than slosh.
Rest for 15 minutes, then chill until cold before running a small knife around the edge and unmoulding; turning them out warm makes the caramelised top smear instead of shine.

note: The coconut naturally settles into a chewy base, which becomes the top once unmoulded.

name: Karachi Crisp Prawn Pakora Coins
hook: Hot gram crust, sweet little prawns

ingredients.name: raw peeled small prawns, thawed if frozen

steps.t: Pat the prawns very dry and roughly chop any large ones; surface water thins the batter and makes the oil spit.

Mix the gram flour, rice flour, onion, chilli, ginger-garlic paste, spices and salt, then add the cold water to make a thick batter that drops slowly from a spoon; a runny batter slides off the prawns.
Fold in the prawns and rest the bowl briefly while the onion softens; if there is a puddle at the bottom, stir in a spoonful more gram flour before frying.
Heat the oil in a frying pan until a small dab of batter sizzles at once and floats, but the oil is not smoking; cool oil makes greasy pakoras and smoking oil burns the spices.
Spoon in small coin-sized mounds, leaving space between them, and fry until the undersides are deep golden and the prawn pieces at the edges have turned pink.
Turn, press each coin lightly to even the thickness, and fry until rigid-crisp with the prawns fully opaque through the centre.
Drain on a rack or crumpled kitchen paper and eat while the crust still scratches; stacking them in a bowl traps steam and softens the gram-flour shell.

note: Small frozen prawns keep this cheap; thaw them in the fridge, never on a warm counter.

name: Saffron-Steam Hake with Garlic Potatoes
hook: Golden broth, soft flakes, winter warmth

steps.t: Warm the olive oil in a wide lidded pan and soften the onion with a pinch of salt until it slumps and smells sweet; if it catches now, the broth will taste scorched later.
Add the garlic, saffron and smoked paprika, stirring for a few breaths until the oil turns brick-gold; do not walk away, because paprika burns bitter in seconds.
Lay in the potato slices, pour over the fish stock and add just enough water to barely cover them. Simmer uncovered until a knife slides through the thickest slice without cracking it apart.
Season the hake on both sides, set it on top of the potatoes, then cover the pan and lower the heat so the liquid murmurs rather than boils; hard boiling makes hake tighten and shed its juices.
Lift the lid and check the fish: it should flake in thick, pearly pieces with no glassy centre. If it still looks translucent, cover for another minute, not five.

Spoon the potatoes into shallow bowls, settle the hake over them and ladle the saffron broth around. Finish with parsley and lemon; too much lemon in the pan will flatten the saffron, so squeeze it at the table.

note: A Spanish winter bowl somewhere between caldo and fish stew, but steamed gently so the hake stays plush.

name: Ember-Grilled Pork Boudin Breakfast Tartines
hook: Smoke, mustard, yolk, crisp bread

steps.t: Light a small bed of coals and wait until they are grey with no tall flames; flame-licked boudin splits and leaks before the middle is hot.
Stir the crème fraîche, Dijon, cornichons, shallot, vinegar and chives into a sharp spooning sauce. Taste now: it should cut the sausage, not taste like plain cream.
Brush the boudin lightly with butter and grill over medium coals, turning often, until the skins are taut, lightly blistered and the centre is piping hot.
Grill the sourdough on the cooler edge until the ridges are dark and the middle still has chew; if it turns brittle all the way through, the tartines eat like crackers.
Fry the eggs in a small pan with the remaining butter until the whites are fully set and lacy at the edge but the yolks still tremble.
Split the hot boudin lengthways, pile it onto the toast, spoon over the mustard-cornichon cream and cap with the eggs. Serve immediately, before the toast steams soft under the yolk.

note: Boudin blanc is gentle and milky, so breakfast smoke and sharp cornichons do the heavy lifting.

name: Citrus-Cured Halibut with Chive Oyster Cream
hook: Silky fish, cold citrus, briny cream

ingredients.name: sushi-grade halibut fillet, skinless and pin-boned
pink grapefruit, segmented and 2 tbsp juice reserved

steps.t: Chill the halibut for 10 minutes to firm it, then slice across the grain into neat 5 mm pieces; warm fish smears under the knife and looks ragged on the plate.
Mix lime juice, reserved grapefruit juice, salt and sugar until dissolved. Spoon it over the halibut in a shallow dish, turning once so every piece is glossed, not drowned unevenly.
Refrigerate until the edges turn opaque and the centres remain satin-translucent; leave it too long and the fish becomes chalky instead of luxurious.
Finely chop the oysters, then stir them and their liquor into the crème fraîche with half the chives. Keep it cold; oyster cream loses its clean snap if it sits warm.
Toss the fennel and grapefruit segments with olive oil and a tiny pinch of salt. Be gentle, because crushed grapefruit bleeds and stains the whole salad bitter-pink.
Lift the halibut from the cure and blot the underside lightly. Plate with fennel, grapefruit and small spoonfuls of oyster cream; pouring on the curing liquid will make the dish harsh.
Finish with Aleppo pepper and the remaining chives, then serve cold, while the fish still gleams.

note: Use fish sold for raw preparation and keep it refrigerated until serving.

name: Wok-Seared Mackerel with Chimichurri Corn
hook: Hot pan, oily fish, green bite

ingredients.name: mackerel fillets, pin-boned and cut into large chunks

steps.t: Pat the mackerel very dry and season it just before cooking; wet fish steams in the wok and the skin turns flabby rather than burnished.
Stir parsley, grated garlic, oregano, chilli flakes, red wine vinegar, 1 tbsp olive oil and a pinch of salt into a loose chimichurri. If it tastes flat now, the hot fish will not rescue it.
Heat a wok until a drop of water skitters away, then add 1 tbsp olive oil, corn, pepper and onion. Stir-fry until the corn freckles brown and the onion edges char but still crunch.
Scrape the vegetables onto a platter, then return the wok to fierce heat. Add the mackerel skin-side down and leave it alone until the skin grips, sizzles hard and releases cleanly.
Flip the mackerel and toss for another minute, just until the cut faces turn opaque; keep going and the oily fish becomes dry and metallic.
Return the vegetables for a quick toss with half the chimichurri, then take the wok off the heat. Heat kills the parsley brightness if you cook the sauce hard.
Pile onto plates with lemon wedges and the remaining chimichurri spooned over the mackerel.

note: Argentine flavours, wok speed: charred sweetcorn stands in for the parrilla smoke.

name: Dendê-Griddled Tofu with Cashew-Lime Farofa
hook: Crisp tofu, nutty crumbs, lime

steps.t: Wrap the tofu in a clean tea towel and press it under a plate until the towel is damp and the block feels firmer; unpressed tofu spits on the griddle and browns in patches.
Cut the tofu into thick dominoes. Mix soy sauce, lime juice, grated garlic and malagueta, then brush it over the tofu; soaking it for ages makes the surface wet, not more flavourful.
Toast the cassava flour and cashews in 1 tsp dendê over medium heat, stirring until the flour smells nutty and turns pale gold. If it goes deep brown, it will taste dusty and burnt.
Stir lime zest, spring onion, coriander and a pinch of salt into the warm farofa, then tip it out of the pan so the herbs stay green.
Heat a ridged griddle until properly hot, then brush with the remaining dendê. Lay on the tofu with space between pieces; crowding traps steam and steals the crust.
Griddle until the underside has clear dark bars and the edges look crisp, then turn once and repeat. Fiddling before the crust forms tears the tofu.
Arrange the tofu on a shared plate, scatter over the cashew-lime farofa and serve with extra malagueta for spooning, not drowning.

note: Dendê brings the Bahia-style depth; farofa turns it into a snackable table plate.

name: Buenos Aires Egg Carbonada
hook: Silky yolks in smoky tomato broth

steps.t: Warm the oil in a wide saucepan over a medium heat, then cook the onion and red pepper with a pinch of salt until the onion turns glossy and the pepper smells sweet; if they catch hard now, the stew tastes burnt all the way through.
Stir in the potato, paprika and cumin for a minute, coating every cube in red oil; do not let the spices sit dry on the pan base or they will go bitter.
Add the tomatoes and stock, scrape the bottom clean, then simmer briskly until the potato corners are tender but not collapsing; if the potato is still chalky, the eggs will overcook while you wait.
Stir through the sweetcorn and taste the broth, seasoning until it tastes slightly bolder than soup; bland liquid makes bland eggs.
Lower the heat to a gentle bubble, make four hollows, and crack in the eggs one by one; dropping them from a height breaks the yolks and clouds the stew.
Cover and simmer until the whites are just set and the yolks still wobble when you shake the pan; a rolling boil gives rubbery whites and hard centres.
Spoon into shallow bowls and finish with parsley, taking care to lift from under each egg so the yolk lands whole.

note: Fast, filling and best with bread for dragging through the tomato-rich yolks.

name: Moranga Inteira com Farofa Verde
hook: Sweet pumpkin, crunchy coconut crumbs

ingredients.name: collard greens or spring greens, shredded

steps.t: Scrub the pumpkin, cut a neat lid around the stalk, then scoop out the seeds and stringy fibres; leaving strands inside makes the filling watery and slippery.

Rub the pumpkin inside and out with 2 tbsp oil and salt, set it on a lined tray, replace the lid, and roast at 180°C until a knife slides through the shoulder with only gentle resistance; if the skin splits early, your oven is too fierce.
Lift off the lid and roast for a further spell so the inner flesh dries at the edges and tastes nutty rather than boiled.
Meanwhile cook the onion in the remaining oil until soft and pale gold, then add garlic and chilli just until fragrant; burnt garlic will dominate the whole pumpkin.
Add the greens and cook until they slump but stay emerald; if they turn khaki, they have gone from silky to cabbagey.
Stir in cassava flour and coconut, tossing until the grains feel sandy and lightly toasted; stop before they darken, as cassava flour turns dusty when scorched.
Pour in coconut milk a little at a time until the farofa clumps softly, then sharpen with lime zest and juice; too much liquid turns it from crumbly stuffing to paste.
Spoon the farofa into the roasted pumpkin, scatter coriander over the top, and carve wedges at the table so each portion gets sweet flesh, crisp skin and crumbs.

note: A Brazilian-inspired vegetable centre-piece for a slow weekend lunch, with no meat or fish.

name: Lahori Dhuaan Cod Tikka
hook: Clean fish, charcoal spice smoke

ingredients.name: cod or hake loin, cut into large chunks

steps.t: Pat the fish very dry with kitchen paper, because wet cod steams under the marinade and flakes before it colours.
Mix yoghurt, lemon juice, ginger-garlic paste, chilli, cumin, garam masala, turmeric, oil and salt into a thick rust-coloured coating; if it runs like milk, it will slide off the fish.
Fold the fish through gently and chill for 15 minutes, no longer than 30, or the lemon starts tightening the outside before the heat reaches the centre.

Lay the pieces on an oiled foil-lined tray with space between them, then grill under a hot overhead grill until the edges char in freckles and the fish is opaque at the thickest point; crowded pieces leak juice and stew.
While the fish grills, heat the charcoal with tongs over a gas flame or barbecue until it is glowing grey all over; black charcoal gives harsh smoke and can taint the yoghurt.

Put the cooked fish in a heatproof bowl, set a small foil cup in the middle, place the glowing charcoal in it, drizzle on a few drops of oil, and cover immediately; do not let charcoal touch the food.
Smoke just until the bowl smells like a tandoor when opened; longer smoke turns clean white fish acrid.
Discard the charcoal safely, scatter with coriander, and serve hot with salad or rice, keeping the flakes intact rather than stirring them into rubble.

note: Lean, smoky and protein-heavy, with yoghurt keeping the fish moist without making it rich.

name: Cà Phê Caramel Steamed Flan
hook: Cool custard under bitter caramel

ingredients.name: strong brewed Vietnamese coffee or espresso

steps.t: Put sugar and water in a small pan and cook without stirring until the syrup turns deep amber at the edges; stirring crystallises it into gravel instead of caramel.
Divide the caramel between six ramekins and swirl quickly to coat the bases, stopping before it turns mahogany-black and bitter.
Whisk eggs, yolks, milk, condensed milk, vanilla, coffee and salt gently until smooth; beating hard traps bubbles that leave a pockmarked flan.
Strain the custard into a jug, then pour into the ramekins; skipping the sieve leaves white egg threads in the set custard.
Cover each ramekin tightly with foil and set in a steamer over barely simmering water; fierce boiling makes the custard honeycombed and rubbery.
Steam until the centres tremble like set jelly when nudged, not liquid waves; if a knife comes out completely dry, they have gone too far.
Cool uncovered for 20 minutes, then chill until properly cold so the caramel loosens and the custard slices cleanly.
Run a thin knife around each flan and invert onto plates, letting the coffee caramel spill over the top.

note: A Vietnamese-style bánh flan with coffee bitterness to keep the sweetness polished.

name: Calabrian Coal-Grilled Beef Polpette Piadine
hook: Charred edges, peppery lemon folds

steps.t: Light the coals and wait until they are covered in grey ash with no tall flames; cooking over flames burns the outside before the mince is safe inside.
Mix beef, breadcrumbs, egg, pecorino, garlic, oregano, chilli flakes, salt and pepper with your hand just until combined; overworking makes the polpette springy like sausages.
Shape into 16 small oval polpette, pressing out cracks so they do not split and drop fat into the coals.
Grill the polpette over medium-hot coals, turning often, until they are crusted in dark patches and cooked through with no pink mince in the centre; guessing by colour outside is not enough.
Warm the piadine briefly on the edge of the grill until bendy with a few toasted spots; leave them too long and they snap when folded.
Toss rocket with lemon juice, olive oil and a pinch of salt just before serving, because dressed leaves wilt into black strings if they sit.
Fold each piadina around four polpette and a handful of rocket, scraping in any resting juices for extra savoury bite.

note: Cheap mince becomes coal-grilled street-food energy, with sharp leaves cutting through the richness.

name: Lahori Crisp Lamb Keema Cutlets
hook: Crackly edges, spiced lamb, sharp lime

ingredients.name: small onion, coarsely grated and squeezed dry

steps.t: Tip the lamb, squeezed onion, ginger-garlic paste, chilli, spices, egg, gram flour and 1 tsp fine salt into a bowl. Mix with your hand until the mince turns sticky; stop early and the cutlets split in the pan.
Shape into 12 thin cutlets, about 1 cm thick. Keep the edges smooth and even, because ragged edges burn before the middle is cooked.
Heat the oil in a wide frying pan over medium-high heat until a pinch of gram flour fizzes at once. If the oil only sits there, the cutlets will drink it and turn heavy.
Lay in half the cutlets without crowding them. Fry until the undersides are deep chestnut with crisp little bubbles at the edges.
Turn once and fry until firm, crisp and cooked through; if you keep flipping, the crust tears off. Drain on kitchen paper and repeat with the rest.
Squeeze lime over the hot cutlets and serve straight away. Leave them stacked and the steam softens the crust you worked for.

note: Use mince with a little fat; very lean lamb makes dry cutlets.

name: Saigon Pickled Mung Bean Gỏi
hook: Bright crunch, sour herbs, nutty beans

steps.t: Rinse the mung beans until the water loses its chalkiness, then soak them in plenty of cold water overnight. Skipping the soak gives you beans that are floury outside and hard in the centre.
Drain the beans, cover with fresh water and simmer gently until tender but still holding their shape. A rolling boil smashes them into paste, so keep the surface barely trembling.
Drain well and spread the beans on a tray to steam-dry. Dress them while wet and the salad tastes watery rather than sharp.
Toss the carrot and daikon with the rice vinegar, sugar and 1 tsp salt. Pack down, cover and chill until floppy, glossy and sweet-sour all the way through.
Whisk the soy sauce, lime juice, chilli and 2 tbsp of the pickling liquid. Taste it; if it is only salty, add a pinch more sugar, because the beans need a bright dressing.
Squeeze the pickled vegetables lightly so they stay juicy but do not flood the bowl. Toss with the mung beans and dressing until every bean shines.
Fold through the mint, coriander and peanuts just before serving. Add them too early and the herbs blacken while the peanuts go limp.

note: The long timing is mostly soaking and pickling; the final assembly is quick.

name: Baked Tuscan Chicken with Ricotta Beans
hook: Lean chicken, creamy beans, lemony crust

steps.t: Heat the oven to 210°C fan. Put the beans, tomatoes, spinach, garlic, oregano, olive oil, lemon juice, 1 tsp salt and plenty of black pepper into a roasting dish; toss until the spinach is slick, not clumped, or it steams in a wet lump.
Nestle the chicken into the beans and turn it to coat. Leave space between the fillets, because packed chicken poaches instead of baking cleanly.
Mix the ricotta, Parmesan and lemon zest, then spoon it over the chicken in rough ridges. Smooth it flat and you lose the golden, savoury peaks.
Bake until the ricotta is spotted gold, the tomatoes have slumped and the thickest part of the chicken reaches 74°C.
Rest the dish out of the oven so the juices settle back into the chicken. Cut immediately and the board fills with the moisture you wanted to eat.
