Scrape off heavy excess marinade and press each piece into gram flour; too much wet yoghurt makes the coating slide off in the oil.
Heat oil in a wide frying pan until a pinch of gram flour fizzes instantly, then lay in the cutlets without crowding; a crowded pan drops cold and gives a soft crust.
Shallow fry until the underside is crisp, brick-gold and releases when nudged, then turn once; flipping early tears the crust.
Cook the second side until crisp and the pork is piping hot throughout, with clear juices and no raw pink centre; undercooked pork is not safe.
Rest on a rack, not kitchen paper, while you toss cucumber with mint, lemon and salt; paper traps steam and softens the crust you worked for.

note: High-protein, lean and crisp without deep-frying.

name: Vietnamese Coffee Caramel Egg Cups
hook: Silky custard, bitter coffee caramel

steps.t: Melt the sugar in a small pan until it turns deep amber, then swirl in the coffee and divide between four ramekins; pale caramel tastes flat, but black caramel tastes acrid.
Warm milk, condensed milk, vanilla and salt until steaming but not bubbling; boiling milk scrambles the eggs the moment it hits them.
Whisk eggs and yolks just until blended, then slowly pour in the warm milk while stirring; whipping in foam leaves pockmarks in the finished custard.
Strain the custard into the ramekins over the set caramel; skipping the sieve leaves stringy egg white in a dessert that should be satin-smooth.
Cover each ramekin with foil and set in a steamer over barely simmering water; a rolling boil makes the custard bubble and turn honeycombed.
Check for a gentle wobble like set jelly in the centre, then turn off the heat and rest covered; pulling them while liquid in the middle means they slump when unmoulded.
Chill until cold, then loosen the edges with a thin knife and invert; unmoulding warm custard breaks the caramel layer and tears the sides.

note: Steam gently: texture matters more than speed here.

name: Tuscan Potato Pepper Traybake
hook: Jammy tomatoes, crisp potatoes, rosemary oil

steps.t: Heat the oven to 220°C and put a large baking dish inside; starting in a cold dish makes the potatoes cling and steam.
Toss potatoes with 2 tbsp olive oil, salt, oregano and rosemary, then tip into the hot dish in one layer; piling them up gives pale, waxy edges instead of crisp corners.
Bake until the undersides are golden and the top edges look dry and blistered, then turn them with a fish slice; turning too soon rips off the crust.
Add peppers, onion, tomatoes and garlic, stirring only enough to coat; overmixing crushes the tomatoes before they have time to roast jammy.
Bake until the peppers slump, the onion tips char and the tomato juices bubble around the potatoes.
Scatter breadcrumbs over the top with the last 1 tbsp oil and bake until the crumbs are crisp and sandy-gold; add them earlier and they burn before the vegetables finish.
Splash with red wine vinegar and rest for a few minutes so the juices thicken; serving straight away floods the plate and softens the crumbs.

note: No meat, fish, eggs, beans or cheese — just cheap vegetables made properly filling.

name: Pomegranate-Sumac Roast Mackerel with Hot Tahini Onions
hook: Oily, tart, warm-bellied winter comfort

ingredients.name: mackerel, gutted and scaled, about 450 g each

steps.t: Heat the oven to 220°C fan and put the potatoes and onions in a roasting tin with 2 tbsp oil, half the sumac, allspice and salt; spread them cut-side down so they roast rather than steam into pale softness.
Roast the vegetables until the potato cut faces are chestnut-gold and the onion tips are singed; if you stop at beige, the fish will be ready before the wintery base has any depth.
Pat the mackerel very dry, score each side three times to the bone, then rub with garlic, remaining oil, remaining sumac and salt; wet skin sticks and tears instead of blistering.
Lay lemon slices in the slashes and bellies, then set the fish on the hot vegetables; if the fish sits flat on a cold tray, the underside goes flabby and fishy.
Roast until the eyes turn opaque, the skin bubbles at the cuts and the thickest flesh lifts cleanly from the backbone; underdone mackerel clings glassily, overdone mackerel turns chalky.
Whisk tahini, pomegranate molasses, lemon juice and 2 tbsp warm water until glossy and pourable; add the water slowly or the sauce seizes into a grainy paste.

Spoon the hot onions and potatoes onto plates, lift the whole mackerel on top, then stripe with tahini sauce and parsley; sauce the fish at the end or the crisp skin softens before it reaches the table.

note: Ask the fishmonger to gut the mackerel but keep the head on for a properly whole roast.

name: Olivewood-Smoked Pepper Zaalouk with Warm Batbout
hook: Woodsmoke, cumin, tomatoes, hot flatbread

ingredients.name: food-safe olivewood or oak smoking chips
batbout or other soft Moroccan flatbreads

steps.t: Line a wok or deep pan with foil, add the smoking chips, set a rack above them and arrange the aubergine, peppers, tomatoes and garlic cut-side up; if the vegetables touch the chips, they scorch bitter instead of taking clean smoke.

Cover tightly, put over a medium-high heat and smoke until a thin steady thread escapes and the vegetable skins dull and wrinkle; loose foil leaks smoke into the kitchen and leaves the zaalouk tasting only boiled.

Move the smoked vegetables to a board, peel the pepper skins where they slip off easily and squeeze the garlic from its skins; scraping obsessively wastes the sweet flesh that makes the breakfast feel generous.

Chop everything roughly, then cook it in a frying pan with olive oil, cumin, harissa and salt until the tomato water hisses away and the aubergine turns silky; if it looks soupy, it will soak the bread to a sponge.
Fold in the preserved lemon and half the coriander off the heat; boiling them hard makes the lemon harsh and the coriander swampy.
Warm the batbout in a dry pan until puffed and freckled in spots; too fierce a heat burns the outside before the middle loses its fridge chill.
Spoon the smoky zaalouk into shallow bowls, scatter with the remaining coriander and serve with torn hot batbout; plate it thick, not spread thin, so it stays warm through breakfast.

note: This is breakfast without eggs or meat: smoky vegetables, oil, spice and bread doing the work.

name: Saffron-Steamed Lamb Albóndigas over Sherry Potatoes
hook: Soft lamb, golden steam, velvet broth

steps.t: Mix the lamb, breadcrumbs, egg, garlic, paprika, half the parsley and salt until the mince just turns tacky; knead past that point and the albóndigas steam up rubbery.
Roll 20 walnut-sized balls with damp hands and set them on a tray; uneven balls cook at different speeds, leaving some pink while others tighten.
In a wide pan, bring the potatoes, stock, sherry and saffron to a gentle simmer; a hard boil breaks the potato slices and drives off the sherry aroma before it perfumes the lamb.
Set a parchment-lined steamer over the pan, arrange the lamb balls in one layer and cover tightly; crowding them makes them sweat together and lose their neat guest-table shape.
Check one albóndiga in the centre: it should be firm, steaming and no longer pink, with clear juices; guessing by colour on the outside is unsafe with minced lamb.
Lift off the steamer, add the piquillo peppers and olive oil to the potatoes, then simmer uncovered until the broth looks glossy and coats a spoon; stop too early and it sloshes around the plate.
Slide the saffron potatoes into a warmed dish, sit the steamed lamb on top and finish with the remaining parsley; pouring everything from a height breaks the potatoes and dulls the presentation.

note: A bamboo or metal steamer both work; the key is a tight lid so the lamb cooks in fragrant sherry steam.

name: Coal-Grilled Panisse with Lemon Lentils and Fennel
hook: Crisp chickpea edges, cool anise crunch

steps.t: Light the barbecue first and let the coals burn down to a grey, even bed; cooking panisse over flames blackens the outside while the middle stays pasty.

Whisk chickpea flour, water, 1 tbsp olive oil, salt and the crushed garlic in a saucepan, then cook over a medium heat, stirring, until it pulls from the sides like thick polenta; if you leave lumps now, grilling will not hide them.
Discard the garlic, spread the hot panisse 1.5 cm thick on an oiled tray and chill until it feels firm at the edges; cutting it warm makes ragged pieces that fall through the grill.

Whisk lemon juice, zest, Dijon, 2 tbsp olive oil and salt, then fold through the lentils, fennel, tomatoes and tarragon; dressing the salad early enough lets the lentils taste bright rather than dusty.
Cut the panisse into fingers, brush with the remaining oil and lay them across the bars over steady coals; if they run with the bars, they soften and drop into the fire.
Grill until the edges blister and release without tugging, then turn once; forcing them early tears off the crisp chickpea crust you made the coals for.
Pile rocket and lemon lentils onto plates, add the hot grilled panisse and serve before the crust steams itself soft against the salad.

note: Cooked pouch lentils keep this summery; if cooking lentils from dry, cool them fully before dressing.

name: Everything-Spice Salmon Crudo with Pickle-Brine Cream
hook: Cold fat, dill snap, seeded crunch

ingredients.name: sashimi-grade salmon fillet, previously frozen and fully thawed

steps.t: Chill a serving plate and keep the salmon cold while you set up a clean board and knife; warm oily fish smears under the blade and tastes heavy.
Slice the salmon across the grain into 5 mm pieces and lay them in one layer; thick chunks feel greasy, while paper-thin slices collapse under the seasoning.
Mix the salt, sugar and lemon zest, sprinkle lightly over the salmon and rest until the surface looks glossy and slightly tightened; leave it too long and the fish turns cured and woolly.
Whisk soured cream with pickle brine and a squeeze of lemon until it falls from the spoon in ribbons; too much brine makes it split and run across the plate.
Spoon the pickle-brine cream onto the chilled plate, then lay the salmon over it without stacking; stacked raw fish warms slowly in the centre and eats clumsy at a shared table.
Scatter celery, red onion and everything seasoning, then gloss with olive oil; seasoning earlier draws out water and turns the seed crunch damp.
Serve immediately with small forks or crisps on the side; this dish depends on cold fat and sharp crunch, not sitting around.

note: Use fish sold for raw eating, keep it refrigerated, and do not reuse boards or knives for ready-to-eat garnishes after raw fish contact.

name: Orange Paprika Pork Escabeche
hook: Warm vinegar, soft pork, smoky winter edges

ingredients.name: pork shoulder, cut into 5 cm chunks
orange, zest pared and juice squeezed

steps.t: Season the pork well, then brown it in the oil in a wide casserole until the flat sides are deep chestnut; if you crowd the pan, it steams and the escabeche tastes thin.
Lift out the pork and add the onions with a pinch of salt. Cook until they collapse and turn glossy at the edges; if they catch black now, the vinegar will make the bitterness louder.
Stir in the garlic, paprika and orange zest for 30 seconds, just until the paprika smells smoky; go longer and it scorches into a dusty taste.
Add the vinegar, orange juice, stock and bay, scraping up the sticky base, then return the pork. The liquid should come about halfway up the meat, not drown it.
Cover and braise gently until a spoon pushes into the pork with almost no resistance; a hard boil tightens the meat and clouds the dressing.
Slide in the potatoes, cover again and cook until their edges are tender but not collapsing; if they break up, the pickle turns murky instead of glossy.
Rest off the heat for 10 minutes, then spoon the warm sharp dressing over the pork and finish with parsley. Serve warm, not boiling hot, so the orange and vinegar read clearly.

note: Escabeche is even better the next day; reheat gently and add parsley at the end.

name: Croissant Halloumi Morning Gratin
hook: Buttery layers, salty cheese, crisp golden peaks

ingredients.name: day-old butter croissants, torn into large pieces

steps.t: Heat the oven to 190°C. Butter a medium baking dish, then tumble in the croissant pieces, halloumi and tomatoes; pack it loosely, because a tight dish bakes heavy in the centre.
Whisk the eggs, milk, cream, Dijon, thyme and a little black pepper until no streaks of egg remain; under-mixed custard sets in rubbery yellow patches.
Pour the custard evenly over the dish, pressing the croissant tops down once so they drink it in but still sit proud for crisp edges.
Leave it to soak until the croissant feels damp through the middle, not dry and papery underneath; rushing this gives you custard below and toast above.
Scatter over the Comté and bake until the top is bronze, the tomatoes have slumped, and the centre wobbles only slightly when nudged.
Rest for 5 minutes before spooning out; cut too early and the custard runs instead of settling into soft layers.
Finish with chives and serve hot, while the halloumi is still squeaky and the croissant peaks crackle.

note: Use stale croissants if you can; fresh ones collapse too quickly in the custard.

name: Summer Hake Chupín
hook: Clean broth, tender fish, bright tomato heat

ingredients.name: hake fillets, cut into large pieces

steps.t: Salt the hake lightly and keep it chilled while you start the stew; warm fish softens at the edges and breaks up too easily later.
Cook the onion and red pepper in olive oil until soft and shiny, with no raw crunch left; if they stay firm, the short fish simmer will not fix them.
Add the garlic and paprika for 30 seconds, stirring until fragrant; paprika left on the heat too long tastes flat and dusty.
Add the tomatoes, stock, wine and potato slices, then simmer uncovered until the potatoes bend when pressed against the pan side but still hold their shape.
Lower the heat so the surface barely trembles, then lay in the hake pieces in one layer; a rolling boil knocks the flakes apart and makes the broth cloudy.
Cover and poach until the fish is opaque and separates in thick moist flakes at the press of a spoon.
Finish with lemon zest, a squeeze of juice and parsley. Taste for salt after the lemon, because acid makes the broth feel brighter without needing more seasoning.

note: Chupín should be brothy, not heavy; serve in shallow bowls with the fish pieces left whole.

name: Whole Roasted Mushrooms with Lime Farofa
hook: Juicy caps, toasted cassava, sharp lime smoke

ingredients.name: large chestnut mushrooms, wiped clean and left whole

steps.t: Heat the oven to 220°C and put a heavy roasting tray inside; a cold tray makes mushrooms leak before they roast.
Toss the whole mushrooms with olive oil, garlic, smoked paprika, chilli flakes and half the salt until the caps are slick all over; dry patches wrinkle rather than brown.
Tip them onto the hot tray stem-side down and roast until the caps are burnished and the juices bead underneath, not swimming across the tray.
Turn the mushrooms once and roast until they feel springy but not shrivelled; over-roasting leaves you with salty little sponges.
While they roast, melt the butter and cook the shallot until sweet and translucent; if it is still raw, it will shout through the farofa.
Stir in the cassava flour and toast until it turns pale gold and rustles like dry sand against the pan, then take it off the heat before it tastes scorched.
Fold lime zest, a squeeze of lime juice and coriander through the farofa, then spoon it over the hot whole mushrooms with the remaining salt flakes.

note: Set out cocktail sticks or small forks; these are best eaten warm, one juicy mushroom at a time.

name: Miso Butter Griddle Chicken with Charred Leeks
hook: Deep savoury warmth, edges caramelised dark

steps.t: Mix the miso, soy, mirin and softened butter to a glossy paste. Pat the chicken very dry before coating it; wet skin steams and never gets that sticky lacquer.
Rub the paste over the flesh side of the thighs, keeping most of it off the skin so the sugar in the miso does not scorch before the chicken cooks through.

Heat a heavy griddle or cast-iron pan until a drop of water snaps away, then oil it lightly. Put the chicken skin-side down and press it flat; if the pan is lukewarm the fat leaks out without crisping.
When the skin is deep gold with dark caramel spots, turn the chicken and lower the heat. Cook until the thickest part feels firm and the juices run clear; pulling it early leaves the centre slippery.
Lift the chicken to a warm plate. Lay the leeks cut-side down in the chicken fat until the ridges are blackened and the inner layers have softened; moving them too much gives you pale, squeaky leeks.
Rest the chicken for 5 minutes so the juices settle instead of flooding the rice. Slice thickly across the grain.
Spoon hot rice into bowls, add the charred leeks and sliced chicken, then finish with sesame and a squeeze of yuzu or lemon to cut through the butter.

note: If using bone-in thighs, add 8–10 minutes and check the flesh nearest the bone is fully cooked.

name: Gochujang Pork Breakfast Cutlets with Sesame Cabbage
hook: Crisp pork, sharp cabbage, runny morning egg

ingredients.name: thin pork loin steaks, about 120 g each

steps.t: Bash the pork between baking paper to 5 mm thick. Keep the thickness even; a fat middle stays undercooked while the thin edges burn.
Stir gochujang, soy and vinegar together, then smear a thin layer over the pork. Do not leave thick clumps on the surface or they will scorch in the oil.
Set up flour, beaten egg and panko in three shallow bowls. Coat each cutlet flour-egg-panko, pressing the crumbs on firmly; bare patches turn leathery instead of crisp.
Toss the cabbage with sesame oil and a pinch of salt until it looks glossy and just starts to soften. If you crush it hard, it dumps water onto the plate.

Heat 1 cm oil in a frying pan until a panko crumb fizzes immediately. Fry the cutlets without crowding until the crumbs are deep golden and the pork is cooked through; oil that is too cool makes the coating greasy.
Turn the cutlets and fry the second side until crisp and audibly scratchy when tapped with tongs. Drain on a rack, not kitchen paper, or the underside sweats soft.
Pour off most of the oil and fry the eggs until the whites set with lacy edges but the yolks still wobble. Serve rice, cabbage, sliced pork and egg straight away while the crumbs crackle.

note: Breakfast energy, but it also makes a strong brunch plate with kimchi on the side.

name: Black Vinegar Pickled Halloumi with Smashed Cucumber
hook: Salty squeak, dark vinegar, chilli gloss

steps.t: Slice the halloumi into 1 cm slabs, then rinse briefly under cold water and pat completely dry. Skipping the dry pat leaves the pickle cloudy and salty rather than clean.
Whisk black vinegar, soy, sugar, chilli oil and grated garlic until the sugar dissolves. Taste it now; once the cheese goes in you cannot evenly fix a flat dressing.
Cut the halloumi into bite-sized tiles and fold it through the dressing. Leave it to pickle until the edges take on a tea-brown tint; less time tastes like dressed cheese, not pickled cheese.
Smack the cucumber with a rolling pin until it splits, then tear it into rough chunks. Clean cuts look neat but do not catch the dressing in their cracks.
Salt the cucumber lightly and let it shed a little water, then drain it. If that water stays in the bowl, it thins the black vinegar until it tastes dull.
Fold cucumber, spring onions and coriander through the pickled halloumi just before serving so the herbs stay bright instead of turning khaki.
Pile onto a shallow platter and spoon the chilli-black vinegar dressing over the top. Finish with sesame seeds where guests can see them.

note: Serve cool, not fridge-cold; halloumi tastes waxy when it is too chilled.

name: Salsa Verde Pork and Calabacitas Bake
hook: Bright tomatillo pork, barely sweet courgettes

ingredients.name: pork tenderloin, sliced into 2 cm medallions
jarred salsa verde or tomatillo salsa

steps.t: Heat the oven to 220°C fan. Use a wide baking dish; if everything is piled deep, the courgettes boil and the pork turns grey.
Toss courgettes, tomatoes, onion and sweetcorn in the dish with olive oil, cumin and a pinch of salt. Spread them to the edges so moisture can escape.
Nestle the pork medallions among the vegetables and spoon salsa verde over each piece. Do not bury the pork completely or it poaches instead of roasting lightly at the edges.
Bake until the salsa is bubbling hard and the pork is just cooked through with no raw centre. Overbake tenderloin and it goes chalky fast, so check the thickest medallion.
Scatter over the crumbled cheese and return the dish to the oven only until the cheese softens and catches in a few spots; leaving it longer makes the plate heavy and salty.
Rest for 5 minutes so the salsa stops spitting and the pork relaxes. Cutting in immediately sends the juices into the bottom of the dish.
Finish with coriander and lime at the table. The lime is not decoration; it sharpens the courgettes and keeps the whole bake summery.

note: Good with warm corn tortillas, or simply as a lighter plate with shredded lettuce.

name: Yiayia’s Slow-Braised Eggs with Tomato, Olive and Oregano
hook: Jammy eggs in olive-rich tomato

ingredients.name: ripe tomatoes, grated, or tinned chopped tomatoes

steps.t: Warm the olive oil in a shallow lidded pan and cook the onion with a pinch of salt until soft and honey-coloured at the edges. Rushing this leaves a raw onion bite in the sauce.
Add the garlic, oregano and paprika, stirring until the garlic smells sweet rather than sharp. Let it darken and the whole braise tastes bitter.
Pour in the tomatoes and vinegar, then simmer gently until the sauce thickens enough that a spoon leaves a brief trail. A watery sauce makes the eggs slide around and cook unevenly.
Stir in the olives and taste for salt before adding feta later; olives vary wildly, and over-salting now cannot be rescued.
Make six shallow hollows and crack an egg into each one. Keep the heat low, cover the pan and braise until the whites are set but the yolks still tremble; a hard boil turns the whites rubbery.
Remove from the heat and leave covered for 2 minutes, as the residual heat finishes any glassy patches on top without overcooking the yolks.
Scatter with feta and parsley, then bring the pan to the table with bread for scooping. Serve from the edges first so the yolks stay intact for sharing.

note: For a meze spread, serve with cucumber, warm pitta and a plate of grilled peppers.

name: Kashmiri Slow-Braised Cod with Saffron Potatoes
hook: Saffron warmth, tender flakes, velvet sauce

ingredients.name: skinless cod loin or haddock, cut into large pieces
floury potatoes, peeled and thickly sliced

steps.t: Stir the saffron into the warm fish stock and leave it to bleed gold; if the stock is cold, the threads stay stubborn and the sauce tastes flat.
Warm the ghee in a heavy casserole, add the onion with a pinch of salt and cook until the strands slump and turn honey-brown at the edges; rush this and the braise tastes sharp, not sweet.

Add the garlic-ginger paste, chilli, fennel and turmeric, then stir until the ghee stains red and the paste stops smelling raw; if the spices catch black, scrape them out or the whole pot will taste bitter.
Lay in the potatoes, pour over the saffron stock, cover and keep at a lazy bubble until a knife slides into the potato with only slight resistance; a hard boil breaks the slices and clouds the sauce.
Whisk the yoghurt with a spoonful of hot stock, then stir it into the casserole off the fierce heat; add it cold and fast and it may split into grainy flecks.
Season the cod, nestle it into the sauce, cover and braise gently until the flakes just separate when pressed; leave it longer and the fish tightens into cotton wool.
Rest off the heat for 5 minutes, scatter with coriander and spoon the sauce over the fish rather than stirring; stirring now shreds the pieces you worked to keep whole.

note: The comfort comes from the long potato and yoghurt braise, with the fish added only at the end so it stays plush.

name: Bangkok Morning Mung Bean Stew with Jammy Eggs
hook: Coconut steam, soft beans, bright lime

steps.t: Lower the eggs into boiling water for jammy yolks, then cool them in cold water; skip the cooling and they keep cooking to chalky centres.

Put the mung beans, water, lemongrass and galangal in a saucepan and simmer until the beans swell and start to fray at the edges; a rolling boil makes foam climb the pan and leaves the centres gritty.
Stir in the shallots, curry paste and coconut milk, pressing the paste against the pan so it dissolves; leave lumps of paste and someone gets a harsh chilli mouthful.
Simmer gently until the stew looks creamy and the beans collapse when pressed to the side of the pan; if it thickens like mortar, loosen with a splash of hot water before it scorches.
Season with fish sauce and lime juice, then fold in the spinach just until it wilts glossy green; boil the greens and they turn dull and swampy.
Peel and halve the eggs, ladle the stew into bowls and finish with coriander; add the eggs at the table so the yolks stay molten rather than disappearing into the pot.

note: For a vegetarian version, use soy sauce instead of fish sauce and add an extra squeeze of lime.

name: Kyoto Miso-Crusted Whole Roast Beef Fillet
hook: Glossy miso crust, blush-pink centre

ingredients.name: centre-cut beef fillet, trimmed and tied

steps.t: Take the beef out of the fridge, pat it very dry and check the tying is snug; a wet fillet steams in the pan and loose ends cook before the centre.
Mix the miso, mirin, soy, sake, sugar and ginger to a smooth glaze; if the miso stays in lumps, it burns in salty patches rather than forming a lacquer.
Heat the oil in a heavy ovenproof pan and sear the beef on all sides until the surface is chestnut-brown and no grey raw patches remain; move it too soon and the crust tears away.
Brush the fillet with half the glaze and roast at 200°C until the thickest part reads 48°C for rare or 52°C for medium-rare; guessing by colour from the outside is how expensive beef gets overcooked.
Lift the beef to a warm board and rest it uncovered until the juices settle and the glaze turns tacky; slice early and the pink juices flood the board.
Put the roasting pan on the hob, add the stock and remaining glaze, then simmer and scrape until the sauce coats a spoon; leave the sticky bits behind and you lose the best savoury depth.
Whisk in the wasabi off the heat, slice the beef thickly and spoon over the jus with spring onions; boiling the wasabi flattens its clean heat.

note: Use a probe thermometer here; the roast is simple, but the margin between elegant and overdone is small.

name: Hot-Smoked Gochugaru Mackerel with Cucumber Pear
hook: Smoke, chilli, cucumber crunch

ingredients.name: Asian pear or crisp conference pear

steps.t: Rub the mackerel with the salt, sugar and gochugaru, flesh side first; miss the thick shoulder ends and they taste bland beside the thinner tail.
Rinse quickly, pat completely dry and leave on a rack until the surface feels slightly tacky; wet fish collects soot and turns acrid in the smoke.
Line a wok or deep roasting tin with foil, add the applewood chips and set a rack above them; if the foil has gaps, resinous smoke stains the pan for weeks.

Heat until a steady pale smoke appears, then lay the mackerel skin-side down, cover tightly and hot-smoke until opaque, glossy and flaking at the thickest point; thin smoke tastes clean, billowing black smoke tastes bitter.
Rest the fish on a clean plate while you make the salad; pulling it straight from the rack can tear the hot skin and spill the oils.
Ribbon the cucumber and pear, then toss with rice vinegar, soy and sesame oil until just dressed; salt it early and the salad collapses into watery strips.
Serve the warm smoked mackerel with the cold cucumber pear, spring onions and sesame seeds; keep the fish in large pieces so it eats light rather than mashed and oily.

note: Ventilate well and use hot smoke, not a cold-smoking setup; the fish should be fully cooked and flake cleanly.

name: Cantonese Silken Tofu with Black Bean Steam
hook: Silken wobble, black-bean savour

ingredients.name: fresh ginger, cut into fine matchsticks

steps.t: Slide the tofu onto a shallow heatproof plate and blot the puddle around it; if you leave the packing water, the sauce thins and tastes washed out.
Roughly chop the black beans and mix with ginger, garlic, soy, Shaoxing wine, sugar and chilli oil; whole beans give sudden salty blasts instead of seasoning the tofu.
Spoon the black bean mixture over the tofu, keeping some on the top rather than all in the plate; sauce underneath perfumes less and can scorch at the rim.
Steam over briskly boiling water until the tofu quivers and is hot in the centre; a weak simmer makes it weep before it heats through.
Carefully spoon away any excess watery liquid from the plate without disturbing the tofu; tip the plate hard and the block splits into curds.
Scatter with spring onions, heat the groundnut oil until it shimmers, then pour it over the onions so they hiss; lukewarm oil tastes greasy, smoking oil burns the ginger.

note: Serve with other small plates and plain rice, using a wide spoon so the tofu keeps its soft shape.

name: Coal-Kissed Ancho Lime Lamb Tacos
hook: Smoke, lime, lamb fat, fast

steps.t: Light a small chimney of lumpwood charcoal and wait until the top coals are ash-grey; cooking over black coals gives sooty smoke and a cold grate.
Mix the ancho, cumin, lime zest, half the lime juice, olive oil, sugar and salt, then rub it over the lamb. Keep the coating glossy, not wet, or the steaks steam before they char.
Toss the cabbage, onion, coriander and remaining lime juice with your hands until the cabbage just slumps; if you crush it hard, the slaw turns watery.
Spread the coals in one fierce layer. Grill the lamb until the edges blister dark and the surface springs back, about 2 minutes each side; moving it constantly stops the crust forming.
Rest the lamb on a clean board while you warm the tortillas directly on the grate until they puff and freckle; skip the rest and the juices run straight into the first taco.
Slice the lamb thinly across the grain, pile into tortillas with the slaw and cheese, and spoon over any resting juices that smell smoky rather than burnt.

note: Thin lamb steaks make this genuinely fast once the coals are lit.

name: Santorini Tomato Water Scallop Crudo
hook: Cold sea sweetness under tomato rain

steps.t: Put the scallops, still covered, on ice in the fridge; leaving them on the worktop while you prep is how raw shellfish loses its clean, sweet smell.

Coarsely grate the tomatoes and cucumber, stir in 1½ teaspoons salt, then tip into a muslin-lined sieve over a bowl. Chill until the bowl holds a clear rosy water; pressing the pulp makes it cloudy and harsh.
Shave the fennel paper-thin and mix with the vinegar, sugar and remaining salt until bendy but still crisp; thick slices stay woody in a raw dish.
Crush the barley rusks into rough crumbs and moisten with 1 tablespoon olive oil; powdery crumbs drink the tomato water and turn to paste.
Slice the scallops horizontally into coins with a sharp cold knife. If they smell sour or ammoniac rather than like clean seawater, do not serve them raw.

Lay the scallops on chilled plates, season with lemon zest, a little lemon juice and the remaining olive oil, then spoon tomato water around them. Finish with fennel, capers, dill and rusk crumbs, and serve before the acid makes the scallops woolly.

note: Use only very fresh scallops sold for raw eating and keep them below 4°C until slicing.

name: Ankara Pul Biber Chicken Sac Bowl
hook: Lean chicken, pepper heat, yoghurt cool

steps.t: Slice the chicken into thumb-thick strips and pat them dry; damp chicken drops the pan temperature and gives you pale juice instead of browned edges.

Heat a wok or wide frying pan until a bead of water snaps away, then add the oil and chicken in one layer. Leave it alone until the underside has bronze patches; stirring too early tears the meat and cools the pan.
Turn the chicken and cook until the strips are firm, opaque all the way through and piping hot in the centre, then lift them to a plate; half-cooked chicken must never wait under vegetables.
Throw the peppers and onion into the same hot pan and toss until the skins blister and the onion edges scorch; if they soften quietly, the pan is overcrowded or not hot enough.
Add the garlic, tomato paste, pul biber, cumin and salt, scraping hard until the paste darkens brick-red; pale paste tastes tinny and flat.

Return the chicken with any juices and toss for a final minute until the sauce clings in a shiny coat. Serve over hot bulgur with cold yoghurt and parsley, keeping the yoghurt off the pan or it will split.

note: Built around lean breast meat and strained yoghurt for a high-protein plate.

name: Orange Blossom Steamed Egg Custards with Date Tahini
hook: Silky custard, dates, orange blossom

steps.t: Set a steamer over barely simmering water; a rolling boil punches bubbles through the custard and leaves it honeycombed.
Whisk the eggs, milk, sugar, orange blossom water, cardamom and salt until the sugar dissolves, but stop before it turns foamy; foam sets as pockmarks on top.
Strain the mixture into a jug, then pour into four ramekins and cover each with foil. Straining catches stringy egg white that would otherwise set in rubbery threads.
Steam gently until the edges are set and the centres wobble like soft jelly, not liquid milk; if the tops puff, the heat is too fierce.
Lift the ramekins out and rest them for 10 minutes so the centres finish setting; spooning sauce on immediately makes the surface weep.
Blend the dates, tahini and boiling water to a glossy drizzle. Spoon over the warm custards, then finish with pistachios and orange zest so the nuts stay crisp.

note: Best served warm after a rich meal, when the orange blossom is most fragrant.

name: Crisp Chermoula Paneer Couscous
hook: Golden squeak, cumin, lemon crunch

steps.t: Put the couscous in a bowl with half the salt, pour over the boiling water, cover and leave until the grains swell; stirring it now makes clumps.
Cut the paneer into bite-sized slabs and blot them very dry. Wet paneer spits in shallow oil and the crust slides off in patches.
Mix the flour with cumin, ras el hanout and the remaining salt, then coat the paneer on all sides; bare corners fry leathery instead of crisp.
Heat the oil in a frying pan until a pinch of flour sizzles at once, then shallow fry the paneer in one layer until the bottoms are deep gold and rigid before turning.
Turn the paneer and crisp the second side; if the pieces touch, they steam at the edges and lose the squeaky crust.

Fluff the couscous with a fork, then fold in the carrot, coriander, garlic, lemon zest and a good squeeze of juice. Top with the hot paneer and spoon over a little of the spiced frying oil, stopping before the floury sediment comes with it.

note: Paneer is filling, fridge-stable and usually cheaper than a takeaway-sized portion of meat.

name: Crisp-Edged Karachi Beef Chapli
hook: Cumin-cracked beef with lacy fried edges

ingredients.name: crushed toasted cumin and coriander seeds

steps.t: Tip the mince into a wide bowl and scatter over the onion, tomato, chillies, coriander, ginger-garlic paste, spices and salt. Mix with loose fingers, not a squeezing fist, or the chapli will fry up bouncy instead of tender.
Beat in the egg, then fold through the gram flour. The mixture should feel tacky and hold a ridge; if it looks wet and slumps, leave it for 3 minutes so the flour can drink up the tomato juice.
Divide into 6 thin patties, pressing each one wider than you think, about 1 cm thick with ragged edges. Thick centres are the usual mistake here: they steam before the outside crisps.
Heat the oil in a heavy frying pan over medium-high heat until a crumb of mixture sizzles at once and leaves tiny bubbles. If the oil is only shimmering quietly, wait, or the patties will soak it up.
Fry 3 patties at a time until the undersides are deep brown and lace-crisp at the edges, then turn once. Do not keep flipping; that knocks off the crust you came for.
Cook the second side until the centre is piping hot with no pink mince visible, then drain on kitchen paper for 1 minute. Serve immediately while the edges still crackle.

note: Fast enough for a weeknight, but keep the patties thin so the beef cooks safely before the crust darkens.

name: Saigon Banana-Leaf Mackerel Steam
hook: Oily fish, lime steam, peanut crunch

steps.t: Run your fingertips over the mackerel and pull out any pin bones; banana leaf makes a beautiful parcel, but it will not hide a missed bone at the table.

Mix lemongrass, ginger, turmeric, fish sauce, sugar and the juice of 1 lime into a gritty gold paste. Rub it over the fish flesh, cover and chill; if you skip this rest, the seasoning stays on the surface and the oily fish tastes flat underneath.
Rinse the banana leaves and pass them briefly over a gas flame or hot dry pan until glossy and bendy. Use them cold and they split the moment you fold them.
Soak the vermicelli in just-boiled water until flexible but not mushy, then drain and rinse. Over-soft noodles collapse under the hot fish juices.
Lay the fish on the banana leaves with dill underneath and on top, then fold into snug parcels with the seam underneath. Leave a little room for steam; tight parcels squeeze out the marinade.
Steam the parcels over briskly boiling water until the fish flakes opaque at the thickest point and smells sweetly herbal, not raw and metallic.
Rest the parcels off the heat, then open at the table with vermicelli, mint, crushed peanuts and wedges from the remaining lime. Opening too early lets the fragrant steam vanish into the kitchen.

note: A slow marinade makes this a weekend dish; the actual steaming is short and gentle.

name: Tuscan Coal-Grilled Tofu Tagliata
hook: Charred rosemary tofu, sharp bean salad

steps.t: Wrap the tofu in a clean tea towel and weight it with a pan until it feels firmer and the towel is damp. Unpressed tofu hisses on the grill and sticks before it chars.
Cut the tofu into 2 cm slabs. Whisk lemon zest, half the lemon juice, garlic, rosemary, 1 tablespoon olive oil, oregano and salt, then coat the tofu all over.
Light the coals and wait until they are ash-grey with no tall flames. Flames scorch rosemary black before the tofu has taken on proper grill marks.
Toss the cannellini beans, tomatoes, rocket, balsamic, remaining lemon juice and remaining olive oil in a bowl. Dress it now rather than later so the beans taste seasoned, not like a garnish.
Oil the grill bars lightly and lay on the tofu. Leave it alone until dark stripes appear and the edges look drier; moving it early tears the surface.

Turn with a thin spatula and grill the second side until the tofu is hot through and lightly smoky. If the coals are fading, slide the tofu to the hottest patch rather than extending the cook until it dries out.
Slice the slabs diagonally like tagliata, pile beside the bean salad and finish with Parmesan shavings. Serve straight away while the char is still crisp at the corners.

note: Big tofu portions plus beans make this gym-friendly without turning dinner into punishment.

name: Saffron Cardamom Steamed Caramel Eggs
hook: Silky custard under bitter caramel

steps.t: Put the sugar and water in a small pan and cook without stirring until the syrup turns the colour of strong tea. Stirring makes it crystallise; walking away takes it from caramel to burnt in seconds.
Divide the caramel between 4 heatproof ramekins and tilt to coat the bases. Set them aside until the caramel hardens with a glassy tap.
Warm the milk with saffron until it steams at the edge, then take it off the heat. Boiling milk dulls the saffron and can scramble the eggs later.
Whisk the eggs, condensed milk, cardamom and rosewater just until smooth, then slowly whisk in the warm saffron milk. Too much whisking traps bubbles and gives a pocked custard.
Strain the custard into the ramekins and cover each tightly with foil. The sieve catches egg strands; the foil stops steamer drips making watery craters.
Steam over a gentle simmer until the edges are set and the centres wobble like soft jelly, not liquid. Hard boiling makes the custard tough and honeycombed.
Cool for 10 minutes, then chill or unmould warm by running a knife around the edge. Finish with pistachios; unmoulding too soon breaks the custard before the caramel loosens.

note: This is an Indian-leaning steamed caramel custard, scented with saffron, cardamom and rose.

name: Bangkok Basil Chickpea Smash-Fry
hook: Hot wok chickpeas, basil, lime

ingredients.name: green beans, cut into 3 cm lengths

steps.t: Cook the jasmine rice with a pinch of salt until the grains are tender, then keep it covered. If the rice is still wet when you serve, it will turn the stir-fry soupy on the plate.
Pat the chickpeas dry and lightly crush a third of them with the bottom of a mug. Wet chickpeas spit in hot oil; fully mashed ones turn pasty instead of catching char.
Stir soy sauce, fish sauce, sugar and the juice of half the lime in a cup so the sauce is ready. High-heat stir-frying gives you no time to hunt for bottles.
Heat a wok or large frying pan until a drop of water skitters away, then add the oil, garlic and chillies. Stir for a few seconds until sharp and fragrant; brown garlic tastes bitter fast.
Add onion, green beans and chickpeas, then stir-fry hard until the beans blister in spots and the chickpeas pick up golden freckles. If the pan sounds quiet, it is overcrowded or not hot enough.
Pour in the sauce and toss until it clings and the pan looks almost dry. Boiling it for too long makes the chickpeas salty all the way through.
Tear in the Thai basil off the heat and squeeze over the remaining lime. Serve over rice while the basil is just wilted and still smells peppery.

note: Tinned chickpeas keep it cheap, while the hot wok treatment makes them feel intentional.

name: Silky Courgette & Pepper Türlü
hook: Tomato-soft vegetables, minty lemon finish

steps.t: Warm the oil in a wide pan, then cook the onion with a good pinch of salt until it slumps and turns glossy; if you rush this, the stew tastes sharp rather than sweet.
Add the garlic and green pepper and stir until the garlic smells warm, not browned; burnt garlic will make the whole pot bitter.
Stir in the aubergine and courgettes, coating every cut face in oil; dry patches stay spongy instead of turning silky.
Push the vegetables aside, fry the tomato paste in the oily gap until it darkens a shade, then mix it through; raw paste leaves a tinny edge.
Add the tomatoes, pul biber and 100 ml water, then simmer uncovered until the vegetables are soft but still recognisable and the oil beads orange on top.
Crush in the dried mint between your fingers, add lemon juice, and rest for 3 minutes off the heat; serving it boiling hot flattens the mint and lemon.

note: Good with flatbread, but the stew is complete on its own.

name: Za’atar Salt-Crust Sea Bass with Walnut Tarator
hook: Fragrant fish under a crackling shell

ingredients.name: whole sea bass, gutted and scaled
lemons, one sliced and one juiced

steps.t: Pat the fish very dry inside and out, then chill it uncovered for 30 minutes; a wet skin steams under the crust and tastes muddy.
Stuff the cavity with lemon slices and half the parsley, keeping the filling loose; overpacking blocks heat from reaching the thickest part of the fish.
Mix the salt, egg whites and za’atar until it feels like damp sand that clumps in your fist; if it is powdery, add another spoon of water or it will crack open early.
Spread a third of the salt mix on a lined tray, lay the fish on top, then seal it completely with the remaining salt, leaving the tail just visible; gaps leak steam and dry the fillets.
Roast at 220°C until the crust is hard and faintly golden at the edges, and a probe through the crust into the thickest part reads about 55°C.
Rest the fish in its crust so the juices settle; smashing it straight away sends the moisture onto the tray.
Blitz walnuts, tahini, yoghurt, lemon juice, garlic, olive oil, pomegranate molasses and the remaining parsley to a rough sauce; stop before it becomes a heavy paste.
Crack the salt crust with the back of a knife, lift away the skin, and spoon the fish off the bones; scraping through the salt will over-season the flesh.

note: Ask the fishmonger to gut and scale the fish but keep it whole.

name: Smoked Chermoula Mushrooms on Lentil Skyr
hook: Coal-scented mushrooms, cool creamy lentils

ingredients.name: king oyster or large chestnut mushrooms, torn
plain skyr or thick Greek yoghurt

steps.t: Toss the mushrooms with olive oil, ras el hanout, smoked paprika, garlic, lemon zest and salt; season before cooking so the torn edges take on the spice rather than just wearing it.
Sear the mushrooms in a hot dry frying pan until the edges look mahogany and the pan stops flooding with liquid; if you crowd them, they boil and never taste meaty.

Line a lidded pan with foil, add the smoking chips in a little pile, set a small rack or foil ring above them, and put the mushrooms on a heatproof plate; keep the food off the chips or it will taste acrid.

Heat until the chips smoke steadily, clamp on the lid, lower the heat and smoke the mushrooms; open a window first, because lifting the lid too often dumps smoke into the room and weakens the flavour.
Warm the lentils with 2 tbsp water, half the lemon juice and a pinch of salt until glossy; boiling them hard splits the skins and turns the bowl stodgy.
Spread the skyr on plates, ripple through the remaining lemon juice and a little salt, then spoon lentils over it; mixing everything together makes the cool base disappear.
Pile on the smoked mushrooms, coriander and almonds while the mushrooms are still warm; if they cool completely, the smoke tastes flat rather than rounded.

note: Use only food-safe smoking chips, not treated wood.

name: Orange Saffron Flan al Vapor
hook: Silken custard with bitter caramel

steps.t: Cook 100 g sugar with the water in a small pan until it turns deep amber and smells toasty; stirring once it bubbles can crystallise it into sandy lumps.
Immediately divide the caramel between six ramekins and tilt to coat the bases; wait too long and it sets in one thick bitter coin.
Warm the milk, cream, orange zest, saffron and cinnamon until steaming at the edges, then take it off the heat; boiling the dairy gives the flan a cooked-milk heaviness.
Whisk eggs, yolks, vanilla and the remaining 50 g sugar just until smooth, not foamy; too much air leaves pockmarks in the custard.
Strain the warm milk into the eggs in a slow stream, whisking constantly; adding it all at once scrambles the yolks into threads.
Pour into the ramekins, cover each tightly with foil, and steam gently until the centres wobble like set jelly rather than liquid cream.
Cool for 15 minutes, then chill until firm; unmoulding warm flans makes the caramel run out while the custard slumps.

note: Run a thin knife round each ramekin before turning out.

name: Charcoal Sardines with Mustard Potato Crush
hook: Smoky silver fish, sharp warm potatoes

steps.t: Light the charcoal and let it burn until the coals are grey with no tall flames; cooking over flames scorches sardine skin before the flesh is safe and opaque.
Boil the potatoes in salted water until a knife slides through without cracking them apart; undercooked centres make a waxy crush that will not take the dressing.
Whisk mustard, vinegar, 2 tbsp olive oil, garlic and capers, then crush in the hot potatoes so the rough edges drink the dressing; cold potatoes repel it.
Pat the sardines dry, rub with the remaining oil and salt them lightly; wet skin welds itself to the grill bars.
Grill the sardines close to the coals until the skin blisters and releases, then turn once and cook until the flesh pulls from the backbone at the thickest part.
Fold parsley through the potatoes, plate with the sardines and squeeze over lemon; adding lemon before grilling makes the fish surface mushy and more likely to stick.

note: If sardines are unavailable, use small mackerel and add a minute or two per side.

name: Arrabbiata Halloumi Orzo Bake
hook: Lace-edged cheese over fiery tomato pasta

steps.t: Heat the oven to 220°C fan. Tip the orzo, both tomatoes, garlic, oregano, chilli flakes, stock and 1 tablespoon olive oil into a snug baking dish; stir right into the corners or dry orzo will catch there.
Bake uncovered until the sauce bubbles hard at the edges and the orzo is just short of tender; if the top looks dry before the pasta bends easily, splash in 50 ml boiling water.
Stir the bake from the bottom up, scraping the corners where starch likes to glue itself down. Taste the sauce now; halloumi is salty, so only add salt if the tomato tastes flat.
Lay the halloumi slices over the top, drizzle with the remaining oil and return to the oven until the cheese edges blister lace-brown; pale halloumi will squeak rather than turn savoury.
Rest the dish on the side until the sauce stops spitting and tightens around the pasta; serving straight away makes it soupy and molten-hot.
Tear over the basil just before plating so it smells green rather than stewed.

note: Use paneer instead of halloumi if preferred; add a pinch more salt because paneer is milder.

name: Tamarind Vindaloo Pork Shoulder
hook: Sour heat, spoon-soft weekend pork

ingredients.name: pork shoulder, cut into 5 cm chunks

steps.t: Mix the pork with tamarind, vinegar, garlic, ginger, chilli, cumin, coriander, pepper and 1½ teaspoons salt. Rub it into the cuts; dry patches mean the spice will taste dusty later.
Leave the pork covered in the fridge so the acid seasons the middle, not just the surface.
Heat the oil in a heavy casserole and cook the onions slowly until deep bronze and jammy; stop at pale gold and the braise will taste sweet but thin.
Lift in the pork and all its paste, then fry until the masala darkens and clings to the meat. Keep scraping the base; burnt spice turns bitter fast.
Pour in the water, bring to a gentle simmer, cover with the lid slightly ajar and braise on the lowest heat. You want lazy blips, not a rolling boil that tightens the pork.
Uncover and continue until a spoon can split a piece of pork and the sauce shines with red oil at the rim; if it dries before tender, add small splashes of hot water.
Rest off the heat, then skim only the excess fat, leaving enough red oil to carry the spice. Taste for salt and vinegar while warm, when the sourness is easiest to judge.

note: Best with rice or soft pav; it reheats even better the next day.

name: Kai Palo Tofu Egg Stew
hook: Five-spice broth with jammy golden eggs

ingredients.name: coriander roots or stalks, finely chopped
palm sugar or light brown sugar

steps.t: Boil the eggs until just hard-set, then cool under running water; if the yolks stay soft they can break up and cloud the stew.
Peel the eggs and pat the tofu dry. Wet tofu spits in the pan and steams instead of taking on flavour.
Warm the oil in a saucepan and fry the garlic and coriander roots until the garlic is light straw-coloured; darker than that and the broth will taste scorched.
Stir in the five-spice for a few seconds, then add soy sauce, fish sauce, sugar and stock. Get the liquid moving before the spice sticks to the pan.
Add the peeled eggs and tofu, then simmer gently until the eggs stain tan and the tofu tastes seasoned through; a hard boil will crater the tofu and make the eggs rubbery.
Fold in the spinach until it collapses but still looks bright green; grey spinach means it has given all its freshness to the pot.
Halve the eggs into bowls and ladle over the stew, making sure each portion gets tofu and the aromatic broth.

note: For gym meal prep, keep the eggs whole in the broth and halve them after reheating.

name: Yuzu Caramel Steamed Purin
hook: Silky custard under bittersweet citrus caramel

steps.t: Set four heatproof ramekins in a lidded steamer or a deep pan with a rack. Check the lid closes cleanly now; rattling lids drip water and pit the custard.
Cook 50 g sugar with the water in a small pan until the bubbles slow and the caramel turns the colour of strong tea. Pull it before it smokes or it will taste acrid.
Stir in the yuzu juice carefully, then divide the caramel between the ramekins. Work while it runs; once it hardens, scraping gives you shards not sauce.
Warm the milk with the remaining sugar and salt until steaming but not boiling. Boiling milk scrambles the eggs the moment it hits them.
Whisk the eggs and vanilla just until smooth, then slowly whisk in the warm milk. Strain into a jug; skipping this leaves stringy whites in the finished purin.
Pour into the ramekins, cover each with foil and steam over low heat until the edges are set and the centres wobble like soft jelly, not liquid.
Cool for a few minutes, then chill until fully cold before unmoulding; warm purin tears instead of sliding out cleanly.

note: The chilling time is included because the dessert needs it to finish properly.

name: Smoked Pollock Kimchi Rice Bowl
hook: Campfire fish over sharp kimchi rice

ingredients.name: smoked pollock or smoked haddock flakes

steps.t: If using smoked haddock rather than ready-flaked pollock, poach it gently in barely simmering water until it flakes, then drain well; frying salty fish straight from the pack can make the bowl harsh.
Heat the rapeseed oil in a frying pan and add the kimchi. Fry until it smells rounded and the cabbage edges look glossy, not wet and raw.
Stir in the gochujang and soy sauce with 2 tablespoons water. Let it loosen before adding rice, or the chilli paste will clump in one fierce spot.
Add the chilled rice and press out the lumps with the back of a spoon. Cold grains fry separately; warm rice turns stodgy and pasty.
Fold through the smoked fish just until hot. Rough stirring breaks it into salty dust, so leave some flakes big enough to taste.
Turn off the heat and add sesame oil, half the spring onions and half the torn gim. Sesame oil cooked hard goes flat, so keep it for the finish.
Bowl it up with the remaining spring onions, gim and sesame seeds on top for crunch before the seaweed softens.

note: Made for a rice cooker and one pan; leftover rice is the point here.

name: Ginger-Soy Steamed Mushroom Silk
hook: Brothy mushrooms with winter-warm ginger steam

ingredients.name: mixed mushrooms, such as shiitake, oyster and chestnut
fresh ginger, cut into fine matchsticks
cornflour mixed with 1 tbsp cold water

steps.t: Trim the mushrooms and tear the larger ones into spoonable pieces; if you cut them too small they collapse into the broth and lose their bite.
Lay the silken tofu in a shallow heatproof bowl, then pile the mushrooms over and around it so steam can move through the gaps; a tight mound cooks patchily.
Mix soy, Shaoxing wine, sesame oil, sugar, hot stock and the cornflour slurry, then pour it around the mushrooms rather than straight over the tofu, which breaks easily.
Scatter the ginger over the top, set the bowl in a steamer over vigorously simmering water, cover and steam until the mushrooms slump glossy and release dark juices into the bowl.
Lift the lid away from you and check the thickest shiitake stem; if it still feels squeaky and raw, steam a little longer rather than serving chewy mushrooms.
Spoon the hot broth back over the tofu, finish with spring onions, and serve at once while the ginger is still sharp and fragrant.

note: Deep winter comfort without heaviness: soft tofu, dark mushroom liquor and clean ginger heat.

name: Coal-Grilled Mushroom Chilaquiles Rojos
hook: Smoky tortillas, runny yolks, bright salsa

steps.t: Light the coals and wait until they are ashed over with no licking flames; flames scorch the tortillas before they crisp.
Grill the tomatoes, onion, jalapeño and unpeeled garlic until blistered and black-speckled, turning when the skins split rather than when they are merely warm.
Grill the mushrooms cap-side down first until they leak juices, then turn until the edges wrinkle and smell smoky; move them aside if they drip and flare.
Blend the grilled tomatoes, onion, peeled garlic, jalapeño, salt and a squeeze of lime into a rough salsa; blending it perfectly smooth makes it taste flat and jarred.
Brush the tortilla triangles with oil and grill them in batches until stiff and spotted brown, not pale and leathery.
Fry the eggs in a small pan on the grill or hob until the whites are set and the yolks still wobble; underdone whites make the plate slippery and unpleasant.
Toss the crisp tortillas quickly through warm salsa so some corners stay crunchy, then top with sliced mushrooms, eggs, cheese, coriander and lime.

note: A coal-fired breakfast with enough crunch and smoke to justify getting up early.

name: Ouzo-Cured Mackerel Cucumber Plate
hook: Cold silver fish, fennel, lemon oil

ingredients.name: sushi-grade mackerel fillets, pin-boned and skinned

steps.t: Check the mackerel for pin bones with your fingertips and pull any out; guests notice one bone more than they notice perfect plating.
Mix salt, sugar, ouzo, lemon zest and fennel seeds, then rub it over the fillets in a shallow dish; uneven curing leaves harsh salty patches.
Chill the fish until the surface firms slightly and turns glossy rather than opaque all the way through; this is a quick cure, not a full preservation cure.
Meanwhile shave the cucumber into ribbons, avoiding the watery seeded core if it starts to make the ribbons collapse.
Wipe excess cure from the mackerel and slice it on a shallow angle with a very sharp knife; sawing crushes the oily flesh and makes it look ragged.
Whisk lemon juice with olive oil until it thickens lightly, then fold in dill and capers; if the dressing separates completely, it runs off the fish instead of glazing it.
Arrange cucumber, mackerel, olives and dressing on a chilled plate, serving immediately while the fish tastes clean and cold.

note: Use only fish sold for raw consumption, keep it refrigerated, and serve the cured mackerel the same day.

name: Sumac Tofu Sac Tava
hook: Fast-charred tofu with tomato summer snap

ingredients.name: firm tofu, pressed and cut into 2 cm cubes

steps.t: Pat the pressed tofu very dry; surface moisture drops the pan temperature and gives you steamed tofu instead of browned edges.
Heat a wide wok, sac or heavy frying pan until a drop of water skitters off instantly, then add the oil; lukewarm oil makes the tofu stick.
Add the tofu in one layer and leave it alone until the underside forms golden freckles, then toss; constant stirring tears the cubes before they crust.
Add onion and pepper and stir-fry hard until the onion edges singe and the pepper stays bright green, not dull and floppy.
Push everything aside, fry the tomato paste, garlic and pul biber in the cleared oil until the paste darkens brick-red; if it stays raw, the whole dish tastes tinny.
Tumble in the tomatoes, salt and sumac, tossing just until the tomato skins tighten and the cut sides start to gloss.
Take off the heat, add lemon juice and parsley, and serve warm or just off-hot; cooking the herbs in the pan kills the summer freshness.

note: A Turkish-style high-heat pan dish made light with tofu, sharp sumac and barely collapsed tomatoes.

name: Baharat Lamb Köfte with Pomegranate Onions
hook: Charred lamb, sharp onions, warm spice

ingredients.name: small onion, grated and squeezed dry

steps.t: Mix the sliced red onion with pomegranate molasses and lemon juice, scrunching until glossy; if you leave it untouched, it stays harsh and raw.
Combine lamb, squeezed grated onion, garlic, baharat, cumin, salt and parsley with your hand just until tacky; overworking makes the köfte bouncy rather than juicy.
Shape into short oval patties about 2 cm thick, pressing a slight groove down each one so they do not puff into meatballs on the griddle.
Heat a ridged griddle until smoking lightly, then oil the köfte rather than the pan; a wet oily pan smokes bitterly and prevents clean char lines.
Griddle the köfte without moving them until dark bars form and the edges bead with fat, then turn once.
Cook the second side until the centre is hot and no longer raw, with juices running clear rather than red; lamb mince must be cooked through for safety.
Rest the köfte briefly, then pile onto warm flatbreads with the pomegranate onions so the juices soak the bread instead of the board.

note: Built for a shared mezze table: pick up with bread, onions and plenty of napkins.

name: Maple Cranberry Halloumi Wedge
hook: Salty cheese, warm berries, icy crunch

steps.t: Quarter the iceberg through the core, rinse inside the leaves, then dry it properly; wet lettuce makes the maple dressing slide off into the plate instead of clinging.
Slice the halloumi into thick cold slabs and pat both sides dry; if the surface is damp, the warm cranberry dressing turns milky and the cheese tastes rubbery.
Toast the pecans in a dry frying pan until they smell buttery and the skins darken in patches; take them off before the scent turns sharp, or they will taste bitter.
Bubble the cranberries, maple syrup, cider vinegar and 2 tbsp water until some berries burst but plenty still hold their shape; boil them to jam and the wedge loses its clean winter snap.
Pull the pan off the heat, whisk in the Dijon and olive oil, and taste for salt; whisking over a hard boil splits the dressing into greasy spots.
Plate the cold wedges with halloumi, thin apple slices, warm cranberries, pecans and chives; serve at once, because fridge-cold dressing leaves the halloumi squeaky rather than softly warmed.

note: Barely warmed rather than fried, with the comfort coming from maple, pecans and hot cranberries.

name: Buenos Aires Revuelto Gramajo
hook: Silky eggs tangled with crisp potatoes

steps.t: Cut the potatoes into matchsticks, rinse until the water runs clear, then dry them in a tea towel; damp, starchy potatoes steam and clump instead of going crisp.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt only until streaky; over-beaten eggs go foamy and set into a dry sponge in the hot pan.
Heat the olive oil in a wide pan until it shimmers, then stir-fry the potatoes hard until the tips are golden and the centres are tender; a crowded pan gives you pale hash, not Gramajo crunch.
Add the sliced onion and ham and toss until the onion edges soften and the ham freckles brown; if you add the eggs before this point, the onion stays raw and harsh.
Throw in the peas, butter and chilli, then pour in the eggs and fold fast over high heat until glossy curds cling to the potatoes; wait for fully dry eggs and breakfast turns heavy.
Finish with parsley and slide straight onto warm plates; leaving it in the pan carries on cooking the eggs until they squeak.

note: A high-heat breakfast stir-fry inspired by Argentina’s revuelto Gramajo.

name: Griddled Feijão Preto Cakes with Pineapple Vinagrete
hook: Inky bean cakes, bright tropical snap

steps.t: Mash two-thirds of the black beans until thick and pasty, leaving the rest whole; mash everything smooth and the cakes eat like baby food, not feijão.

Stir in cassava flour, egg, sliced spring onions, grated garlic, cumin and salt until the mixture holds when squeezed; if it feels wet and shiny, add a spoon more flour or it will weld to the griddle.
Shape 8 small cakes with oiled hands and let them sit so the cassava flour hydrates; skip the rest and the outsides crack before the centres firm up.
Dice the pineapple, tomatoes and red onion, then dress with lime juice, chopped coriander and a little salt; make the vinagrete too early and the tomatoes slump into watery salsa.
Heat a flat griddle until a drop of water skips, oil it lightly, then cook the cakes until the undersides form a dark speckled crust; turn too soon and the crust tears away.
Flip with a thin spatula and griddle the second side until the edges feel set when nudged; pressing down hard squeezes out the soft bean middle you want.
Serve the cakes stacked with pineapple vinagrete spooned over the top; drowning them in advance softens the crust you worked for.

note: Black beans and cassava flour make a sturdy, glossy cake that looks restaurant-ready without deep-frying.

name: Lahori Crisp Chicken with Cucumber Kachumber
hook: Crackly spice, cool lemony crunch

steps.t: Slice the chicken into thin escalopes and pat them dry; thick wet pieces burn outside before the centre is safely cooked.

Mix yoghurt, lemon zest, half the lemon juice, ginger-garlic paste, spice mix and salt, then coat the chicken; leave it just long enough to stain orange and smell garlicky, not so long that the lemon toughens it.
Combine gram flour and rice flour on a plate, then press each piece in firmly; a dusty loose coating falls off in the oil and leaves bald patches.
Chop cucumber, tomatoes, red onion and mint, then dress with the remaining lemon juice and salt right before serving; salt it early and the kachumber becomes a puddle.
Heat a shallow layer of oil until a pinch of flour fizzes instantly, then lay in the chicken without crowding; if the pan goes quiet, the coating drinks oil instead of crisping.
Fry until the crust is rough, golden and rigid, turning once, and the thickest piece reaches 75°C; guessing by colour alone is risky with chicken.
Drain on a rack, not kitchen paper, then plate with the cold kachumber; paper traps steam underneath and softens the crackle.

note: Rice flour keeps the shallow-fried crust crisp enough for a summer plate rather than a heavy fry-up.

name: Hanoi Pickled Prawn and Pomelo Gỏi
hook: Sweet prawns, sharp pickle, fragrant herbs

steps.t: Poach the prawns in barely simmering salted water until opaque and curled into loose commas; glassy centres are unsafe, tight spirals mean they have turned rubbery.
Lift the prawns into cold water, then drain and dry them; dressing wet prawns dilutes the lime and makes the salad taste flat.
Cut carrot and daikon into fine matchsticks, then toss with rice vinegar, half the sugar and a pinch of salt; chunky pieces stay harsh instead of quick-pickling.
Whisk fish sauce, lime juice, the remaining sugar and sliced chilli until the grains dissolve; undissolved sugar sinks, leaving the first bites sharp and the last bites syrupy.
Squeeze the pickle lightly and fold it with prawns, pomelo, mint and coriander; crushing the pomelo breaks the pearls and waters down the gỏi.
Dress the salad in two additions, stopping when everything glistens but no pool forms underneath; too much dressing turns small-plate salad into soup.
Scatter with chopped roasted peanuts at the table; add them early and they lose the dry crunch that makes the prawns taste sweeter.

note: Cooked prawns are pickled and dressed after chilling, keeping the shared plate bright and safe.
